After eating we went to her on our motorbikes and head back to town in order to go tubing, but there was a problem...my bike wouldn't start, it didn't even make a sound like it was trying to start. We messed around with it and tried to kick start it with no luck. So we thought we might have to double up and ride back on the bumpy road to the town to let them know. Luckily however, we were able to get one of the locals to help us. He quickly called over some of his buddies and after chatting in indiscernible Lao they were able to get it started! So we started back to town! However the bike I had was really crappy (as you might have guessed) and the key would fall out of the key slot when riding (it still ran without the key in it). This wasn't a problem when we were riding earlier since the key was tied onto the bike, however I untied the key when we were planing on leaving the bike at the lagoon and forgot to tie it back on after we got it started again. Well sure enough after about two minutes of riding after we left I remembered this and looked down and sure enough the key was gone, it fell out on the bumpy road (just my luck!). So we decided to drive back and look for it...nothing. 'Alright let's just get the bike back and explain what happened' we thought, so we left again. However, This time on the way out my dad spotted the key on the road and was able to pick it up! So we got the bike back to the rental shop as quickly as possible and got another bike! We were really lucky everything worked out!
-Dad riding, notice the cows, it's common for them to walk on the road here
After getting the new bike we went and changed and got ready for tubing. The tubing rental was in town and they would drive you out with your tube about 5km upstream on the river. Once you started tubing down the river there were 3 bars (really close to the start) that would throw a rope out and pull you in. It was really cool. My dad definitely felt out of place since he was probably the oldest one there haha! We stopped at each of the bars and had a beer.
-Dad looking out of place
Unfortunately I didn't take many photos with my phone so you'll have to look on Facebook for the rest. After the three bars we got back on the river and headed toward town. Well it turns out that it's the dry season right now and there's not as much water in the river (only 4ft deep at the most) this meant the trip into town would take 3 hours instead of 1 hour (during the rainy season). This is due to the fact that the current is slower with less water. Well we didn't know this prior to leaving so we left the last bar around 3 and figured we had plenty of time to make it back in...we didn't...not even close! The temperature starts to drop around 4pm as the sunsets, at this point we had been tubing for a good hour (and not just lazily, we were full on paddling and kicking to try and speed up!) with no end in sight we saw a random latter with a sign saying tuk tuk service to town, we jumped at the opportunity to get out of the cold water and get back. Of course the tuk tuk ripped us off and charged us double what it should have cost, but we were in no position to haggle being sopping wet and cold! Such a scam! It still only cost about 4 dollars for the 5 min ride, it was totally worth it! We got the tubes back just as the sun was setting.
After returning our tubes we went back to the hostel and decided to ride the motorbikes around town for a while before we had to return them. After an hour of ridding we went back and returned the bikes then went looking for a place to eat. We settled on a place down by the river. The seats were kind of bed like so I hopped on up and noticed they had WiFi so I went to grab my phone but it wasn't there!! I panicked! I had no idea where it could've been! My whole life was on that phone pictures, books to read, texting, Skype, email, blogger, music, the thought of losing it made me absolutely sick! I figured it must have fallen out while we were riding! We decided to check back at the hostel to see if I left it there...no luck. We went back to the motorbike shop to check..nothing. We searched everywhere and asked shops if they had anything. After an hour and a half I figured I'd never see it again. We happened to be by the riverside restaurant again so we decided to go back there again. Thoroughly depressed I walked into the restaurant and headed towards the same booth, I say down, and sure enough MY PHONE WAS SITTING IN THE BOOTH!! It must have bounced out when I sat down, I felt like a complete idiot, but I was a very happy idiot! :) we ordered and ate and the food was delicious!
-Dad at the table
After dinner we walked back to the hostel. I chilled in the lobby for a while to use the internet and got to Facetime with Rachel :)! It turned out to be someone's birthday and they were celebrating in the Libby and have me some cake and ice cream! My day got so much better! Around 10 I went back to the room and to bed. Tomorrow we go dirt biking!
Well that was a long post! Sorry I was late too post it, super busy lately! Thanks for reading! I hope my rants aren't to confusing!

item.title: Day 13 - Bussing to Vang Vieng
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early and had breakfast. We got a tuk-tuk to the southern bus station around 9. For those that don't know a tuk-tuk is basically a motorcycle turned into a car. It's hard to explain but here's a picture of the one we took.

 
They are tiny! Thankfully it was only a 10min ride to the bus station. We got on the bus around 930. The bus was pretty much full but there was an open row in the back where my dad moved to for more legroom which gave me two seats to myself which was awesome. The bus ride took 6 hours with two stops. Basically the whole way was through the mountains which made for some awesome views of the landscape.
 
The pictures don't do it justice. One of the stops we were given some soup witch was pretty delicious. The bathrooms at the stop were definitely lacking however. They were basically a hole in the ground and you had to pour a bucket of water down when you finished, all I can say is that I'm glad I'm a guy!
 
We finally arrived in vang Vieng around 430 where we took a tuk-tuk to our hotel. We booked a hot air balloon ride for tomorrow morning and a dirt bike ride for Thursday so were gunna be pretty busy! After that we walked around the town and found a place to eat at on the river with some incredible views and inexpensive food.
-View from out table...doesn't give it justice
My dad had the garlic steak and a beer while I had the Lao steak and a strawberry smoothie. It was delicious and only cost is about $12...total, gotta love the exchange rate!
-Lao steak and smoothie
After dinner we stopped at the ATM and walked around town some more before heading back to the hotel. We leave at 6am tomorrow for the hot air balloon ride so well be up early again!

item.title: Day 12 - Bikes and Massages
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was our last day in Luang Prabang and it started out early. The conference championships for football were on so my dad and I went to the Aussie bar at 7am to watch it since they had American sports channels. I didn't eat anything while there but I did try a redbull. The redbull here is supposedly different and is much more potent than the redbull in America. It definitely woke me up! Seattle won, and after the game we made our way back to the hostel. We didn't have anything planned today so we decided to rent bicycles. We had heard that there was a golf course not far from town (6km) so we figured we'd give it a shot. There were two problems: 1. We didn't have a map or really any idea how to get there (we were told there were lots of signs and to follow them) and 2. The bikes we had were AWFUL! I'm talking horrendous, not only were they built for a midget and not nearly big enough for me or my dad but they also DIDNT HAVE ANY GEARS! I could've live with the fact the bikes were small, but trying to pedal uphill without being able to change gears was a nightmare! On the plus side the bikes were only 2 dollars to rent for the whole day, I guess you get what you pay for.

-Me on the bike
So against our better judgement we decided to search for the golf course in hopes of maybe being able to get a round in. We quickly made a wrong turn and got lost. The map we had didn't have any street names just landmarks  and was missing some of the smaller streets, so as we passed the soccer stadium I was able to regain our bearings and get us back on track. We finally got to the road it was supposed to be on and rode for about 15mintues, we saw the golf course! The only problem was we had no clue where the entrance was and thought it may have been on a different road. So we turned around and went back about 2km (this was not a flat ride by any means) we finally made it to this gate that said 'sport club and resort'. This must be it!...wrong, but the guard knew where it was and drew us a map since he couldn't speak English. It turned out we had gone the right way just not far enough! So we rode all the way back and the turn for the course entrance was literally 100 feet from where we turned around just after a turn. We finally make it to the gate of the course and the guard there is incomprehensible, doesn't speak a lick of English. After trying to communicate with him for 15 min, he wasn't letting us past the gate or getting someone who spoke English. We were exhausted and demoralized and had to turn around and ride back to town.
-View of the course from the road, so close!
The worst part was we saw a few people playing and the course looked empty! Anyway sorry for the long rant!
Once we got back into town we changed since it got much hotter and went to lunch. We stopped at a place on the main strip called The Coconut Restaurant where I had the coconut burger and a banana smoothie. It was delicious, the burger was interesting, it had egg, bacon, pineapple, cheese, lettuce, and tomato.
-Coconut burger
After lunch we returned the bikes and walked to get a massage. We were recommend a place called the Red Cross massage.  They were busy and told us to come back in an hour so we started walking around. We found a random temple and explored it for a bit. Temples (or Wats as they're called here) in Laos are kind if like churches in America, they're everywhere, but there are a few really big ones that everyone sees. After looking at the temple we see signs for la pistachio pool and figure what the heck lets follow it and check it out. Fast forward 30 minutes later and were walking down this random dirt side street between houses following the signs looking for this pool.
-One of the many signs
We finally end up finding the pool but there's an entrance fee so we decide to head back since the hour was almost up anyway.
-Street the pool was on, the entrance is the wooden fence on the left
We finally got to the massage place around 4 and the were as busy. The massage itself was interesting it was only the second one I've ever had. The masseuse was a little laotion dude (better than a he-she I guess). It was a little weird at first but felt good and was very relaxing. The best part was it only cost $5 for an hour long massage!!! And all the money they make goes to support the Red Cross, so I'm being charitable at the same time! After the massage we walked back to the hostel and rested until dinner.
We went out looking for a place to eat and decided we wanted to eat at one of the restaurants along the river. We found a Lao BBQ place (where you cook in the middle of the table) and decided to have it again. It was delicious! The place was packed so we figured it would be good and we weren't let down.
 
After dinner we walked through the night market and picked up a few gifts and made our way back to the hostel. We leave tomorrow by bus to Vang Vieng at 9:30am. It's an 8 hour trip so I'll get some reading in!

item.title: Day 11 - Buddha Caves and Whiskey Village
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Was rudely awoken today but rosters go literally won't shut up! Our bus was leaving at 8am anyway so it wasn't a big deal. After a quick breakfast we were on out way to the dock for our boat trip to visit the Buddha caves and whiskey village. I made a amateur mistake that morning wearing shorts and a thin shirt thinking the sun would come out and it would warm up. Man was I wrong, the boat trip was a 2 hour ride up the Mekong river with freezing wind blowing in my face, it was miserable! I'm pretty sure by the time we got there I had mild hypothermia and frostbite. Anyway all that was fine, I can stand being cold in order to see cool stuff. However here's the kicker, when we get out of the boat our driver says '30 minutes!'. I thought to myself 'he's gotta be kidding right?! We just spent 2 hours on a boat ride from hell and we only get 30 minutes?! WTF!!'. Well turns out the boat driver was right, we didn't even need the whole 30 minutes. I think we took like 15 minutes and 10 of those were climbing up to the cave from the dock. The cave, which I would hardly call a cave, was so small and It was filled with hundreds of Buddha statues of various sizes, which was kinda cool if you're into looking at statues.

-Outside of the Cave
-Some of the Buddha Statues
I probably wouldn't have been so harsh about the caves if it wasn't such a long trip, but the two hours it took to get there left me disappointed. After the 30 minutes was up we got back to the boat and stopped at a small village on the way back. The village was called whiskey village, there wasn't too much to see there, mostly people trying to sell you different stuff. We did get to try some of the whiskey which was good, but a little early to be drinking.
-Whiskey
They also like to put lots of various animals in the whiskey bottles, I'm not sure why but they put everything from snakes and scorpions to geckos. I thinking adds flavor or something.
-Snake in whiskey
After the village we finally headed back to town. The ride back was much better for two reasons: the sun was finally out so it wasn't freezing cold and we were going down river so it only took an hour and a half to get back.
Once we got back we made a stop at the biggest wat in the town as well as the royal palace museum. Both of these were interesting but noting too crazy. We then stopped at a random restaurant for some pizza. I was thoroughly disappointed, it's amazing but none of the countries I have visited in my life have ever been able to make a decent pizza. After lunch we walked back to the hostel to rest until dinner. For dinner we stumbled on some street food by the night market that was a buffet, all you could fit on your plate for 10,000 kip...that's about $1.50. I had to try it! But of course my dad was being really annoying and didn't want anything to do with any food that is different than the US. After much convincing I finally got him to try it. The place was packed with people so you know it had to be good. I was not disappointed, I was finally able to  eat and not still be hungry!
-The Buffet
After dinner we wanted to look for massages but in the process of looking one of the places we came across had a ladyboy waving at us to come in for a massage. For those that don't know, a ladboy is a transvestite and for some reason they are very popular in Southeast Asia. Anyway the thought of being rubbed down by someone of a questionable gender really freaked me out so we decided against it.
We finally made our way back through the night market to our hostel. Tomorrow we don't have much planned so well see what happens, it's our last day in Luang Prabang and then were off too Vang Vieng on Tuesday!

item.title: Day 10 - Elephant Riding and Waterfalls
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I slept surprisingly well considering I had to share a bed with my dad. Woke up today around 7 and went to eat some breakfast. The dinning area of the hostel was full of some of the weirdest people I've ever seen they were some sorta hippie hipsters wearing the most ridiculous clothes. One girl even had whiskers painted on her face...so confused. Breakfast was very small basically eggs and bread (typical for a hostel). We got picked up from the hostel at 8 which took us to the elephant camp. We drive with a newlywed couple from Mexico so I got to practice some Spanish with them. The elephant trek was awesome! There were about 9 elephants and since there were so many people I got to ride on the neck of the the elephant.

 
It was really cool, the elephants hiked around for about an hour going through the river at some points. After the hike we were able to feed our elephant bananas as a treat.
 
Once we finished with the elephants we drove back to the main village for lunch. I can't remember the exact name of the food but I had a rice and beef soup that was very peppery, which I'm told is a very common Lao food. It was delicious!
After lunch we got picked up by another bus and made our way to Kung Si Falls. We met some more people on the bus who were from Holland and they had their two kids traveling who were adorable! Kung Si Falls are the biggest waterfalls in the area. On the way to the falls they also have a bear sanctuary so we got to see all of the bears which was pretty fun.
 
The falls were  about a 5 minute walk from the bears and they were incredible! The color of the water was a surreal light blue.
We were able to hike all the way up and over the falls which was a pretty steep climb but had some pretty cool views of the falls.
The falls also had a rope swing you could use to jump it which was really fun but the water was ICE cold so as soon as I hit the water I swam as fast as possible to shore.
-Swinging into the falls!
 
After about two and a half hours we left the falls and had some delicious crepes and shakes while we waited for our bus to leave. 
 
On the way back to Luang Prabang we stopped at what I think our guide called 'monk village' which was basically a small poor little village that we walked through where they tried to sell us souvenirs. We finally got back to the town at around 430. 
 
We had just enough time to hike Phou Si hill (big hill in the center of the town with some wats/temple relics). It was a short but steep hike to the top which offered some incredible views of the city. 
 
-Overlooking the town
 
-Temple type thing at the top
 
-View of the sunset
 
After chilling on the to of the hill and watching the sunset we made our way down and stopped at a restaurant called Lao Lao garden. 
 
The restaurant was super cool and we ordered the Lao BBQ which basically was like fondu but they put a fire and metal cooking thing in the middle of your table to grill the meat and cook the veggies. 
 
 
The food was awesome!! Along with vegetables we had beef, water buffalo (a Lao favorite), and chicken all of which were very tasty! 
 
After finishing our meal we made our way back to the hostel but decided to stop at the spa. The spa had a foot treatment that consisted of putting your feet in an aquarium of about one hundred fish and letting the fish eat the dead skin off of your feet! It tickled at first but it was definitely a cool experience and afterwards my feet felt pretty good! 
 
 
I took some cool pictures with the underwater camera that I'll post later! 
 
After having our feet chewed on by fish we made our way back to the hostel. One interesting fact I learned about Laos is that it is the most bombed country in the world! I never would've guessed. Tomorrow we are visiting whiskey village and Buddha caves!

item.title: Day 9 - Welcome to Laos
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Woke up around 8 today to get some breakfast then take a cab to the airport at 9. Getting to the airport took about an hour and getting through airport security took about 3 minutes. It was seriously a joke, people walked through the metal detector with watches on and the metal detector would clearly go off but the guard still waved them through. Our flight was scheduled to leave at 12:30 and since security took no time we were at the gate two hours early. To make matters worse our flight got delayed another hour. The airline bought everyone free drinks to make up for it so that was nice. Once it was finally time to board we were bused out to a propeller plane! The plane was fairly small with only about 60 passengers.

 
Nevertheless it was a short, smooth 1 hour flight. When we landed in Luang Prabang the weather was awesome! Really sunny and warm. We made our way through visa on arrival and customs and shared a cab with a girl from holland to get to our hostel. No shoes were allowed in the hostel so in order to enter you had to take them off and leave them at the front door. That was all fine and dandy but when they showed us the room there was a problem...
 
They booked us in a single bed! There weren't any double beds open for tonight either so it looks like we're sharing until tomorrow haha. Another weird thing was the shower in the bathroom was literally just a hose and drain next to the toilet, no walls, no tub, just a drain haha.
 
Other than that the place was great! Haha
After getting settled we went out to explore the town and get some food. Luang Prabang is a much much smaller town than Hanoi (only like 2 miles long and a few blocks wide for the main area). This makes Luang Prabang much less hectic and more laid back (no one honking their horn every two seconds while driving like in Hanoi). We stumbled into a random restaurant off of the main strip. I ordered the Lao soup and beer Lao.
 
The beer was great and the soup was good. It tasted very peppery and I wasn't sure what all was in it but there were wood chips in it! I guess the use it to cook the soup? Also I'm pretty sure there was seaweed in it (I couldn't tell what it was but I know seaweed is a very popular Lao dish). After dinner we ventured farther down the main strip where they have the night market, basically what you'd expect - a million tents filled with people selling the crafts. It was very big and kinda cool, I think I'm going to buy some elephant pants tomorrow haha. We also stopped at one of the tour shops and booked an elephant riding and waterfall trip which will go all day tomorrow and should be really fun! To end the night we stopped at an ice cream place then made our way back to the hostel. On the way back we ended up running into one of the people we went on the cruise with in Ha Long Bay, talk about a small world!

item.title: Day 8 - Last Day in Vietnam
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today's the last full day we had in Vietnam. We got up and had breakfast relatively late. We left the hotel around 11 to head to the Vietnamese army mueseum (one of the few things left in the city we hadn't see), however it didn't open till 1 so we had an hour and a half to kill. We decided to walk over to the temple of literature which was a 5 minute walk away. From the place was a large courtyard with buildings and relics scattered about. From what I could gather the place was used since the early 1400s as a school/temple for students.

-At the entrance
The temple of literature was much more relaxing than the hectic streets of Hanoi so we decided to hang out there for a while.
-No clue what this is but it looked pretty cool. There were many other things like this.
Once it was one we left and headed over to the army museum. The museum had tons of old planes, tanks, and other vehicles and weapons that were used in the war. Again it was really interesting to see the Vietnamese perspective of the war.
They also had a big tower with a flag, appropriately called 'Flag Tower' which you could climb about half way up.
The museum also had some pre-Vietnam war artifacts from the Vietnamese conflicts with the French and Chinese.
After the museum I reallyyy wanted to go to Le Mat, the snake village, and try eating cobra. However, my dad was being a ...for the sake of keeping this blog pg...huge baby and didn't want to go. This was royally frustrating. We ended up going to some random place on the street instead. After eating my dad decided he wanted to lay in the hotel the rest of the day, our last day in Vietnam mind you! So after a few hours of being cooped up I couldn't take it anymore and went out into the city by myself to explore some more and get some dinner. I ended up at a small street shop near our hotel that had different types of kebabs. I ended up having a beef one, chicken one, and a squid one. All of them were good! While at the restaurant I started talking with an older ditch couple that was sitting by me (everyone was next to each other since it was a small restaurant). Anyway they were really cool and I talked to them for a few hours about travel and the Holland (where Dutch people are from). We had to leave at 11 since that's when everything closes down in Hanoi. Tomorrow we leave for Luang Prabang, Laos which is an hour flight to the west.

item.title: Day 7 - Trip Back to Hanoi
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7 and went down to breakfast at the hotel. I tried the Vietnamese breakfast today which consisted of a big bowl of beef soup, which was a weird thing to have for breakfast but nonetheless was good! After lunch we got on the bus and headed to the dock. The trip back to Hanoi was the same routine as before but reverse and after about 4 hours we made it back to the Hanoi bus station where we had to haggle to get a cab for a decent price. Finally after a short cab ride we made it back to our hotel. They had the room set up with flower petals on the bed and everything, so romantic! Hahah

 
After getting settled we headed out for lunch. Today we we to an English place called the Moose and Roo Pub. I had a bacon cheeseburger which was delicious and a good reminder of home.
 
After lunch we went back to the hotel to rest and watch tv. Today was a rest day since we had already done most of the things we wanted to do in Hanoi. Since we had a late lunch we went out to dinner at a place called Bun Bo Nam Bo. Like most of the shops in the old quarter it was very skinny and long, almost like a long hallway. When we arrived they didn't give us a menu instead the waitress asked "how many". At first we we're confused about when we should order however after a couple minutes we were handed a big bowl of Bum Bo. This turned out to be one of the only things they served which is why we weren't offered a menu. The food was awesome! We were the only white people there and the place was packed with tons of local Vietnamese so we figured the place must be good.
-Big Bowl of Bum Bo
-Outside the restaurant (my dad's excellent photography skills)
After the restaurant we walked back to our hotel through the "bar street" which was literally one block filled only with bars. Everyone was packed in the street sitting on there little plastic chairs. It was pretty small but very cool (Hanoi isn't know for it's nightlife).

-The Bar Street

item.title: Day 6 - Cruising and Kayaking Lan Ha Bay
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got up fairly early and headed to the Asia Outdoors shop next door to our hotel to meet up for our cruise/kayak trip of Lan Ha bay. After a 5 minute bus ride to the bay we boarded what's called a "junk boat" which is just an old wooden ship. Our boat had a main cabin and a top deck which we sat on as we cruised out to pick up the kayaks. On our way we passed the floating markets, which, you guessed it, are markets that are floating in the bay. Lots of people live on these floating villages and fish, it's not super touristy at all.

-Floating Markets in the Bay
Another awesome thing about today was that the sun was finally out! Which was nice even though it was still relatively cold (60 degrees)! Once we got in our kayaks out tour guide, mike, took us around the bay which was full of incredible views. Unfortunately most of the pictures I took were on the waterproof camera so I'll have to upload them later. We then kayaked to a cave where we got out of our kayaks and were able to walk through. I wore flip-flops which wasn't the best choice as one of them broke on me as I was walking through the cave, but thankfully I was able to borrow my Dads water shoes since he didn't feel like going further. The cave led to a small lagoon at the other side with more incredible views. After the cave we kayaked some more and stopped at Moody beach which was on one of the small islands in the bay.
-Moody Beach
-Bouldering on the beach
After hanging out and climbing some of the rocks on the beach we made our way back to the boat for lunch.
The lunch was surprisingly good and consisted of rice, salad, salmon, spring rolls, and tofu. After eating we cruised for another 45 min out into the bay for another bit of kayaking. This time my dad decided he was too tired and stayed on the boat while I went with another person in our group. We kayaked around the bay through some stone arches and too a few beaches. One of the beaches we went to had a temple on it with a shrine of sorts which was really interesting. Once again the views were awesome! Finally we made our way back to the boat and cruised back to Cat Ba. Once we got back to the hotel I showered and passed out before we even went to lunch! Tomorrow we had back to Hanoi for a couple days before we fly to Laos which I'm super excited about (the weather should finally be warmer!)

item.title: Day 5 - Exploring The Island
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
It's day 5 and we still aren't quite adjusted to the time difference. Today I woke up around 5 (better than 12am I guess!) we took the morning slow eating breakfast and than laying around watching the movie channel. Around 9:30 we went and rented motorbikes again. The first stop today was the Cat Ba national park. The park is huge and has a trail that goes to Ngu Lam Peak. The hike was very fast and steep and only took about 20 minutes to reach the top. The views were awesome as expected.

 
There's a big watch tower at the peak however it was blocked off 😠...of course I decided to climb up anyway. I got about halfway up and stopped since the tower was so rusted the bolts looked like they were gunna break any minute.
 
After the national park we motorbiked all the way to the north pier (the only part of the island we still hadn't seen). The ride was fun with lots of hills and twists and turns but very cold. I was able to get the motorbike going about 55 miles an hour which was super fun and really makes me want to get a motorcycle once I get back. The pier itself wasn't anything special compared to the other.
 
On the way back to the main town we stopped at Trung Trung cave. We were able to walk around the entrance but the door to the cave itself was locked.
 
After the cave we ate lunch at mr zoom's restaurant. I had beef with rice and pineapple, it was great. After lunch we went back to the hotel to rest. Before dinner I decided to take the motorbike out one last time for fun and stumbled upon a cool shirt hike to the top of this mountain with a viewing deck and statute thing. There was an awesome view of the main strip where our hotel was.
-Panorama of the view
After hiking back down I drove around the town a little more and decided to go up this hill, however when I tried to make it up the hill the bike stalled and shut off. I started the bike back up and tried again, the bike stalled out again. However this time the bike wouldn't start back up! It had plenty of gas so that wasn't the problem. I ended up having to coast all the way down the hill back to the rental place. They didn't seem to care which was good and they didn't have my name or anything to rent the bike so I figured I was good. After dropping the bike off I went back to the hotel.
We decided to eat dinner at the restaurant right outside of our hotel. I ordered a hot pot. I wasn't quite sure what is was when I order it but I was cold and hungry and the name was appealing. The hot pot certainly did not disappoint!! It was essentially a large pot heated on the table where the waitress cooked the meat and other ingredients for me and served them to me in a bowl. It was a ton of food and it was awesome!
 
After dinner we made it back upstairs to our room to watch some more movies and sleep. Tomorrow were going on a cruise and kayaking day trip of lan ha bay!

item.title: Day 4 - Ha Long Bay Trip
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 4 was another early start, we had to be up for a 4 hour bus and boat trip to get to our final destination, Cat Ba Island. After breakfast we took a quick taxi ride to the bus station to start our trip. The bus was much nicer than I expected and was only about half full (winter is the slow season for tourism). The bus took us to this huge industrial port with shipping containers everywhere and we boarded the speedboat. The boat ride was nice and only took 30-45min to get to the island. One last bus to the main town and we were at our hotel. The hotel was very nice and right in the center of the town. After getting settled in we are some lunch and decided to rent motorbikes.

 
The motorbikes were awesome! They only cost 4 dollars to rent for the day and about 2-3 dollars in gas. There was no paperwork to sign or anything, the guy renting them to us didn't even get our names! Needless to say it was much less strict than the US. Anyway the first stop we made was cannon fort which had awesome views of the island.
-One if the cannons
 
The views were amazing and the weather was much nicer than the cloudy and foggy weather we had in Hanoi up to this point. After the fort we made our way to the main road to go visit hospital cave. This was in the middle of the island and is literally a hospital type bunker that was built inside a cave during the war.
-Entrance to the hospital
-Inside the cave
-Inside the hospital
After we left the cave we drove around some more on the motorbikes and made our way to the three closest beaches on the island. Since it isn't particularly sunny or warm this time of year not many people visit some the beaches were empty with almost no one in the water.
 
After the beaches we biked some more around the island until dinner which we had at My Way Cafe. I had shrimp and rice which was delicious, and as always everything was very inexpensive. After dinner we made our way back to the hotel to sleep.

item.title: Day 3 - The Coffee in Vietnam is Shit...Literally
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Like I mentioned in the last post today started very early waking up at 12 am because of the jet lag and being wide awake. I stayed up the rest of the night researching some stuff to do for the rest of our trip. To start the day we had breakfast at 7am I tried dragon and passion fruit with banana pancakes. Everything was delicious! We then booked a food tour of Hanoi.

-Dragon fruit! Feels like you're eating a pear but a different flavor
The food tour started at 11:30, our guide, Ha (no clue if that's how you really spell it), came to pick us up at our hotel to bring us to their office and the start of the tour. Right when we got to the office he offered us shots of different rice wine that had been mixed with various things. There were three other people that joined our tour, all of them were from Australia but one of them had lived in Hanoi for about two years and was bringing her friends on the tour. The tour was a walking tour around the old quarter of the city stopping at various small restaurants and street stalls.
The food was amazing! And there was tons of it! The first thing we tried was pho ga tran, which was basically chicken noodle soup without the soup part. Also at the same restaurant we had bun cha, spring rolls and sticky rice.
It's amazing to see everywhere you turn street stalls with very fresh food. Many people will actually sit on the street in little chairs to cook and eat their food.
 
To get to the next restaurant we went through lots of narrow winding alleyways that connected to people's houses. This next restaurant was much larger than the first. The first thing we tried here was thit cho aka dog meat!! It was very interesting it tasted like chicken but stronger and much more chewy. Dog meat is a very common food for locals here and is supposed to give you good luck and virility.
-About to taste Dog meat!
A few more foods we tried were banana flower salad, pumpkin leaves, spinach, and tofu in tomato sauce. I had never tried anything like these before and everything was delicious!
 
On the way to our next restaurant we made a stop for some coffee. Now I'm not much of a coffee drinker but, as I mentioned in the title this, wasn't normal coffee it was cafe chon, also know as weasel poop coffee! The beans are actually gathered from the fecees of a weasel. Supposedly the weasels select the best coffee beans to eat and their digestive systems acid and enzymes add to the flavor of the coffee! It was delicious! And very strong!
-weasel poop coffee beans
- tasting the coffee
It is interesting to note that in Hanoi all their are streets for specific things for example we went to the coffee street where almost every shop on the street sells only coffee. This occurs for many other items as well, we walked past the street for baby items, street for door knobs, street for silver jewelry, and a street for herbs. It's really interesting how it's set up, it's very similar to Peru.
We made one final stop at another small restaurant where we tried even more awesome food! My favorite by far was the deep fried shrimp with coconut! But we also had stir fried chicken, grilled fish Hanoi style (catfish), and mixed fruits.
 
After the tour we made it back to our hotel for a little rest before going to a water puppet show at 8pm. It was pretty cool, however we didn't have any idea what was going on because it was narrated in Vietnamese! It was basically a puppet show on a big pool of water.
 
After the show we made our way back to the hotel to hopefully get some sleep. Tomorrow we leave for Cat Ba island in Ha Long Bay at 730am it's about a 4 hour total journey on bus then boat.

item.title: Day 2 - Good Morning Vietnam!!!
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Even though I hadn't slept for almost 2 days I still managed to wake up at 5:30am, must be something to do with the time difference. We went down to breakfast around 7:30 it was much better than what I'm used to at hostels I had the standard eggs, ham, toast, etc.

 
After breakfast we went back to the room and planned out what we wanted to see for the day. The first stop was Hoan Kiem Lake, which was a couple blocks from our hotel. The lake is pretty small and has a temple that goes out onto the lake that we explored. We also took our first selfi of the trip 😬.
 
Since all we had was American money we stopped at the ATM. The currency here is called the Vietnamese Dong and the exchange rate is approximately 1 USD to 20,000 Dong. So I took out 1 million Dong, no big deal.
-Holding a million Dongs in my hand
After visiting the Ngoc Son temple we made our way around the lake to the Hoa Lo Prison which is now a museum. It was interesting to see the Vietnamese perspective on the war.
Being white and talk my dad and I stuck out like a sore thumb. Lots of people asked to take pictures with us haha it was an interesting experience.
 
Another weird thing about Vietnam is their traffic. There are probably 20 billion motorbikes in the city, they are literally everywhere. Also the city has no traffic rules, and stop lights are a scarcity. In order to cross the street you have to play a real life version of frogger, it's insane and very chaotic. Also I think people literally live on their motorbikes they fit so much stuff on their bikes it's ridiculous.
 
After the prison we walked to the one pillar pagoda and Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum which were pretty interesting. Finally, we made our way back to the hotel where we got some advice on where to go eat our lunch/dinner. We ended up going to a Vietnamese restaurant called 96 restaurant which was about a block away. The restaurant was very small but the food was delicious! I ended up getting Vietnamese style beef with pineapple and Hanoi beer.
After we ate about 5pm we got back to the hotel and really started feeling the effects of jet lag. We ended up falling asleep and waking up around midnight feeling wide awake! So tomorrow the plan is not to fall asleep until a normal time haha.

item.title: Day 1 - Made it to Hanoi!
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
The first flight to Seoul South Korea was painfully long, 13 hours, by far the longest flight I have ever been on. The plane was pretty awesome though. The plane was a Boeing 777, every seat had it's own personal tv, a pillow, blanket, toothbrush, headphones, and even slippers. Even though we stayed up most of last night I couldn't really sleep on the plane, instead I spent my time watching 4 movies some tv shows and playing games. I had two pretty good meals on the flight along with two Korean beers which were free like any normal beverage  so that was awesome. 
Needless to say once we landed I was exhausted. The layover ended up being 2 hours and the airport had free wifi so I got to skype with Rachel which was awesome! 😁. The flight to Hanoi was on a Boeing 747 (double decker), it was a much older plane than the 777 but it was still pretty sweet to fly on.
Once we landed we were able to get our visa on arrival and go through customs really quickly. Once we got out of the airport we took a taxi to our hotel. The taxi driver didn't speak a word of English so to communicate with us he just said "Vietnam!" In different tones and pointed at stuff. When we finally got to the place where the hotel was supposed to be we got out and he pointed us down a dark alley and said the name of the street like 5 times. Thankfully the hotel was there! It's a pretty nice place and the beds are comfy. I'm pretty sure I haven't really slept for two days now so it'll be nice to get some rest! Goodnight!
