item.title: Day 1 🇺🇸🛫🛬🇨🇳
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I decided the best strategy was to wait until the last minute to pack all my stuff so I finished packing last night around 10pm, slept for ~4 hours and then hit the road to the Atlanta airport at 2am 😫. ATL is about a 3.5 hour drive from my house, which sucks but the plane ticket was $800 cheaper than flying from Savannah! The ride up was smooth, I had to chug red bull to keep myself awake.

Getting to the airport from the parking lot and through security was super easy and I got to my gate like 3 hours early...shoulda slept another hour! First I flew to Detroit which was about a 2 hour flight and then had an hour and a half layover until my 14 hour flight to Beijing. I think I caught a few minutes of sleep here and there but for the most part I stayed awake and watched wizard of lies, unforgettable, split, and gone girl.

Jamie and I ended up landing right around the same time (~2pm), however we were arriving in different terminals. The plan was for Jamie to take the shuttle and meet me in my terminal. Seemed simple enough, but the shuttle signs were not obvious and there were a ton of different buses all going different places. Finally after about an hour she finally made it to my terminal!

From there we took the train into city and then the subway to get right by our hostel. They lady at the front desk was super helpful and gave us the overview of what all we needed to see and what to avoid. After quickly dropping off our bags we walked a few blocks to Jingshan park.

The park is pretty massive and right in front of the forbidden city. Also there are 5 pagodas you can hike up to that give you a great view of the city.

After hiking for a bit we were hungry so we walked to a nearby restaurant district which wrapped around a big lake that had paddle boats you could rent and weird old Asian dudes in speedos swimming 😂.

We ended up stopping at this hot pot restaurant (basically China's version of fondue). We were the only white people in the whole place which made us stand out. Not only that but let's just say my chopstick skills are not up to par (I'm blaming some of it on the jet lag/exhaustion) and I was constantly dropping the noodles and meat while trying to move them from the pot to my plate. Basically this meant the table became a big plate for me. Needless to say the people next to us were laughing at me...oops!

One thing we noticed is that it seems like nowhere accepts cash. They all use this app called wechat which is basically China's version of iMessage combined with Venmo. I forgot to mention that Facebook, google, Instagram, etc are all blocked in china unless you use VPN. Crazy! Another weird thing we noticed on the way back was there were a lot of old Asian dudes walking around without there shirts on, apparently this is a thing in China?

Well I've been up for about 30 hours now (trying to fight the jet lag). Hopefully this post is at least semi coherent, I promise I'll do better with the next ones!

item.title: Day 2 Temples and Crunchy scorpions 🦂 😬
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I slept great last night! I think I may have actually beat the jet leg by staying up so long. We woke up today around 7am and had the "American" breakfast at our hostel which consisted of eggs, ham, sausage, and toast.

After breakfast we took the subway south of the city center to the temple of heaven park. One thing you notice about Beijing is even though everything seems close it's all really really spread out, which makes it difficult to walk anywhere. At the temple of heaven park we saw...the temple of heaven! Shocker right? It was basically another big pagoda in the middle of the park. I asked a Chinese guy to take a picture of jamie and I. You'd think Chinese people would be good at taking pictures right? Wrong. After 3 attempts this was the best he got. Totally cut off half the pagoda!

I guess it must be the Japanese that are good picture takers 😂. In order to avoid any other bad pictures I ended up buying a selfie stick, which I've put to good use even though it makes me look like an idiot. Anyway there were a couple more temples in the park and this echo spot called the mound that was pretty cool. It was in the middle of this circle where you could hear yourself echo if you talked (Purdue had something similar on campus).

Probably one of the tallest people in china

After exploring the park we made our way back to the subway to head towards Tiananmen Square. In order to get into the square you had to go way out of the way to go to the security checkpoint which consisted of a long line of people. The square itself was pretty uneventful, just a large open area of concrete really. We also climbed up one of the old city gate entrances that was near the entrance to the square.

weird thing we saw were kids with, presumably, potty training pants. These were basically crotchless pants for babies (I guess so there was easy access to the diaper? Idk it was strange but they all wore them). Also Beijing in general is very dirty, dusty & smoggy. There is a visible haze over the city, I really don't blame the locals for wearing surgical masks.

Another thing about the square is they don't make a big deal about the famous protestor who stood in front of the tanks. In fact the picture is blocked on the Chinese internet and I'm not really sure how many people are aware of it like they are in the US.

After the square we made our way to see the forbidden city. This is where the old emperors and their families used to live when they ruled over china. Again there were a ton of temples/pagodas to see and a really cool imperial garden.

After the forbidden city we stopped at the hostel and then set off to find lunch. We were looking for a restaurant called quanjude that was famous for roast duck (the best in Beijing I'm told). Our first attempt was to use google maps to find it. Well that completely failed, there wasn't a single restaurant near where it said quanjude should be. We talked to a tourist information hut and they pointed us down a busy street and gestured that the restaurant was on the left side. After walking around with no luck for 20 minutes we were on the verge of giving up. I was furiously googling to see if there were any hints as to where this place would be. I stumbled across some pictures of the restaurant store front. It was really inconspicuous with just some Chinese lettering and a door. Then I looked up from where we were sitting and there it was! Right in front of us 😂. It turns out you had to go inside this nondescript building and take the elevator down to the basement...super obvious.

Once we were there the restaurant ended up being really cool! And the roasted duck was delicious! What you do is take this pancake/tortilla and make what I'd call a duck taco with the roast duck and some random veggies. Yumm!

After eating we walked to see the Bell and drum towers which were nearby. These were big towers that they used like clock towers to bang drums and bells every quarter hour. We climbed up both towers (the steps were super steep!) and got to see a demonstration of how they would play drums.

The hike up the tower

After the towers we decided to go to the central perk cafe. It's basically a replica of the coffee shop from Friends and since I'm a huge fan of the show I though it would be fun. So we fired up the google maps and off we went. It wasn't very close so the subway ride and everything took about 40 minutes along with about a mile of walking. Well....when we get to where it's supposed to be it was nowhere to be seen! Dammit google! Failed us again! After doing some research I found out that the cafe is actually on the complete opposite side of town! Super convenient... 😫. At this point we had already walked about 13 miles and Jamie was clearly pissed off I convinced her to go this far 😂 to see a cafe that wasn't even there.

We ended up abandoning the cafe (maybe next time) and made our way back by the hostel to a bar called Great leap brewing. I made sure to double check the place was actually going to be there before we left this time. It took another 40 minutes and more walking to get there but it was worth it! It seems like this was the only place to get craft beer in all of Beijing (I guess it's not really a thing here). The atmosphere of the place was also really cool, even though it was in the middle of the city it had its own secluded little courtyard.

Another note about Beijing is there are a TON of Asians. Now I know that might seem obvious but I was also expecting there to be a lot of tourists at all these different sites of different ethnicities. Nope, in fact the most white people we saw in one place since we arrived were at the brewery/bar!

After drinking a few good beers we decided to make our way to the Wangfujing night market. This market is know for its 'exotic' foods and if you know anything about me I love trying crazy foods! To get to the market we decided to try taking the bus, according to google it was the fastest way to get there. It actually ended up being way easier than I thought! We waited at the stop and hopped on bus #82 for 2 yuan (like 30cents) and were dropped off at the market in 15 minutes.

definitely stood out on the bus The night market was really cool! Tons of shops selling all kinds of snacks. In no time I found what I was looking for...fried scorpions! 🦂🦂🦂

They looked super disgusting! They even had live ones that were still moving skewered and waiting to be fried.

[video ] I was feeling confident after the two IPAs I had earlier, but Before I decided to try one I bought another beer from the next stand over so that I had something to wash it down with and avoid puking. It turns out they conveniently only sell them 3 to a stick so even though I only wanted 1 I ended up with 3 of these things! I decided to say "fuck it" and closed my eyes and bit one off the skewer!

Honestly, it didn't taste half bad! It was really crunchy and tasted crispy. I was trying to see if anyone wanted to try one since I had two more left but nobody was daring enough so I decided I might as well eat another one 😂. After eating two I successfully convinced Jamie that they weren't bad and she ate the last one!

We ended the night by walking around the rest of the market and getting a bubble waffle with ice cream to get rid of any after taste from the scorpions.

We made our way back to the hostel by subway. It felt amazing to finally take my shoes off and lay down! We walked a total of 16.5 miles! My feet were sore and actually had a few blisters of my toes 😳. Tomorrow is going to be another long day of walking. We're heading out on a tour to one of the more remote sections of the Great Wall to do some hiking.

item.title: Day 3 (Aka Leg day!) - The Great Wall
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 4am (I guess I didn't beat the jet lag after all!) which worked out well because I didn't have time to finish my blog from the previous day so I was able to get that done. We got the 'American' breakfast again in the lobby at 6:45 and waited to be picked up by our tour guide at 7. The 'guide' met us and a few other people in the lobby of the hostel. He clearly didn't speak much English and motioned for us to follow him. He the proceeded to sprint down the street, occasionally looking back to motion us to keep following him 😂.

Right before he decided to make a run for it!

We were all so confused but did our best to keep up. It turns out he was rushing ahead in order to get to the main road and signal the bus to stop for us. We ended up getting on the bus and settled in for the 2 hour ride to the Simatai section of the Great Wall! On the way the tour guide gave us a brief history of the wall, only about 20% of which I was able to actually comprehend 😂 (his English wasn't the best but he was very enthusiastic!).

The Simatai section of the wall has never been restored (supposedly...I have my doubts). We arrived at the base of a mountain where the entrance to a trail that took you up to the wall began. The area at the base was like a resort. Everything was clearly brand new and looked really nice. Even though this section of the wall is one of the least busy sections it seems like they're able to handle a lot more visitors.

The hike up to the wall was very quick, it only took about 15 minutes till we got on the wall. The morning was a bit foggy so it was more difficult to see the sections of the wall but it cleared up as the day went on.

The views on the wall were incredible. It's amazing to think something so massive was built so long ago, high up on the mountain ridge. By the way...why the hell did they need a wall on the mountain?! I don't get it! It would've been ridiculously hard to move an army through the mountains as it is so was the wall really adding any extra protection? I asked the guide and I don't think he understood my question 😂 he just said it was to stop the Mongolians.

Anyway! Once on the wall we hiked up the ridge going through 10 watch towers. The hike on the wall took another 45 minutes allowing for plenty of time to stop and take selfies. The selfie stick definitely paid for itself at this point. I'm not sure how high we hiked but it was pretty strenuous. Apparently Jamie is a professional mountain climber or something because she practically sprinted up the wall! I was struggling to keep up with her at times! 😂 it was good training to help prepare us for the 10 mile spartan race were doing next month. here are a few of the many selfies we took on our trek up to the top!

Once we got to the final watch tower we had about two hours before we had to get back to the entrance so we hung out at the top for a while and enjoyed the view and talked with some of the other people in our tour group. We met two different couples from the Netherlands so I talked to them for a while about my recent trip there for work. They were both extremely nice and well traveled. I'm envious of all the vacation time they get (50 days a year for the one couple!). I also met a group of people from France (which is where I was for work for 8 weeks last year) so we talked to them for a while. After about an hour we slowly decided to make our way back down the wall.

Before the tour started they tried to sell us on taking the cable car on the way down the mountain, we decided not to and I'm glad we didn't! The view coming down was much better. You could actually look out at the wall and scenery (not your feet like you had to do on the way up). Also the fog had mostly cleared so it was much easier to see the wall and how far it extended down the mountain ridge. The hike down was much less strenuous.

When we reached the bottom we regrouped and all went to lunch at a nearby restaurant. The food was all laid out on a big lazy Susan on each table. There was a ton of different food and it was all really delicious!

After lunch (around 3:30) we got back on the bus and made the 2 hour ride back to Beijing. I took a quick nap on the bus which was probably not the best idea, I felt super groggy when I woke up. The bus ended up letting us of a subway station. We (aka I) decided we should continue our quest to find the ever elusive central perk cafe from friends. We took the subway to this big mall (the new address to where it was supposed to be). The mall was huge and we had to go all the way up to the 6th floor in building A (there were 4 buildings) and we found it!

building the cafe was hidden in

I was way more excited than I probably should have been that we found it 😂. We ended up getting drinks and cheesecake and watched an episode or two of friends.

Afterwards we took the subway back to our hostel and called it an early night. Tomorrow we have to get up super early tomorrow to make our flight to Hong Kong!

item.title: Day 4 - Going ⬆️ On a Tuesday in Hong Kong 🇭🇰
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Buckle up this is a long one. (Sorry in advance for all the rants, but not really)

This morning we woke up at 4:45 in order to check out of our hostel in Beijing and have enough time to make it to our flight at 8:30. What we failed to realize was that the metro doesn't even open until 5:45! ...Rookie mistake. We definitely could've slept almost an extra hour. To kill time we wandered around and found a local grocery store and picked up some breakfast snacks to hold us over. We got on the metro right as it opened at 5:45 and finally were able to get a seat! (Usually the metro is super packed). The metro took us to the train station which then took us to the airport. Since we didn't have our boarding passes we had to wait in the long line of people who have bags to check like a bunch of peasants (I hate waiting in meaningless lines). Even though we got a later start than we planned we still made it to our gate with plenty of time to spare.

The flight from Beijing to Hong Kong took just over 3 hours, which normally wouldn't have been so bad, however no electronics were allowed to be used on the flight...at all...like for the whole flight. I ended up getting yelled at 3 times by the flight attendants to turn off my phone 😂. It was an honest mistake actually, the first time I thought they just wanted me to keep it turned off during taxi and takeoff. I started using my phone again when I thought we reached cruise altitude and got told yet again to turn it off. I figured I just turned it on too early and had to wait until we were at a higher cruising altitude or something. Finally the third time they sent their best English speaking flight attendant over to explain to me that no electronics of any kind are allowed to be on during a flight in china. I tried to explain how there's this mode you can use on the phone for airplanes but he said that still wasn't allowed 😂.

Anywaysss...after all that I gave up and decided just to watch the inflight movie they had playing. I'm not sure what the movie was called but essentially it's about this girl who is super sick at home because her immune system is so weak if she goes outside she'll die. It gets to the last ~20 minutes or so of the movie and then it decides to restart all the way back to the beginning! So I watch the whole beginning of the movie all over again and right when it's about to end then same thing happened! So I still don't know if this girl survives or not, very frustrating, avoid flying China Southern if you can help it!

As we descended through the clouds on the final approach to HK you could see the massive amounts of sky scrapers that lined the shores of the city, it was really incredible.

Once we landed we quickly made our way out of the airport. On the way we were stopped by a nice lady who I originally thought was trying to sell us something but ended up giving us a map and a lot of good advice on how to get around and what to see (I'm already starting to like this place!). We took the bus to the nearby cable car station to head to Lantau island.

The cable car trip over was really cool and we got to see some great views of the island and airport.

Lantau really looked similar to Hawaii to me. Also there was a monk on our cable car which was neat 🤓. The cable car lets you off near the top of the mountain in a small village. In the village there were a bunch of cows/buffalo (in not really sure) so of course We had to get a selfie with one. Luckily they were friendly and only tried to lick us.

One of the main attractions on Lantau island is a big Buddha that sits on the very peak which had stairs you could hike up to. The hike was a struggle with our already sore legs and blistered feet. Jamie and I made our way to the top just in time to get some good pictures before a cloud passed over and made the whole area foggy.

Also nearby on the island was a Buddhist temple that we stopped to see. Honestly it looked like all the other temples, there wasn't anything special about it that I could tell.

After the temple we took the cable car back down. In the cable car we met an Australian and English couple that were super friendly and gave us some advice on things to see in Hong Kong and also recommended going to Macau (a nearby island) for the day, which we plan to do tomorrow.

The cable car dropped us off right by the metro which we took over too Kowloon (the mainland portion of HK). Our hostel had a metro stop right next to it which was super convenient. Our hostel was tucked away on the 14th floor of a building right in the middle of downtown, couldn't have picked a better location!

Some things I noticed about Hong Kong is that it's very westernized, they have a lot of the same restaurant chains you'd see in the US and also 7-11s are literally everywhere (I think they maybe went bankrupt in the US? But they are thriving in HK!). Hong Kong was a British colony at one point. So they drive on the wrong side (left side) of the road and all their cars have the steering wheel on the right. The also walk on the left side which led to some awkward moments trying to move around people on the sidewalk. Oh and one last thing, there is a ton of money in HK, basically every car you see is $70k or more. We saw at least 2 Bentleys, Rolls Royce, if you drove a Mercedes you were poor.

Back to the story, after checking in and dropping off our bags we made our way to the ferry in order to take it across the bay (a 10 min trip) to get to the island of Hong Kong. We got on the ferry just as it was pulling away from the dock. The trip over gave us a great view of the skyline.

We we landed on the other side we quickly realized we went to the wrong port! It wasn't a big deal just added an extra mile of walking. You'd think a mile wouldn't be bad right? Wrong. Apparently whoever designed the city hated pedestrians and didn't want people waking around. The place was a fucking maze! Some streets had side walks others didn't. There was construction everywhere (they don't have enough sky scrapers apparently) which definitely didn't help. Because of all the buildings the GPS signal was about as useful as an inflatable dart board. After running around in circles we finally made it to our destination, the peak tram. This was a tram that was going to take us up to Victoria's peak (the highest in HK) to give us a gray view of the city. At this point it was around 6pm and it was packed with people and the line was wrapping around the building. If there's one thing I hate more than lines it's crowds of awful people! Everyone was pushing and trying to cut in front of us... so much fun. After about an hour we finally made it on the tram (in hindsight we should've just hiked up and not had to deal with all the people).

The tram took us to the viewing deck which again was packed with the worst kind of people (more pushing and shoving). We were able to squeeze in and get a few really cool pictures of the skyline all lit up with flashing lights, it was really incredible.

We tried to get out of the observation building but it took forever to find the exit, I was super hangry at this point so my patience was running low. After ~20min we made it out and found a nearby restaurant called Maks Noodles. I got the beef wonton which really hit the spot and the prices were super cheap.

We went to the team to make our way back down and the line was even bigger! 😡😡. There was an ice cream store next to the line(couldn't have picked a better location) so we got some to make the wait a little better. When we got back to the street level we decided to try this rooftop bar called ce la vie. Now when we checked in I specifically asked the receptionist guy if the bars had a dress code and he said no. Well of course we get to the rooftop and they tell us they can't let us in because they have a strict dress code policy! More frustration! 😂

We left the bar and walked to see the worlds longest escalator which was right by us. Honestly it was pretty lame, idk what I was expecting...it was just a really long escalator. The escalator dropped us off at Hollywood street which we heard was a cool street to walk around. I'm not sure if we were at the right part of the street but it didn't seem very cool!

We decided to make our way back to the hostel. On the way we stopped at the 7-11 to get Jamie some shampoo (hers was confiscated at the airport 😂) and I got a beer, I needed one!

At the hostel we got changed into some nicer clothes and decided to go to the Ozone bar, the highest bar in the world. We called ahead to make sure we knew he dress code! I had to wear pants and the walk there was about a mile and a half. I thought Savannah was humid but Hong Kong is just as bad if not worse! By the time we got there I was drenched! We took the elevator up 118 floors to get to the bar. It was an open air bar and had an awesome view of the HK skyline below. Not only was it the highest bar in the world but it also had the highest prices! 😂. Totally worth the experience though. They also had the nicest bathroom I've ever seen in a bar.

After having a beer and hanging out at the top we took the metro to avenue of stars which is supposed to be a cool path along the bay you can walk. The problem was it was under construction 😫 so we walked back to the hostel. Today was a super long and exhausting day! In total my phone says we walked over 14 miles! Tonight will be another early day as we plan to take the morning ferry over to Macau 🇲🇴.

item.title: Day 5 - Las Vegas... I mean Macau 🇲🇴 Gambling Capital of the 🌎
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up early again around 4am luckily I was able to fall back asleep for another couple hours before we left the hostel at around 8 am. The plan was to take the ferry over to Macau for the day. On our way to the port we stopped at a small little bakery and picked up some things to eat for breakfast. I got like 5 different pastries and they were all really delicious and super cheap! Definitely going to stop there again tomorrow. Again google struggled to give us good directions (they really need to fix that!) and finding the ferry was not very obvious but we eventually made it! The trip to Macau was an hour ferry ride each way and cost about $40 US, definitely worth the trip if you're ever in Hong Kong. The ferry was super nice and even had wifi! For those of you that don't know and are too lazy to google it (probably my mom 😜) I'll help you out- Macau was a territory of Portugal up until 1999 when it was given back to China. Macau is technically considered a special administrative region (SAR) of China but it's essentially it's own country. It has its own currency, flag, and most of the people speak Portuguese as well as Chinese. It's a really interesting mix between the two cultures. On the ferry ride over I blogged the whole time to try and catch up with everything that happened yesterday and was able to finish just as we pulled into the Macau port. Once we got off we had to go through customs and everything like you would if you left or entered a new country. Once we got out we were able to find a bus that took us too the historic district of Macau. Side note: Macau is known for all its casinos but there is an old section of the country with forts and ruins that is preserved. The bus ended up dropping us off in front of the Grand Lisboa (a really cool and massive casino just outside the historic section). You can see the incredible disparity between rich and poor. Some areas look super run down almost like the favelas in Brazil but then you see these massive casinos and super nice and exotic cars everywhere. We ended up walking through the Grand Lisboa casino and it was really cool. I'm not much of a gambler but it seemed like the game of choice was bacarat which I know absolutely nothing about. We then made our way into the historic district to see the ruins of St. Paul's Cathedral. It almost looked like a prop set of a town from an old western movie. It was literally just the front wall of the church that remained standing. Next we hiked up an old Portuguese fort which was right next to the ruins called Monte Fortelza. I forgot to mention it was EXTREMELY hot and humid. I'm used to Savannah weather but this was another level. By the time we got to the top I was drenched in sweat and exhausted but we had some cool views of the city which made it worth it. We hiked backed down and made our way towards the center of the historic district, senado square. The walk was really interesting and the houses all looked like bird cages because their balconies were barred, I guess there worried about criminal ninjas or monkeys or something. The architecture was really interesting in the historic area, you could definitely see the Portuguese influence. We also stopped at two cathedrals: Se cathedral and Igreja de sao domingos. Both churches had an 'island' style to them (lots of pastel colors) that was really unique and something I've never seen before in a church. Next we made it to senado square where we stopped in a small cookie shop that offered samples of basically every cookie they had, which was a lot. I must've had at least 30 samples 😂 they were mostly good but I had a few that were pretty terrible and I'm not sure how anyone could like them. The free samples didn't completely fill us up so we went to a Portuguese restaurant called boa mesa (it was rated highly on google). Jamie and I both ended up getting the daily special which consisted of a bean soup, pork, salad, and desert. We also split a pitcher of sangria which was perfect for such a hot day. After eating (the food was delicious btw) we tried to walk to another old Portuguese fort about a mile a way. We ended up hiking about halfway up and couldn't find a way to get to the top! Every entrance was blocked off so we weren't able to see it :(. Our final stop in the historic district was the A-Ma temple which is apparently how Macau got its name and that's all I really know about it. Well we tried to take a bus over to the temple but instead of taking bus 18A we took bus 18 which got us about a mile away from where the temple was. We grudgingly walked the rest of the way. We stopped at a small store to get some water and I also tried a Portuguese egg tart. The thing was I didn't realize it was egg, it looked more like a Rene brûlée so I was expecting it to be much sweeter, so it took me by surprise and I wasn't a big fan of it. The temple was pretty cool it was in the middle of city buildings kinda built into this little mountain/cave. Jamie's I'm annoyed at you face 😂 After checking out the temple we caught a bus to the Venetian casino. The Venetian is actually the biggest casino in the world, it's pretty incredible how massive it is. Even though I'm not much of a gambler I decided to test my luck at this weird dice game which I ended up losing on my first try :(. We also walked over to the Parisian casino which was also huge and had a giant replica of the rifle tower outside. Jamie and I both played the penny slots, which are probably the dumbest things I've ever seen...is it even possible to win money on those?! I played a dollars worth and jamie ended up cashing out at 30 hon Kong cents (about 4 US cents worth) 😂I'm still not sure why she even bothered. We finally made our way back to the ferry by bus to return to Hong Kong. The ferry ride was smooth but it ended up taking us to a different port than we left from which was super confusing! Once we got back we made our way to a restaurant called the Australia Dairy company. I absolutely loved the place! It was jam packed and Jamie and I were the only foreigners in the whole place. We even had to share a table with two other people who were very friendly and gave us recommendations on what to order. The food was so weird but good. I had a soup with macaroni noodles, egg, and ham and I also got the 'famous' steamed milk pudding which I though was delicious but Jamie didn't really enjoy. During the meal I was thirsty so I decided to drink the water that was on our table in a cup, seems normal right? Well I start to look around and nobody's drinking the water...it was weird. Then I realized the cups were supposed to be used for your silver ware when you were finished. So essentially I was drinking dish water looking like an idiot 😂😂. Another plus was the food we got was superrr cheap I think the meal was a total of $12 US for the two of us. Maybe they gave me a discount for drinking the water haha! Cup I was drinking from 😂 After dinner we walked to see the night market which was your typical tent shops selling all sorts of crap you don't really need. It was a massive market though! We also went to the ladies market, which was essentially the same as the night market and finally pet street. Pet street was a street that...had a ton of pet shops on it...shocker right?! 😂 there were a ton of cute puppies and lots of cats for sale. If only I could bring them back on the plane with me! We ended up taking the metro back to the hostel and hanging out on the terrace for a bit which has an awesome view of the city. According to my phone we did another 12.6 miles today! Good training for the spartan race! Tomorrow we've got about half the day to hangout in Hong Kong and then we're off to Guilin china!

item.title: Day 6 - HK ✈️ Guilin, China
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 7:30 we were flying to a city in China called Guilin today so we didn't have much planned. We decided to go check out Wan Sin Temple which was a few miles north of the hostel. We packed up all our stuff and headed to the metro. On the way we stopped at the bakery we ate at yesterday and got some more tasty pastries! Once we got off the metro we tried following the GPS to the temple only to realize we walked about 10 minutes in the wrong direction...thanks again google! We quickly made our way back to where the temple was. Honestly the temple was less than impressive, I guess they all kinda look the same 😂. This one did have a big garden which was pretty cool I guess. Just as I was about to tell Jamie how it wasn't worth the trip a very excited Asian man yelled at us "hey hey!!!" And frantically motioned for us to come over. At first we were super confused and then realized he wanted us to join him and what in guessing is his family and friends. The dude was super happy and thankful we took a picture with them. It was a pretty funny experience that made the trip to the temple worth it 😂. We made our way back to the downtown area to get lunch. It turned out that an old friend from grade school (who was also my setter in high school) had just got into Hong Kong! So we ended up meeting up with him for lunch at 10:30. The original place we planned to meet was closed (even though they had multiple signs saying their hours as being open at 10). Since the place we wanted to try fell through we walked around the city and found a small noodle restaurant to eat at. I got some weird looking beef with vermicelli noodles, it actually tasted a lot better than it looked! It was great to catch up with Nick, I hadn't seen him since high school! After eating we had to run to the airport to catch our flight so we took the metro to the airport train. The trip went smoothly and we used up exactly all the rest of our Hong Kong money on the train ticket (pretty good planning if you ask me!). Getting through passport control they questioned my passport again! This is the third time it's happened on this trip! I can't really blame them though - here's what my passport photo looks like 😂. Back when I thought I was a surfer and long hair was cool 😎😂 No wonder they questioned me every time. It's almost time for a new one! Also Jamie for her nail clippers confiscated, on last flight they took her shampoo so I'm pretty sure they've got it out for her too. Once we got to our gate we had some time to kill. Hong Kong airport is on its own little island and our gate had these massive windows facing the runway so I got to need out and watch planes fly in 🤓. We boarded our flight on time only to learn that we were going to have to sit on the taxiway for an hour because the airspace in china was too busy? Ugh frustrating! We eventually landed in Guilin and took the shuttle bus downtown. There was some lady speaking in Chinese who I assume was trying to sell tours to see some of the different sites. The us dropped us off about a mile from the hostel. Akon the way we passed by the elephant hill but didn't stop because we were way too hungry and just wanted to drop our bags off and eat. We also walked through this really cool lake and a night market. Even though Guilin is a 'small' city there's really no such thing as a small city in china 😂, Guilin has a population of around 5 million and is a huge tourist destination (mostly Asian tourists) because of its really cool landscape (hopefully I'll get some pictures that do it justice in the next few days). Once we got to the hostel we got a quick meal there and then went out to walk around the market some more. We also booked our tour of the rice terraces for a day trip tomorrow. The market was similar to most of the other ones we've seen. I ended up getting this bubble tea from a stand that didn't speak any English. I don't really know what it was but it tasted really good! it's much less common to speak English here is seems which has made it a little more difficult to communicate. We made it back to our hostel to get some rest. Our hostel is actually really cool it's on the rooftop of a building in the middle of downtown with a great view of the city! Tomorrow we leave for our tour at 7am, another early morning! Today we only did 7.7 miles of walking, gotta step it up tomorrow!

item.title: Day 10 - Munich
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7 am, Becca ate breakfast and got ready for her early flight (10:30). We Checked out and left the hotel around 8am for the airport. After dropping off I went to a small hill/park right by the airport to hang out and wait for Pat to drop Sarah off at the airport.

I hung out there plane spotting for 45 minutes or so before picking Pat up from the terminal (they took the train in). After picking him up we drove about 20 minutes to the Dachau concentration camp (just northwest of Munich).

We visited the camp

Scooter downtown, main square (all streets shutdown) - concert and euro championship, haubrahaus, park with surfers and Vball, beach Vball, escape game, airport to Poland.

item.title: A week in Poland
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 0/1 Sunday/Monday

Airport hotel, drive to Zakopane. Good breakfast place. Airbnb with hot tub. Burger i Piwo (beer) restaurant for dinner. Worked

Day 2 Tuesday

Forecasted rain but good weather. Eggs for breakfast .Went to moreski oko, hiked Rysy (tallest point in Poland). Sand which on top Horse cars there and back call on way down. Worked in car to pilzno (pat’s grandparents house). Stopped at Nowy Targ for call. Got smoothies. Restaurant hotel for dinner. First stop had lost power.

Day 3 Wednesday

Explored small town of pilzno. Church, kebab, bakeries, square, grocery store (lots of little things to try), weird ice cream (Lody) store. Droned at house, laundry. Worked. Really good. Another restaurant hotel for dinner, more fancy.

Day 4 Thursday

Explored town in the morning again. New ice cream shop. Dinner with Pats 2nd aunt (grandpas brothers Family), tons of food, very nice.

Day 5 Friday

Early leaving to auschwitz. 10:15 tour. Finished around 12:30. Some droning. Drive to krakow (1 hour) get to airbnb. Walk up to castle. Escape game (pirate themed, fun). Dinner at Mexican burrito place (like chipotle).

Day 6 Saturday

Walking tour, Castle tour, things full. Scooter around. Jewish quarter. Dinner at Hamas. Salt mine tour. Raining, pat dinner, no ice cream (closed). Back to airbnb.

Day 7 Sunday

Early flight, left 4am to airport. Pat left for Munich at 6 am I left for Amsterdam at 6:30am. Smooth flight. Connected through Atlanta. Got on earlier flight to Savannah. Back home!

item.title: Bonaire Day 0/1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early at 3:30, ate and got the car loaded and headed to the airport. No issues parking and checking in this time thankfully! Savannah also just opened its new security checkpoint so we went through that. Our flight to Miami was on time and uneventful. At Miami my dad landed from Chicago and happened to be just a few gates away so we met him at his gate and then walked to our connecting flights gate.

The connecting flight was also smooth to Bonaire. We landed and made our way through passport control. The airport is completely open aire and the terminal is tiny! I went across the street to get our rental car, a truck that can hold the scuba gear. It’s also a manual so I’ll be driving. We loaded up the truck and then drove about 5 minutes to our Airbnb to meet our host and unpack. After unpacking the guy we are renting scuba tanks from came and delivered our tanks and gave us the run down about diving at Bonaire. The guy was a little strange but overall really nice!

After sorting out the tanks we hung out at the little pool outside our unit and checked out the ocean.

For dinner we drove into town, trying to go to a restaurant called Mezze, however it wasn’t open so we went to a place called Unbrella instead. The food was good, I had the tuna steak. It was right in the coast so there was a good view of the water and a massive cruise ship at port.

After eating we went to the grocery store, van de twell, to get some snacks and breakfast food for the mornings. Then we drove back to the Airbnb and hung out a bit before going to sleep.

Day 1

Today we woke up around 7 am. We ate some eggs, toast, and sausage for breakfast. I got all of the scuba gear sorted out. We decided to dive from our Airbnb beach which is just south of bachelors beach. We wanted to stay close since the gear is all new. We ended up doing a ~50 min dive with an average depth of 44 feet. The dive was nice, the reef slopes off just off the coast so really easy to get to. Also navigating wasn’t bad we ended up pretty close to our Airbnb on the way back.

After diving we hung out at the Airbnb for about 2 hours. Next we went to another dive site called Hilna Hooker. This one is a wreck dive just off the coast. Finding the parking lot was pretty easy. The dive was really cool, the story is the boat was smuggling marijuana, and got caught in Bonaire. After a few years of sitting off the coast, they decided to sink it to make it up scuba site/reef. The max step of the dive was 85 feet in an average of 46 feet and 48 minutes long.

After the Dive, we went back, got all our gear washed and put away in the Dive lockers. Then my dad and I drove up the road to donkey Beach to try the cactus blue food truck. They are known for their lionfish burgers. The burgers were $26 , super pricey (all the food here is). We brought the food back to the Airbnb for lunch. The burgers were good, however, I wouldn’t go out of my way to get them for the price.

After eating, we hung out at the Airbnb in the pool, the water was a bit cold, but then it loves splashing in it. We also saw a little turtle by the concrete pier by our Airbnb. We snorkel the bit and got some pictures of him. He has one of his fins missing.

After hanging out, we drove downtown to go to dinner at a place called Mezze. It turned out we were way too early (5:30ish) for most of the restaurants, and that one was closed. We ended up going to a restaurant across the street called umbrella.

The food was good. I had the tuna steak with fries. The only downside was the bugs outside were kind of miserable. After dinner, we drove back to the Airbnb and went to sleep.

item.title: Nicaragua Day 7- 10
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 7

We woke up today at 5 am and made some eggs and bacon for breakfast. We also had bananas which Bennett was super excited about. After eating we went and played in the pool. Then we went for a walk down the beach.

The beach is maybe a mile long, fairly short and surrounded by cliffs on both sides. We were the only ones walking on the beach this morning, which was nice.

After walking we played in the ocean until Bennett lost interest, and then went and played in the pool. We had a snack by the pool, built some sandcastles on the beach, and played in the pool some more.

Around 11am we had some sandwiches for lunch and Bennett went down for a nap at 11:15. Becca and I went out to the pool area (our baby monitor had great range) and rested on the chairs while Bennett napped.

Bennett woke up around 2pm. We played at the pool and beach some more and then had an early dinner around 4:30pm. Becca made tostados with ground beef and an onion, pepper, tomato mix. It was really tasty!

After eating we went back out to watch the sunset on the beach and eat some more mangoes!

After the sunset we went back and got Bennett ready for bed.

Day 8

We woke up at 5 with Bennett and had another big breakfast of eggs, bacon, and bananas. After eating we went for another beach walk

We decided to go explore

Day 9

Today we woke up at 5 again ate a breakfast of eggs, bacon, and bananas. We did our “normal” routine and went for a beach walk. We found a bunch of cool things: crabs, slugs, sand dollars, hermit crabs, feathers.

After the beach we played in the pool until around 10:15 and then went inside for a snack. We had massages scheduled for 10:30 and 11:30. Becca went first while I put bennnet down and then I went second. The massage was good but not as good as Lydia in Ometepe, hard to complain when they’re only $30 though!

After the massages we got in the car and drove up to San Juan del sur. The first stop we tried was the light house but it ended up being too hard to get to (I’m not sure if it’s even possible to drive there). The second stop with the Christ statue on top of the mountain just both of the beach.

Day 10

Today we woke up

We loaded the car and made our

item.title: Panama Day 0
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was an early morning made even earlier thanks to Scott :). We got up officially at 3:45 to get ready, eat, and head to the airport.

Overall the travel day went very smooth. We flew from Savannah to Miami on the 6am flight which Scott and I got thankfully some sleep on.

We landed in Miami after ~1.5 hours. Originally our flight to Panama was planned to leave from the same gate we arrived at, however they ended up moving it to another terminal which we took the train to (Bennett was excited about it!).

Also in the E terminal there is a really cool playground area so we hung out there while we waited for the flight. The flight was a little delayed (~20-30min) due to the slow boarding process and traffic getting out of Miami. Once airborne the flight was relatively smooth, but Bennett didn’t nap for a second. Also we were all in the same row but not on the same side. Becca and I had asile seats and Bennett had a middle. We thought whoever was in the window next to Bennett would want to switch but they didn’t!

Once we arrived it took a bit of time to get our checked car seat and then get the rental car. By the time we got everything loaded in the rental car my mom’s flight had landed and she was on her way through customs. We met up and loaded my mom into the car. Everything fit just fine in the car, it was a rav 4. We were a little worried after our Denver trip so we packed much lighter than usual.

We got to our Airbnb after about 30 minutes. It had parking but it was a superrr tight garage, we had to pull the side mirrors in to make it fit and to add to the challenge we had to back in all while Scottie was screaming :D.

Our place was nice! It’s called hotel Colombia and it’s right in the middle of casco viejo (the historic district). We hung out at the room for a while and then went out for an early dinner at a restaurant called the pulpería- it was really good! I had the steak sandwich and a passion fruit beer.

After dinner we went back to the hotel and put Bennett and sleep. My mom offered to stay in with the kids so Becca and I could go out. However Scott was being a little difficult so we ended up strapping him on with the carrier and bringing him with. We stopped at a gelato shop, I had the dulce de leche to go and we walked around the old town. We went to a place called the paseo de bóvedas.

item.title: Panama Day 1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 6:30 after a really good night of sleep, I needed it! The kids were all still sleeping so Becca and I got ready and walked to a nearby cafe to get breakfast. Unfortunately even though the cafe opened they only had coffee and no food until 7:30.

We decided to walk back to the room and then ended up stopping at a mini mart even closer to our place to get some waters and eggs and bananas for breakfast.

When we got back everyone was up so we had breakfast in our place and then got loaded into the car to go see the Miraflores visitor center of the Panama Canal. The drive was about 30minutes and we got there around 8:30.

There were a ton of people- super touristy. We were able to buy the tickets while in line so that we didn’t have to wait for the massive tour bus of people in front of us.

We went straight to the viewing platform once we got in. Luckily there was a ship already in the locks and another ight behind it. It was really cool to see but so crowded.

There was also a small playground there so Bennett was happy for that!

After watching the two ships pass through we went back inside to watch the 3D imax movie about the history of the canal and how it works. The movie was really interesting and it was Bennetts first time in a theater so he loved it.

Some interesting facts - the canal was originally attempted by the French who tried to just dig everything out, however the rainy season and disease carrying mosquitoes killed their progress and they stopped. After 10 years of construction the US was successful using a lock and lake system that exists today. The entire system works without pumps, it’s all gravity fed so essentially letting water out of the lake every time a boat passes (this limits the number of boats to around 40 per day depending on the level of the lake). The big ships pay ~$1 Million to pass through and 5-7% of maritime trade passes through. The cheapest fee was $0.36 by Richard Halliburton who took 10 days to swim through the canal in 1928 (charged by his displacement tonnage).

After the movie it was a mad rush of people to leave, all though a tiny gift shop which took forever. Once out we loaded into the car and drove down the amador causeway to flamenco island to see the Panama sign. We took a few pictures and the. Had lunch on the water at a restaurant called the fisheria.

The service was slow (seems typical here) but the food was really good, I had a meat skewer and a shrimp skewer.

After eating we made a quick stop to fill up gas and then went back to the hotel to try and get Bennett a nap. Unfortunately that was unsuccessful so we ended up just going to the roof for a swim instead, bennett absolutely loved the pool- there was a big shallow end that was perfect for him.

After the pool we decided to do a walking tour of the city. Unfortunately it started to rain on the way there, but we were still able to do the tour. The boys were not really having it so Becca ended up taking them to a cafe for about an hour before rejoining us for the end of the tour.

On the tour we saw a few churches and learned about some of the history of Panama City. The old town looks kind of like New Orleans thanks to the early French influence and later American influence. Panama City itself is one of the only major cities in Central America with skyscrapers thanks to the lack of earthquakes and volcanos that the other countries suffer from. We also learned that the famous “Panama hat” is actually made in Ecuador and got popular because of photos of Roosevelt wearing it when he visited, the real Panama hat is round and depending on how you wear it (from turned up, sides up, back up) it means different things (single, mad, friendly, etc). Panama is made up of 10 provinces (states) and 7 different indigenous peoples that are nations within a nation.

On the tour we stopped into a small museum and learned about the Guna people and the different molas (basically fabrics with patterns) that they make.

The tour ended near the paseo de bóvedas so we ended up walking through that again with the kids and my mom. Luckily the rain has completely stopped at this point.

We got some fresh magi from a street vendor which of course Bennett loved.

Then we made out to a traditional Panamanian restaurant that our guide recommended Called nacional. The food there was really good! I got the chicken and rice dish.

After eating we made a quick stop at a cheesecake place my mom was recommended (she got a small one to go) and then we went back to the room and got the kids down for bed. Once they were all asleep Becca and I got some churros and ice cream at the restaurant just across the square from us.

The churro spilt was really good but maybe just a little too much food!after eating we went up to the rooftop to hangout a and enjoy the views of the city before going down to bed.

item.title: Panama Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was an early day, we woke up at 4:40 to have a quick breakfast of eggs and then load up the car to drive back to the airport around 5:30. We missed a turn twice on the way due to the confusing streets! Eventually we made it and I dropped everyone off at terminal 2 and then drove the car over to terminal 1 to return it. I had to take a small shuttle bus back (the terminals are kind of far apart). Security ended up not opening until 6:30 so we had to wait about 30 minutes.

Our flight left on time and was super short <1 hour. When we landed we got all out checked bags and loaded up the rental car from hertz (which took some time to get). Once we loaded up we drove about and hour to boquete. Since we couldnt check into our Airbnb until 4 we decided to first stop at the bees and butterfly tour.

The tour ended up just being a butterfly house you got to walk around in. There were a ton of butterflies which was cool to see but for $12 a person it was kind of pricey.

We stayed for about an hour and then went to lunch at a place further up the mountain called La Brulerie. The restaurant was a part of a farm and had great views. The food was also really good! I had the ribs.

After eating we decided to go in a nearby hike called the 3 waterfalls. On the way they Bennett puked in the car :/ so we gave him a quick change. It was a short (2 mi round trip) but steep hike. I carried Bennett on my back and Becca carried Scott. We all made it to the check in gate where you had to pay $10 a person to continue. My mom wasn’t up for it so she decided to head back to the car. Becca and I hiked to the first two waterfalls together. They were nice the second one was the best.

The third waterfall required some light scrambling with ropes so Becca opted to stay with the kids at the second waterfall while I ran up to see the third. It was a fun little hike but the third was nothing super special just another similar fall.

I met back up with Becca and the boys and we made our way back to the start. There was a cool little suspension bridge we took our picture on at the end.

The hike in total took us just under two hours you could definitely do it faster though without carrying a 35 lb Bennett :).

We loaded back into the car and made a stop back in town to pay for our volcano tour tomorrow and to get some groceries for the next few days.

Then we drove to check in to our Airbnb a place called hotel valle del río. The place was huge, 3 bedrooms and a big living room/kitchen area.

After settling in we decided to go back into town for dinner. We went to a restaurant called Bid Daddy’s grill. I had the taco salad which was really good. Bennett also really enjoyed watching the guitarist get set up to play while we waited for our food.

After eating we went back for an early bedtime in preparation for our early tour tomorrow.

item.title: Panama Day 3
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 3:45am to get ready and picked up for our tour at 4am to see the sunrise on the volcano. We made a quick stop in town to pick up 4 other people and then started toward the summit. The summit is only accessible by 4x4 suvs it’s all dirt/rock road and steep at some points. You can also hike up but it’s 16 miles. The whole trip up took about an hour and a half.

At the summit we parked at the radio towers and then made a very short hike up to the peak to watch the sunrise. The peak itself was a pretty small area and super crowded. The volcano is called Baru and it is the highest point in Panama. The other unique part is that you can see both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. The views of the sunrise were really nice.

Technically you could see the crater of the volcano but it really didn’t look like much of a crater to me. The volcano has been dormant for hundreds of years.

After hanging out a bit we made our way about halfway down, away from the crowds and launched the drone for some cool photos and videos. There were some clouds, all below us, but the visibility was still really good.

Just as I was landing it a park ranger with a big rifle came up and told me to stop :/. Our guide had said it was ok 🤷.we continued down to the radio towers where we had our small “breakfast” and hit chocolate. We FaceTimed my mom to check in and see how the boys were doing.

After eating we got back into the suv and drove down the mountain. Are guide was a little strange and told us all about his life, his English was really good because he lived in the states and his father was from Finland and spoke English.

We made it back to the Airbnb around 9am and hung out with everyone. We made a proper breakfast/brunch with some eggs and sausage.

After eating we decided to drive to los Cangilones de Gualaca. It was about 40 minutes away with some driving on rocky/dirt roads. The entrance was $2 for the car. Basically it’s a tiny Little Rock canyon carved by the river with plenty of areas to swim and jump in off the cliffs.

The water was super refreshing and Bennett loved swimming in the “pool” with us. We ended up staying for around 2 hours. I got some GoPro footage jumping off (they weren’t too high maybe 15-20’ and also some drone footage of the area.

After packing up we drove another 40 minutes to the hit springs in caldera which was in the way back toward boquete. Bennett threw up in the car again:/ and then fell asleep. We decided to leave the kids in the car sleeping with the AC. My mom and I went first. It was a short hike to get to the hit springs and then $3 a person to enter. They were 100% natural and there were 3 different springs one was 42 C and the others were 40 and 38 C. We went straight to the hottest one and hung out corn 10-15 minutes.

We went to checkout the other two springs and then my mom and Becca swapped so that she could go in. Becca and I mostly hung out in the hottest one and then went to the colder one for a bit before my mom called letting us know Bennett woke up. We ended up staying for about an hour in total.

After the springs we drove back to town and stopped to get gas on the way. Becca decided to hang out with Bennett and the boys at the Airbnb.

My mom and I went into town. We had to pay for our rock climbing tour tomorrow and then we walked down the main road. We made a stop at one of the chocolate shops and had a sample of their hit chocolate and I also had a frozen chocolate shake. Then we walked down all the way down to the end of the main strip (it’s not very far).

We found a good looking Italian restaurant called Tre Scalini to try. On our way back toward it we stopped at the boquete brew co to try a beer (it was only 4:30 so a little early for dinner). I had the hazy IPA beer which was pretty good.

After the drink we walked to the restaurant. The food was really good we had the bruschetta and I had a pasta called Boscaiola- it was delicious.

They had everything gluten free so we ended up getting Becca the portobello to go. On our way back to the car we stopped at a pharmacy to pickup some pedialyte for Bennett.

We made it back to the Airbnb and hung out before putting the boys to bed. Bennett puked again as we were putting him down :/ poor guy! Luckily we were already planning on doing laundry here.

After the boys went to sleep we ended up playing a game of quixx (a dice rolling game) before going to sleep ourselves.

item.title: Panama Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got to sleep in, however I ended up waking up at 4:45 anyways :). We had some breakfast at the condo before leaving at 9:15 and driving about 10 minutes to get to Los ladrillos- giant basalt rock formations that formed hundreds of years ago during the last eruption.

We met our rock climbing guide, Jose, he set up a slack line for us to play on while we waited for him to set up the top ropes for our climbing.

He took about 20 minutes to set up 5 different top ropes. I started the first climb which was the easiest called “The Border” it only took me a few minutes to reach the top.

Becca went first and had a bit more of a struggle but eventually she made it to the top!

The next routes were: mermelada, throne of the king, the orchid, and finally the fingers. They got progressively harder and the fingers had an exceptionally difficult part that took me a long time to get past.

Becca was done after the second route and I repeated a couple until my forearms and hands were absolutely dead.

After the rock climbing we drove back into the main town and stopped at a Peruvian restaurant called Inkas for lunch. I had the Peruvian chicken stir fry and it was delicious.

After eating we went back to the condo to check in on the boys. Bennett is still puking and having diarrhea so it’s been a fun time. Pray that we brought enough diapers with!

After hanging out for a little my mom and I drove to the chocolate shop to do the chocolate making class. It turned out I had accidentally booked the wrong day but they still let us join the class anyway.

The class was fun and very small we were with one other family with 3 little girls all from the Netherlands. We got to see how the cacao beans are processed and she showed us how all the different types of machines worked.

After seeing all the machines we got to make our own chocolate bars. It essentially consisted of pouring the chocolate on the table and spreading it around to cool it off until it got to the perfect temperature (31C) and then pouring it into the bar mold and adding some toppings.

I used the 80% (dark) chocolate and made a plain bar, a bar with nibs (cacao bean fragments) and cookies, and an Oreo cookie.

After we poured the bars we got a free chocolate drink to wait for the bars to cool and be ready, I got a chocolate frappe.

After the chocolate class we made a quick stop at the pharmacy to get some sunscreen and then went back to the condo.

Arepas food truck

Quixx
