item.title: Panama Day 8
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22

item.title: Day 7 - Longshen Rice 🍚 Terraces
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: I think my body hates me, Today I woke up around 1am feeling like death, I'm not sure if it was something I ate (maybe the scorpions or the dishwater 😂) but my stomach was not feeling good at all. I was able to get a little bit more sleep and eventually got out of bed around 6am. Luckily we had a 3 hour bus ride ahead of us in order to get to the famous rice terraces so I could relax for a bit. What I didn't realize was that our tour guide spoke absolutely no English and for the first hour of the bus ride spoke completely in Chinese which I can only assume was about the history of the rice fields. Some where in the middle of talking he started singing haha! Surprisingly not a bad voice but again no clue what the hell he was saying 😂. Side note: One thing I noticed about china is that the Chinese don't do lines. I'm not sure if they just don't understand them or if they don't care. I guess when you live in a country with nearly a billion and a half people if you don't push and shove your way to the front you'll never get in. Another thing is they really like to spit... like an abnormal amount. Which wouldn't be that annoying except when they spit it's like they're in some sort of competition to see who can make the most noise while spitting. It's weird and kinda nasty haha. Anyway, The 3 hour bus ride took us deep into the northern mountains. We finally stopped at what we thought was the entrance to the rice terraces but it turned out we had to switch over to another smaller bus. I was feeling a bit better until we left in the new bus. This ride took almost another hour and the driver was flying up one of the curviest roads on the side of a mountain that was just small enough to fit the bus and had sections of the road that had collapsed in what I would assume was some sort of landslide 😳. On the plus side though the views were pretty incredible! When we finally made it to our destination in one piece. I wasn't feeling good again, but thankfully Jamie had some meds that seemed to help. We were given the choice to take the cable car up to the peak or to hike. We of course chose to hike it! We had a ton of time so we figured we might as well (it's more fun if you have to work for a view). The only other people in our group that chose not to take the cable car were three French girls. They told us they were going to follow us as they were smoking their cigs (good luck 😂). They were able to keep up with us for all of about 10 min of the 40 minute hike. Along the way we saw some pretty cool views and ran into some Chinese people from another tour group that we made friends with and of course wanted to take a selfie with us. Exhausted we finally made it to the top which had more amazing views of all the rice terraces that my photos don't do justice. We walked around the mini village at the top enjoying the views and then stopped at one of the restaurants. Jamie and I both tried the bamboo rice and I also had the beef and fried rice. The bamboo rice is essentially rice and some meat and veggies shoved into a little bamboo stick, cooked, and then split in half. It was actually pretty good! While we were eating it got super foggy out and started raining (glad we were able to make it to the top before that started!). The rain didn't last too long and once it cleared up we left the restaurant to walk around some more. Near one of the hotels at the top Jamie and I found the 4 cutest little puppies! So we ended up playing with them for a while, I was tempted to try and take one with me! At this point it was about time to head back. Before we did we stopped and had some ice cream. We decided to take a different route back to the bus which ended up being longer but turned out to have much better views than the one we hiked up. It took us through a couple different villages on the way back. All of the locals were super friendly and fun to talk to. We made it back to the bus which left almost immediately but we ended up having to wait a good 40min at the second bus before we left. Once we got back to Guilin we went to our hostel to drop off some stuff and then walked to try and get to the elephant hill. It was closing soon so we rushed over as fast as we could. One thing I like about Guilin is that crosswalks aren't really a thing. Instead if you want to cross the street you have to just go for it and hope you don't get hit, it's like playing frogger on steroids. Unfortunately they closed the entrance to the hill earlier than advertised so when we got there we weren't able to make it in :(. On our walk over however we ran into more Asians that wanted to get a picture with us 😂 this must be what it feels like to be famous. We ended up walking back to the main strip and found what looked like a really cool restaurant from the outside. When we got in we realized no one there spoke any English and the menu was completely in Chinese. 'That's okay' we thought, we can use google translate to figure everything out...that didn't work so well. I successfully ordered a beer 🍻 while Jamie, who tried to order wine, ordered a fifth or some kind of hard liquor 😂. The food we ordered to share was alright, there wasn't any meat in it. We also order dumplings that ended up being filled with some kind of lettuce. I'm pretty sure the place was a vegetarian restaurant haha. Luckily all the food was super cheap so we didn't feel bad about not eating a lot of it. After dinner we stopped at the smoothie shop across the street and then made our way back to the hostel. According to the phone we walked 10.7 miles today. Hoping tomorrow I feel better because we have another busy day planned!

item.title: Day 8 - Climbing Stuff in Guilin
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: I woke up this morning still feeling bad, hoping I start feeling better soon, my plan today was to eat as much American food as possible to fix my stomach...that'll work right? We started it off right by getting the 'American breakfast' at the hostel. After breakfast we hailed a cab outside to take us to Yaoshan mountain. The cab ride over was very strange, the car in front of us kept randomly throwing fires peeks out of their window!? I have no idea why but they did it at least 6 times and our driver acted like it was just normal. Yaoshan mountain is the highest peak in Guilin. Our plan was to hike it and then take the tobaggon slide down. However when we got there we were told we couldn't hike and that the slide was closed because of the rain so we ended up taking the cable car up to the top which was essentially an old ski lift. The views on the way up were pretty spectacular. Creepy advert for the tobaggon 😂 At the top the weather got a lot cloudier and the view was completely obscured. We spent the rest of the time walking around the top which had a few temples. Some of the temples had thousands of what I assume were some sort of prayer flags tied to the trees. It was really cool to see, I wish I was able to read some of them. Wonderful view at the top! After exploring for a bit more we decide to catch a taxi back to the hostel. The Chinese are the master of the concept 'exit through the gift shop'. In order to leave the mountain we had to go through a gift shop that was essentially a binge maze that zig zagged as much as possible forcing you to walk past rows and rows of stuff that they're trying to sell you. You basically have to walk 100 feet to get to an exit that (if you were to just walk straight) is 5 feet away 😂. Finding a taxi from the mountain was pretty easy. Trying to explain to them where we were going however was next to impossible. I have a suspicion that the locals here don't know what a map is and have never used one before. I showed our driver the exact google maps route on how to get back to our hotel and she looked at it like it was some weird kind of picture. I even showed her the address to the place figuring that would help. Nope, the thing is everything has both a Chinese and English name and the address is not an exception. So even bough I showed her the name of the street and where it was on the map she still had no idea where to take us. Finally she ended up calling someone who knew English and he helped translate where we wanted to go. Another side note: all our drivers here have been terrible! I mean texting and driving, talking and driving, one of our drivers was even taking pictures of something...while driving! After making it back to the hostel we decide to give elephant hill another try. This time it was early enough so we were able to get in! We hiked up the hill first which gave us a cool view of the city and then hiked around it to get some good views of the hill itself. It's called elephant hill because well...it looks like an elephant 😂. We ran into more people outside who wanted to take their picture with us so of course we obliged. After elephant hill we went back to the main strip for lunch. I was determined to eat American food so I went in search for McDonald's. Unfortunately as I've mentioned google maps really sucks here and both places that were supposed to have McDonalds didn't 😔 so I ended up settling for Kentucky fried chicken. Apparently asians really like KFC because inside was a madhouse, it was packed! The chicken sandwich I ordered definitely had a bit more spicyness to it than what you'd get in the US. Next spot on the agenda was the reed flute cave. Again we took a taxi out there, this time we were more prepared and had our hostel write the Chinese names of places down. When we were waking to the entrance of the cave this Chinese guy approached us asking us if we wanted to take a bamboo raft. His English was surprisingly very good and supposedly the raft was going to take us to the entrance of the cave and save us time walking. It was only $3 so we decided why not, hell I would've gave the guy money just for being able to speak English as well as he did! The bamboo ride was fun but also kind of a scam. Basically they took you 100 yards across the lake and there's no way it saved you any walking 😂. The cave itself was just alright. It was super commercialized, everything was lit up in different colors, there was a speaker system, and even photo booths inside the cave. I definitely think it would've been cooler to see the cave units original form. All of the rock formations even had little name tags of what they were supposed to look like, some of them were definitely a stretch. Outside the cave we found stairs and were able to do some more hiking! This spot gave us some amazing views of the city. Once again we were forced to exit through the gift shop 😂, still haven't bought anything yet! We caught another taxi to take us back toward the city to Diecai hill (more hiking). This hill gave us more awesome views a little closer to the city and even had a makeshift slide you could take back down that was kinda fun! After all the hiking we did we were exhausted and made our way back to the hostel to relax and hang out. Jamie and I played some pool and chess and had a pizza (more American food!) which was surprisingly good! Then we called it a night. Tomorrow we make our way to the city of Chengdu.

item.title: Day 9 - Guilin to Chengdu ✈️
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was a pretty uneventful day so I'll keep it short. We slept in till around 10:30 this morning. I woke up feeling a lot better, I guess all the American food I ate yesterday did the trick! This morning I had the Oreo pancakes for breakfast. They were okay, they definitely could've used some more syrup because they were kinda dry. In china they really don't seem to like the stuffing. All the Oreos I've had here have basically been two cookies with the tiniest amount of filling between them. After breakfast we checked out of the hostel and walked around the main strip, picked up some snacks for our flight, and then hailed a taxi to the airport. Again we had some communication difficulties with the driver 😂. You'd think the taxi would at least know what airport was in English! After what was essentially a mini game of charades he figured out what we wanted. China has surprisingly been the most difficult country to communicate in that I've been to. We made it to the airport and got through security with no problems this time! We ended up boarding our plane then having to de-board because our flight was delayed again because of too much traffic. We waited another hour or two before they let us board again and head to chengdu. When we arrived at Chengdu we took the airport shuttle downtown and then walked to our hostel. Our hostel ended up being hidden in an alley behind a parking lot for a much larger hotel. Of course google couldn't figure this out so we had to talk to a couple different people and wander around before we finally found it. After dropping our bags off we went to a restaurant recommended by one of the hostel receptionists. Chengdu is in the Sichuan region of China which is known for its very spicy cuisine. Luckily at the restaurant there were two waiters who went to college in the US and spoke very good English. They showed us how the restaurant worked. It was a hot pot style restaurant where you picked out all the food you wanted and cooked it. The pot we got was half spicy and half not spicy. I ended up trying the spicy side which started off okay but by the end of the meal my mouth was on fire! Overall it was pretty good food and very unique. The whole meal only cost ~$12 for both of us including drinks! After dinner we made our way back to the hostel and tried to plan our trip to Leshan for tomorrow.

item.title: Day 10 - Leshan Mountain Giant Buddha
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: After sleeping on probably the thinnest mattress I've ever seen I woke up 6:30 and made our way to the lobby. I had another American breakfast before we left to see the giant Buddha in a town about 2 hits south of Chengdu called Leshan. Another side note about China: they don't accept credit cards anywhere. It's super annoying! Being one of the worlds super powers and largest GDPs you'd think credit cards wouldn't be an issue. I'm pretty sure all of the Southeast Asia countries I went to even accepted credit cards. It wouldn't be such an annoyance if the atms worked, but of course half of them don't so if you need to get cash you have to wander around until you get one that works. On the plus side everything here is super inexpensive! Our plan to get to the big Buddha was to take public transportation. This turned out to be a little more complicated than we thought. At first we got on the right bus number but going the wrong direction so we had to get off and catch another bus going back. There is absolutely no English lettering or words for any of the stops so trying to explain where your trying to go is next to impossible. We finally made it to our stop, the bus station south of the city. We went to buy tickets and they asked for our passports...I didn't have mine 😫. Luckily the lady hesitantly accepted my drivers license! Another funny note about China is you have to be careful of the water fountains/coolers. The Chinese like their water hot (I guess for their tea and noodles) so a lot of the times the water fountains will have steaming hot water! The 2 hour bus ride to Leshan was pretty uneventful. When we got there we were approached by a "taxi driver" who said he could take us to the Buddha. I was skeptical, like I usually am with people that approach me out of nowhere. We go to his car and it's unmarked with no meter...double red flag. He negotiates a price of 40 rmb to take us there. I had a feeling it was a bit high but we didn't see any other legitimate taxis so we figured we might as well. Surprisingly we made it to our destination! We had to hike a little to arrive at the base of the giant Buddha. It was massive and carved into the mountain side. It looked like something you'd see in an Indiana jones movie or something. Besides the giant Buddha there were a bunch of other random temples and caves we hiked to see. While we were there we ran into the ditch couple that we met on our tour of the Great Wall...small world! Jamie super stoked to see a random temple On the way back to the bus station we hailed a taxi (from farther away then we were dropped off) and it only ended costing us 17 rmb! The first guy totally ripped us off! At least 23 rmb only comes out to be like 3 US dollars it could've been worse. The 2 hour bus back to Chengdu was orettt uneventful. Another observation about the Chinese is they never will get up from their seat to let you out. So if you have the window seat on the plane and need to get out you have to awkwardly shuffle past. The bus station in Chengdu is right next to this famous bridge (don't ask me what it's famous for) so we decided to walk over there and check it out. The bridge ended up being closed so we weren't able to walk across it. Afterwards we caught a bus back to where our hostel was (more communication struggles!). Nothing in Chengdu is close and although there is a metro it's very limited as far as where you can get to with it so you are pretty much forced to take the buses everywhere. After resting at the hostel for a bit we got recommendations to eat at a nearby restaurant. The place was all in Chinese and of course no one spoke any English but at least the menu had pictures! Our waitress was a good sport trying to use google translate to understand what we meant. I ended up getting some chicken and peanut dish that was pretty good and had a little bit of a spicyness to it. Jamie had some sort of pork ribs and struggle to try and eat them with her chopsticks 😂. After dinner we made our way back to the hostel for the night. Tomorrow we're going to the famous Chengdu panda research base 🐼

item.title: Day 11 - 🐼🐼
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 6:30ish and got all our stuff packed up. Today we were heading to the city of Xi'an, but first we were going to see some pandas! We went downstairs to the lobby at 7, the time breakfast is supposed to start and when you're able to checkout. Of course they weren't ready for us 🙄. It took another 15 minutes before the guy showed up to check is out and there was no sign of breakfast being ready anytime soon so we left for the bus stop. This time we were sure to get on the correct bus, however we had to transfer to bus 87 at the end of the route. Well of course bus 87 was no where to be found. I asked at least 5 people, all who pointed us in different directions 😂. Well it turned out the #87 bus driver slept in too late or something because he finally showed up about 20 min after he was scheduled to. The whole trip probably took just over an hour, but we made it! I forgot to mention we had to carry our bags with us all day. Our hostel said we could leave them at the hostel, which usually means there's a secure bag room or something...nope we could leave them in the middle of the lobby for anyone to grab. I really didn't trust their competence considering they couldn't even make breakfast on time, so that's the long story as to why we had all our bags. Anyway, the place is called the Chengdu panda breeding research center and is world famous for being able to very successfully breed pandas in captivity. Another thing I think they're famous for is having the most white people in all of Chengdu, maybe even all of china! Seriously though, I guess white people really like pandas 😂. The place was pretty massive and had all different types of enclosures with different types of pandas (unfortunately the red panda exhibit was closed) and also the split the panda up by age group. If you really wanted to you could pay ~$300 US to play with some of the pandas. It was a little out of our budget, but maybe next time! I forgot to mention we ran into the same ditch couple again! Third time in a row haha, it was pretty funny. Overall the pandas were a cool thing to see. I feel like a trip to china wouldn't be complete without them 🐼. After spending the morning with the pandas we took the bus back to the city to see the Wenshuyuan monastery. We were finally starting to get a hang of the bus system! On the way we stopped at a Chinese fast food restaurant called dicos. I had a pineapple chicken sandwhich that was pretty good. The monastery was really interesting, we hung out there for about an hour, I had a coffee and then we walked around the grounds to see the big temple. I didn't know monks could have iPhones! After the monastery we decided to check out one of the parks. There was a metro from the monastery that went straight there so we decided to take it. Before this according to google chengdu's metro line was very limited and not extensive at all. Well it turns out Google was wrong again! Jeeze! The metro (which to googles credit seemed very new) had a ton of different lines with stops all over the place. They even had a stop at the airport! We made it to the park and walked around a bit. There was. Bunch of people dancing and a nice lake. Since we found out the metro basically went everywhere we decided to head further south to see the new global center, which is supposedly the biggest mall in the world! On the way we also saw tianafu square which has a big statue of Mao (the founder of the Chinese communist party that took over power in the 40s). We entered the mall from the basement t and at first glance didn't seem like much, but when we got to the main entrance we saw just how massive it was! The place has a ginormous indoor water park, ice stake rink, movie theater, and tons of shops and stores. We got a bunch of snack food and walked around for about an hour. We ended up taking the metro to the airport which went really smoothly and our flight even left on time! (A rarity in china). Once we arrived in xi'an we caught the bus downtown which took about an hour and then a taxi from there to our hostel. Our hostel was packed!! There were so many people, most of them seemed to be British. Since we had some time we decided to drop out bags off and go explore the city. We saw the bell and drum towers which were all lit up since it was night time, they looked really cool. We also explored the nearby Muslim quarter which is we'll know for all its street food. Of course now that my stomach was feeling better I had to try some! 😂. I had some sort of grilled meat and potatoes along with a rice cake desert. They were all super delicious! Afterwards we made our way back to our hostel. Trying to find an ATM that would work for us (that took foreverrrr). But eventually we found one and made it back. Tomorrow we're doing a tour of the famous terra-cotta warriors!

item.title: Day 12 - Xi'an Terra-Cotta Warriors ⚔️
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: This morning we slept in until about 8:30. We got ready and made our way down to the lobby of the hostel for breakfast. It was only 30 yuan (~$5.50 US) for an all you can eat breakfast, it was delicious and I definitely stuffed my face 😁. After eating we got picked up at the hostel by our tour guide to go see the terra-cotta warriors. We picked up about 12 people and made our way by bus. It was around and hour and a half drive to get out there. Along the way our guide, JaJa (definitely not how you spell it but that's what it sounded like), gave us a rundown on the history behind the warriors. Here's the 2min version: The first emperor to unify china had ~7,000 people build all these clay soldiers to surround his grave. He believed they would help protect him in the afterlife. And in case that didn't sound crazy enough, the emperor decided to kill ALL of the people that helped build all the soldiers so that they would remain a secret. Fast forward to the 1970s and a farmer in china trying to dig a well on his farm stumbles across one of the warriors. For his efforts the Chinese government gave him 10 yuan (~$1.5) in exchange for his land...sounds pretty fair 😂. The terra-cotta warriors were very cool to see. There were 3 pits in different stages of restoration. To date there's been ~8,000 warriors that have been found. Most of them were completely shattered so essentially it's a massive puzzle to put them back together and restore them. After viewing all 3 pits we made our way to a nearby restaurant for lunch. It was another big table with a lazy Susan and all different kinds of dishes. On the tour we met 3 people from New Jersey (the first Americans we've met on our whole trip!) and also some people who were from Brussels. After lunch we got a free tea tasting session. One of the teas (I think it was called black lychee) was delicious! The second tea we tried...not so much haha. It was a really fun experience. After tea we took a short bus ride to see the hill where the emperor was actually buried. His tomb had still yet to be opened because they're worried once its exposed to air it will deteriorate. Also you're not allowed to go too close because the emperor had mercury rivers in his tomb and the land is supposedly still toxic. It wasn't really much to see honestly, kinda just a hill, but hey it was included in the tour! We took the car back to Xi'an and got dropped off at the east gate of the wall. Xi'an city center is surrounded by a pretty large (I'd say about 40-50 foot) wall. We went up to the top and rented bicycles and rode around the whole wall which was around 8miles. It was a bumpy ride but was a cool way to see the city! The one difficulty was that the bikes only had one gear 😫. After dropping the bikes back off. We walked back to the hostel to relax for a bit. We decided to meet the friends we just met from New Jersey at the rooftop of their hostel which was really close to ours. They had surprisingly good food there! After dinner we all caught a bus down to the wild goose pagoda to try and see the free show they do there every night. Unfortunately we just missed it! :( We walked around a bit to see the pagoda then went back to their hostel to play beer pong 😂. Even though we missed the show it was a fun night! Tomorrow we wake up early to head to mount huashan to hike "the worlds deadliest hike" hopefully we survive!

item.title: Day 13 - I Survived The "Deadliest Hike In the World" At Mount Huashan ⛰😳☠️⛰
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up to Jamie shaking me at 6:00am I was a little hung over from last night (it was only $1.50 US for a big beer 🍻!). I slowly gathered my things and got ready for the day. The plan was to hike Mount Huashan, the one of the largest sin China and also know as "the deadliest" in the world! We walked to the metro which took us to the train station. While trying to figure out where to by the train tickets (the first 3 offices were closed) we ran into a young couple (David and Noelle) from New York City who were also trying to hike the mountain. Together we were able to find the ticket office and caught the 7:25 bullet train to the mountain. The train took about 40 minutes which was just enough time for me to finish my blog for the day before. When we arrived we took the free shuttle which brought us to the base of the entrance to the mountain (only a few minutes from the train). We bought our tickets for the park entrance and got on yet another bus which took us to the north peak cable car. It is possible to hike up the mountain from the base. Our hostel receptionist said we had enough time to hike it...yea right! To get up to where the cable car took you was over a 5 hour hike and literally tens of thousands of stairs! And then you still have to hike the peaks when you get there! So we opted to take the cable car up with David and Noelle. The views of the mountain were absolutely incredible. We were lucky that the day wasn't too cloudy which allowed us to see for miles. The mountain has a trail that loops around to the four highest peaks. We started at the North peak then made our way to the East, South, and West peaks. The hike up to the North peak was thousands of steps...definitely a good leg workout! Hopefully I'll gain a couple inches in my vertical by the time I get home 😂. There were a ton of awesome viewpoints along the hike. Some parts of the hike were super steep and you actually had to climb up what was essentially a ladder that was carved into the rock face...don't slip! Also on the way up I had to use the bathroom and in China they don't have western toilets they use what Jamie and I like to refer to as squatty pottys. Essentially they're just holes in the ground...so that was a fun experience 😷. At the top of the peak there was an overhang that you could climb out too and get your picture on. It was exhilarating, my feet were dangling over 6000' in the air. There were many more great views and of course we were asked a few times to get our picture with a few more asians 😂. The highlight of the hike was when we hiked the "plank in the sky" which was by the South Peak. The plank in the sky is where Mount Huashan gets the reputation for being the deadliest hike in the world! By the time we made it to the plank we had hiked for at least 2-3 hours so my legs were already exhausted and on the verge of shaking not only that but I was still not feeling he greatest from all the drinking the night before 😂 definitely not the best conditions for this section of the hike! The plank walk was essentially 2-4 2x4s nailed into the side of the mountain that you walked across to get to a semicolon spot in the mountain. The problem is it's crowded! So even though it's not a super long distance it takes a while because everyone that goes out has to come back the same way! We got our harness which cost about $5 US (it went around your shoulders and I'm really not sure how effective it would be if you fell...I wasn't going to find out!). On the way down you had to stop and wait for people coming back up, it was torture! I would have much preferred to go through it and come back fast, sitting up there contemplating all the things that could go wrong and how bad it would hurt to fall made it worse! Surprisingly Jamie hiked the plank like a boss, even though she's afraid of heights she was less framed out than I was! She was the one that took all the pictures, I was way to nervous I'd drop my phone so I didn't take it out 😂. Even though I was freaking out I was able to stop myself from shaking long enough to hang off the wall with one arm, so that I good get some good insta and Facebook pics! 😁 The funny thing is the viewpoint the planks take you to wasn't even that cool! The worst part was on the way back you had to pass everyone who was coming down. This meant you had to step farther off the wall and move your clips around them 😳. The whole plank hike took around and hour - hour and a half to finish because of the crowd. It was definitely on of the most thrilling and adrenaline pumping experiences I've done in my life. When we got back I was relieved to be back on solid ground. There was a restaurant nearby so we all stopped for lunch. We continued hiking to the top of the South and West peaks. One funny thing was the Chinese really like screaming when the get to the top of the mountain it was pretty hilarious. The mountain was getting noticeably more crowded as the day went on. After the West peak we made our way back down on the West cable car. In total I think we hiked for around 5 hours on the mountain. According to apple we did about 2,300 feet. Once we got down we had to take a bus back down to the park entrance and then shuttle to the train, train back to the metro, and metro back to the hostel...were getting pretty good at using the public transport in china! At the hostel we rested for a little and went down to hang out in the lobby. While there we met some cool people, one from another part of China, Italy, and Belgium. They invited us out to dinner with them. For dinner we went back to the Muslim quarter and found a secluded restaurant that the Chinese guy we met heard was good. It was awesome having someone who could speak Chinese with us! We ended up trying a soup that had bread, noodles, and lamb. It was delicious and super cheap! After dinner we walked back through the Muslim quarter and tried some rice cakes with rose jelly that our Chinese friend recommended to us. They were really good but very sugary! I also tried a drink that was made from sugarcane that was alright. It kind of had a waterway coconut taste to it. Once we got back to the hostel we hung out and talked with our new friends over beer. One interesting thing we learned was that a lot of people in china actually really like Trump?! Apparently they really like his "Make America great again slogan" 😂. We also learned that people spitting in public is actually considered very rude and it's usually the uneducated that do it. Another funny thing I forgot to mention is what we like to call the "Beijing bikini". A lot of men like to fold up the bottom of their shirts (holding it up with their belly) too cool off and walk around in public like that 😂. I'll see if I can get some good pictures of it, supposedly it's also mostly the uneducated people that do it. Tomorrow we head back to Beijing to see the wall one last time to finish off our trip!

item.title: Day 14 - Pork Lungs and Baijiu in Beijing 🍻
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 7, made our way downstairs for another all you can eat America breakfast. After breakfast we quickly got packed and took the metro to the train station to catch our train to Beijing. Xian to Beijing is fairly far away but we were on one of China's bullet trains to we were able to make the trip in 5 hours going 200+ MPH! I was able to finish my blog on the train and get some much needed rest. I watched some British chick flick on Jamie's iPad called "Love, Rosie" which, if I'm honest, actually wasn't too bad haha! We ended up getting into Beijing a little before 2pm and then caught the metro to our hostel which took ~an hour. We dropped our bags off at the hostel and then went out looking for food. I was hungry and didn't want to walk that far so we stumbled into the first place we saw that looked decent. Everything was in Chinese but there were pictures so I figured we'd be fine....I've never been more wrong. I ordered what I thought was some kind of a beef and noodle soup...nope! The meat looked a little weird but I'd tried to keep an open mind. I'll be honest, It wasn't the best, sometimes when go for something new it's awesome and other times it's not. This time it definitely was not. I wasn't about to let the food go to waste so I eat just about the whole bowl when Jamie decides it would be a good idea to google what we're eating and see what it really is. That was the worst idea! So it turns out we had order a pork soup...doesn't sound bad right? Wrong! We his was not your typical pork. The soup consisted of Pork lung and intestines (what I thought was some kind of sausage)! 😖 after gaining that knowledge I couldn't eat another bite haha. We quickly left the restaurant, I'm sure the waitress thought we were crazy 😂. From the restaurant we ended up taking the metro out to the summer palace. It was quite the hike to get to and took over an hour. The palace itself was really cool! It surrounds this lake and the main part of the palace is on a hill. We needed up walking around for about 1 and a half hours. We ended up taking a bus back to the metro and then the metro back to our hostel for dinner. I ended up getting the sweet and sour chicken, which was delicious and was the first food I've had over here that I would think of as Chinese food back in the states 😂. After dinner we ended up walking about 30 minutes to meet our new friends from New Jersey out at a nearby tiki hut bar. We ended up going to a few places with them and stayed our way later than we probably should have! We also tried China's liquor which was called baijiu (pronounced "bye-Joe") which I would highly recommend 😂😂. It tasted like rubber and industrial chemicals! Tomorrow we head back to the Great Wall to hike the "wild" unrestored section.

item.title: Day 15 - The Wild Wall
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was another early day, Jamie woke up around 7am to get some breakfast in the lobby of our hostel. I was definitely feeling the baijiu and lack of sleep from night before! Today we were going to see an unrestored section of the Great Wall and hike more of it. Our driver came and picked us up at our hotel around 7:30. It took about 2 and a half hours to get to the start of our hike. It was at the base of this mountain. Our driver, who spoke essentially no English got out of the car and motioned for us to follow him down this path through the dense trees and up the mountain. As we started we noticed a sign that said "this section of the wall is closed to the public"... yes, I already knew this was going to be cool! The area was very remote. We followed our driver/guide for about an hour up the mountain. He was very out of breath during the hike and we had to stop a few times to rest (kinda weird because I figure he does this all the time). After about an hour we finally made it to the top where jiankou tower was. Because this section of the wall was unrestored it was partly grown over by bushes. It was really cool to see the effects of nature over time. We hiked from Jiankou all the way to Mutianyu (a popular section of the wall). It was cool to see the wall get more and more restored the farther we hiked. Certain sections of the wall were super steep! And because it wasn't restored there were a ton of loose stones so you had to be really careful not to trip! After probably 2 hours of hiking through bushes we finally made it to the more restored area of the wall! There were a ton more people at this section. In total I think we hiked around 6 miles to get to the end of the wall and about 4.5 hours. It's still incredible to think that they built all of it so long ago. In order to get all the way down we took a tobaggon slide! It was a ton of fun! The people in front of us were slow though so we had to keep slowing down and stopping :(. At the bottom of the slide we took a short shuttle ride down to the town where our driver was waiting for us. We stopped at a restaurant in the town that our driver recommended. We were starving so we ordered way too much food! Some dumplings, chicken, and fried rice. It was all super delicious. After lunch we made the drive back to Beijing. The traffic in the city was pretty bad so it took a little longer. It was kinda funny because our driver kept giving us drinks. I think he gave each of us about 5 waters, a coke, and iced tea 😂. Once we got back to the hostel we rested for a couple hours. Once it got dark we walked to the Hutongs to walk through some of the shops there. We also got some froyo (I think it's better in the states honestly haha). After walking around for a while we took a short metro ride up to the Olympic park. It was really cool to see the birds nest and water cube all lit up! The whole area was massive and very crowded. We also saw the wall that listed out all the medal winners from the Beijing Olympics. After walking around we made our way back to the hostel. We leave tomorrow around lunch!

item.title: Day 16/17 - 316,205 Steps 159.5 Miles 🇨🇳✈️🇺🇸
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
One last post to close out the trip!

According to the Apple health app over the course of our trip Jamie and I walked/hiked 159.5 miles and over 10,000'! Overall it was a hugely successful trip and I'm glad I got to experience with my little sis (even though I'm sure I got on her nerves more than a few times 😂)!

Today was a very relaxed day we slept in had the 'American; breakfast again at the hostel and then left by metro/train for the airport at noon. I ended up getting to the gate like 3 hours early.

The flight went smoothly, just after take off I'm pretty sure I saw the great from the plane.

it was about 12 and a half hours to Detroit and I think I watched about 6 or 7 movies. I'm really getting to be a pro at skipping past the opening Ad that Delta puts before each of the movies haha! I got into Detroit just before 5pm local time and had a ~2 hour layover until my flight to Atlanta. The first thing I did now that I was back in America was get a massive burrito, it was beyond amazing!

Once I got to Atlanta I hopped on the shuttle to get to the parking lot where I parked my car. The place was called Peachy Airport parking and if you ever need a cheap place to park near the Atlanta airport I definitely recommend them. The drive from Atlanta back to my house was another 3 and a half hours so I didn't make it home until ~2:30am. To make matters worse the AC in my house wasn't working 😳! after a couple unsuccessful attempts to fix it I went to bed (I had to wake up at 6am for work!).

I think the biggest surprises for me were the lack of people that understood English, China was probably the most difficult country to communicate out of the 23 countries I've traveled to. Another surprise was not accepting American credit cards; having to use only cash was such a pain!

My favorite parts of the trip by far were the Great Wall and hiking mount huashan. I'd highly recommend them if you ever visit China!

Now it's back to reality for at least a few few days then on Friday I head back to Chicago to visit the fam!

That's it for now, I Can't wait to start planning the next adventure! Thanks for reading ✌️🙃✌️🇨🇳

item.title: Kilimanjaro Trip September 2018
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
It's finally that time of year again! The itch to travel has almost become unbearable. This year I'm heading to Africa to climb it's tallest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro. Kilimanjaro is one of the 7 summits (the seven highest peaks on each continent). I somehow convinced my best friend to join me on this "vacation". We both have pretty minimal experience climbing and camping so hopefully we make it. I'm going to do my best to keep up a blog (depending on how good the reception is).

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Can’t believe it’s finally here! You’ve been so excited about this all year :)

item.title: Dubai Layover
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Quick update. I spent the day in Chicago, went on a bike ride with my mom in the morning and then met my grandparents for lunch and dinner and hung out until my flight which left Chicago around 8:45. Here's everything I packed, I tried to keep it to just one backpack but that proved to be impossible. Thankfully I was able to borrow Jamie's backpack to fit everything and also be stylin (it's purple). The airplane was a 777-300 and the interior was decked out I had a window seat and no one sitting next to me so I was able to spread out and get comfortable. The flight to Dubai was 13.5 hours which left plenty of time to watch movies. I watched Altered carbon, Breaking and exiting, Tomb raider, True grit, and Gringo. Surprisingly I was able to get some sleep which I usually can't do on an airplane. We arrived in Dubai around 6:30 pm and had an 18 hour layover until our next flight. Of course as we're going through immigration Patryk realized he forgot his kindle and charger on the plane. He went back to try to see if he could get it before the plane left but didn't have any luck. Hopefully he can get it on the way back. We left the airport and made our way to the hotel by way of the metro. It became immediately apparent this place was in he desert...it was hot! I'd like to think I'm used to the heat after living in Savannah for so long but this was a whole other level. The sun was down and it was still 96 degrees outside! The hotel was surprisingly nice. We checked in and left our bags in the room to head to downtown Dubai. Unfortunately the Uber helicopter wasn't available so we had to settle for a regular Uber. Our first stop was the Dubai mall. It was filled with a ton of shops (surprisingly very westernized). The mall was massive and seemingly built as a maze to keep you inside as long as possible. We made our way through the mall to the outside promenade which had awesome views of the Burj kahlifa (currently the tallest building in the world). The place reminded me of a mix between Las Vegas and Epcot. The man made lake right in front of the Burj had a pretty cool water fountain show every 30 min accompanied by a light show on the buildings. We hung outside for ~ a half hour at a cafe and had some smoothies. Afterwards we made our way back to the hotel. The next day we booked tickets to go up to the top of the Burj Khalifa. The hotel provided breakfast which was surprisingly awesome. It was a buffet with tons of different options. After we made our way by under back to the Burj. The observation deck was outside and it was a relatively clear day so there were some great views of the city. It really does look like an oasis in the desert. Afterwards we made our way back to the hotel and chilled before catching the metro back tor the airport. What we didn't realize was that this time we were flying out of terminal 2 which is on the complete other side of the airport so we had to take another taxi to get there. On top of that going through security the tried to confiscate my hiking poles even though I didn't have any issues getting them on the previous flight. I had to convince the police officer that they were harmless. Luckily he let me keep them. The plane to Kilimanjaro was the opposite of the previous flight. It was super old and even though it had TVs they charged you to watch movies. We also realized that no food or snacks were provided on the flight...what a ripoff! To top it off we ended up having to fly to dar es salaam first and then onto Kilimanjaro so the whole trip took ~8 hours. We eventually made it and met up with our driver outside the airport. It was about a 45 min drive to where we're staying. We got in around 10 at night so I'm pretty exhausted. The hike starts tomorrow at 9am!

item.title: Day 1 Kilimanjaro hike
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was the first day of our Kilimanjaro hike. I woke up around 4am because the roosters outside were making a ton of noise. Luckily I was able to get a little more sleep until we woke up around 7. Unfortunately the place we're staying in is basically a hut so warm water essentially doesn't exist which meant my shower was awful! But I enjoyed it because it's probably the last shower I'll get to take for the next 10 days. We ate breakfast at 8 and finished packing up around 9. There's a really cute dog that lived at the house named Frankie. So obviously I became friends with him. Our guide, Moses, met us at our house and gave us a quick brief of the hike. We're doing the 6 day Machame route (called the whiskey route because of its difficulty) which basically starts at the east end and works it's way up to the peak. Kilimanjaro is the tallest peak in Africa at over 19,300 feet and it's a volcano. After the briefing we loaded into a van with about 10 other people including our guide, assistant guide, chef, waiter, and porters. We made a quick stop in the town to pick up some things and then headed to the Machame gate, the start of the hike. We arrived at around 11 and had a quick lunch while preparing for the hike. Everything seemed to be going smoothly...so we thought. Well it turns out they switched to some new payment system for the permits and our guide wasn't able to get the permit for us to climb the mountain. We ended up having to wait OVER 5 HOURS for them to get it sorted out! 😫 while we were waiting we met some cool people from Sweden (who were also stuck waiting for their guide to get payment through), played a board game that pat brought, and took a picture with some random Kenyans who really wanted a picture with us for some reason...must be my stunningly good looks. Anyways after we finally got the payment sorted we began the hike. The guide told us this hike should take around 5-8 hours to get to the first camp. Great, that meant getting to camp at 10pm, well after sunset! We ended up hiking a much faster pace and arrived at 7:40 only 3 hours! I didn't think the hike was that bad but Patryk was definitely struggling. I ended up carrying his pack for about half the hike to help him out. The elevation ofthe first camp was ~11,000 feet. Pat had some diamox (altitude sickness pills) so I felt really good. When we arrived at camp the porters had everything already set up so we quickly washed up and changed and the had some dinner in the meal tent. Dinner was actually really good we had hot chocolate, cucumber soup, potatoes, veggies, tilapia, and salad. After dinner our guide did a quick health check and then briefed us about tomorrow's hike. I'm pretty exhausted now so I'm gunna get some sleep!

item.title: Day 2 Machame to Shira Camp
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Last night I slept terrible, I went to be around 11pm and woke up at 1:50am 😫. The ground is super hard and even though we have a sleeping pad it feels like we’re sleeping on concrete. I just couldn’t get comfortable. I ended up watching a couple movies to try and pass the time and fall asleep but I wasn’t really able to. The reception here is absolutely terrible. Not that I was expecting much but it does make me realize how much I take for granted modern technology, and my comfy bed for that matter. We ended up getting up for tea around 6am and the started getting our things packed back up and organized. Another thing, the bathrooms here are absolutely disgusting...I’ll just leave it at that. For breakfast we had omelet, sausage, porridge, and bread. It was really filling and good! After breakfast our guide briefed us and checked our pulse and oxygen levels then we started day 2 of the hike around 8am. Today we went from Machame camp to shira camp. The distance was less than day 1, but the hike was much steeper. Luckily the weather was perfect, it was sunny with awesome visibility. Also today we went at a muchhhh slower pace. At first I was kind of annoyed because I like to hike fast but after a little bit I enjoyed it. Much more of a relaxing pace, I didn’t sweat at all. It also gave me more time to enjoy the views which were awesome today! Since it was sunny I decided to rock the sunhat and I must admit even though it looks goofy it’s pretty awesome. Along the trail we ran into some Chinese lady who asked Patryk if he could tie her shoelace because “she didn’t know how to”......she was at least 30, how the hell do you hike Kilimanjaro and not know how to tie your shoes?!? My mind is still blown. After about 4 hours we made it to shira camp! I forgot to mention this section of the hike is moorland which is a whole different set of vegetation compared to the jungle that we hiked through yesterday. At camp we took of our gear and had some lunch. It was soup, some sort of meat epenanda, fries, and bread. It was pretty good and really filling! After lunch we took a nap. I completely passed out for like an hour and a half, I don’t think I’ve ever slept so hard in my life. We were supposed to go on a small hike at 4 to help acclimate us,however it started pouring rain so we ended up staying in our tent till 5. After the nap we walked like 5 min to see the shira cave. It’s a pretty tiny cave but has a really interesting story. So before 1998 the tour companies didn’t give the porters tents to sleep in. So because of that they would race to the cave so that they would have shelter from the rain and wind. Otherwise they would have to sleep under a tree or worse. They fit 60+ people in that tiny cave. But in 1998 during a storm one of the other caves on the mountain collapsed and killed a bunch of the porters. So the government made a law that requires tents for everyone. After the cave we walked around the camp a bit and then had dinner around 7:45. Dinner was leek soup, fried chicken, vegetable sauce, rice, and fried bananas. It was really good! I’ve been eating a ton of food here. I probably eat better than I do back home! After dinner our guide briefed us on tomorrow’s hike and chatted a bit. It turns out our guide has met a lot of famous people who’ve hiked Kilimanjaro. He was the assistant guide for a bunch of the Philadelphia eagles after they won the super bowl! Another interesting thing we learned was when he married his wife he paid his father in law a goat! After dinner we got ready for bed. Here’s to hoping I sleep better tonight than yesterday! Tomorrow we wake up again at 6 and start hiking at 8.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Lol I love the note about Patryk helping a woman tie her shoes!

item.title: Day 3 Shira to Barranco Camp
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up at 1:45 again! 😡 this time it was because Patryk had to go to the bathroom. Figuring it’d be difficult to fall back to sleep I used some ear plugs and eye mask I grabbed from the plane. Luckily I was able to fall back asleep and pat had to shake me to wake me up at 6 for the hot tea and “washy washy” as our guide likes to say. There are no showers on the mountain of course so basically they give you a bowl of hot water to attempt to wash yourself. We had egg omelet, porridge, sausage, and fruit for breakfast. Luckily the sun was out this morning and the weather was awesome. Side note: the other mountain in the photo is mount Meru. There were some really nice views of it during the hike. After breakfast we packed up and began our hike. We hiked from shira camp up to lava tower (around 15,000’) for lunch around 12:30. It started to rain while we were there which kinda sucked. Lunch was very simple, just a lunch box with bread, chicken, juice, fruit, and chocolate. After lava tower we made our way down to barranco camp which was only a few hundred feet higher than yesterday’s camp. There were some cool views along the way. We saw some really interesting trees. This one was over 150 years old (25 years for each branch)! For some reason our guide decided to set up camp far away from the main camp, which he referred to as the “refugee camp” 😂. The annoying thing was we were in the opposite direction of where we’re hiking tomorrow. When we got to camp we changed and set up our tent and then had some peanuts, popcorn, and tea for a snack. After the snack we chilled and watched oceans 8, horrible movie would not recommend, and then had dinner around 7. btw that's not the peak, not even close For dinner we had pumpkin soup, spaghetti, green beans, a pancake type thing, and pineapple. Mosses (our guide) told us a lot of really interesting and funny stories during dinner. But one of the craziest things he told us was what people in his town do to thief’s if they catch him. Basically he said they pour gasoline on them and then light them on fire....and the police don’t care! I guess this is a normal thing here? Note to self: don’t steal anything in Tanzania. After dinner we went to bed. Hoping to get some better sleep tonight!

item.title: Day 4 Barranco camp to Barafu camp (base camp)
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was even worse sleep than yesterday! I first woke up around 11:30....pm and then was pretty much in and out of sleep the rest of the night. We finally got up around 6 for tea and then 6:30 for breakfast. For breakfast we had the usual pouridge, fruit, and toast. Patryk is notorious for being late so it wasn’t a surprise that we ended up waiting an extra 25 min for him to get ready to go, our guide was starting to get mad 😂. Our first stop today was karanga camp, to get there we had to climb over this massive wall called barranco wall which required some actual climbing using your hands which was pretty fun. It was crazy to see the porters running up the wall with a bunch of stuff easily. On top of the wall had some pretty sick views After the wall we hiked another 3 hours or so to the camp. Along the way another Chinese person came up to pat to ask him for a snack. Idk why but it seems like all the Chinese people love him haha. We got to karanga camp earlier so we decided to keep going to barafu camp instead of stopping for lunch. On the way to barafu camp it started pouring rainy which really sucked. Even though I had on all my “waterproof” clothes, everything got soaked! As we started to get higher the rain turned to snow/icy pellets which honestly was better than rain. We hiked for what felt like forever until we finally got to the camp. We arrived a little earlier than expected so our tents weren’t ready yet so we waited in the ranger tent attempting to dry ourselves. Once the tents were ready we had some popcorn and tea and then went back to our tent to relax. At 5:30 we had dinner which consisted of cucumber soup, pasta, and pineapples. After we went to bed. “Tomorrow” we’re waking up at 11 to get ready, eat “breakfast” at 11:30, and begin the summit hike at midnight! Reallyyyy hoping my clothes dry.

item.title: Day 5 Uhuru Peak Summit!
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 11 pm (I probably got like 2 hours of sleep) and then got all our stuff ready to hike by 11:30 and ate “breakfast” which was the typical porridge. We left for the hike a little late, around 12:15. It was dark but the sky was clear and the moon was almost full so it lit everything up. It looked awesome, I’m so thankful that we had great weather today! It was really cool to see all the groups of people making their way up the summit lit up by only their headlamps. I tried to get some shots of the hike but it was really difficult because of how dark it was. The hike was super steep and seemed to last forever. We moved slowly one step at a time. I was focused on following Moses the whole time. The higher we got the more difficult it was to breath. Up to this point I hadn’t had any issues with the altitude, but now my head was pounding if I moved too fast or didn’t breath deep enough. It was crazy. We reached Stella point at around 5:30am just as the sun was starting to come above the horizon. From there we hiked to uhuru peak and got there right at 6:20am. Finally reaching here the peak was simultaneously the best and worst feeling ever, the best because we finally made it and the worst because we had a longggg way back down. The hike back down took about 3.5 hours and it was the most miserable I’ve ever felt, I just wanted to stop hiking. After what seemed like forever we finally made it back to base camp around 10. We had 1 hour to rest and then lunch. After waking up from the nap I had the worst headache I’ve ever felt in my life, I can’t even describe how bad it felt. For lunch we had soup but I only had like two bites because I felt like I was gunna puke, my body hated me. The best part is That after lunch we had another 4 hour hike down to Mweka camp. It was pretty miserable but I started feeling a lot better the more we descended. As we got lower we got into the clouds which created a mist which was kinda nice but got everything wet and also made the trail muddy and slippery. We finally made it to our final camp just as the sun started to come out. We checked in and set up our tent, everything was superrr muddy. We had dinner around 6:30 which consisted of soup, rice and veggies, pineapple. After dinner we passed out in our tents. It was the best sleep I had all trip.

item.title: Day 6 final day at Kilimanjaro
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up early (5am) to get on the trail early so we could make it to the safari on time. We had breakfast at 5:30 which was porridge, lentils, and pineapple. We gave Moses the money for tipping and after breakfast gave it to the team. In total we had 11 people helping us: 1 guide (Moses), assistant guide (Jackson), 1 chef, 1 waiter (Francis), and 7 porters. We definitely couldn’t have done the trek without them. After breakfast we made the 3 hour hike back down to the gate where we stopped in a small gift shop and then got picked up by our van. Right before you get to the van little kids run up to you on the road and ask you to give them basically anything. One kid walked up to me and asked me for my hiking poles, I said no, then he asked for my hat, I sad no again, he basically asked me for anything he could see 😂. The drive back to Moshi took less than an hour. It turns out there was some confusion with the safari and now we have a day in Moshi to relax. We cleaned and dried most of our clothes and then hung around the property the rest of the day. For lunch we ended up just eating at the main house. It was chicken and rice with fruit. After lunch we played a board game in this treehouse they have that has an awesome view of the mountain. For dinner we walked to a nearby restaurant called the kitchen which was surprisingly nice. I ended up getting the "American burger" which had egg, cheese, and everything on it. It was delicious. Afterwards we got our stuff packed and ready for the safari tomorrow. It's a far drive to get out for the parks so we have to leave at 5am.

item.title: Day 7 Tarangire Safari
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up super early to head out for the safari. We left the hotel around 5am to drive to the town of Arusha which is about an hour and a half from where we were in Moshi. We got to Arusha around 6:45 and found out from he safari company that we wouldn't be leaving until 8:30! We could've slept at least another hour! Arusha is a much bigger city than Moshi but still small for US standards. Since we had some time to kill we walked a couple blocks to a nearby breakfast place to eat and chill. I had eggs and sausage. Apparently there was a race going on in the city which we could see from the restaurant. Finally around 8 we made our way back to the safari office and loaded up into the car. It was us and two girls from Spain going. The drive to tarangire took a little over two hours so I took a nap in the car. Once we got there the drive got the permits and then we went on a game drive through the park. The vehicle we rode in is pretty cool it had a ceiling that popped open so you could stand up and see all the animals. On the trip we saw elephants, giraffes, zebras, water bucks, impalas, pumbas, wildebeest, pumbas, and ostriches. It was cool to see the animals up close in they're natural environment. We ate lunch in the park which consisted of chicken, a burger, and banana. There were monkeys at the lunch spot who would run up and try and steal your food so you had to be careful! After lunch we went on another game drive. The landscape here is really beautiful but also super dusty! Mostly because it's he dry season. After we drove to the campsite called panorama view, which actually had a pretty good view! 😂 since were only doing a 3 day safari we had to transfer to another safari car. We met our new driver and other people in the new car who were all really nice. For dinner we had the typical rice with meat. After dinner we went to sleep. We're sleeping in these weird igloo looking huts. I'm not complaining though because we were supposed to be sleeping in tents. Tomorrow we start again at 7am.

item.title: Day 8 Ngorongoro Safari
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 6 to get ready. I slept really well tonight (we actually had beds!). I went to the little view point area to catch the sunrise before breakfast, it was pretty cool. For breakfast we had the typical food eggs, sausage, pancakes, toast. I'm pretty sure they only eat one type of meal here it's starting to get a bit monotonous haha. We left camp around 7am to head to the Ngorongoro Park. The drive took a little less than 3 hours to get to the park. The park is essentially an old volcano that blew up a million years ago and now is a crater that is filled with a ton of wildlife. We drove up the rim and then down into the crater where the animals were. The views at this park were stunning and totally different from tarangire. We saw a bunch of new animals in the park, most notably lions, hippos, and hienas. At one point we got within a couple feet of two lions who were crossing by our truck! We stopped and ate lunch in the crater in our car. It was basically the same lunch as the day before (like I said the meals are kinda monotonous). We drive around more after lunch and then made our way back to panaorama camp. At camp we ended up playing board games with the two French people that were in our group until it was time for dinner. Dinner was fried potatoes and fish. After dinner we went to bed. Tomorrow we start a little later and go to a nearby lake for our last day of Safari-ing before heading to Zanzibar!

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: The funny thing about the meals is that they think we eat like that all the time, which is probably why they serve them to us so often. I don't think I've ever eaten so much food in my life! Did you see the rhino in the crater? Even our guide got giddy and excited about that one!

item.title: Day 9 Lake Manyara Safari
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today is our last Safari day! It's getting kinda old so I'm ready to get to Zanzibar and relax on the beach. I'd definitely recommend a two day safari unless you're super into animals. Breakfast was at 8 this morning with the usual eggs, sausage, toast, etc. we ended up leaving for the safari around 9am. The drive to lake Manyara only took 20min. This park is a lot smaller than the last two we visited. It basically consisted of a really big lake and Forrest surrounding it. Unfortunately we really didn't see any new animals this trip and actually saw a lot fewer animals than the other two parks. We ended up mostly driving around the lake. For lunch we stopped by the lake/hot spring (which really just looked like a mash) and had the standard lunch box meal. After lunch we drove around a bit more and then made our way back to the campsite to drop some people off. Afterwards we made the ~2 hour drive to Arusha to meet a driver from our hotel to take us back to Moshi. Our driver was very aggressive and overtaking anyone he could. The car we were in was super old and rickety, definitely one of the less safe drives in my life 😂. Side note: apparently they have never heard of traffic lights in Africa so the traffic around even small cities/towns is horrible! It was a Tuesday night and it took us forever to get out of Arusha. There also appears to be no real traffic laws, at least none that are enforced. The only police presence we really saw were the random checkpoints they have on the roads which were told they're looking for drugs and guns. Another thing is apparently there is no form of EPA here because sitting in traffic you can smell nothing but gasoline and exhaust fumes. By the time we made it back to the hotel my head was pounding. Once back at the hotel we walked over to The Kitchen restaurant for another "American Burger" and a milkshake (delicious) and then went back to bed. Tomorrow we make our way to Zanzibar by plane to enjoy the beach and relax!

item.title: Day 10-13 Zanzibar
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 6:30 to get ready and had a small breakfast in the main house at 7. The brothers of the house were staying at drove us to the airport. We left at 7:30 and got to the airport around 8:30. Patryk was struggling to get his bags to be the correct weight so he had to frantically reorganize everything and give me some of his stuff so that he was allowed to check his bag. We ended up flying on a small ATR which is a propeller plane. The flight to Zanzibar only took a little over an hour. Once we arrived we met our driver outside the airport (which was one of the smallest worst looking airports I've seen haha). The driver took us straight to our resort, the Royal Zanzibar beach resort. The drive took about an hour and 15 min. On the way we passed by tons of tiny, very poor villages that. It was really strange being on our way to a beautiful resort. We got to the resort a little after 1. It was freaking awesome! It had like 5 pools, an awesome beach, and everything was all inclusive! The first two days we just relaxed by the pool and beach. Pat and I played some vball against the staff and they were really impressed with how good we were 😂. I don't think they were used to losing. On the third day we went scuba diving near another island about 45 min from our beach called Menemba. It was known to be the best diving in Zanzibar, we enjoyed but we weren't too impressed, I think it was a little over hyped but it was still a lot of fun and much needed break from laying at the beach. On the last day we woke up early to have a quick breakfast and then make our long journey back home. We left the resort by taxi around 7am to drive us to stone town on the south end of the island to catch the 9:30am ferry. The ferry was a complete cluster f*ck. I'm honestly not surprised they had issues with overcrowding. Once we were on the ferry however it was a smooth ~2hour ride to dar es salaam. At the port we met our second driver who took us tow the airport. The airport in dar es salaam is one of he worst airports for such a large city that I've ever seen. We arrived like 4 hours early so we had a lot of time to kill. We ended up watching the movie sky scrapper which was so over the top and not realistic it was hard to watch. The flight from dar to Dubai was on a 777 and only ~5.5 hours. Which would've been easy.... if the smelliest person in the world didn't sit next to us. I'm not really sure what was wrong with this man but he wore a winter glove on one of his hands and it smelled like death. I'm not sure what exactly was going on with it but I didn't want to know. On the flight I watched American animals (pretty interesting) and dear dictator (not very good). When we arrived in Dubai shortly after 11pm and made our way to the complimentary hotel emirates booked us (it was a big hassle to book). The hotel was a 2 min shuttle from the airport, the shuttle was super packed. This layover was not long enough to go to the city (plus we were exhausted) so we just slept and woke up around 6am to eat breakfast and catch the flight back to Chicago at 9:40am. After a long 14 hour flight (and plenty of movies later) we finally made it back to Chicago! My parents picked me up from the airport. Tomorrow I head back to Savannah to get back to reality for a little while. Can't wait for the next trip. Looking at Costa Rica! But for now, as they say in Tanzania, Hakuna Matata!

item.title: Costa Rica December 2018
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I can't believe it's already time again for another trip! Rachel and I are traveling to Costa Rica with my best friend Patryk and his girlfriend Sarah. We originally planned to take this trip early next year, however Rachel got some extra time off for a furlough so we decided to take advantage of it and travel! This will be the first time Rachel and I travel together so we'll see if she can handle it! We'll be renting a car and driving around exploring the country.

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1kwLsoGINUZOavqaCbF4VAIm-C01dwbBe&w=640&h=480] Trip Map
