item.title: Day 1 Canyoning in La Fortuna
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Rachel and I were a little delayed getting to San Jose arriving around 11:30 pm. Pat and Sarah were already at the airport so we met with them and got the rental car. We had about a 3 hour drive to La Fortuna, where we were staying. The road to La Fortuna was pretty nice it looked like it was recently paved, the only problem was that it twisted and turned through the mountains the whole way. To add to the misery it was also super foggy out due to us basically being in the clouds, needless to say it was very difficult to see. The other obstacle we encountered were rouge speed bumps, they were massive and literally would pop out of no where. They weren't painted or anything so seeing them in the low visibility was nearly impossible. We hit a few of them full speed in our little SUV. The SUV was a small Japanese car I never heard of that barely had enough power to make it up some of the steep roads. Finally we arrived at our Airbnb around 2:30 am. We were exhausted and feel right to sleep. We woke up the next day around 9 and walked to a nearby breakfast place for the "typical" breakfast which consisted of egg, rice and beans, and chicken. After breakfast we drove around the town to check out the area. La Fortuna is fairly small but has lots of outdoor activities. The town is right next to a super large volcano called Arenal that looks really cool! At 12 we made our way a few miles up the road to the tour company to do a canyoning trip. I had no idea what canyoning was but my sister recommended it so we figured we'd give it a shot. We had a quick lunch, more chicken, and then began the tour. It ended up being a ton of fun! It was a lot of different types of rappelling down waterfalls. We ended up getting soaked! On our way to start the trip, it was a super bumpy ride to get there! All geared up! The first descent! Over 160 feet! They ended up swinging us underneath the water fall on the way down which got us absolutely drenched! The tour was a really cool experience and we had a ton of fun, would definitely recommend! We used a company called pure trek. Afterwards we made our way back to the Airbnb and relaxed in the jacuzzi for a little while. We went back into town for dinner at a really tasty restaurant called Pollo Fortuneño (recommended by our tour guides), Rachel and I spilt a big plate of ribs and chicken. After dinner we stopped at the super market to pick up a few things and then went back to the Airbnb to sleep, we were pretty exhausted from the lack of sleep from the previous night.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Mom literally had to watch the gps to tell me when to turn cause it was so foggy when we drove!
I’m impressed you guys made it haha.

item.title: Day 2 Water Fall, Hot Springs, and Cooking
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 8 and went to eat breakfast at a nearby restaurant. I had an omelet and fruit. After breakfast pat and I went to go try and hike an old volcano called Cerro Chato however we were turned back by the guy at the start of the trail because it's technically illegal to hike and supposedly the park rangers were on the mountain stopping people. I was pretty sad we weren't able to hike it 😢. Disheartened we drove back to the hotel and met up with the girls to go do a sloth tour. It was cool to see the sloths but I probably could've just spent 15min there...not the full hour and a half the tour lasted. i wouldn't recommend unless you're really into sloths. Sloth chillin in the tree. After the tour we got our bathing suits and went to the La Fortuna water fall. To get there you hike down about 500 steps. It was an incredible view on the way down. Once we got there we jumped in, the water was freezing! I tried swimming as close to the waterfall as I could but the current was incredibly strong. We dried off and made our way all the way back up to the top and decided to drive over to the hot springs. Instead of paying $70+ to go to a fancy "spa" hot spring we decided to try and find the free hot spring the locals go to. We drove about 20 min away from the city and found a spot with a ton of cars parked on the side of the road so we figured we were close. While parking I nearly flipped the car because of how steep the side of the road was 😳. We walked down the road a ways and quickly found the spot. It was just off the side of the road down a bit of a hill. You had to got through a cut portion of a barbed wire fence to get to the water. It was worth it though! The water was nice and warm and it was really relaxing! We hung out there for a little and then drove back to our hotel. Once at the hotel we got ready to get picked up for our cooking lesson. We drove to a house that was actually really close to where we did the canyoning yesterday. The house was on a little farm that had all kinds of animals and things on it. We got a little tour and saw monkeys, emus, turkeys, ducks, bulls, goats, and some other weird little rodent thing I'm not sure what it was. After the tour we began our lesson. We learned how to make a traditional dish that consisted of tortillas, chicken, rice and beans, and a mix of veggies. I was already a really good chef according to the lady so I had to help out the others 😜. The meal ended up not being half bad! After the meal we returned to our hotel and then went down to the main city to eat ice cream and play a board game. Afterwards we went back to the hotel to sleep. Tomorrow we head out to Monteverde.

item.title: Day 3 Cerro Chato, Hanging Bridges, and Monteverde
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was a busy day! I woke up around 7 and called the green lagoon resort (an entrance to cerro chato) to see if it would be possible to hike today. The guy on the phone told me he didn't speak English and very clearly said it was illegal to hike. I asked him if we could hike the observatory trail and he said sure. So Pat and I decided to drive over there and give it a shot. This time there was no guards in the parking lot so we decided to just go for it. However after a min someone caught up with us and told us we had to pay...whoops. We ended up seeing the same guy at the reception as the day before however this time he told us the rangers were gone and it should be okay to hike cerro chato! I was pumped! We made our way up the observatory hike for about 30 min, there were great views of La Fortuna. Once you get to the end of the hike you have to take a small side trail which leads you to the edge of the green lagoon resorts property. Eventually we arrived at a barbed wire fence with signs that clearly say don't keep going. We obviously kept going. The trail was very obvious but also very rutted out. As we continued hiking up it started raining which caused the trail to get really muddy and slippery. After about an hour we were almost at the top when we heard people up ahead. Fearing that they were rangers and we're going to send us back pat and I ran off the trail to hide. As they approached we could tell they clearly weren't rangers...they were Americans who were also hiking the volcano 😂. After a quick laugh we finished our ascent to the rim and then hiked down into the crater where the lagoon was. The hike down was super sketchy and slippery. If you weren't careful you could easily get hurt. The view of the lake was amazing. We ended up going for a quick swim just to say we did and then hung out and enjoyed the view. Luckily the weather cleared up so the visibility was decent. After about 20 min we made our way back up to the rim and then started our descent back to the parking lot. On the way down we ran into about 20 or so more climbers. Before driving back we rinsed off (we were super muddy from the hike). We met up with the girls at the Airbnb and got all of our things packed up in the car. We drove about 20 min to a place called mistico park, know for its hanging bridges. The park was very well kept and the bridges were also pretty fun. The whole trail was about 2 miles and took us about an hour to complete. After the mini hike we had lunch, the views of Arenal volcano were incredible. After lunch we continued our drive to monteverde. The drive took a little under 3 hours. We had to drive all the way around Lake Arenal and through the mountains with plenty of windy and pothole ridden roads. It was quite the experience! Monteverde is a small town in the middle of the mountains with lots of poorly maintained and very steep roads. I had a couple of close calls maneuvering our car which was a stick shift. Our Airbnb was really nice and about a half mile away from the main strip. After settling in we decided to walk down to town to eat. We ended up eating at a really cool restaurant called the tree house, it literally has a live tree growing in the middle of it! The food was also delicious and there was a live band playing a mix of Spanish and popular American songs. After dinner we took a taxi back to the Airbnb and went to bed.

item.title: Day 4 Monteverde Cloud Forrest, Bungee Jump, and Coffee and Chocolate Tour
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we got up around 7:30 and made our way to the Monteverde cloud Forrest. It was about a 15 min drive from our Airbnb. When we arrived we got some coffee and bakery snacks and made our way down the trails. There's a reason they call it a "cloud Forrest" the whole hike we were basically in a cloud! The whole trail was a little over 4 km and took us about an hour and a half to complete. The scenery was really nice but not a whole lot different from the hanging bridges park from yesterday. This park actually had one hanging bridge also. In the clouds! After the hike we drove back into town and stopped at a small sandwich shop called panderia Jimenez. The plan was to get picked up by the bungee jump company at 11, however after like 10 min no one showed so I called them up. Apparently there was a misunderstanding and we missed our bus so we ended up driving to the park. The place was called Monteverde Extremo and was only like a 20 min drive away so it wasn't a big deal. Once we arrived I started getting a bit nervous about the jump. This bungee jump was off a platform suspended between two ridges of the mountain 470 feet in the air. The actual drop itself was about 200 feet! 😳 Despite our best efforts the girls did not want to jump with us 😂 so they ended up being our photographers instead. There was a concerning lack of preparation before we jumped, we basically just walked up to the platform and we started heading out as they put our harnesses on. I ended up jumping first and Pat went second. It was a really awesome view and I was surprisingly a lot less nervous about the jump then I though I'd be. The worst part was hanging by your feet after the jump waiting to get pulled back up. I'd definitely bungee jump again if I get the opportunity. After we got back on solid ground we went back to the Airbnb to rest. We had about an hour and a half to relax before getting picked up to go on a coffee, sugarcane, and chocolate tour. We got picked up around 2:30 and drove out about 25 minutes to the farm. The tour was pretty interesting, we got to see how coffee and chocolate were made and of course got to try some samples! Coffee bushes Rachel extracting the sugar from the sugarcane. After the tour we got dropped off downtown and went to a taco restaurant. I got a burrito and it was really good. We took a taxi back to the Airbnb after and played a board game then went to bed.

item.title: Day 5 Isla Tortuga Cruise 🚢 🏝
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up early, around 6 AM and hit the road at 6:15 for a 2 hour car ride to punta arenas, the port we were leaving from to go on our cruise to isla tortuga. The drive took about two hours and only about half of it was on rough roads. We arrived at 8 AM. The tour included a typical breakfast Of eggs rice and beans and fried plantains. We boarded the catamaran at 9. There was about 40 people on our tour, which was "low" they can hold up to 100 people. The boat ride over to isla tortuga took about an hour and a half. The views along the way were really nice. The boat was also pretty nice it had a net area in the front you could lay out on and two little mini pools you could sit in. We layed out on the net area the whole way. The island was very remote, it appeared to be uninhabited besides the beach area which was really nice. When we arrived we unloaded our stuff to the picnic area and then got back on the boat to do some snorkeling. The snorkeling was not the best I've done but it was still fun. There really wasn't a whole lot of fish where we went. After an hour we boated back to the beach for lunch. Lunch consisted of a surprisingly good pasta salad and chicken and rice. After lunch we hung out on the beach. I worked on my tan while Rachel applied as much sun screen as humanly possibly to try and avoid burning. It was a perfect day out with no clouds in sight. About an hour or so after lunch they had banana boat rides that we went on. We chose the "fast" ride of course. It went for about 15 minutes and we fell 3 times. Back on the beach they also had hammocks and a slack line which is basically a tight rope you try to balance on. I tried it a few times and failed miserably 😂. Around 3:30 we boarded the boat to head back to the mainland. We went a slightly different way back but it still took about an hour and a half. Once we got back we packed up all our things and headed to Jaco. A small beach town about an hour south of punta arenas. We arrived around 7 PM. The Airbnb was super nice and massive! It was the 6th story on a beach front condo with great views from the balcony. After a quick shower we walked down the main strip of town to go to tacobar jaco for dinner. I had 3 tacos that were all really good. The place was also unique because it had swings for seats instead of bar stools. After dinner we went back to the Airbnb and crashed for the night.

item.title: Day 6 Jaco Beach, Surf Lessons, and Quepos
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: This morning I woke up around 7. I decided to go for a run along the beach to get at least some exercise in on this trip. I ran from our condo to the south end of the beach and back around 3.5 miles. Today the weather was again super nice! After the run we all hung out at the condo until 11, when we had to check out. After packing into the car we walked down the main strip to get some lunch. We stopped at a pizza place called totally baked. It was really delicious and the owner was super nice! After lunch we walked a little more around town, got some ice cream, and then went back and chilled at the pool till around 3. At 3 we drove to the south end of the beach to meet for our surfing lesson! We did a 2 hour sunset lesson where we did some drills on the beach and then went out on the water with an instructor. surfing actually wasn't that difficult! It definitely helped that the instructor told you exactly when to start paddling and when to pop up on the board. My instructor looked exactly like what I picture a surf instructor to look like, he had super long hair and was from Venezuela. He'd been teaching surfing for over 10 years and had just moved to Costa Rica a year ago. We surfed for about two hours and got to see the sunset at the end of the lesson. The water was actually really warm which was nice. After the surf lessons we drove for about an hour to our final stop, Quepos. We arrived at the resort and got settled in our room and then got dinner at one of the restaurants on site. The resort is super nice!

item.title: Days 7-10 Quepos/Manuel Antonio
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: We didn't do a whole lot at the end of our trip since we were mostly relaxing so I'm combining all the days into one post. The first day at the resort we got up and had breakfast. It was included with the room and it was a big buffet that was really delicious so naturally I stuffed myself. After breakfast we hung around the pool relaxing. The resort has 3 main pools: 2 big pools for everyone and a more private adult pool. The resort also had a variety of activities to do. We played mini golf, which ended up being pretty competitive (I won of course 😂) we also played tennis and went on the 1 mile walking trail. The trail has a bunch of animals and plants. We saw a lot of monkeys and a few sloths too. For dinner we ended up driving into the center of Manuel Antonio and went to a place called Samui Thai I had the pad Thai and it was really good. At the end of the meal the waiter ended up giving Sarah his Snapchat handle 😂, I guess he didn't realize her and pat were dating? After dinner we went back and played some board games and crashed in our room. The next day we had another big breakfast and then got picked up from our hotel to go white water rafting on the naranjo river. Rachel was nervous because this was the same river a bunch of tourists died on two months ago but our guide assured us the conditions were much different. We went with a company called H2O and our guide had been rafting for 9 years all over the world and told us he was going to try out for the Olympics in 2024 when rafting is added. Overall the rafting was really fun! We did class II-III which was a little to easy for me I think class IV would've been fun but the river was really low so no parts of it were class IV yet. We got back from rafting around noon. Pat, Sarah, and I decided to go check out the nearby beach while Rachel hung out at the pool. The beach was a golf cart ride and a steep 5 min hike. The views were pretty nice but the beach itself was really rocky so after about 20 minutes we ended up going back and hanging out at the pool. For dinner we ended up driving a little farther to a rest called Ronny's which had a great view of the coast and sunset. I had a burger that was really good! Our final day at the resort we had another big breakfast, checked out, and then hung out by the pool till around 2. At 2 we decided to check out the Manuel Antonio Park which had been highly recommended. Our experience was a little different 😂. The minute we got near the park people were flagging us down to try and get us to park in their lot. We ended up parking about 10 minutes from the entrance (we later found out there was free parking right at the entrance 😠). The place to buy tickets was hidden inside a random bank which didn't take credit cards for some reason. The ATM also didn't work for the majority of our cards. Luckily pat was able to get one of his to work and get enough cash out to buy all the tickets. The park itself was mediocre at best. The real attraction is the beach itself which was nice. We only had about an hour to explore before the park closed so we did the small loop to check out the beaches. After the park we drove to our Airbnb in San Jose near the airport. The drive back took about 3 hours, but the roads were mostly good. The town our Airbnb was located in was absolutely packed! It also had the most cop cars I've seen so far in Costa Rica, there was one every block. Luckily our Airbnb had a secure parking spot. We ended up showering and getting settled then walking about 3 blocks to a Columbian restaurant our host recommended. The restaurant was a weird mix of flavors (I had a cheese, guacamole, and sausage arepa) but I liked it! After dinner we went back and slept. We Woke up around 4 the next day to drop off the car and head to the airport to go back to Savannah! Another great adventure in the books! Can't wait for the next one!

item.title: Greece 2019
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Time for another trip! It's been far too long and I'm in desperate need for a break! I'm headed to explore Greece with my best friend Patryk and his girlfriend Sarah. This trip will be much more relaxed than normal with lots of beach days so sorry, not sorry in advance if the blog posts aren't as interesting. Here's the trip map with all the places we're planning to check out and itinerary. 9/9 🛫 Flight 9AM JFK->SAV arrive 11:20AM (DL3400)

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Can’t wait to see your posts on Greece! We are going there next month!

item.title: Day 1 Athens
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: The trip from Savannah to Athens was long! First I took a shirt 2 hour flight to JFK and arrived around 9:30. My next flight wasn't till 5 PM 😫 while waiting I watched a few really bad movies, walked around the terminal and listened to some podcasts. Leaving Savannah When it was finally time to board I of course had a very large dude sit next to me and basically squish me into the window for the entirety of the 9ish hour flight...not the most comfortable arrangement! I dosed off a little bit mostly couldn't sleep and watched a few more movies. The torment finally stopped when we landed early at 9:30am (2:30am EST). Getting though passport control was pretty quick and painless. I took the metro from the airport to the city, almost getting on the wrong train heading out to the country, oops. The trip from the airport took another ~1.5 hours. I was able to get into the Airbnb with no issues and Pat and Sarah arrived shortly after (they stayed in a different Airbnb the night before). After getting unpacked and a quick rest we made our way out to explore all the sites. First we walked to olympeion, then the Athenain pantehnon, aristotles school lycma. These sites were two ruins and a stadium. Then we rented some electric scooters and scooted up to the base of Mount lybcabettus (the highest point in Athens) and took the short hike to the top which had some awesome views of the city. There was also a restaurant there that we had lunch at. I had chicken and potatoes and a beer that was really good and surprisingly cheap! After lunch we took an Uber to Monastiraki square which seemed to be the epicenter of all the tourist sites and was packed with people. From there we saw Haydrians wall, the ancient agora, and the Roman agora which were all ruins in various stages of restoration. Finally we walked up to see the acropolis, stopping at a nearby hill on the way for a good view. The acropolis is where the famous Parthenon is and is on a plateau that is a short hike above the city which also had some great views. The acropolis was destroyed multiple times and the restoration of the site is still ongoing. After the acropolis we walked back to the Airbnb stopping at the local grocery store for the essentials: wine and gum and then spent some time resting and relaxing. after about an hour and a half we ubered back up to Monastiraki square. It's interesting to note that all the Uber's here are "Uber taxis" and they use meters like a typical taxi, you just can call them from the Uber app. At the square we went to a popular restaurant know. For their gyros called Bairaktaris. The food was delicious and way more than any of us could even come close to finishing. The nice thing about restaurants in Greece is that the portions are large and the prices are cheap! After dinner we walked around the flea market and then grabbed some gelatos and made it back home to get ready to fly out tomorrow morning to santorini!

item.title: Day 2 Santorini
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 5 AM, I slept surprisingly well and did feel much jet lag at all. I had a quick snack for breakfast and finished off the rest of the wine (couldn't let it go to waste!). We finally cleaned and packed up and left around 5:30 for the airport with an Uber. We got to the airport about 30 min later and made it through security super fast and got to our gate. We needed up flying on this super old Boeing 717 that had seen better days. The flight took about 45 min and we flew over the island before turning and landing at the airport at ~8:45AM. We got some great views of the island from above. After landing we grabbed a taxi and took it a little over a mile to an ATV rental place. Even though it was a short trip it still cost 20 euros, definitely more expensive than Athens! To make matters worse the rental company we got dropped off at was super sketchy and told us we could only rent ATVs for 50 euros a day instead of the 35 euros advertised on the website. Because of this we decided to walk to another place our VRBO hosts suggested and rented atvs from them. One note, if you ever come to Greece make sure you have your international drivers permit otherwise they won't rent to you. Once we got our ATVs we Drove to a place called the family bakery to meet our VRBO host and get the keys to our house. The island is super confusing to navigate so we got a little lost on the way but nevertheless made it on time. One funny thing about Santorini is that they don't have addresses for anything, so I guess you kinda just have to know where you're going 😂. After meeting our host he showed us our place which was ~2 min walk away. The house is super cool it's in this little maze of a neighborhood packed with houses and has a really big courtyard and is built like a cave! We chilled at rental house for about and hour and a half and ate some lunch we picked up from the bakery. After resting we decided to take the ATVs to the south end of the island to explore the red beach which was the rocky beach that looked like it was cut out of the side of this big red rock. It looked really cool, but the beach was packed with people and it was more rocky than sandy, not somewhere I'd really hangout for the day. Our next stop was the furthest sourthern point of the island to see the old light house. We hiked around and got some good views of the island and had smoothies for a snack while sitting and enjoying the view. Next we drove to the "black beach" which was another little beach famous for its black sand, which and was more like stones than anything but it was still cool to see! This beach was much less crowded and bigger than the red beach. At this point it was around 3PM so we decided to head back to the house to grab some things and then make are way all the way to the most northern part of the island Oia (confusingly pronounced ee-ah) to relax and wait for the sunset. The drive took about 40min and had some really cool views of the island. We got lost only a few times, I actually ended up just driving with my phone gps in my lap to navigate. We ended up at a place called Lioyerma pool bar. It was a really nice restaurant with an awesome view of the ocean and a pool. We ended up hanging out here swiming, resting, and eating gyros till sunset. I also made friends with a cat at the bar by giving him so if our gyro that fell in the ground. Side note: there are a ton of cats we've seen here. About an hour before sunset the place started to get more crowded. The sunset itself was really nice and we had an awesome view of it. Once the sun dropped we quickly left in hopes of making the long ride back before it got to dark. This plan however did not work out. About halfway back we were cruising home when all of the sudden I heard a loud clunk! Sound and immediately felt my ATV lose power. The road was smooth so I didn't hit anything, just something went very wrong with the transmission. We pulled over and tried in vain to get the ATV into gear with no luck. We frantically called the rental company and explained the situation and they sent a 2 guys with a replacement rental over in less than 30 min! The new replacement ATV was bigger which was nice. We could tell the guy that came was super mad about the ATV breaking down. At this point it was super dark out so we slowly made our way back to our house for the night. Once back we decided to walk around the little town for a little and then played a board game in the courtyard once we got back to the house (pat and Sarah never have a shortage of new games!). I got lucky and somehow won (beginners luck) and then we hung out inside for a little before going to bed. The courtyard

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Great post :)

item.title: Day 3 - Santorini: Acient Thera, 🍷, Skaros Rock, Oia
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we slept in till around 9:30AM, I finally caught up on some sleep! Sleeping in the cave room was pretty cool! It was super dark in there which made it difficult to get up. After getting ready for the day we left around 10:30 to stop at the local bakery for a quick breakfast. I had a pastry with Nutella and another bagel type thing with ham and cheese, both were delicious! After the bakery we made a quick detour to a nearby town to look for a shirt and hat for Patryk who's sunburn wasn't getting any better. Unfortunately we had no luck in the town (we were told to go here by the bakery cashier). So we decided just to continue on with our day. Our first stop was Ancient Thera. It was ~20 min drive up and down some very windy switchback roads. The weather today was perfect again without a cloud in the sky. Ancient Thera is the ruins of a very old town from around 600 BC (if I remember correctly) and it's situated a top a mountain, hence the switchback rounds. Once we made it to the top we parked the ATVs and continued on foot. At the top of the mountain it was SUPER windy. The hike to the city ruins was very short. The ruins themselves were really cool and the views from the top of the mountain were awesome! After exploring the ruins we made our way back down the mountain and made a quick stop at Kamara beach, which was practically at the base of the mountain. This beach was much bigger than the previous ones we'd seen and was unique because it had black sand (which was actually sand and not pebbles). After the quick stop at the beach we made our way back towards where our house was to stop at the Santo winery for a tour and tasting. Santo winery is situated on the side of a mountain and is the biggest winery in Santorini. Their facility was really interesting and the wine was almost as good as the views, which were amazing! Definitely recommend. After the winery we drove the ATVs to Thira, or Fira? Or Thera? We're really not sure the name of the city, but at any rate it's the largest city on Santorini. We finally ended up finding some clothes for Pat and stopped for some more delicious gyros for lunch. After eating we walked around the city some more to enjoy all the views and see where we need to meet (at the port) for our boat tour tomorrow. After Thira we drove another 15 min to skaros rock (on the way to Oia). Once there we climbed down and then up to the top for some more awesome views of the island and all the house built into the side of the mountain. Hiking up the rock had some sketchy parts that required some skill and actually climbing to make it up, but it was definitely worth it! Probably one of my favorite things to see on the island so far. After hiking back from Skaros rock to our ATVs we drove the final ~15 min to oia. Once there we walked around the city and saw the Ancient ruins. The city in general was super crowded which was somewhat annoying. That being said the city is really cool, it's like a vertical maze, I have no idea how they were able to build everything into the side of the mountain like it is. After walking around we went to a bar called Pelekanos to watch the sunset. Again the views were awesome! After the sunset we made our way back to the house by ATV, this time none of the ATVs broke which was good! Once back at the house we rested for a bit and then went down to the main square of our town for dinner. I had the sea bass and some wine. The food and the atmosphere was fantastic. After dinner we walked back and hung out for the house then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 3: Santorini Boat Cruise ⛵️🌅
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 8:30 And got ready to head off on our boat cruise. The boat left from the old port in Fira so we drove our ATVs ~20min and parked in the town. Since we were there fairly early we were able to get really good parking spots. While in the city we picked up our tickets from the tour office and then stopped at a small restaurant with a great view of the coast for breakfast. I had eggs and pancakes that were tasty. After breakfast we made the long walk down to port. It's 587 steps supposedly and the walk wouldn't have been bad besides the fact that the path was filled with tons of donkey poo! Instead of walking you can pay to ride a donkey up or down the steps. It must be very popular. While we were walking down we passed at least a few dozen donkeys heading up. Once we got to the port we found our boat and boarded. Our first stop was the small island in the middle of the crater called Na Kamena. The whole island formed in the last 400 years so the name literally means new island. The boat ride took ~20min and once at the island we got off and did a short hike around some of the craters. There were also some great views looking back at Santorini. I will day our boat tour probably had about 50 people and it felt very touristy so it wasn't my favorite, but the tour was cheap so I couldn't really complain. After the island we got back on the boat and we to the back of the island where there is a "hot" springs. We jumped off the boat and swam over to it but in my opinion it wasn't really hot. It also had a lot of mud that people were rubbing all over there body, I guess it's supposed to be good for you? After hanging out at the hot springs for ~30min we loaded back onto the boat to head to our final stop Thirasa. At the island we walked around the port area and found a nice little spot for lunch. I had some meatballs that were served with fries. It was an interesting combination! After lunch we took the boat back to the port in Fira. On the was we went past Oia and skaros rock and we're able to get some nice views from a different perspective. Once we landed we decided to take the donkeys up since we were not feeling like walking back the whole way. The donkey ride was pretty fun actually and was much faster than walking up ourselves. When we made it to the top our first stop was to get some gelato and then we walked around the city to do some shopping with Sarah, there are a tonnn of small shops throughout the whole city. We also found a great spot to drink a beer and watch the sunset. Honestly I thought the sunset in Fira was better than Oia, it was much less crowded with tourists and had some great views of the city and the water. After sunset we took our ATVs back to the house. We stopped to drop off our stuff and then went down to the little town square for dinner. I ended up eating some lamb and fried feta cheese with wine. While at dinner we ended up making friends with a British couple that was sitting at the table next to us and ended up talking and drinking with them till nearly 2AM. It was a really fun time! Tomorrow, sadly, we leave Santorini to head to Naxos for a few days.

item.title: Day 4 - Naxos
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up around 8:30 and got all my stuff packed up and ready to go. Pat and Sarah slept a little longer and we ended up leaving the house at around 10:30 and made one final stop at the nearby family bakery for breakfast. I had a really good ham and cheese bagel and pastry filled with chocolate. After the quick breakfast we drove our ATVs to Athinios port which was close by but very busy. There was a huge line of buses trying to get down so it ended up taking like 20 min. We ended up leaving the ATVs parked at the bottom of the road to be picked up and then waited for our ferry. The port area was a complete cluster, nothing was organized at all. Luckily we were able to find someone who knew what was going on and made it on the correct ferry. The ferry itself was actually really nice with big seats and lots of legroom, and it was really fast! We left a little after 12:15 and arrived around 1:30 at the Naxos port. Once we arrived we walked across the street to meet our host who took us on a quick car ride to our Airbnb. The Airbnb we got was the best so far! It's in an awesome location close to the city and beach and is really big with an awesome rooftop! After unpacking and settling in we made a 5 min walk to the nearby Saint George beach. The beach was the best we've seen in Greece so far! It actually had sand instead of pebbles/rock and also crystal clear water. Also the weather this whole trip has been perfect which made it perfect for relaxing on the beach. After a couple hours of relaxing I decided to go for a 3 mile run on the beach then take a dip in the water. The water is a little cold but felt really good after the run. After the beach we went to grocery store to pick up some breakfast food and of course some more wine! Then we made our way back to Airbnb to shower and then went to a nearby restaurant that our host recommended. I had the "special" chicken which was chicken and tomatoes, taziki sauce, and fries. It seems like just about everything in Greece comes with fries, but hey I'm not complaining! After dinner we got lost on our way back to our Airbnb but luckily found it again and we're able to get to the roof just before sunset to enjoy the amazing views of the city and water. After chatting for a bit we decided to walk back into town and get some gelato! We went to a restaurant called Waffle House and I got the waffle cream flavor, it was delish. After eating we went back (without getting lost this time) and hung out at the Airbnb watching some Netflix. Tomorrow the plan is to rent a scooter and ATV to go hike Mount Za then hit the beach again!

item.title: Day 5 - Mount Zas 🍕
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 8 I made some breakfast eggs and bread. Then we packed up and went down to the square to rent a scooter and ATV. The rental place was pretty slow so we didn't end up getting on the road till a little after 9. The trip to mount Zas was very picturesque and took about 30 min. Zas is the name for Zeus and the reason the mountain is named after him is because there is a cave in the mountain where Zeus was born. Once we got to the start of the hike we parked our vehicles and started. The trail itself was super beautiful. The beginning of the hike was paved but then quickly turned to shale and we had to scramble our way up. About 15 minutes into the hike we found the cave of Zeus. It was surprisingly large. Another cool thing about the mountain is there were goats climbing all over. They all had bells attached to them so we could hear them jingling. After the cave we pressed onward. The trail quickly got steeper and the rocks were looser making it more difficult to climb. It was almost like climbing up a dune but instead of sand it was rocks. Eventually we had to actually climb. I went ahead of pat and Sarah since they were taking their time. Soon I was high enough to realize that we went the wrong way and the trail was supposed to go around and then up the mountain ridge. I called pat and Sarah to let them know and decided I would try to keep pressing forward since I already went so far. This was probably not the best idea. The more I climbed the steeper it got and I'm not going to lie there were a few points I got really nervous, but at this now trying to climb down would've been even worse. So I just kept on going making sure all my foot and hand holds were solid and didn't look down! I was also worried I wouldn't be able to actually find a way up from here but luckily I was eventually able to make it to the top! I ended up waiting at the top for about 45 min for pat and Sarah, who took the longer way. The views at the top were awesome! The weather was clear so we could see everything. After enjoying the views for a bit we made our back down, this time using the actual trail! We made it back to our vehicles around 1 and decided to head to the nearby town of Filoti to have lunch. We stopped at a local restaurant and I had grilled pork and pita, it was really good. After lunch we decided to make to quick stops at two historic sites: Bazeos tower and dinitras temple. The tower was more like a little house so we ended up just looking at it from the outside. The temple was very typical Greek ruins but looked cool in the middle of the country side. Once we got back to the Airbnb we changed and drove to agios propios beach which was about 15 min away. This beach was even nicer than the beach from yesterday. We hung out for about 3 hours. I went for a walk down the coast to check out the area. After the beach we went back to the rooftop of our Airbnb to enjoy another sunset with some wine, Greek yoghurt and conversation. After the sunset we went down to the square to try another restaurant for dinner. I had the house special which was a really good chicken and cheese baked thing, it was tasty. After dinner we walked around a bit before heading back to the Airbnb to hangout then go to bed.

item.title: Day 6 - Naxos Exploring and Cliff Jumping
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up around 7, I decided to go for a run to clear my head, I ended up doing 6.5 miles up and down coast, mostly on the beach but I also ran around the Apollo portara which is a famous arch ruin in the town. It was a really nice run and good to get some exercise and a great way to see the city. part of the run was through a dry lakebed so it looks like I was running in water on the map. After my run I got back and cooled down on the roof of the Airbnb then showered and made some Greek yoghurt mixed with oats and honey for breakfast. Pat and Sarah woke up shortly after around 10ish and once everyone was ready we decided to go take the scooter and ATV and explore the island. Our first stop we drove to engares to see an olive oil museum. There was a free tour that was surprisingly really good and we got to try some free samples at the end. They had this olive marmalade that was delicious but unfortunately the containers were too big to take back :(. After that we drove to some small ruins called kouros that are famous. It's basically a statue of a guy made in marble laying down. To get to the ruins we had to drive through little towns and the mountains which was really fun. Also next to the ruins we decided to take a path which we thought would lead us to an old quarry but it turned out to not go anywhere. Oh well, the scenery on the path was nice at least! After Kouros we drove to try and find a church called panagia (I think that's what it's called) but instead we ended up in a random town in the mountains so we had lunch at a local restaurant called the ARTernative bar. It was a really cool atmosphere and the food was great I ate calzone that was more like open pizza with all the toppings under the cheese. After lunch we drove to the southwest area of the island to a beach Called Prygaki. We found through googling that there was cliff jumping here. After a short hike on a jetty like coast we found the spot! Pat was too nervous to jump at first so he had me be the guinea pig. There were basically 3 heights to jump from so I started on the smallest and worked up to the largest. It was a ton of fun! And after I priced it was safe pat and Sarah both jumped too. After the cliff jumping we continued to drive up the west coast of the island and made a stop at an abandoned building we found that ended up being filled with graffiti art. It was really cool! there were some really talented ones and some that were clearly amateur haha! Next we made a very quick stop at okros beach because we a ton of people kite surfing. We asked about renting/taking lessons but they said you need at least 6 days to learn so that was out. Finally we Made it to Plaka beach at this point is was ~5:30. We ended up relaxing here for about and hour or so. I ended up getting a nice nap in. After the beach we made our way back to the Airbnb to watch the sunset again on the roof. Tonight was a bit cloudy so the sunset wasn't as nice but we still enjoying hanging out in the roof. A bit later we went down to the square for some gyros that were delicious (they included fries of course) and super cheap I got 2 for like $6. After dinner pat and Sarah got some gelato and then we went back to the Airbnb and watched some Friends before bed.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Awesome! You did so much!

item.title: Day 7 - Naxos Final Day
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up around 7 and had some more Greek yoghurt for breakfast. I watched some Netflix till ~10 when pat and Sarah finally woke up. Today we didn't really have anything planned. One thing we were debating was doing a day trip to Mykonos, however it's about a 2 hour boat ride each way and it really didn't seem like there was anything too unique on the island so we decided it wasn't worth the trip. So instead we decided to explore Naxos some more. We ended up driving up the northwest coast all the way up to a town called Appollonos (about an hour away) to see another kouros ruins. The ride was very picturesque as usual here and on the way we found a cool looking tower that we stopped at and explored. We continued our drive to kouros and stopped for some pictures, it was another large guy carved out of marble. After seeing the Kouros we were going to stop at a mountain town just south called Kronos. However we weren't really hungry yet so we just drove though the town and then kept going all the way down to Prigaki again on the south end of the island. On the way we found a cool church called Pagiani Drossani. One thing about this island is there are tons of little churches everywhere and in the most remote places. We relaxed at the beach for a while and then decided to go do some more cliff jumping. This time we had Pats GoPro so we shot some fun videos and took more pictures of us jumping. We also met a German couple who was at the cliffs. The guy dove headfirst off the highest spot which was a little crazy since the water wasn't that deep! Once we got tired of cliff jumping we drove up to plaka beach again to relax some more before the sunset. We napped on the beach for about 3 hours and then drove back drop off scooter and ATV at the rental place. Then we went up to our roof to enjoy one last Naxian sunset. Tonight was clear and the weather was perfect. After the sunset we ate at gyro gyro again and then got some gelatos for desert. Finally we got back to the hotel and hung out and watched some Netflix before sleeping. Tomorrow we head back to Athens :(

item.title: Day 8 - Back to Athens
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today I woke up around 5:30 for some reason. I fell asleep pretty early so I guess that's why. I spent the morning getting everything packed back up and then cooking and eating some eggs for breakfast and then watching some Netflix till 9:30 when our Airbnb host came to take us to the airport. The airport is super close and really small one of the smallest I've seen. We took an ATR (propeller plane) for a 40 minute flight back to Athens. Once we arrived we got our luggage and took the metro to downtown to find our Airbnb. We got there right on time for our 2PM checkin. Our Airbnb was a super big apartment and had an awesome view of the acropolis. After resting for a bit we made our way to the main square (monstraki) and had some gelato along the way. After walking through the street markets for a bit we went to a rooftop for a beer before our cooking class at 4:30. Our finally activity for the trip was a tradiontional Greek cooking class that was highly recommended by my sister. We walked to the restaurant it was in which was about 10min away. Our teachers name was Rena and there were about 10 of us total in the class, besides us there was a family from Atlanta and two couples from England. The restaurant was very fancy and had a really nice view of the acropolis. We learned how to make a bunch of different dishes. The main dish was lamb and potatoes and we also made some taziki, a spinach pie, fried zucchini balls, Greek salad, and a Greek yoghurt desert. They all have very Greek names for the dishes that I'm not even going to try and spell. The class was really fun and afterwards we got to eat everything and it all tasted delicious! After the class we walked back and watched a Netflix movie called contagion (which was recommended by one of the people in our class who worked for the CDC). After that I passed out. Tomorrow I start the long trip back home to reality with an overnight stop in New York and then back to Savannah. Overall the trip was a blast and I'm extremely grateful I was able to do it with my friends. Update on the trip home since I don't want to write another whole post. Woke up around 7 and left the Airbnb around 8:30 to go to the main square with pat and Sarah for brunch. I had some pancakes with chocolate syrup. After we ate went went to a nearby coffee and gelato shop for one last scoop! Pat and Sarah's flight was two hours earlier so they left before me. I ended up walking around the market and agoras for a bit and then hung out in the main square before grabbing a gyro to go and hopping on the 11am metro to the airport. Getting through security was pretty painless. The flight ended up taking about 10 hours I watched a couple movies one called the upside was really good. I stayed up the whole flight to try and get back on EST time. Once I landed I got an Uber to the Airbnb I'm staying at since my flight doesn't leave till tomorrow. The Airbnb was interesting to say the least. I guess I didn't really read the fine print that it was actually a shared room lol. The bed I had a curtain around it which was nice but I was not expecting a hostel type setup. Luckily it was only for one night but some Asian lady was in the same room and woke me up turning the light on and talking on the phone. Super annoying! I left the Airbnb around 6:30 in the morning and got to the airport and my gate with no issues. The flight to Savannah left on time and I got in at 11am...back to reality. Stay tuned for more adventures in about a month when I go to Jordan, Israel, and Egypt with my sister and her friend Sam!

item.title: Jordan, Israel, & Egypt 2019
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I can't believe I'm about to head out again for another adventure. Just last month I was getting back from an amazing trip in Greece. This time I'm headed to explore Jordan, Israel, & Egypt with my sister Jamie and her friend Sam. The last time Jamie and I traveled was 2 years ago to China and that trip was a blast. This trip will be more of a mix between running around to see sites and relaxing, I guess I'm slowing down with age! In any case I'm incredibly grateful that I'm able to do these awesome trips.
