item.title: Day 1 - Amman & Wadi Rum
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was an extremely long travel day. I packed up everything last night and went directly from work to airport around 6pm. The first leg of the trip was Savannah to Atlanta which was fast and painless. I listened to a Jocko podcast which if you haven't heard of him, and you want to get motivated, do yourself a favor and look him up. I only had a 2 hour layover till my Atlanta to Paris flight so I really just only had time to get to the terminal and eat a snack before boarding. The flight to Paris was ~8 hours. I fell asleep a few times watching a couple good movies (the last breath and supreme) and listened to a few more podcasts. Once in Paris I had a 5 hour layover until my final flight to Amman. I did some reading and watched another movie (hotel Mumbai) to kill the time. The flight to Amman was on an older aircraft that didn't have any TVs in the seat-backs but I had my tablet so I watched two movies: in the loop and when Harry met sally. This flight was only about 4.5 hours and there was no one in the middle seat which was nice and let me stretch out a bit. The dinner on the flight was some vegetarian meal which wasn't that great, but since the flight was from France at least the wine was good! I finally landed in Amman around 11:45pm it's been ~24 hours since I started traveling so the exhaustion was starting to set in. Going through the passport control was a pain. Apparently even though I already bought a visa I still had to go through the "purchase visa" line. I conveniently found this out after waiting in the passport line so I had to go all the way back, and at this point the line for visas was long 🤬. While getting through all the lines I ran into Sam. After we finally made it out of the airport we took the shuttle to the hotel (which was like 2 min away) and checked in to meet Jamie. We had booked a two person room because on the website there wasn't an option for 3 but when we got there the reception was able to change us to a bigger 3 bed room. At this point it was about 1am so we pretty much passed out right away. The next morning we got up at 6am for breakfast which was a buffet style so we loaded up on everything. After we took the shuttle back to the airport to pick up the rental car and head on our way to Wadi Rum. We got on the road around 7am and the trip down was about 3.5 hours. The driving here is about what you'd expect, a cluster*. Apparently there are no lanes and whatever lines are on the road are purely there for decoration and at best are a suggestion of where you should drive. However, the funny thing is that there are everywhere and apparently they are very strict on the speed limit...I found this out the hard way 😂. Less than an hour into the drive we see a cop ahead of us run out into the middle of the highway and start waving at us to stop and pull over to him. It seemed really sketchy at first. After a quick interaction he told us that we were going 121kmph in a 110kmph zone, which is like 6mph over the speed limit. We thought that we were going to have to bribe him or something but Luckily I guess I was charming/convincing enough (aka I had a US passport) that he decided to give us a warning and let us go on our way. As if that was enough to teach me a lesson about an hour later we get pulled over AGAIN! The same things happened, once he found out we were tourists from the US he was super nice and let us go on our way. Fortunately we didn't get pulled over by any police after that and made it to Wadi Rum around 10:20 to meet our tour guide. He drove us through the desert in his Jeep to the camp and we planned out the rest of our day over some tea. After resting for a few hours we had some lunch at camp which was pita with tuna and some veggie mixes. At 1pm we began our Jeep tour of Wadi Rum. Our first stop was this giant sand dune. Our guide brought a sandboard with so that we could hike up and board down. It was a blast. I only went down twice though because hiking up the dune was a lot of work! Our second stop was this old carving in the rock that Lawrence of Arabia carved as directions to get through the desert. It was up on a rock so we had to do some climbing to get to it. Our next stop was the Lawrence house. This was a cave in the side of the mountain where Lawrence of Arabia supposedly lived. Our guide told us that wasn't really true, they were actually Nubian caves and they did some of the filming for the Lawrence of Arabia movie there. Side note: a lot of famous movies have been filmed in Wadi Rum including Star Wars, Prometheus, and the Martian. We ended up climbing on top of the caves for some stunning views and of course some good photos. After the Lawrence house we made our way to Um Frouth rock bridge which was a cool rock formation in one of the mountains that looks like a bridge. Next we went to Mushroom rock. This ones pretty self-explanatory, it's a rock that looks like a mushroom....really not that cool honestly haha. Our final stop on the Jeep tour was a drive through a canyon and to see some faces carved in rock. The faces were supposed to be Lawrence of Arabia and the first kind of Jordan. They weren't super realistic looking but the area was cool. Finally we made our way back to camp around 5. We washed up quickly and then got to our camels for a short sunset tour. For the camel ride the 3 of us rode out about 30 min from our camp, stopped to watch the sunset, and then rode back. Our camels were the best at walking, I was in front but Jamie's camel kept trying to get in front of me messing up the line. Overall I thought the camels were fun but you definitely don't need to ride them that long to get the experience. Once the sunset Jamie wanted to take some "artsy photos, one of which was a handstand with the sunset. I'll let you decide who did it better.... Once we got back to camp we had a traditional Bedouin dinner where they cook the food under ground. The meal consisted of rice, chicken, and veggies. After dinner we hung out in the main camp tent then showered and got ready for bed. It's super quiet in the desert and also great for star gazing since there's hardly any light pollution. Tomorrow we have another early day hiking around Wadi Rum.

item.title: Day 2 - Wandering Wadi Rum and Petra
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Last night was pretty rough. We went to bed around 10 and I fell asleep pretty fast but then woke up to the sound of a car revving it's engine for a solid 15 min. I checked the time...10:50 I couldn't believe it. Of course after that I couldn't fall back to sleep. It was really hot in the room so we opened up the windows....that let the mosquitos in. Literally all night they were biting me and I couldn't hide under the covers because the room was so hot! I ended up listening to a podcast. I think I fell asleep for maybe like 2 hours :/. We finally got out of our sauna...I mean tent... at 6am for a sunrise hike. We hiked away from our camp for about 30 min to this large dune and hiked up to the top for a cool view. Hiking out here is like hiking on another planet it just looks so surreal. Hiking in the morning also has the benefit of it being way cooler than the afternoon making the hiking much more enjoyable. After getting off the dune we continued hiking through a canyon (they call it a siq here) our guide told us about his family and a few stories but his English was not very good so it was very difficult to understand him think. From what we could gather was he has like 4 brothers and 3 sisters and is training to be a hot air balloon guide? I'm not really sure on the last one though 😂. Our guide also showed us how to make soap from some of the desert bushes, it was a little distracting though because there were a TON of flies. We finally hiked back to our camp around 9am and ate breakfast. Today we had eggs, pita, a meat vegetable mix, and hummus. After breakfast we cleaned and packed and left the camp around 10:30. We decided to do Petra today instead of tomorrow since we finished seeing/doing all the things we wanted in Wadi Rum. The drive took about 1.5 hours. We stopped at a grocery store right before to pick up some snacks for the day. We ended up getting in to Petra around 12. Oh and I bought a head scarf thing to try and fit in. Once inside we walked down the main trail which leads you to the famous treasury building. Along the way there are other various buildings carved in the rock and you walk through a big siq (canyon) to get there. The whole thing doesn't seem real and when you finally get to the treasury it's breathtaking. I ended up taking off my hat for a little and trying to put it back together, it was quite the ordeal but I think jamie got it right. After enjoying the view we decided to walk around the area. Petra is pretty huge and the treasury building is just a small portion of it. We ended up seeing the coliseum and then took the trail to see Petra from above. The trail was a lot of stairs and took probably about an hour but the view was worth it. One of the guys at the spot must've takin like 1000 pictures (including flexing poses) so you know the view was good! 😂 After the trail we hiked back down to the entrance. On the way out there were tons of people trying to sell horse rides back, some even went as far as saying the ride was included with your ticket...yea right. Once we got out we stopped at the cave bar which is right next to the entrance for a beer. The cave bar is supposedly the oldest bar in the world, idk if that's true or not but the beer was tasty. After the beer we went to meet our Airbnb host. We met him at little Petra which was about 15 min away. When we met him he told us to go check out the little Petra ruins quick before taking us to the cave. Little Petra was very similar to Petra, just smaller (get it?) There was not nearly as much hiking and way less people which was kinda cool. It also advertised the "best view in the world" the hike up to it was short but really cool, Sam choose difficult path at first until we realized there was a way easier way to go. After checking out the ruins we made our way back and then followed our host to our cave Airbnb. Not gonna lie it was a little sketchy...okay a lot sketchy. It looked like the guy literally picked a random cave and decided to make it his. It was a big cave room with no bathroom and a light powered by car battery 😂 his advertisement of an "authentic" experience was no lie! words truly can't describe this place. After dropping our stuff off in the cave we had dinner on the roof. To their credit it was a really delicious stew of rice with goat meatballs and potatoes and vegetables. We ended up hanging out on the roof for a bit as the sun went down it was really nice honestly, the weather was perfect...for now.... We were super exhausted so we went to the cave to try and get some rest. That's when the weather started picking up. It was SUPER windy outside and sand was blowing into our cave at some points because the top half of the door area was open. We were originally supposed to stay here two nights but because of all the running around we decided to treat ourselves and booked a room and the Hilton spa at the Dead Sea for tomorrow instead. Looking forward to a night of air conditioning and no bugs!

item.title: Day 3 - Petra and the Dead Sea
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: We somehow managed to survive the night in the cave. The sandstorm seemed to last pretty much all night. The makeshift front wall/door of our cave was falling down 😂. Luckily nothing flew in and hit anyone. The whole room was COVERED with sand though. My headscarf thing really came in handy to keep my face protected while I attempted to sleep. I think I did end up getting a few hours of sleep in somehow. Everything was layered in sand! We packed up our stuff into the car and made our way out of the cave fast! We went back to Petra for another day of hiking. This time the plan was to go all the way to the monastery, which is a bit more of a hike with lots of stairs (800 to be exact). To get to the start of the hike we walked back through the siq past the treasury building to the main city center of Petra. There were a ton of buildings here the biggest was the ruins of this old church. From there we took the Al Dir trail to get to the monastery. I forgot to mention we got to Petra around 7/7:30 so there was a lot less people and it wasn't as hot so hiking was enjoyable. After about an hour of hiking we made it to the monastery. The monastery is very similar to the treasury except it's larger and a little less intricate. It's also not nearly as busy since the hike is farther and more difficult. As a reward for making the long hike up we treated ourselves to some ice cream. We hiked around the area of the monastery to get some other view points. We found another spot that advertised "the best view in the world"...it's funny how many of them there are here 😂. Afterwards we made our way back down to the city of Petra. This time once we got to the city we took a different trail that goes south of the city that goes to the temple of high sacrifice. Along the way there were more buildings cut out of the rock. There was a cool temple I think called the garden temple that was in a siq on the way to the high temple. Also on the way was an old "waterfall" that was dried up so it wasn't really much to see. After another 30min or so of hiking we made it to the temple of high sacrifice. It was surprisingly crowded. The temple itself was basically a square cut into the ground really not much to see but the views from the top of the siq looking down on the city were nice! After the high temple we took another route down to the main route to leave Petra. We passed by the treasury building one last time on our way out, it really is cool and I definitely recommend going to see it if you get the chance. We left Petra around 12:30. I realized I left some clothes in the cave so we made a quick stop back to get them and then continued on our way to the Dead Sea. The drive to our hotel was about 2.5hours and had some cool views going over the mountains and down into the valley where the sea is. One interesting thing we learned is that the Dead Sea is actually technically a lake (since it's no longer connected to the ocean) and also it's the lowest land point on earth at -431 meters below sea level. The hotel we stayed at was the Hilton Dead Sea luxury resort and it was bad ass! Jamie has a bunch of points through her work travel so she was able to book it for us and since she's a gold status we were able to get an awesome room, free drinks at the executive lounge, and free breakfast! After we checked in we made our way down to the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea is "dead" because it has a super high salt content and nothing can survive it. The other thing the high salt content does is make it super easy to float. Once we got in we floated around for about 15min. It was insane how easy it was to float. You could literally "stand up" without touching the ground, it was impossible to sink! After floating you're supposed to rub this mud on you and let it dry for 15min, I guess it's good for your skin or something? We looked like idiots doing it but it was kinda fun, and I guess my skin felt softer afterwards 😂. After floating in the sea we went up to the pool and got some drinks at the swim up bar. I tried a drink called the Dead Sea breeze, it was good, not great. Then after the pool we went to the executive lounge for some free drinks and food. We stayed in the lounge for about 2 hours and then we checked out the rooftop bar but it was pretty dead so we went back to the room shortly after to get some sleep.

item.title: Day 4 - The Dead Sea and Amman
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Best sleep of the trip so far! Woke up around 9am and went downstairs to get some breakfast. It was a full buffet style so we loaded up on everything. After breakfast we went back down to the Dead Sea to get another float and mud session in. Afterwards we hung out at the pool for the day. It was really nice to have a day to rest and recharge! We ended up checking out of the hotel at 2. Next we drove to mount Nebo which was about 30 min away and kind of on the way to Amman. Mount Nebo is where God showed Moses the promised land and also where Moses was buried (although the exact location is unknown). There was a really cool view of the surrounding area as well as a nice church with lots of restored mosaics. Next we drove to Amman which took about an hour. The closer we got to the city the worse the traffic got and the crazier the drivers were. We dropped off the car at the rental place, it turned out we had it booked for an extra day we didn't realize but we returned it anyway because we really didn't want to drive around the city. To get to our hotel we tried to get an Uber but the driver cancelled 5 times so we ended up hailing down a random taxi. The ride to be hotel was about 30min because the traffic was so terrible. Also the taxi driver was a smoker and was smoking in the car which wasn't enjoyable. I think he realized we didn't like the smoke because he pulled out a perfume bottle and sprayed us all with it 😂 he didn't even ask he just did it which was really weird. Once we got to the hotel we dropped off our stuff and then walked to rainbow street to get some falafels at a place called Al-Quds. The place was recommended to us by one of Jamie's friends. The restaurant was super small and they only offered one thing: falafel sandwich and either spicy or no spice. The falafel was delicious so I ended up ordering 2 more since I was pretty starving. After the falafel we went to the ice cream store right next door for some delicious gelato. Side note: walking around Amman is not the nicest, lots of people seemed to be eying us so my guard was up also the city is very dirty, luckily we're only here one more day. After eating the gelato we walked back to our hotel. We ended up hanging out in the room and watching the movie driven for the rest of the night.

item.title: Day 5 - Jerash and Amman
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 8 and got some breakfast downstairs at the hotel. The breakfast was the typical pita with cheese and a hard boiled egg, kinda strange but it was super cheap so can't complain! After breakfast we grabbed our bags and met our driver (the hotel set us up with) to go see the city of Jerash. Jerash is about an hour north of Amman but our driver was fast so we made it there in 40min. Jerash is known as the "Pompeii of the Middle East" and the "city of 1,000 columns". It's basically a big city that has been around forever and has been inhabited by a bunch of different people, destroyed a few times from attacks and twice from earthquakes. I think the most recent inhabitants were the Romans and you can see their architecture style in all the buildings ruins. There are a bunch of different temples in the city, the main ones being the temples of Zeus and Artemis and there is a main road called the corda that's lined with hundreds of columns that connects everything together. There were also two big amphitheaters and a hippodrome (horse racing track). After exploring the city for 2 hours we met back up with our driver who took us back to Amman and stopped at a famous mosque. Apparently when we got there it was prayer time so we weren't allowed to go in but we did get a picture of the outside (which was enough for me anyway to be honest). The mosque had a gift shop attached you had to walk through and the people there were trying really hard to sell you one of their overpriced trinkets. After the mosque our driver took us to the Amman citadel which are famous ruins that sit on top of one of the many hill tops in the city. The ruins were cool a bit more of the same kind we've been seeing so nothing too unique, but the views of the city were really cool. The city is so densely packed into the hills, the organized chaos is really cool. From there we walked down the hill about 10 min to the Roman theater. Before entering we grabbed food at a nearby restaurant that had some kind of gyros. We all ordered 3 different things but they ended up all looking the same😂. We ate our lunch inside the Roman theater, it must be a popular place because there were a bunch of people (tourists and locals) hanging out. After exploring the theater and the attached museums we made our way back to our hotel. We hung out at the hotel and played some cards/rested until dinner time. We went out around 7 for dinner and walked 15min to a place we found on google called wild Jordan. The restaurant had a really nice terrace with a view of the citadel. We all had some delicious smoothies and I had a cheese stuffed chicken. The food was pretty good. After dinner we walked back to the hotel and called it a night. Tomorrow we head to Israel by car. Jordan was a super cool country and I definitely recommend it!

item.title: Day 6 - Jerusalem Old City
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up just before 7 to gather our stuff and meet our driver outside to take us to the Allenby bridge border crossing. The drive took about an hour. Once there we had to go and pay the exit tax and go through passport control then get on a bus that drives you though "no-mans land" into Israel. When we arrived in Israel we had to go through passport control and security again. There was a food shop in the building so we used the rest of our Jordanian money on falafel sandwiches and snacks. The interrogation at passport control was no joke, they talked to me for a good 5 min asking me all sorts of questions about the trip, my life, job, family, etc. once we made it through we were picked up on the other side by our Israeli driver. It was probably another hour drive from the border, which is technically Palestine (I'm still not sure how that whole situation works), to Jafa gate of the old city of Jerusalem. There was a big Jewish festival going on today so we had to get dropped off a little farther from the gate. It was only a 10 min walk to the hostel from where we were dropped off. After dropping off our stuff we checked out the small rooftop of the hostel which had a really nice view of the old city. We left the hostel shortly after to go see the tower of David which is literally across the street from our hostel. The tower had a free English tour so we decided to join it. I'm usually not much for tours, but the tour guide was awesome! He explained the crazy history of the city and why it's so important to Christians, Jews, and Muslims. He explained all the different civilizations that occupied Jerusalem. One funny thing is that the tower of David wasn't actually the tower of David, it was built by someone else but people consistently mistook it for the tower of David. We got to go on top of one of the towers in the citadel which had an awesome view of the whole city. The guide pointed out all the important buildings. We also got to see the old prison where archeologists discovered tons of different history buried beneath the structure. After the tour we walked to western wall. It was super crowded with tons of people. We wrote down some prayers on pieces of paper and as tradition we went to the wall and put the paper in between the cracks in the stones. Next we made our way to a restaurant called Basti for lunch, I had shawarma that was delicious. Shawarma is basically a gyro except it's chicken instead of lamb. Walking the streets here is like walking through a maze. Everything is enclosed and there are shops literally everywhere. It's really cool to see. Also the military presence here is very noticeable. We've seen dozens of guards armed with automatic rifle patrolling the streets. We even noticed the guards arresting someone right outside the restaurant we were eating at. Once we finished lunch we decided to walk the Via Dolorosa aka the stations of the cross. The path is relatively short and marks out where Jesus fell and all the other stations. It finally ends at the church of sepulchre which was built on top of where Jesus was crucified and buried. It was really cool to see the path and the spots Jesus went. Inside the church we had to wait in a crazy long line to see the burial tomb. The church is considered to be the holiest site in Christianity. There was a priest in front of the tomb that was essentially a bouncer and had to kick people out of the tomb on a few occasions because they didn't follow the rules or were taking too long. After seeing the church we walked back to the hostel to rest for a bit. We watched a simpsons episode on Jerusalem that our guide had recommended as funny and also informative. For dinner we walked about a mile to the 'newer' side of Jerusalem to an area called the shuk. The streets on the way there were crazy crowded for the Jewish holiday. We went to a place called the beer bazar and had some good beers. While we were there we met some locals who gave us some food recommendations. After beer we walked further down the shuk for dinner. I ended up getting a chicken sandwich. After dinner we made our way back to the hostel. On the way I stopped for a gelato :)

item.title: Day 7 - Jerusalem Underground
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Woke up around 8 this morning. It's a little annoying in the morning because they have the church bells going off for what feels like forever and I think it's every hour starting at like 5am! For breakfast we ended up stopping at a shop just outside our hostel for some pastries and water. I had a chocolate filled crossiant and a cheese filled bread thing, both were delicious. While we were eating a random Jewish guy came up to Sam and started talking to him about the cubs (he was wearing a cubs hat) he thought Sam was Jewish and was trying to see if we wanted a tour of one of the synagogues. After eating we walked a different route to the western wall. Along the way I stopped at a shop to get a frozen coffee slushy, it was really good. Our plan was to do the tunnel tour of the walls, however all the tours were sold out because of the holiday. So instead we went out of the city gate and walked 10min down to the city of David. David was one of the kings of Israel, he's also the David from the story of David and Goliath. The city ended up being super cool. It had its own underground tunnel system, but this one was filled with water. So after a short hike through the city you get to the entrance of the tunnel system. I ended up taking off my shoes because the water was going to be up to thigh level at some points. The cave was super tight at some points and completely dark. Luckily I had my headlamp which made it easy to see. Definitely wouldn't recommend if you're clostraphobic! The tunnel system went on for more than 500 meters and took us at least 20-30min to walk through. The ceilings weren't very high either so most of that I was hunched over. The tunnel finally let us out at the pool of the city. This was the end of the route so we made our way back out of the city and then walked back up the hill to mount Zion. Mount Zion had the tomb of king David. For those that don't know, David is also responsible for writing the psalms (a book of the Bible). Also right above David's tomb was the room of last supper where Jesus ate with his 12 disciples. I'll be honest the room didn't look anything like the painting it was just a plain room. Afterwards we walked back into the old city towards the western wall and stopped for lunch at a small cave restaurant called al buraq. I had shawarma which was tasty but not as good as the shawarma I had yesterday. After we finished eating we walked down Via Dolorosa and out of the old city through the lion gate and up the mount of olives. Walking up the mountain we saw the birth place of Mary, the church of Mary, and the tomb of Mary. They weren't anything super unique, but still pretty cool to see. We also saw the massive Jewish cemetery that faces the Temple Mount. Apparently it is almost impossible to get a grave there. The reason it's so popular is because the Jewish faith believes that during the end of the world the mount of olives will split open and the souls of the riteous will be able to get up and walk to the Temple Mount which is where heaven on earth will begin so they want to be as close as possible. Next we walked a little further up mount olives to another church that had a great view of the Temple Mount from the Eastern side. After hanging out there for a bit we walked back to the hostel going through the suqs, Sam bought some souvenirs. Back at the hostel we relaxed and watched the movie True Lies. If you haven't seen it it's a completely ridiculous action movie with Arnold Schwarzenegger. It was a little after 5 when we finished the movie and we had booked an escape room for 6 so we walked out of the old city near where we were last night to get there. We were there a little early so we decided to stop at the nearby Irish pub for a drink. It ended up being happy hour (buy one get one free) so we had two! The escape room was really fun. We made it out really fast and only needed one extra clue. The room was set in the 1930s during prohibition and the point was to find out the secret recipes of the drinks. The nice thing about the room was there was food and drinks that you were allowed to eat and drink! Needless to say we destroyed all the chocolate 😂. We ended up escaping in a little under 40 min.After the room we ended up going back to the Irish pub to get some food. Jamie and I ended up splitting the large crunchy chicken and fries. After eating we made our way back to the hostel and went to sleep.

item.title: Day 8 - Tel Aviv
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 8 and got our stuff packed up to head out to Tel Aviv. Since today is Saturday (day of rest) the buses were not running...We didn't plan for this and even Google had it wrong saying the buses were running. I'm not sure how they overlooked that since it's literally every week that they shut down. We walked around about a mile to try and find one of the unofficial busses called a shurut that we read about. It's supposedly a van they fill up with people to take to Tel Aviv. We were unsuccessful in finding one so we ended up just taking a taxi. Tel Aviv was about a 45min drive from Jerusalem. The taxi dropped us of at our hostel around 10. The hostel was super packed and had a cool vibe. Check in wasn't until 2 so we dropped off our luggage and had breakfast. Breakfast wasn't much just bread and hummus and veggies. After eating we walked down to beach which was a 15 min walk and hung out till 11. At 11 we went to the nearby bell tower in old Jafa to meet up with a free walking tour our hostel told us about. The walking tour went through the old city of Jafa. One of the interesting stories was the clock tower, it was donated to the city by one of its citizens who apparently owned the only clock in town and up until that point everyone constantly asked him what time it was. Naturally he got tired of this so he donated the clock tower to the city so that no one would ask him for the time again 😂. We also walked through some gardens which had a good view of the city and the coastline. From the gardens we went over the "wishing bridge" towards the port. Legend has it that if you stand by your zodiac symbol (carved into the rail of the bridge) and look at the sea and make a wish it will come true. I'll let you know if it works! We finished up the tour at the port. There was also a really weird orange tree that was suspended by wires that we stopped to see. Apparently oranges were a big thing in Tel Aviv, the tour guide wasn't very engaging and it was hard to hear some of the details of the stories. After the tour we walked back to the dog beach to hang out and relax. There were a ton of dogs at the beach. Israel is actually super dog friendly so you see dogs walking around almost everywhere you go, makes me miss having a dog! Sam decided it'd be fun to dig a hole at the beach so he spent a good hour digging, this attracted the attention of a few dogs who stopped by to try and help. We stayed at the beach for a few hours and then went to a shawarma place nearby that was recommended by Jamie's coworker. The shawarma was good as usual! After eating we walked back to the hostel to checkin and rest for a bit. We hung out at the hostel till dinner and then left to go to a nearby restaurant called Florentine 10. I decided to change it up and have a burger and it turned out to be much better than I expected! After dinner we went back to the hostel for happy hour. The hostel was a mostly younger crowd and definitely the party atmosphere. We met some cool people from Germany and the Netherlands that we hung out with for a while. After happy hour was over a huge group went to go out to the bar. We decided to go with but it took forever to walk there. The first stop was a bar with cheap drinks. We stayed for a little while and then ended up heading back to the hostel. I really didn't want to walk all the way back so we decided to go back on electric scooters. For some reason Jamie's app wasn't working and I was the only one able to get a scooter so we decided to share. This turned out to be a little more difficult than we first anticipated and we totally crashed within the first minute 😂. That didn't stop us though, we tried again and we're able to make it back to the hostel in one piece

item.title: Day 9 - Tel Aviv to Cairo
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we slept in till 9ish. We didn't have too much planned for today. We went upstairs to have some breakfast at the hostel again. After eating we decided to check out the Kamel market. It was about a 10min walk from our hostel. The market was really crowded and was your typical street market. They had just about everything you could think of. We spent maybe 15 min walking through the market to the other end. After walking through we decided to head over to the beach which was only a couple blocks away. This beach was not the same one we went to yesterday, it was a little further north and much bigger. We decided to walk up the beach to check it out. Along the way there were some random body weight gym machines. Sam and I had a contest to see who could do the most consecutive pull-ups. When we got to the end of the beach we decided to try the lime scooters again. This time we were able to get it to work so that everyone had their own! We cruised down the beach and then over to a street called Rothschild street which was supposed to be a street with really fancy houses? Idk we really didn't see anything to fancy honestly but at least there was a nice lane for scooter riding and no one crashed! After scooting around we stopped for lunch at another place Jamie's coworker recommended called cafe noir. It was a French themed restaurant that was known, surprisingly for their schnitzel. It was pretty decent! The waiter definitely judged us when we asked for fries instead of mashed potatoes, typical American move 😂. After lunch we scooted back down to the old Jafa city to check out the "famous" flea market. The market ended up being basically a bunch of junk that people were trying to sell. It was seemed to me like the community garage sale held by the homeless people or something....kinda weird. Needless to say I didn't see anything that I wanted. However, I did see a gelato shop right next door which I obviously wanted. So we all got some gelato. After exploring the market we walked back down to the beach to hang out and enjoy the view until we had to leave for the airport. We ended up grabbing our stuff and checking out of the hostel around 3 and then grabbing some scooters and scooting the mile or so to get to the train station that takes you to the airport. Our flight wasn't until 7 but we heard the security in Israel is super strict and takes forever to get through so we gave ourselves some more time for that. Also tomorrow is another Jewish holiday so the last train to the airport was at 4 and then everything shut down till Tuesday. The security at the Tel Aviv airport turned out to not be a big deal at all. I'm really not sure what all the hype is about. We got asked maybe two questions and the line for security was so short. It was literally faster than going through Savannah's tiny airport line. Once in the airport I went to the executive lounge with Jamie (she gets in for free and can take a guest). They had free food and drinks which was great. It was also way more comfy than hanging out at the terminal waiting for a flight. Our first flight was to Athens, since Israel and Egypt have a tumultuous past their are no direct flights from Tel Aviv to Cairo. The flight took a little over two hours, I ended up listening to some podcasts and playing sudoku on my phone. Once at Athens we were supposed to only have a 2 hour layover and leave at 11:45. I'm not sure exactly what happened but we didn't end up taking off till almost 1am 😫. This flight was a little shorter than the last one. When we landed we were planning to get our visa on arrival, of course there were no signs and we ended up waiting in line at passport control only to be told we had to go to a separate line first to buy the visa...ugh! We eventually made it out of the airport and got an Uber to the hotel which was only a few minutes away. I think it was close to 3am by the time we went to sleep.

item.title: Day 10 - Cairo The Great Pyramids of Egypt 🇪🇬
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up around 8am it was a little rough getting in so late last night, but the hotel is super nice! Something kinda cool we figured out was that on our way to Egypt we ended up being in 3 different continents in like 6 hours. We went down stairs for the complimentary breakfast buffet. It was really good and had a ton of food. Our tour guide picked us up at 9am from the hotel to take us over to see the great pyramids. On the way we drove through downtown Cairo. The traffic here is horrible and they also have no idea what lane lines mean 😂. On the way we passed some mosques and the "city of the dead" which is a HUGE area that is filled with old graves and tombs that date back thousands of years. It's weird because people still live in there today among all the graves. After about an hour drive we made it to the pyramids. On the way our guide told us all about the history of Egypt and the pyramids. It's really fascinating! There are three main kingdoms of Egypt: the old kingdom, Middle Kingdom, and new kingdom with dark ages (times of disorder) in between each. The overall span of time is incredible. The beginning of the old kingdom dates back thousands of years to 2700 BCE. The great pyramids of Giza were made during the old kingdom which makes them even more impressive. Although there are 3 "great" pyramids, Egypt has 100s of pyramids. Our guide, Ola, was great! She had been a guide for 10 years and really knew her stuff, she also was into taking lots of pictures and told us all the best spots and poses to do. We went inside the first pyramid to see the burial chamber. In order to get there you had to crawl up this tiny shaft (maybe 4x4 feet) it was really cramped and people were going out the same shaft. Luckily it wasn't super crowded otherwise it would've taken forever! The burial chamber was in the middle of the pyramid and it was ridiculously hot, it felt like a sauna, there was absolutely no air circulation. It's insane to imagine how they built it so long ago. After exploring the inside of the main cave we went for a camel tour around the pyramids. This was way more fun than the one we did in Jordan! Our camel guide was super animated and took tons of photos. We were even able to "drive" the camels ourselves. My camels name was Michael Jackson 😂, Jamie's was named California and Sam's was Charlie. After the camel ride we went to the nearby Solar boat museum. This was a restoration of a boat that they found buried next to the second pyramid. The Egyptians used to believe you took what was buried with you to the after life and they thought having a boat would help you on the journey. Next we made our way down to see the Sphinx. The Sphinx is also in front of the second pyramid. The Sphinx is partly destroyed (missing its nose and beard). There are many theory's to why the nose is missing but no one really nose (get it?)😂. The beard was taken by the British as a spoil of war and is currently in the British museum. We made a quick stop at a papyrus store on the way to lunch where they showed us how papyrus is actually made. Papyrus was the first form of paper and is surprisingly durable. That being said the guy showing us how it's made and doing the demonstration accidentally ripped the papyrus trying to show how strong it was 😆. After the presentation he of course tried to sell us some paintings on papyrus. They were all really cool but not really my style. We also made a stop at a cotton store. Egyptian cotton is a big thing here. The shirts were mostly super colorful with crazy patterns. Sam ended up buying a T-shirt. For lunch we stopped at a shawarma place that had a view of the pyramids. It's really crazy how close the city is to the pyramids. This shawarma was more of a grilled panini style that had cheese, it was delicious. Once we finished lunch we drove to Saqqara which was about an hour south of the city. Saqqara has some of the oldest original pyramids and hieroglyphic tombs. The main pyramid there is a step pyramid that was built for the pharaoh Djoser and was originally just a rectangular structure that ended up being built up into a pyramid. We also went through some the of nearby tombs to see some of the hieroglyphics which tell stories of the Gods. Next we drove a few minutes to Memphis which is an open air museum that had a bunch of statues and monuments. There were two large monuments of king Ramses as well as a smaller version of the great Sphinx After seeing Memphis we started our way back to the hotel. We made one last stop at a carpet shop to see how they created rugs by hand. The process is ridiculously tedious. They create the patterns by tying colored threads in individual knots. Most rugs have 144 knots per square inch and can have over 1 million knots in a whole rug. After the rug museum we made our way back to the hotel. The hotel is super huge so we decided to explore. Sam and I ended up going to the sauna and jacuzzi while Jamie went back to the room to rest. For dinner we ended up eating at the Italian restaurant. The hotel probably had 20 individual restaurants, basically anything you could think of. I ended up getting a calzone and splitting a bottle of wine with Jamie We ended up going to bed early at 10 to get some sleep. Tomorrow we have a super early flight to Aswan to start our nile cruise!

item.title: Day 11 - Aswan and Kom Ombo Nile Cruise
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today was another early day, we had a flight to catch at 5 am so we woke up around 2:45 to take the 3am shuttle to the airport. The flight down took about an hour and relatively smooth. Getting out of the Aswan airport was a breeze and our guide, Big Mac met us outside without bus to start our tour of Aswan. The first stop was the Aswan high dam. It's a huge damn that was finished in like the 1970's to help control the flooding of the Nile and generate power for Egypt. The dam was only 15 min from the airport and it was heavily protected by guards since it's very important for Egypt. The dam created a large lake behind it called lake nasser, after the president who was in office when it was built. Our guide warned us not to swim in the lake because it was filled with lots of Nile crocodiles. Up next we went to the Philae temple aka the temple of love. Along the way we picked up two Italians who were joining us on the tour. To get to the temple we had to take a small motor boat to the island the temple was on. Interestingly the temple had to be relocated because of the construction of the Aswan dam (along with 17 other temples) so that it wouldn't flood. Archeologists had to disassemble the entire temple piece by piece and reassemble it ~500m away on higher ground. The temple itself was cool. It was built for the God Isis and had lots of hieroglyphs covering it. There were also lots of Christian symbols in the temple because later in history the Christians came and took over the temple. After finishing Philae temple we went to see the unfinished obelisk. If you don't know an obelisk is what the Washington monument is, basically a big square pillar with a pyramid top. Anyway the unfinished obelisk was going to be the largest ever built, however during construction (basically carving it out of a massive rock) it cracked and was abandoned. We also learned about how they carved out the rock and moved the massive piece. It's amazing that they were able to do all this thousands of years ago. There are quite a few mysteries that we still haven't figured out today about the Egyptians, some people even believe that aliens helped 😂! After the obelisk we went to the herbs and spices shop. The shop was filled with just about every spice and herb known to man. It was cool to learn about all the different ones and the effects they supposedly have. I ended up getting some hibiscus tea, it's really tasty, if anyone wants to try some let me know! The next stop was the essence/perfume and essential oils shop. Again they showed us a ton of different oils and what all the benefits of each were. One thing I learned was the difference between perfume and essence is that perfume is just essence mixed with alcohol (only about %15 essence). Jamie ended up getting one she liked made from the lotus flower, it's also known as the sweat of the Gods haha. Finally we got to our tour boat to check in. Also side note: basically everywhere in Egypt has metal detectors, but none of them are actually used! You walk through them at every single tourist site and it goes off every single time and no one seems to care or check. The cruise boat was surprisingly nice! We were on the first floor in a 3 bed room. The breakfast/lunch/dinner room was in the sub level and there were 2 levels above us and a deck that had a pool! After settling in we ate lunch downstairs, it was a buffet style all you can eat and was pretty decent. After lunch we walked around the boat a little. One weird thing about the pool is that there are windows in it so people in the bar/lounge on the floor below can see you swimming. After walking around a little we went back to the room to take a nap. While we were napping the boat started sailing to Kom Ombo, our next stop. We arrived around 5:30 and met our new guide in the lobby to start our tour of Kom Ombo temple and the crocodile museum. Kom ombo means mound of gold in Egyptian and as you'd guess, the city had a gold mine that provided gold for all Egypt. The temple took 400 years to build which was the longest time for any temple. The temple itself was built for two gods: the evil crocodile god Sobek and Horus (the falcon God). The temple also had a well that was used to determine the water level of the river Nile. Another interesting feature of the temple was the tunnels they found underneath it that went all the way to the other side of the Nile. Next we stopped at the crocodile museum that had a bunch of the mummified crocodiles that they found buried in the area. The mummification of the crocodiles were a tribute to the God sobek. Archeologists found over 1000 crocodiles buried in the area. After the museum we went back to boat and watched the movie Jumper before going to dinner. Dinner was a similar buffet style. After dinner we went to the lounge on the second floor and played cards. Fittingly we played the game Egyptian rat screw, Sam was actually really good at the game so him and I were good competition, Jamie on the other hand, didn't make it far. After we went to bed early watching Indiana jones as the boat sailed to the next stop Edfu.

item.title: Day 12 - Edfu
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we sailed through the night from Kom Ombo north to Edfu. We woke up at 5:30am for our tour...another early morning. We met our new guide in the lobby to start the day. From the boat everyone was loaded on to small horse carriages to the get to the Edfu temple which was about 10min away. The temple was completely covered by mud when it was discovered and because of that it is the best preserved temple in Egypt. The temple was a Greek temple for the God horus (the falcon God). Although the temple was built by the Greeks its original location, building plans, and foundation were Egyptian. The temple was finished in 57 BCE and took 180 years to complete. The birds eye view of the temple looks like a step pyramid with the main alter at the very top where only the pharaoh and high priest were permitted. Each day they performed rituals 3 times for the God. After seeing the temple we took the horses back to the boat and stopped to buy some waters before re-boarding and going to breakfast. Breakfast was really good luckily we got here early before the crowd and were able to get an omelet without having to wait in a huge line. After breakfast we watched the rest of Indiana Jones and took a nap. After napping we went up to the top deck of the boat to hang out in the sun as the boat sailed to the famous city of Luxor. Sailing was relaxing, we went through locks at one point in order to get to the lower water level portion of the Nile. When we got to the locks a bunch of small tow boats pulled up next to our ship to try and sell rugs, shirts, towels, etc. their sales tactic was to put the item in a plastic bag and throw it up to the top deck. This caused a bunch of unsuspecting passengers to get hit by the items 😂. While on the top deck we also went in the pool which was super cold but refreshing. [wpvideo iE6PjUxX ] After getting roasted on the deck we had lunch and then went back to our room to watch the new movie Spider-Man movie. We went back up to the deck when the sun wasn't as strong to play some ping pong. Sam is about the same skill level as me so we had some pretty good games. After that we met our guide in the lobby to talk about the plan for our next two days at luxor. After meeting our guide we decided to go for a walk around Luxor near the port with one of the people in our group named Ravi. The walk was not very relaxing because Luxor is filled with people trying to sell you something so from the minute you step off the boat you are constantly, aggressively approached by some of the most insistent 'salesman' I've ever seen. After walking through the local souk we made our way back to the boat. On the boat we played some more Egyptian rat screw and then went to dinner and finally to bed.

item.title: Day 13 - Luxor Temple and Karnak Temple
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 7:30 to get breakfast. Breakfast ended at 8 and the dinning hall was mostly empty which was nice but there also wasn't much food left. Fortunately the omelet station was still open so I had two of them. We met our guide shortly after breakfast at 8:30 to head to our first stop, the Karnak temple. The Karnak temple is the largest temple in Egypt and is actually a complex of multiple temples. The complex had a massive entry road that was lined with Sphinx statues. The open area of the main temple had 134 columns representing 3 for each of the 42 governantes of Egypt at the time plus 8 for the Gods. This temple also had two large obelisks in the center. There was also a small statue of a Scarab beatle next to the sacred pool (used to cleanse the pharaoh and high priest before the daily rituals). Legend has it if you walk around the statue 7 times then all your wishes will come true. So of course, like the tourists we are, we walked around 7 times. I'll let you know if my dreams come true 😂. After exploring the temple a little longer we got back in the bus and made our way to our next stop the Luxor temple. This temple was considerably smaller but was interesting because it had been converted to a Christian church at one point and also was covered by dirt and a mosque was unknowingly built on top of a portion of the temple and is still there to this day After walking around the temple we went back to the boat for some lunch (the usual buffet style). After lunch we hung out on the upper deck at the pool again to relax. This portion of the trip is considerably slower than the first half and I enjoy it! Sam and I played some more ping pong until my paddle unexpectedly broke :(. After that we decided to play cards instead. We played a trick taking game Jamie and I used to play all the time as kids called up the creek. After getting more than enough sun we went back to our room and watched the movies 48 hours (a movie with Eddie Murphy from the 80s) and then Jamie and Sam watched hotel Mumbai which I already watched on the flight over. Dinner tonight was way more crowded than usual because new people were boarding the cruise ship. After dinner I talked to my dad on the phone for a while before heading back to the room to sleep.

item.title: Day 14 - Valley of The Kings
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 7 to get breakfast and check out of our room on the ship. Our guide was meeting us in the lobby at 9 so we hung out for a bit of the upper deck of the boat until he arrived. This gave me some time to get caught up on my blogs which I haven't been able to post since the ship doesn't have WiFi. Our first stop was the valley of the kings which took about an hour to get to since it was on the opposite side of the river. The valley of the kings is where they buried a TON of the Acient pharaohs. There are 62 tombs (and 3 others they just found) including the famous tomb of king Tut (the boy king). In the valley we ended up seeing 3 of the different tombs. They are all very similar so this was more than enough in my opinion. The tombs were basically really long tunnels dug into the mountain and filled with hieroglyphics and at one point tons of treasure. Some of the tombs were packed with tourists which was a little frustrating! The tombs all dead end into the burial chamber which has a huge sarcophagus that the pharaoh was buried in. I have no idea how they got the sarcophagus in but they're massive and obviously super heavy. Another interesting thing is the workers would continue the construction of the tombs for as long as the king was alive and ruling. So the longer the tunnel means the longer that king lives and ruled. This is the reason that king Tut's tomb is so small and basically just a room without a long tunnel. After exploring the tombs in the valley of the kings we drove 10 minutes or so to the Temple of Queen Hatshepsut. This temple is where the queen was buried. Hatshepsut was significant because she was a female pharaoh, the first one to do so (well before the time of cleopatra). The temple was really massive and also had a huge stage being set up for a concert they were doing this weekend that was rugot in front of the temple. After walking through the temple we left to head back across the river. We made a quick stop at the Colossi of Memnon for a picture. The colossi are two massive statues of the pharaoh Amenhotep III and were very well preserved. After the tour we got dropped off at the Hilton Luxor for our final night before flying back to Cairo. We got checked in and had lunch at the restaurant down by the main pool. I got the chicken shawarma which ended up being hung up on a skewer. It was pretty good! The views of the Nile from the hotel were also great. After lunch we went over to hang out by the other pool till sunset and relax. Relaxing has been a common theme for the last half of this trip! After sunset we went back to the room to watch a few movies and then get to sleep. Tomorrow we have an early flight back to Cairo.

item.title: Day 15 - Cairo Egyptian Museum and Home
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Today we woke up at 6 and went down to eat the breakfast at the hotel. The breakfast was a buffet and had a ton of options and even some delicious strawberry smoothies. After quickly eating we took a cab to the airport to head back to Cairo. The weird thing about Egypt as I mentioned is they love metal detectors and the airports or no exception. At the airport you have to go through security twice! Once when you get in and then again when you go to your gate. The second security line was extremely long today, luckily we arrived early enough it didn't matter. Another weird thing is they Have separate security lines for men and women. After finally making it through to our gate we boarded and took the quick flight to Cairo, only ~1 hour. Somehow we got first class tickets so we were in the front of the plane with a ton of legroom! Once we landed we took and Uber to hotel to check in and drop off our stuff. This was the same hotel we stayed in our first stop in Cairo. Next we called an Uber again to take us to the Egyptian museum. The museum was MASSIVE and had lots of sarcophagi. It also looked a little disheveled and cluttered since they are moving everything to the new museum that opens next year. The exhibit they had on king Tut was incredible. Even though the boy king didn't live or rule for long his tomb was absolutely PACKED with treasures. Here's a picture of his sarcophagus which was completely covered in gold! The other thing that was particularly interesting was the mummy exhibit which was filled with actual mummies from thousands of years ago. It's incredible how well they were preserved considering how old they are. After walking around the museum we had some lunch at the food stand just outside. I of course had to have one last chicken shawarma before leaving Egypt (I highly recommend if you ever go). Once we finished eating we Ubers back to hotel, traffic here is crazy and getting back out of the city took about twice as long as the trip in. At the hotel we watched the movie the mummy (original) and then went to the steam and sauna to relax. The one employee there was all about the sauna and was super enthusiastic telling us to lay down and sleep in the sauna and bringing us water to not overheat 😂. By the way this sauna was super hot compared to any I've ever done so it was a struggle to stay in for the full 15 minutes. Afterwards we went back to hotel room to watch the new version of the mummy movie (with ton cruise) and ended up ordering room services once we were lazy and didn't want to dress up and go down to one of the restaurants. I ended up getting the butter chicken which was good, but didn't have any naan bread with it! After eating we slept for a few hours and then made our way to the airport and said our goodbyes. My flight back home was at 4:30am so I took the shuttle to airport at 3am. The security was slow again but I made it to my flight on time. My first flight was to Rome and then I was supposed to go to Atlanta but was rerouted through Detroit since the flight was over booked. I ended up getting back to Savannah around 10:30pm. This was another great trip that I'm super grateful I was able to go on. Traveling with my sister and Sam was a blast and hopefully will have the opportunity for some more adventures in the future! Nothing is planned yet for next year, but my dad and I are thinking about maybe going out to Scotland to try and play the famous St Andrews golf course.

item.title: Ecuador 2020
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
What a year it's been, it feels like it's been forever since I've gotten to travel anywhere! A whole year has gone by since the Egypt trip and I've had multiple trips cancelled thanks to everyones favorite pandemic. Luckily Ecuador has re-opened so Becca and I got our negative COVID tests and packed our bags! We'll be in Ecuador for 10 days mostly hiking and exploring, I can't wait to get there!
