item.title: Day 1 - Quito
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
The trip started off a little rough. I got a call from the car rental company while we were waiting to board the aircraft saying that they ran out of cars so we wouldn’t be able to get one when we landed... Luckily I had made two different reservations (I forgot to cancel one). So I hastily called them to confirm that the other reservation was still good...negative, they too had given up our reservation! WTF 😫! Apparently reservation doesn’t mean the same thing in Ecuador 😂. Luckily as we were boarding I was able to get ahold of another car company that had cars, but they were in the city (not the airport) so we decided we would pick up the car the next morning.

The flights were smooth. First we flew to Charlotte, and then back down to Miami, and finally Quito! Every flight was basically full and I was stuck with the middle seat on all of them ☹️. Becca and I watched almost every episode of Utopia, really cool show, def recommend. We were a little worried on the plane because they passed out two forms for everyone to fill out and one was a declaration form stating that you promised to self isolate for 14 days :/?! Once we arrived in Quito they made us all sit and wait in the terminal while people came around to check our COVID tests and our temperature. It turned out that as long as you had a negative COVID test you didn’t have to fill out the isolation paperwork, phew!

We ended up getting out of immigration/customs around 12:30 and the hotel we were staying at sent a driver to come pick us up. We finally made it to our room around 1:30!

The next day we woke up around 8, breakfast was included and delivered outside our door. It was eggs and grilled cheese, pretty good actually! We went to the front desk to get our cab to the city and two dogs that lived on the property came to greet us so of course we gave them lots of pets!

The ride to Quito took about 40 min by taxi. The driver took us to the Avis rental car building. Surprisingly they had a car for us! And they were super nice and helpful. The car itself was really small and as we would find out later not powerful enough for the steep mountains of Ecuador 😂. Quito is basically a massive city built in the mountains, the elevation is just over 9,000’.

Our first stop was a famous basilica, it was super cheap to enter (only $2 a person) and we got to climb the towers and these cool pathways above the vaulted ceiling of the church.

We met a super nice guy and girl working the little “restaurant” at the top of the tower, we got telecoco tea (which is the coca leaf) and cacao tea which tasted like hot chocolate. Becca tried chewing some of the bitter telecoco leaves like locals do to help with the altitude, she was not a fan (the tea was great though).

Becca was not feeling well, we think because of the diamox (altitude pills). So after the church we walked down about a mile to the old town of Quito. There was supposed to be a famous Iglesia (church) there, but we couldn’t find the entrance. After a few minutes of walking around we found a nearby grocery store and got some food, water, and snacks. Becca waited with everything while I walked back and got the car. I had a minor freak out at the parking garage when the car wouldn’t open after multiple attempts. It turns out I was at the wrong car 🤦. To make matters worse the car was too weak to make it up the steep ramp out of the garage and stalled on way up the ramp. I had to let it roll back down the ramp and then speed back up it as fast as I could on my second attempt. Once I finally made it out of the garage I picked up Becca and we drove to the teleferico (cable car) to explore the nearby mountain.

The teleferico was really cool! It took us up to about 13,000' and there were great view of the city from the top and we lucked out with clear sky’s and great weather. Becca still was not feeling too well so she decided to hang out at the cafe near the cable car while I made my way further up the mountain to hike the summit of Ruccu Pinchincha. The hike up wasn’t too difficult until the very end when the clouds rolled in and it got really cold. To make matters worse right before the top, the trail I was on led to what was basically a huge sand dune which was EXHAUSTING to hike up, especially with the limited oxygen at 15,000’ I was about to turn back until I ran into some people coming down and told me that there was an easier way up on a trail just ~20’ to the right and that I was close to the summit. After a grueling ~2 hours of total hiking I finally made it to the top!

Great view from the top 😂

At this point I was pretty exhausted from the hiking and altitude so I hastily made my way back down in about an hour (I descended down the sand dune path which was really fun!) and met Becca who was feeling a lot better. We took some cool pictures together and there was also a swing that had great views of the city.

It was around 5:30 when we finally made our way down and back to our car. According to Google we had about a 3 and a half hour drive to our next spot, Tena. It turns out...that was a lie. Getting out of Quito was a pain with the traffic and steep roads but it turned out that was the easy part! Once out of the city we had to wind through the mountains with our weak little car, and to make it even better the sun had set and the roads were filled with surprise pot holes and debris from mud slides. It was also super foggy because we were basically in the clouds of the mountain making it even more difficult to see. The trip ended up taking a solid 4 and a half hours, I’m honestly surprised our little clown car made it. We had some close calls with some pot holes and more than once I thought for sure the tire blew out.

At last we made it to our hostel in Tena around 10:30 our host was super nice and helped us order some food. I ended up getting a full size pizza and Becca had a salad- not a whole lot of gluten free options down here unfortunately.

Around midnight we went to bed. Tomorrow the plan is to go hiking and caving in Tena and then drive down to Banos.

item.title: Day 2 - Tena
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We woke up today with it pouring rain outside, we’re in the Amazon rainforrest so I guess it’s to be expected. We went to the main house around 8 and had an awesome breakfast of fruit, coffee, papaya juice, granola with yogurt, croissants, and eggs. We talked to one of the hostel owners, Erin, who was from Aspen, Colorado and she gave us a ton of recommendations for the rest of our trip.

After breakfast we went back to our cabin to change and get ready for our caving and jungle hiking tour. We ended up leaving the hostel a little after 9 with Tony (our guide, he’s Ecuadorian and dating Erin). Our first stop was Cavernas templo de ceremonia (the cave). The drive probably only took 30 min to get there and along the way Tony told us a lot about the different people that live in Ecuador. This area is known for the Quichua tribe. Before getting to the cave entrance we hiked about 15 min, Tony pointed out some really interesting plants. The land we were on was owned by a family with a shaman and they grew lots of Ayahuasca. Ayahuasca is the root of a plant that is used to brew “medicine” but is well know because it causes hallucinations (it’s active ingredient is DMT). Also, according to Tony it’s the cure for literally everything, depression, tendinitis, stomach aches, and yes even COVID haha.

They cave itself was really cool! We crawled, and squeezed through for about 45 min. Along the way we had to wade through water and avoid the scary looking scorpion spiders (they’re supposedly harmless but I wasn’t about to test out that theory). We also saw a bat in the larger part of the cave. Once we reached the end we climbed our way out and hiked back to the car.

Our next stop was only ~10min away. We were hiking the canyon trail. I forgot to mention that we were given rubber boots which were helpful in the cave but really helpful here because the trail was superrr muddy. Along the way down to the canyon Tony pointed out more interesting plants. One of the plants you could eat if your were thirsty because it was full of water, it tasted super sour but I liked it.

About an hour into the hike Tony asked us “do you want to jump?”, we had no idea what he was talking about. He explained that there was a cliff jump into the water that we could do or we could continue hiking down. Of course we chose to jump! Tony had us wait for him as he took all of our stuff we didn’t want to get wet and hiked down with it then came back to meet us. The hike to the cliff was super sketch. We had to swim and Boulder across some rocks over a super fast river. Luckily no one slipped and we made it to the spot. The cliff itself was 12m (~36feet) high, way higher than I’ve ever jumped. Tony went first and showed us. Becca went next because she didn’t want to be left up top alone, she jumped without any hesitation. I was next, it was super fun! The little pond area we landed in was awesome there were waterfalls pouring into it and steep walls all the up to the floor of the Forrest above.

After swimming for a bit we saw the nearby “hidden waterfall” and the did some more kinda sketchy rock climbing/bouldering to the next part of the trail.

We kept hiking down until we reached a suspension bridge over one of the rivers.

Then we turned around and started our way back to the car. We took a different, more direct route. Along the way ran ran into a little trail dog who followed us all the way back, he was a really good hiker!

When we arrived back at the car we found out that the battery was dead 😫. Lucky some other people were around and we were able to start it by pushing it down a slight incline to get the engine turning. Our next stop was lunch. We went to a place in Archidona where we had tilapia cooked in a leaf with yuca and Ecuadorian salad (mostly onions lol). The fish was delish!

We also had a drink called wayusa. Apparently it is an energy drink and Channing Tatum is a huge fan of it and invested in a company that makes it in the US, very random but it tasted good! After lunch we drove back to the hostel and showered and packed up. We hung out at the main house for a little chatting with Erin and then made our way to our next stop, Banos.

As we loaded up the car I noticed that we did indeed almost break our little cars tires with one of the potholes we hit 😕. The rims on the right side were pretty badly damaged. We’re very lucky the tires didn’t pop.

Didn’t look great. We borrowed a hammer from the hostel to try and bend the rim back into place a little but had no luck, turns out steel is pretty strong.

The drive to Banos was much smoother, mostly. The roads were in great condition and driving in the day was much less stressful. We were literally less than 10km away from our hotel in Banos when that traffic became horrendous. It took us over 30 min to go the last 5 miles and there’s nothing like stop and go traffic on steep roads with a manual car! Luckily I didn’t roll back into anyone and got lots of practice with hill starts.

We finally made it to our hotel around 7:30pm. The hotel was really nice but it had definitely seen better days. We got a free upgrade because the first two rooms he showed us the electricity didn’t work lol. After unloading we went down to use the hot tub and steam room. Finally around 10 we went to bed.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Coldworking a steel tire rim? This is why you aero guys can't be trusted with structure!
Haha it was worth a shot!
Where's the pic of the trail dog

item.title: Day 3 - Banos Canyoning and Paragliding
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
This morning we woke up around 7:30, breakfast wasn’t open till 8 so we explored the grounds of the hotel. There was an old concrete water slide that looked like a snake, we climbed up for some good views.

In general everything was deserted in the hotel, I think we might be the only ones staying here. We had a pretty standard breakfast of eggs and then got ready for our tour. The driver picked us up at 9 to go to the tour office in Banos. We tried getting cash to pay for the tour but after 5 failed attempts at different machines we gave up and they said we could pay later. The firsts tour was canyoning at Churasco. The drive from Banos took about 45 min. Are guides, Manuel and German (pronounced Hermon) we really funny. After a quick review of the different rope techniques we hiked down to the start of the canyon.

We started by jumping into the water of the river and scrambling down. We end up doing a few jumps off cliffs into the river, my favorite was a 10m jump. We also did one that was kind of a zip line and a bunch of other repels down waterfalls, it was a blast. We finished with a small cliff jump into the the river where you could do a flip.

Faster we finished we hiked back up to the car past a little trout farm. Then we drove ~10 min to a lunch spot with a nice view of the mountains. We had beef, rice, beans, salad, soup, yuca, and some sort of exotic looking fruit. While eating we learned our guide German is a bit of a player when it comes to dating. He told us about all his different European girlfriends and how he has a daughter in Spain that he goes to visit. Also today was his 31st birthday so he was going to fiesta later haha.

After lunch we drive back to banos and to the tour company. Luckily we were able to get the ATM to work so we paid for our tours and then walked around the city for a bit before getting picked up for our next tour, paragliding!

We drove about 45 min to a place called Niton hill. There were really great views of the surrounding cities. The wind was too strong so we had to wait for it to die down a bit. Becca and I walked around while we waiting and found a cow who like getting his nose scratched.

After about 15 min we went back and waiting in the car until it was time to fly! I was up first because I was heaviest. We flew for about 20 minutes around the hill with some really cool views! The landing was right back in the same place we started and was flawless.

Next up was Becca. The winds weren’t as crazy so her takeoff was much smoother. Once she took off I talked to the other guy that was there (he only spoke Spanish). He was 23 and from a coastal town in Ecuador, also traveling with his girlfriend. I also learned that he owned some sort of strip club/brothel with his cousin 😳. Anyway...after talking for 10 min I looked over and saw that Becca was really low and that the wind really died down, then a minute later I saw them crash i a nearby field further down the hill! 😂 the assistant drove down to get her and the pilot. When they returned the wind picked up a bit again so they went for another quick flight, this time the landing went as planned!

We drove 45min back to Banos and were dropped off at the tour office. We ended up running over to the grocery store and a nearby restaurant to get some drinks and dinner. The restaurant was and Argentinian steak place, the owner understood what no gluten meant so that’s how we chose it! We got a ride back to the hotel and ate, the food was delicious! We went down to the hot tub after for a little and then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 4 - Banos Waterfalls and Swing
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7 and then made our way downtown by car (it’s only about a 5min drive). We had breakfast at a place called cafe honey. I had a sandwhich and a hot chocolate (it looked more like a milkshake.

After we ate we drove down the main road to see all the waterfalls (it’s called the Ruta de las cascadas because there are so many). At the first two we stopped at Agoyan waterfall and monato de novio we to a cable car over the river to get a closer view of the falls (it was only $2 to ride it). Everything in Ecuador is super inexpensive, I highly recommend if you’re looking for a budget trip.

The final falls we stopped to see (also the largest) was called Pailin del Diablo (the devils cauldron). We parked where the GPS told us to go for the entrance but ended up walking around the town for a solid 20 minutes before we figured out where the entrance was (we totally would’ve failed if this was an amazing race challenge) to add to our misery it started raining. The falls were really cool! And as we later found out there are two different entrances to see them. The first one was higher and had a bunch of suspension brides. The other entrance (the original and main one) took you lower and right underneath the falls. I think the second one (main entrance) was the best but each only cost $2 to enter so might as well do both if you have the time.

After the falls we made our way back toward Banos. On the main road we stopped to do Ecuador’s longest and fastest zip line. It was something like 1.8 kilometers over the rio verde and the cool thing was you got to go down on your stomach! I’m not the biggest fan of zip lines but Becca had never done it and it was only $10 so totally worth it.

After the zip line we made a quick pit stop in Banos to get more cash from the ATM and then drove up the nearby mountain to casa del Arbol (tree house). This place is famous for its “swing at the end of the world”. It lives up to the hype. We had a ton of fun swinging and taking fun pictures and it only cost $1 per person to enter! Another nice thing was it was, like many of our other activities, mostly empty, thanks COVID! There were so many great views of the volcano and surrounding mountains. After swinging we decided to eat at the restaurant there. The most expensive thing on the menu was $1.50 so we ordered one of everything to try, the whole meal was only $9! Definitely recommend checking out this place if you’re in Ecuador.

After casa del arbol we drove a little ways back down towards Banos and stopped at a really nice hotel/spa called Luna volcano. The day pass for the pool was $20 but totally with it (this place was super fancy). We spent most of our time in one of the hot tubs overlooking Banos and had a few drinks from the bar. I had a beer and a “chocolate Oreo explosion” it was delicious. We hung out there and enjoyed the sunset. Oh yea and they made you wear these swim caps, so you don't get hair in the pool...I guess they don't care about Oreos.

We ended up leaving a little after 7 and made our way back down to town and walking to a new restaurant on the second floor with a balcony overlooking the park. I got some super tasty dish with eggs, avocado, chorizo, and a pancake thing. Becca had the trout and shrimp dish. After dinner we drove back to our hotel and got somewhat packed in preparation for our early drive tomorrow to quilotoa.
item.category: swing at end of the world

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: The swim cap has me cracking up

item.title: Day 5 - Quilotoa Lake
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early, around 5:45, to head to Quilotoa lake. Google said the drive was just under 3 hours and it surprisingly was! These roads were the best we’ve seen so far. Quilotoa is in the Ecuadorian highlands, so there were tons of twists and turn. One interesting thing we saw was tons of dogs along the side of the road, I mean, there was at least 50 different dogs we saw along the way. We finally arrived and had to pay the entrance fee of $4 (2 per person) they didn’t have change so we ended up paying $5. We drove into the little town hoping to find a restaurant and bathroom. The first few places we tried were all closed and didn’t open until 10 (it was about 8:45). Finally after driving a little further we found an open restaurant. Apparently they only had one option for breakfast, scrambled eggs and bread with cheese and coffee or hot chocolate. The meal was only $4 for both of us and we only had a $20...again they had no change. Feeling like this was some sort of village scam I told the girl in my broken Spanish that we’d be back for lunch so that we would get our money’s worth haha.

Quilotoa lake, I think it’s technically a lagoon, is a big lake inside the crater of and old volcano. It looked absolutely stunning. Becca and I did the loop around the rim of the entire crater which was over 6 miles and thousands of feet in elevation gain and loss. Of course along the way we stopped and took tons of cool pictures. The whole hike around took about 4 hours.

Once we got back to our car we got a quick snack and decided to take the trail down to the lake itself. On the trail we made friends with a pup who showed us the way.

At the bottom we checked out the water, it was cold, and took more pictures. Instead of hiking all the way back up we decided to take the burro (donkey) ride. Becca had never ridden one so it was a fun experience, and of course more views. What I was super impressed with was the little girl who ran next to the donkey encouraging it to keep going. She ran up the trail like it was nothing!

Back at the top we made our way back to the restaurant for lunch. Becca got the chicken and I got the guinea pig. I had tried it once before in Peru and it was pretty good so I figured why not, it was only $4...big mistake it was nothing like I remembered, super salty and rubbery. It must’ve been cooked different or something. Anyway after we ate the girl said she had my change and gave me $2, I guess it wasn’t a scam after all! Another weird thing is that $1 bills are not a thing, the exclusively use $1 and $0.5 coins here.

We got back in the car and made our way to our next stop, Cotopaxi. We were staying in a place called the secret garden that Google said was just under 3 hours away. The roads there were great, finally straight highways....until they weren’t...literally the last hour was the worst roads I had ever seen honestly I’m impressed our little car made it 😂. Of course the sun set when we got to the worst part. It was basically like driving a car up and Rocky Mountain with potholes everywhere. I drove in first gear literally the whole time. Nevertheless we finally made it just after 7. Dinner was included, chicken fajitas with rice and guac, it was awesome! We also met some people from the uk (one of them is hiking Cotopaxi with us) and some Ecuadorians. Everyone was really cool and friendly. There were also a bunch of pups that live here and they were all snuggled up together by the fire, super cute!

After dinner the host, Alejandro, showed us too our little room and around the property. After we settled in we went up to the jacuzzi for a half hour and then went back and got ready for bed.

item.title: Day 6 - Secret Garden Cotopaxi and Refugee
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up kind of early, we have a really cool room called “the bird house that has a nice panorama of the surrounding mountains. It was a bit cloudy so you couldn't see the mountains that well. This hostel/Airbnb also has little hobbit rooms you can stay in and a bunch of alpacas that roam around the property.

After playing with the alpacas it was time for breakfast (7:30) . I had scrambled eggs, toast, and yoghurt. All the meals are included with the price of the Airbnb, probably because there's no where else you can easily go haha.

On our drive to the Airbnb yesterday we managed to arrange a last minute trip to hike to the summit of Cotopaxi. Apparently you usually need to give them 3 days notice but because someone else was already going it worked out. We started drinking lots of water in preparation so the altitude wouldn't affect us as much.

After breakfast we relaxed and got our things organized and then went on a little hike from our hostel to check our two nearby waterfalls. The hike was really fun and short with plenty of scrambling and climbing over rocks. The it was a short hike that took like and hour and a half but the waterfalls were cool!

When we got back we explored around the Airbnb some more, it's a super cool location with amazing views of the surrounding mountains including Cotopaxi. They had these really massive nets that were sort of like hammocks that you could lay in and enjoy the views, they were super comfy.

For lunch (1pm) we had a traditional potato cheese dish thing with sausages that was really good, I think it's called llapingachos. After lunch our guides came so we could try on all the gear we needed to borrow for the hike. It's was super convenient that they provided everything we needed. Once we confirmed that everything fit, we followed them in our car to a parking lot close to the mountain so we wouldn't have to drive all the way back. We drove the rest of the way with our two guides, Edgar and Segundo, and another hiker, Lillia to the refugee parking lot. The roads were very rough but our poor little car somehow managed. From the parking lot we had to hike up for about 45 minutes with all of our gear to reach the Refugee. The place is a huge lodge that can fit up to like 80-100 hikers but we were the only ones staying tonight! (Thanks again COVID).

We had a quick dinner in the refugee around 5:30. It was soup, salad, chicken, and rice. We also discussed the plan with our guides, we were going to go to sleep at 7 and then wake up at 11 to get ready and start hiking at midnight. The hike would take all night and then we would arrive at the summit to catch the sunrise!

item.title: Day 7 & 8 - Cotopaxi Summit and Papallacta Hot Springs
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I didn’t get much sleep tonight, as planned we woke at 11pm. I didn't feel too great because of sleeping at altitude and unfortunately, Becca was feeling terrible from the altitude, the refugee is almost 16,000’ where there is only about 55% oxygen compared to sea level so basically every two breaths is equivalent to one at sea level. She decided she wasn’t going to try the summit hike which was a smart decision because it would just get worse the higher we climbed. I think next time we have to spend more time acclimating.

Once I had my gear on I ate a quick breakfast, really just bread rolls with jam and then double checked everything and made sure that Becca was okay and had a way to get back down to the car (at a lower altitude) if she needed.

We finally started hiking around 12 the first part of the hike was on rocky dirt with lots of switchbacks, I used my hiking poles. After about an hour and a half we finally made it to the glacier. There we switched out the hiking poles for an ice pick and put our crampons on our boots (basically big spikes to give you traction on the snow/ice). We also had harnesses on so that we could be tethered to our guides, in case we fell into a crevasse or slipped and started sliding off the mountain.

The rest of the hike up the glacier was super steep! We climbed over some steep crevasses that went down at least 100'. I lost my footing a few times and slipped but nothing serious. We ended up taking a few ~15 min rest breaks because we were hiking too fast and would reach the summit before sunrise.

I don't have too many pictures on the way up because it was pitch black outside and you couldn't see much. The weather was absolutely perfect, the sky was completely clear and you could see tons of stars above and the lights from Quito below, not a bad spot to rest.

After what seemed like forever, the sun started to come up and we could finally see the summit! We made one last push up the steep slope. There was a strong smell of sulfur in the air as we got closer. Cotopaxi is the second highest peak in Ecuador and is the highest active volcano in the world! We finally summited around 5:30am.

We stayed at the top enjoying the view for about 20 minutes. Edgar pointed out all the other mountains in the area you could see. Some notable ones were Chimborazo (highest in Ecuador and farthest point from the center of the earth), Ruccu Pinchicha (which I hiked the first day), Pasachoa, Antisana, and many others.

Afterwards we're started our trek back down the mountain. It actually wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. The crampons made it super easy. Now that it was light out we were able to see everything we passed on our way up.

The whole way back down took less than 2 hours, even with a couple breaks. Once at the refugee we checked on Becca who still wasn't feeling great and then had some chocolate pancakes with fruit and hot chocolate, it was delicious!

After eating I packed up all my stuff and Becca's. Once we checked we had everything we loaded up and made the short hike back down to the car. I ended up carrying both mine and Becca's bag so she wouldn't have as hard of a time descending. At the car we loaded everything up, I took off my boots finally which felt amazing! And then we drove back down to where our car was parked.

After giving back all our gear we followed our guides to Machachi which was about another hour away to get to an ATM so that we could pay for the hike. The roads were much better on this drive!

Afterwards, we said our goodbyes and drove another hour and a half to papallacta, a famous hot springs about 45 minutes from Quito.

This place was awesome! It was super fancy with tons of little cabanas and hot pools outside. They also had some cold pools so you could go back and forth between them. Our cabana was by far the most luxurious place we've stayed on this trip. We ended up getting room service, I had a steak (which was only $16) and then we hung out in the hot pools. Exactly what I needed after a long day of hiking. Becca was also feeling much better now that we were lower altitude (although still 10,600').

After relaxing for a bit we went to the spa for chocolate massage wraps...it was weird and awesome haha. Basically they give you a massage with warm melted chocolate (it's edible) and then they wrap you up with saranwrap and blankets 😂. Afterwards to get all the chocolate off you they give you a "hydro-therapy" massage which basically is spraying you with a fire hose, it felt quite nice actually! And finally they gave you a bar of chocolate to eat. Def recommend trying if you ever get the chance!

For dinner we went to the on-site restaurant I had llapingachos again. After we went back to our cabana and get some much needed sleep!

The next day we woke up and ate breakfast at 8 at the onsite restaurant. It was fried eggs, variety of bread, and fruit. Then we hung out at the hot springs until lunch. After lunch we explored a little trail from the resort that followed the river. It took about 1 hour to do the loop.

After the hike we hung out at the hot pools till our massages at 3:30. The massages lasted about an hour and were very relaxing! We were already checked out of our room at this point so we got dinner at a nearby restaurant, I had the Ecuadorian version of BBQ ribs (they weren't very good haha).

We drove the final hour to the airport, gassed up the car, and then dropped it off at the rental company. They said I should get a cost of the damaged rims in a few days so 🤞🏻 it's not too bad.

Finally we made it to the airport for our flights back. I was able to do my global entry interview on arrival in Miami, so next time I travel I'll get to skip the lines!

Overall it was an amazing trip and we can't wait for the next one! Our flights to Hawaii are booked for the end of the year!

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Did they ever charge you for the damaged rim?
Nope, never got charged and haven’t heard anything since

item.title: Jamaica 2020
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Due to a my trip to Europe getting postponed till next year and work not allowing me to rollover extra vacation time I had to improvise and planned a last minute trip with some friends to Jamaica! We'll be stopping in Negril for a night and then off to Ocho Rios to relax at a resort on the becach. I probably wont post everyday unless something interesting happens. Here are the trip details 'mon:

https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/0/embed?mid=1CFozR9Q2FJFoHq6dlYmn0J0Q_iU6UGOA
Trip Map

Tuesday Dec 8th
Fly Sav->MBJ arrive ~1pm
Drive to Rick's Cafe (1.5 hrs) known for cliff jumping and sunset parties
Stay Negril Airbnb

Wednesday Dec 9th
Drive to Ocho Rios with stops at: blue hole mineral spring, roaring river and cave, mayfield falls, green grotto cave
Stay RIU Ocho Rios resort

Thursday Dec 10th
Dunn’s falls
Stay RIU Ocho Rios

Friday Dec 11th
Blue hole/secret falls and James Bond beach
Stay RIU Ocho Rios

Saturday Dec 12th
Scuba dive
Stay RIU Ocho Rios

Sunday Dec 13th
Fly home MBJ-SAV depart ~3:45

item.title: Jamaica
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Well I never ended up doing a blog for Jamaica, but I wanted to make at least one post before I forgot about all the stuff we did. A Hawaii blog will hopefully follow soon.

Day 1

We arrived in the airport and made our way through the coronavirus check line (basically they made sure that you had proof of a negative test) and then out through customs. Once everyone made it we picked up our rental car and drove to our airbnb in Negril (about 1.5 hours). Driving in Jamaica took a little bit to get used to, not only does everyone drive super aggressive (to be expected in a developing country) but the cars all drive on the opposite side of the road and the steering wheel is also on the other side! I only messed up by getting in the wrong side of the car a dozen times haha.

Our Airbnb was a little sketchy but it was super close to Rick's cafe which was our stop for the night. I forgot to mention that Pat and Sarah drove separately and ended up popping a tire on their way to the Airbnb! Luckily they had a spare and were able to get it changed without too much hassle. Once Pat and Sarah reunited with us at the airbnb we drove 2 minutes down the road to Rick's cafe for dinner and cliff jumping!

Viewpoint from Rick's cafe known for its sunsets.

The food was pretty good, but expensive (definitely a tourist hot spot!). There were 3 different cliff jump heights at 10', 25', and 35' as the highest. You had to start on the 10' jump to prove that you weren't an idiot and then you were allowed to go higher. Of course I did all of them multiple times!

Jumping from the 10' and the 35' cliffs. In the 2nd picture you can see a little pole behind me with a flag and another jump platform, that one is at 80' and only allowed for professionals! 35' was more than enough for me though.

After eating and jumping at Rick's cafe we made our way to a little grocery store to pick up some drinks and snacks for the Airbnb. Once we got back we hung out for a bit and started playing a board game but never finished it.

Day 2

We slept in a bit and then got all our stuff packed up in the cars and drove to nearby cafe for breakfast. I had a spanish omlet which was really tasty. Today was a longer driving day from Negril all the way to our resort in Ocho Rios (3-4 hours). We had plenty of stops planned along the way to break up all the driving. Our first stop was the blue hole, which is creatively named because it is basically a big hole in ground which of course you can jump in.

We jumped in from the edge a few times (which was about 25') and I also did a few jumps from a tree over hanging the hole that was about 35' to the water, it was a ton of fun! Pat jumped with his GoPro on his wrist which proceeded to fall off when he hit the water sinking to the bottom of the hole. Luckily the guides at the blue hole were able to dive down and grab it for him (the bottom of the hole is about 30 feet deep. After jumping one of the guides took us to the roof of the hotel for some nice views. Also inside the blue hole was some 'exfoliating sand' which you could rub on your face, it felt nice afterwards to be honest haha.

After the blue hole we drove through the mountains to our next stop called the roaring river and cave. Unfortunately the cave was closed, we conveniently found this out after we had paid the entry fee. Instead of showing us the cave the "guide" showed us the river (which allegedly Bob Marley would swim in) and then did some sort of weird baptism thing to each of us throwing water on our heads and saying that it had magic powers lol.

After seeing the river he was going to give us a tour of the local village and 'ganja field'. As we proceeded to follow him we realized we were getting farther and farther away from the cars to we ended up just turning around and leaving. Our tour guide just seemed super sketchy and the whole experience had a bit of a scam vibe to it, I think if the actual cave was open it would have been more fun.

After quickly driving away from the sketchy river and cave we made our way through even more mountains and tiny little roads to Mayfield falls. On the way there we made a wrong turn and luckily quickly realized our mistake as the road became superrr skinny, after somehow managing to turn around we made it the rest of the way without a hitch. Mayfield falls is a waterfall hike, there were tons of different falls that you got to climb up, under, and around. Overall it was really fun and not crowded at all (probably due to covid).

After the waterfall hike we made the final drive to our resort in Ocho Rios. By the time we made it there it had just gotten dark. We were all starving so after checking in and dropping off all our stuff in the room we grabbed dinner at the all you can eat buffet. After dinner we hung out near the main stage for karaoke, Sarah was the only one who sang, she was awesome! The whole rest of the trip random people would come up to her to compliment her on her singing.

Day 3

Today we didn't do much besides chill at resort. The weather was a bit overcast sadly but it was nice to have a relaxing day after running all over the place the day before.

Day 4

After breakfast Clint, Pat, Sarah, and I decided to go explore a place called secret falls. Basically it's a hike to a waterfall with some place to jump in. Well because of all the rain the night before the water level of the river was SUPER high and the water (which is normally clear blue) was brown from all the runoff coming from the mountains. This made the hike to get to the waterfall extra fun. instead of walking across the river in a few inches of water, the water was up to our thighs and flowing fast! We had to be super careful crossing at some parts so we wouldn't get swept away down the river.

After jumping into the waterfall we went to another nearby bridge (called the Spanish bridge) which had a rope swing that you could swing off from the bridge and jump into the river. It was also a bunch of fun.

After the rope swing we drove back to the resort to relax and eat. Sarah had brought everyone Christmas light necklaces so we were all very festive! Since it was Friday the 'fancy' restaurants were open so we went to the sushi/asian fusion restaurant. The food was really good!

After dinner the hotel had a game in the main lobby so of course we tried. The challenge was to use a fishing pole type looking thing (a pole with a string and a ring attached to the end of it) and get the ring around the top of a liquor bottle. It sounds easy but it was actually really difficult. A ton of people attempted it but no one was able to do it. On my first attempt I failed, but my second time around (with a new strategy) I got it and everyone nearby went wild! Sadly the liquor bottle wasn't the prize, the prize was a fanny pack with the name of the hotel on it lol. Jess really wanted it so I just gave it to her.

Afterwards we ended up hanging out at the beach bar/disco for the end of the night.

Day 5

This was our final full day at the resort, we finally got some sun and really nice weather! We spent the day playing some beach volleyball (the resort had a really court set up, though the net was really low). We also made our way to the other side of the resort which was a water park with a bunch of different water slides.

For dinner we ended up getting reservations for the Italian restaurant which was also really good and then spent the rest of the night hanging out at the resort. I also almost forgot to mention that the night before Clint met a random Jamaican girl at the beach bar and danced with her...today she ended up looking for him/following him around and asking everyone for his phone number, instagram, etc (basically a stage 5 clinger haha).

Day 6

Our final day in Jamaica :(. We all ate breakfast at the hotel and hung out on the beach to enjoy our last bit of nice weather. The waves were finally calm enough to take out the catamarans and paddle boards so we did those for about an hour.

After hanging out on the beach we went packed and up all our stuff and checked out of the resort. The final 1 and a half hour drive to the airport was uneventful. We said our goodbyes to Pat and Sarah at the airport (their going back to Chicago) and we made our way back to Savannah. Overall a really fun and successful trip with some great friends!

item.title: El Salvador 2021
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Fully vaccinated and ready for another exciting year of traveling. Unfortunately the golf trip I've been planning for the last year and a half with my dad got cancelled for a third time and Becca's dive trip got cancelled (both were supposed to happen this month). Fortunately, that meant time to plan a last minute trip! El Salvador isn't really talked about as a popular Central American travel destination, but we decided on El Salvador for a few reasons: it's super close, easy covid restrictions, very cheap, and lots of interesting things to do from Mayan ruins to volcano hikes to surfing on the coast.

Here's the google map of all the places we plan to hit. Our loop starts out in San Salvador (the capital) then goes through the mountains and finally down to the coast.

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1SAC4faPW0MmESwA64cFqalKRj330Krqo&w=640&h=480]

Here's the current Itinerary:

Arrive SAL Airport 2:09 pm, Drive San Salvador

See: Puerto Del Diablo, Divine monument>cathedral san Salvador>sacred heart basilica>national palace>crypt>Rosario church, Mercado Nacional de Artesanías, Mercado Central, Gerardo Barrios and Libertad square, eat pupusas

Stay San Salvador→Real InterContinental San Salvador at Metrocentro Mall Blvd. de Los Heroes, San Salvador, SS, 544 El Salvador

Day 1 Sunday 16th

Stay Lago de Coatepeque - Equinoccio Hotel : SAN24E, El Congo, Santa Ana, Santa Ana

Day 2 Monday 17th

Cerro verde national park: izalco volcano hike 4.2miles 2k’ 3hr

Lago de Coatepeque jek skis, boat rides, kayaking, sunset

Day 3 Tuesday 18th

santa ana volcano hike 4.5miles 1.5k’ 2.5hr, Tazumal Mayan Ruins, Santa Teresa Hot Springs/Alicante Termas

Day 4 Wednesday 19th

Impossible national park mountain biking/caving

Stay Ataco→ El Carmen Estate
