item.title: Day 1 - Exploring San Salvador
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Let’s start with day 0 (yesterday). I got a call from the rental car company...I knew it wouldn’t be good...my assumption was correct, they had no more cars for us tomorrow, I seriously couldn’t believe it happened again (last time was our Ecuador car rental)! Luckily it wasn’t right before we were boarding the airplane this time! He called back a few minutes later saying he found a car! We finished up packing and getting ready. Becca’s sister and brother-in-law came over (they’re staying and watching the pups for us) we made some creme brûlée with the new torch, it was delish!

The next day we woke up early around 6am. We finished packing, ate some breakfast and made our way to the airport around 6:30. Our first flight was to DC and then onto San Salvador.

We landed at 1:30 which was a little early. Getting through passport control/customs was easy, they just checked our vaccination cards. I had tried to make two other back up rental car reservations, just in case the other fell though, and also because we had to pick that one up in the city (40min from the airport). We tried our luck with the Avis rental car stand at the airport. Of course they “didn’t have the car I reserved” but had another one that was more expensive. Luckily a local person was behind and helped us negotiate the price back down to what it was supposed to be.

Once we got the car it was an easy drive to the city. The roads were surprisingly nice. The hotel was even nicer, after checking in we took an Uber to the centero historico of the city. Once there we visited a couple different churches (all of which had masses going on) and took a tour of the national palace. Lot of people were staring at us as we walked around, I’m not sure if it’s because we’re both tall or because they don’t get a lot of American tourists haha.

We learned a little bit about the history of el Salvador. Apparently it was the most prosperous country of Central America until the 1980s, when their civil war occurred, which didn’t get resolved until 1992. The palace had a bunch of different rooms, all of them were painted a different color and named accordingly (I.e the blue room, yellow room, etc).

After touring the palace we walked around the squares and open air markets. There were tons of people! Everyone was wearing masks even outdoors (it was super hot and humid). We grabbed some pupsas (the National dish) for a street vendor as a snack. After walking around we took another Uber to a restaurant called tapioca margoth, I read online that they had really good pupusas. We had 6 different types of pupusas, horchata, and a fried plantain for desert. A pupusa is a thick corn tortilla filled with different combinations of cheese, meat, beans. Its the national dish of El Salvador.

After dinner we got a ride to the nearby brewery called Cadejo. The beer was good, after a few drinks we went back to the hotel. We went and checked out the pool of our hotel but it was a little cold so we didn’t stay long. There was also a super fancy wedding going on right next to the pool. Afterwards we relaxed and went to bed.

item.title: Day 2 - Volcanos and Mayan Ruins
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up early, around 5:30 (it’s two hours behind Savannah here so I was expecting it). We packed up and had the buffet breakfast downstairs at the hotel restaurant. It was pretty good a bunch of omelets, fruit, waffles, etc. After breakfast we drove just north west of the city to the San Salvador volcano which is in El Boqueron park. The park itself was tiny, we walked through the whole thing in like 20 min. They had a bunch of cool views along the ridge of the crater looking down into the caldera.

There was another trail that left the park and went around the rim of the crater. It was technically closed (no idea why) but since we walked through the park so quickly we decided to walk around the little fence and take the trail. The trail went about a mile and a half around the crater with more views looking into the volcano. There was another path you could take to go down into the crater, but we decided against it because it looked like a long way down. On the trail we ran into a few people carrying supplies on their heads (no idea where they were going) along with some dogs and horses.

After reaching the other side of the rim we decided to turn around because the trail go significantly worse (very tight with lots of brush). When we got back to the car we changed into our swimsuits and drove to los chirros (a nearby spring). Unfortunately the spring was closed (even though everything online indicated otherwise) so we ended up continuing on to one of the Mayan ruins called Joya de Ceren. When we arrived that too was closed! At this point we were getting frustrated! We drove to our next stop, San Andres (another Mayan site) and luckily that was open.

San Andres was a relatively small site consisting of some pyramids that had recently been been unearthed (they were covered after the eruption of a volcano). The site was where the Mayans would perform various ceremonies including human sacrifice! Some of the ceremonies they continue today in order to preserve the history of the Mayans. At least I’m pretty sure that’s what our tour guide said, the whole tour by was in Spanish! It was surprising to me how little English is spoken here compared to some of the other Central American countries I’ve been too, my guess is that it’s due to less tourism.

The tour lasted about 45 min. Afterwards we drove up to our next hotel at the lago de coatepeque. There was a big accident with two trucks on the highway, that caused a massive traffic jam on our way to the hotel. As a side note google maps is pretty useless here, the times we used it it tried to take us on non existent roads or way out of our way. When we arrived at the lake we checked in and unpacked then went to the dock for a snack. We tried the ceviche, which was okay. After eating we took the kayak out on the lake and went around the mini island in the lake. There were some really nice houses on the lake, we saw two helicopters take off from their lake houses on the island while we were kayaking.

We got back to the hotel after about an hour and hung out on the dock and at the pool. There were a few other American tourists (with families in El Salvador) staying here so we talked with them. We had dinner at the hotel, I had a burger and becca ate more papusas (she really likes them haha). The burger was pretty sad, tomorrow we’re going to try eating somewhere away from the hotel to see if the food is better.

After dinner we went to bed. Tomorrow we are climbing the Santa Ana volcano!

item.title: Day 3 Santa Ana Volcano
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early again and had breakfast at the hotel at 7am. Breakfast was included which was nice and consisted of scrambled eggs, bread, and fried plantains. After breakfast we loaded up to drive (about an hour) to the Santa Ana volcano for a hike. Unfortunately even though the volcano is literally right next to where we’re staying we had to drive all the way around the lake to get there because it’s the only road. We got to a place called castle cristal at 8:30 when we were supposed to meet our guide (who we talked to on the phone the day before, he was recommended by our hotel). Not sure what happened but our guide wasn’t there and didn’t answer any of our calls or messages. Luckily we were able to find another guide but had to wait an hour before starting the hike.

Unfortunately it’s not allowed to hike by yourself here. Instead we had to hike with a group of about 9 other people, 2 guides, and an armed police officer. Of course no one the other people in our group were in that great of shape so it was going to be a very slowww hike up.

No more than 10 minutes into the hike we took our first break, most of the rest of the group was already out of breath. Luckily our guide allowed us to continue on with the police officer so that we didn’t have to wait for everyone. The police officer was super chatty! All in Spanish of course so it was good practice for me. He talked about everything from history of the volcano, to family/job, the pandemic, the economy, and even politics (he’s surprisingly pro trump and thinks trump will get re-elected next election haha). After about an hour and a half of hiking we made it to the top! There were some really good views of the lagoon in the crater! The policeman joked that if you can smell the sulfur then you’re COVID negative.

The temperature of the lagoon is more than 125F so no swimming allowed! The last time the volcano erupted was in 2005. We hung out at the top for about 20 minutes or so before the rest of the group caught back up to us. We took some more pictures, you could even see the lake we’re staying at with the little island that we kayaked around. I found out from the policeman that the island is mostly owned by one of El Salvador’s ex-presidents.

After spending some time at the top the guide let Becca and I head down ahead of everyone else since we were faster. It probably took about 30 min to get back to the car. We drove back towards the hotel and stopped at a restaurant on the lake, the food there was much better than our hotel. We both ended up getting the fajitas.

After eating we got back to our hotel, hung out at the pool for a little and then took the kayaks out again. This time we went searching for the “hot spring” which was close to where we were staying. Unfortunately I didn’t have my phone but the “hot spring” was comically sad. It was basically a couple holes (no more than 2 feet in diameter) on the beach with puddles in them with no more than an inch of water. To be fair the water was pretty hot, but it was not at all what we were expecting haha! We’re planning on going to another hot spring tomorrow, hopefully it’s nicer!

After kayaking we hung out on our balcony before eating some papusas and then going to bed.

item.title: Day 4 Tazumal and Hot Springs
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in till ~8 and ate breakfast at the hotel again. After breakfast we packed up the car and checked out of the hotel. We drove further west to another Mayan ruin site called Tazumal that was about an hour away. Tazumal was a Mayan city the was uncovered in the 1920s. It was cool to see the size of the structure, much bigger than the ones at San Andres. We spent about a half hour exploring the ruins. It was fun because here they actually let you climb up on most of the ruins.

After Tazumal we went to another ruin site only half a mile away called casa Blanca. It wasn’t as impressive as Tazumal (more like mounds of dirt than anything) but since we were here we figured we might as well see it.

They also had an area they were excavating that you could go down into. It was crazy to see how deep the layers of bricks went. The guide mentioned that there are likely hundreds of other ruins still buried beneath the dirt.

After casa Blanca we drove another 30 min or so to get to the Santa Teresa hot springs. At first glance the place looked pretty run down and the parking lot looked like a pile of rubble. However, once inside we were greeted with countless pools ranging in temperature from super hot 46C (~115F) to cold.

We enjoyed the pools for a bit and then ate at the on-site restaurant called Manhattan. I had a grilled chicken sandwich that was surprisingly good! Becca had a chicken salad and for dessert we had a brownie with ice cream, nut delicioso!

After lunch we took a nap in one of the hammocks (it was super relaxing). And then hung out in the hot springs till ~5pm. We left for our next destination, El Carmen coffee plantation in the city of Ataco.

We had a bit of trouble finding the hotel because the plantation is very big however luckily we ran into someone who spoke English and was able to direct us to the right building. It was a very unassuming red gate on an alley with no signs whatsoever. After unpacking and settling in to the hotel we walked across the Main Street to the town to get dinner.

We stumbled upon a Mexican restaurant where the food was dirt cheap. We spilt a plate of loaded nachos and I had a pork torta (apparently it’s a burrito but on a bun instead of a tortilla). The food was really good!

After dinner we grabbed ice cream bars from a nearby street shop on our way back to the hotel. We ended up watching some of the god father part 3 (I had downloaded) before going to sleep.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Loving this!!

item.title: Day 5 Waterfalls and Labyrinths
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7 and had breakfast at the house we were staying in. Dora (the host) cooked us a typical breakfast of eggs, beans, bread, cheese, and fried plantain. The bread was super stale but everything else was good! Becca wasn’t feeling so great (as you might be able to tell from her expression), maybe Mexican wasn’t the best idea last night!

After breakfast we got ready and took the on site coffee tour. We were pleasantly surprised to find out that we finally had a guide, Hector, who spoke English! He took us through the whole coffee making process from picking the coffee plants (done by hand) to processing, drying, sorting (done by hand), and roasting. It was crazy to see all the people they had sorting out all the coffee beans (looking for beans with imperfections such as broken or miscolored). It was also really cool that the coffee plant still used the same machines from the 1930s, the year they started producing coffee.

It was also really cool to see the warehouse where they stored all the packaged coffee beans (this was not very full according to hector, he said usually the stacks almost make it to the ceiling. This coffee plant is medium sized and does about 10 million pounds of coffee per season. They process a mix of their own beans as well as beans from other farms in the cooperative.

At the end of the tour we got to try some of the coffee. I’m not much of a coffee guy so I’ll refrain from critiquing but Becca liked it and got a bag to bring back home.

After the coffee tour we drove down what’s known as the ruta de las Flores about 20 min to the town of Juayua (pronounced “why-you-ahh”). There we found another tour company with a guide (Eduardo) that was willing to take us on a tour of the siete casacadas (7 waterfalls). Amazingly Eduardo also spoke good English. We ended up driving to the start of the trail in order to save a few hours of walking. To get to the start of the trail was pretty rough, we drove for about 15min into what seemed like the middle of the Forrest. At this point we were getting skeptical that this wasn’t some sort of ruse, but Eduardo seemed trustworthy and he was tiny so I figured I could take him if I had to :P

The start of the hike was basically all down hill and crossing a few rivers until we arrived at the first waterfall.

After the first waterfall we continued on to see the rest, the second waterfall was tiny so I’m not even gunna bother putting a picture of it, but the rest were great. I think it was around the fifth wasterfall when Eduardo said “okay now we climb up”. So we climbed up the waterfall, which was pretty steep and a ton of fun!

We then made our way through the last two waterfalls and took a “shower” under the final (7th waterfall).

Luckily the trail was a loop so we didn’t have to climb back down any of the falls. After returning to the car Eduardo took us to a place for lunch called cafe Goya. The food there was really good and super inexpensive (it was $10 for the 3 of us). We all had the chicken with vegetables and rice. At the restaurant we watched some of the sand soccer game which apparently is really popular here.

After eating we dropped Eduardo back off at the tour office and continued back to another town on the route called Apeneca our first stop was the labyrinth. We really weren’t expecting much but it was actually super cool! We spent about 15 minutes finding our way to the center to ring the bell and then explored the rest of the labyrinth.

Afterwards we decided to drive up the mountain behind the town to a place called laguna verde (green lagoon). It was recommended as a cool place by the police officer on our Santa Ana hike so we figured we’d give it a shot.

The lagoon turned out to be really disappointing, it basically looked like a homeless encampment with kids playing with trash in the murky water of the lagoon. We took a quick picture and quickly headed back to town. A guy came up as we were leaving to try and get us to pay a “fee” but I told him all we had was a credit card (which of course the didn’t accept) so he let us leave, after all we were only there for like 2 minutes.

After exploring Apeneca, we made our way back to Ataco and parked at the main park to explore the city. There are tons of cool murals painted on the walls of all the buildings here. We ended up stopping at a coffee shop called Brewers, I had a delicious snickers milkshake.

Afterwards we made our way up the hill and the northern end of town and found another labyrinth, this one was smaller and only cost $1 so we figured might as well. it ended up actually being more tricky than the large one we did. After about 15min we escaped and went to dinner at the next door restaurant which was on the rooftop with great views of the city below. We also saw a peacock roaming around the grounds.

I had the special pizza and Becca had a kebab. The pizza toppings were great but the crust was really bad, I think it was stale (it was really difficult to chew). We kept seeing signs for pizza so I figured they must make good pizza in El Salvador...false, stay away from the pizza here.

After dinner we went back to the hotel. I finished up blogging then we watched some more of the god father and went to sleep.

item.title: Day 6 Vamos a la Playa
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up and had the typical breakfast at 7, same as yesterday’s. Then we packed up and hit the road for our final stop, the surf town El Tunco (recently renamed surf city, I suppose this is a marketing ploy by the el Salvadoran tourism department).

On our way to Tunco (~2hrs) we stopped about halfway at a beach called los Cobanos. On the drive down we saw a ton of stray dogs along the road. Also there’s a really weird trend we noticed, people just walk casually along the road with machetes, I mean literally everyone young, old, man, woman. I’m not sure what they do with them.

Los Cobanos was a small beach known for its golden sand. Parking in the Tony town was confusing, we ended up parking by a restaurant in a tiny alley. There’s really no direct access to beach here you have to go through a building of some sort. We walked down the beach and then relaxed for a couple hours.

The waves at the beach were massive! Also there were a ton of large rock formations in the water so we didn’t end up going in very far. After a few hours we decided to venture over to the other side of the cove. We parked in another alley and ate at the restaurant there. The restaurant was literally inches from the water. I’m pretty sure that where we were sitting would be in the water at high tide.

The waiter told us they only had to options for food: fish or shrimp. I went with the fish, which I got to pick out from a cooler filled with fish, and Becca had the shrimp.

The food took a while to get but it was really good! There were also a bunch of stray dogs and cats scouring the restaurant for food, some of the little puppies were really cute.

After eating we walked around the beach for a little longer and then packed up to continue on our way to our hotel in Tunco, Los Farallones, another hour away. This hotel was super nice and had awesome views of the ocean.

Our hotel was right on the coast with a couple pools and our room even had its own balcony with a hot tub! We decided to go to the city to eat and get some groceries since we heard the reviews of the hotel restaurant weren’t great. The little city of Tunco was really cool! By far the most touristy part we’ve seen yet, there were also a ton of white Americans we saw for the first time.

We ate at a small shop in town, I had a “gyro” that was basically a weird shaped burger in a tortilla and Becca got tacos. Unfortunately we didn’t realize the tacos were fried so they became veggie tacos. Afterwards we ended up grabbing some pupusas in town so that Becca could get some more food.

We walked around the town and beach some more and watched the surfers catch some waves. Apparently the world surfing championships are next week so lots of professionals are out here practicing, the top 5 men and top 7 women will get a bid to the Olympics in Japan (the first time surfing will be in the Olympics).

After exploring the town we made our way back to the hotel and hung out in our hot tub for a bit before watching some more of the god father (it’s a really long movie) and then fell asleep. Tomorrow we’re taking surfing lessons!

item.title: Day 7 Surf City
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up and took our at home covid tests. We needed to do it in order to get back into the US. The test was relatively straightforward nose swab that you do while FaceTiming a test “proctor” to make sure you do it correctly. My test kit was missing the reagent but luckily beccas had enough for both of us. Luckily both our tests came back (after 15 min) as negative.

After testing we had our complementary breakfast at the hotel on the balcony facing the ocean. I had the “americano” breakfast and Becca had the traditional. Nothing too special about either.

After breakfast we changed and met our surf instructors at the hotel parking lot. There were 3 guys, two instructors and one photographer (I can’t remember their names). We ended up going to the next beach over called San Blas, because the waves weren’t as big there...they were still really big though! They actually almost cancelled our lesson because of the size of the waves.

The beach we went too had this really cool black sand that shimmered in the sun. We ended up doing some stretches and going over the basics of how to position yourself and how to pop-up while we were on the beach.

After going over the basics we tried it out for real in the waves. I’ve only been surfing one other time (in Costa Rica) and the waves were way farther out, here by the time you popped-up you were almost at the shore, this made for some very short runs. Also the waves were pretty powerful. The instructors weren’t all that great either, I kept asking him for tips and what to do but he didn’t other up much advice. We still had fun though!

Afterwards we drank some coconut water and relaxed on the beach.

After our tour we hung out at the hotel for an hour and then drove to the other nearby town called La Libertad. We walked along the beach and onto the pier, there were a bunch of random shops lining the beach and a big seafood market that we explored.

We made our way to the end of the beach to a place called punta roca. There was a little shop there with drinks where you could watch some of the really good surfers catch waves. After all the surfers came in we made our way back to the center of town and stopped at a restaurant with a view of the water.

I had some sort of beef and cheese sandwich, it was delicious, and Becca had a fish stuffed with shrimp. One thing to note is restaurant service in El Salvador is superrr slow it took about 40 min just to get our food after we ordered!

After eating we drove to El Tunco to look for some potential surf lessons again tomorrow afternoon. The traffic to get back was really bad, and for no apparent reason, it seems like they just like to block the road sometimes, not really sure why. In el tunco we picked up some pupusas for dinner later from the really good street shop and also found a different company to do surf lessons with.

After el tunco we went back to the hotel and hung out at the pool and our room until bed. Tomorrow we’re planning to go to another waterfall about 30 min away and then surf again in the afternoon!

item.title: Day 8 Cliff Jumping and Surfing
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up and had breakfast at the hotel at 7:30. This time the breakfast was a buffet style which was way better because I was able to load up my plate with a ton of everything: eggs, bacon, hash browns, pancakes, yogurt, and fruit.

After breakfast we drove to Taminique to meet Pedro for a waterfall tour. Taminique is only like 20 min away up the mountains. I found Pedro’s number in a random blog online and messaged him the day before, he only spoke Spanish but agreed to meet us in the park at 8:30. Sure enough when we pulled up to the park in Taminique Pedro was there waiting for us!

After meeting Pedro we made our way directly to the trail which was only two blocks away from the park. Another kid was with us, he was from the town and wanted to come. Pedro was super friendly I got to practice a lot of Spanish with him. It took about 20 min to hike down to the waterfall. In general the hike was pretty easy. At the first waterfall there was a cliff jump that was 4-5 meters high, not that high but still a lot of fun!

We jumped a few times and also did the “water slide” down the waterfall. The water was super refreshing after the hike down.

After jumping and sliding we hiked another few minutes down to the second waterfall that was much higher. There was no jump on the waterfall because the water was too shallow but we did swim in it and get a “free massage” from the falling water.

After enjoying the final waterfall we made the hike all the way back up to town, it’s way more tiring going up! we said goodbye to Pedro and drove back to the hotel to hang out at the pool. At 12:30 we drove to tunco town to meet for our second surf lesson. This time we went to majahal beach (right next to where we were the previous day). The instructors started us with some stretches and then had us do some drills on the beach before heading out into the surf. Our instructors (Wayo and Gato) were much better than the ones yesterday constantly giving us advice and tips. We were probably put on the water for 45 min, I was exhausted! The waves were constant and strong! Just getting back out through all the waves was a struggle, and then when you finally made it far enough out you had to focus on your form and balance.

Needless to say we were dead afterwards, much different than yesterday’s lesson. After finishing we rode back to tunco (in the back of the truck, el Salvadorian style).

In Tunco we got some smoothies and pupusas from our favorite place, la esquina, which happens to be right next door to the surf shop. After getting the pupusas we went back to our hotel and hung out at the pool watching the surfers. We also saw one of the hotel guests propose during their dinner (the restaurant is right next to the pool). Finally we went back to our room and got packed up for our journey home early tomorrow morning.

Day 9: We checked out and left the hotel at 6:30. Dropping off the car was a bit confusing, we had to call the Avis guy to come meet us in the parking lot to get the car. Our first flight to DC was a breeze, we had a 3 hour layover that we spent in the United club, becca had passes, it was really nice! Overall it was a great last minute trip! Definitely one of the least “touristy” places I’ve been but still a fun adventure! Can’t wait for the next one!

item.title: Glacier National Park 2021
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 0

We left after work, flights were Savannah to Atlanta to Salt Lake City and finally to kailspell (town right outside Glacier). The flights were all on time so no issues there. The airports were super packed, ive never seen Savannah with such a long line, it was literally out the door, thankfully I have pre-check so no waiting for me!

When we landed we got our car very smoothly the lady at the counter was super nice and friendly. It was a little Toyota Camry but was plenty of space for just the two of us. The drive from the airport to the place we’re staying, glacier acres was 15-20 minutes away. The place was a little tiny home/cabin. It was super new and had everything you needed. we went to bed pretty late.

Day 1

Today I woke up super early (around 4am local time) because I had to work. I worked most of the day while Becca went out to get groceries and explore the nearby town. Unfortunately my phone (personal not work) died randomly today :(. It had previously gotten some water damage and I was somehow able to revive it, but I guess time was ticking. Luckily it happened before we took any cool pictures, so everything was backed up and no data was lost!

After work we went whitewater rafting on the flathead river. The guides were super hyped up and energetic, it was fun! There was also an Amish family there that had people that couldn’t swim, not sure who thought that was a good idea. The rapids were okay there were some pretty fun ones and the views were awesome. We volunteered to sit in the front which meant we got splashed a ton with the glacially cold water, it was a blast! Near the end of the ride there was a spot you could jump out of the raft and swim, the water was cold but refreshing (it was super hot out, heat wave). There was also an old bridge we passed under at the very end that we learned that you could jump from it. So of course we drove and did it. It was pretty high! Probably 25-30 feet or so, I jumped from the top of the railing which was a little nerve racking to try and balance on.

Afterwards we decided to drive into the park. We drove up to the top of lake Macdonald and then turned around and went back to the south near the entrance. There was a lodge and shops, we got ice cream (they’re known for their huckleberry) and ate by the lake. I also picked up a new hat from one of the stores.

After ice cream we made our way back to the cabin and grilled some brats and corn for dinner. A storm was close so it was really windy and a little drizzly (it never rained that bad though). After dinner we got ready for tomorrow and went to bed.

Day 2

Today we woke at 5:30, ate some cereal for breakfast and then hit the road to get into the park (we’re about 15 minutes away). Our first stop was the lake Macdonald lodge. There we parked the car and then took the sperry trailhead (across the street) to the mount brown lookout. The trail was 5 miles (one way) and extremely steep! It was around 4,300 feet of elevation gain. The interesting thing was many of the trees we hiked through were burned and scorched by the fire a few years ago so there wasn’t a whole lot of vegetation. It took us about 2 hours and 15 minutes to make it up to the lookout but the views of the mountains and lake Macdonald were worth it!

After resting for a minute at the summit we decided to try and continue on to the summit of mount brown, which we could see was relatively close. Becca got tired on the way so I continued alone. I was really close to getting to the summit when I came across some very sketchy terrain that would require rock climbing. Although it wasn’t that steep and was totally doable, if you did happen to slip it was a shear drop off the side of the mountain. So sadly I decided to turn around and head back to Becca.

We continued down the trail, it was a real leg burner going downhill for so long. Eventually we made it back to the car a little after 12 with our legs completely exhausted. Once at the car we decided to drive up to Logan’s pass (about 45 min away). The drive there was awesome with great views the whole way. Unfortunately the two trails that begin there (high line and hidden lake), which we were planning to hike tomorrow, were both closed due to snow and bear sightings :(. However I think we found a good back up for tomorrow.

After hanging out at the pass we made our way back down to the avalanche parking lot stopping at various vistas and waterfalls along the way (there were plenty of them). One called redrock, was a little spot to swim in the lake with another spot to cliff jump!

We lucked out finding a parking spot right by the avalanche lake trailhead. The trail starts off on the trail of cedars for a little less than a mile and then goes mildly uphill for another almost 2 miles till you get to the lake. This trail was significantly more crowded than the one we hiked this morning.

Once we finally got to the lake we were greeted with some stunning views. Of course we decided to take a dip in the icy cold glacial water (it actually felt very refreshing with the 90 degree weather). We hung out at the lake for a while before heading back to the car.

From there we went back to redrock (only a mile away) and I did the cliff jump and swam around in the icy river for a bit (it felt really good on the sore legs). After redrock we drove back stopping to fill up on gas and pick up a few groceries.

Back at the cabin we grilled steak and corn and had salad for dinner, it was delicious!

Day 3

Today we woke up around 5am and packed all our stuff in the car (tonight we’re staying on the other side of the park). We drove into the park and made our way to the loop trailhead. Luckily we were able to get the last parking spot, I’m not really sure if it was a spot since it was literally right in front of the stairs, but oh well we didn’t get a ticket.

We were hiking the loop because the trail we originally wanted to do, highline, was closed. The loop takes you to the same place granite chalet, it’s just a steeper route. The hike was fairly steep but only took us about one and a half hours to make it up the 4 miles to the chalet. At the chalet we stopped for a quick bathroom and snack break. The views were awesome!

We decided to head up another trail called swiftcurrent lookout (another steep, about 3mile hike to the summit). Right when we started the trail we ran into a girl named Amanda and her friend coming back down who told us they had just saw a grizzley bear a short way up the trail and asked if we had bear spray (we did not). She decided to go look and see if there were any rangers at the chalet. In the meantime another couple showed up, Miles and Beth, they were also planning on hiking the summit and they did have bear spray so the five of us decided to go as a group up the trail.

Fortunately we didn’t run into the bear (although it would have been cool to!). We did however run into a ton of marmots which are basically mountain raccoons, they’re really funny and have no fear of humans. We made it up the the peak in about an hour, the views were great. We rested at the top and ate some snacks before heading back down to the chalet.

At this point Amanda left but Miles and Beth went with us to hike up another lookout trail called the grinnel lookout. This one was much shorter but also steeper. Also at the point in the day the sun was beating down on us. We were exhausted but made it up to the view. From the lookout I climbed up some nearby rocks, there was a guy trying to rock climb up to the final peak (unsuccessfully) but I stopped there, it was way too sketchy.

After the grinnel lookout we made our way back down the loop trail. We also found out from other hikers that the highline trail had opened. The hike down the loop was alright, I had my knee brace sleeves on which helped. The bigger problem was the heat/sun, we were baking. We chatted with Miles and Beth on true way down which helped pass the time. By the time we got to the car we were exhausted and chugged the water we had in the car (we ran out of water in our packs).

From the parking lot we drove up to Logan’s pass and stopped to fill up our water bottles. We also saw a bunch of big horn mountain goats across the road. After we filled our water back up we continued east toward the other side of the park and stopped at one last trail called saint marys waterfall. The trail was only 2 miles round trip. The waterfall was cool and had a spot you could cliff jump from so of course I did! We hung out in the cold water for a bit before heading back.

Once back at the car we drove to saint marys (town) and stopped to get some dinner at a Mexican place. Somehow we ended up getting another persons food order and they let us keep it so we had a ton of food. It wasn’t the best but we were starving!

After dinner we drove another 10 minutes to duck lodge, where we were staying. Unfortunately this place doesn’t have ac but it cooled off enough at night that it was fine. They also shot off some pre 4th of July fireworks.

Day 4

Today we woke up early around 5:30 and drove into the park. This was a separate entrance on the east side of the park. The initial road was gravel and super dusty but once we got into the park it was paved again. We got a prime parking spot at the iceberg lake trailhead.

We ran into a solo hiker, Sam, who asked if she could hike with us so of course we obliged. The trail actually ended up being fairly crowded. The distance was only about 3 miles to the lake so we got there pretty quickly. We had brought our bathing suits to jump in but the water was literally ice cold so we abandoned that idea pretty quickly. I did however manage to make it out far enough to jump in one of the icebergs which was kinda fun!

After hanging out at the lake we explored the area a little more and ran into some deer right on the trail. We started making our way back about a mile to where the trail forks and decided to go up the other trail to a place called ptarmigan tunnel, about another 2 miles away. This hike was a bit steeper and took you to a cool little lake and then directly up the side of the mountain to where they built a tunnel to get to the other side. Becca decided she was too tired so she decided to wait for me at the lake while I climbed up. Unfortunately the tunnel door was locked so you couldn’t go through. There was also a really weird ranger or volunteer sleeping at the top and telling everyone that they had “nice legs” when they got up there.

After enjoying the view from the top I started to make my way back down I noticed that there was a large patch of snow up the one side of the mountain and it wasn’t super steep so I decided to take the quick route and slide down! It was pretty fun, the only downside was somewhere along the way I lost my selfie stick :(.

After meeting back up withBecca we somewhat hurried back to the car, I was a little worried the ranger would try to come down and yell at me. Back at the car we drove to the nearby grocery store and got some Gatorade and ice cream! This time I got a mix of vanilla and berry.

Next we drove a little further to the Many Glacier hotel for lunch, I had the huckleberry pulled pork sandwich which was pretty good. This hotel was definitely fancy! We hung out near the lake for a bit, I decided to do the short 2.5 mile trail around the lake (it was super flat) while Becca chilled at the shore near the hotel.

After the lake we made our way out of the park and had dinner at a place called two sisters cafe. It was one of the only places near the entrance of the park so it was packed! We had to wait about an hour to get a table. I had a double burger with bacon, pulled pork, and a bunch of other toppings, it was delicious.

After dinner we made our way back to the lodge. They had a bunch more fireworks to shoot off and also a random laser show going on the barn (one of the laser designs was a lady dancing on a stripper pole 😂). Needless to say it was very redneck.

Day 5

Today we woke up at 5:30 again, loaded up the car, and made our way to the grinnel glacier trailhead. On the way in we stopped for a quick photo at the park sign. Once we were at the trailhead we ate a quick lunch, I had two bagels and a leftover taco. Then we got ready and made our way down the trail.

This trail started near the many glacier hotel and went up alongside the swiftcurrent lake, lake Josephine, and grinnel lake. The trail was about 5 miles one way. Unfortunately however the trail to the glacier was blocked by snow. We had our crampons but Becca was uncomfortable continuing. I went on myself for about another mile until I ran into more steep icy terrain which I promised Becca I would stop at, so I turned around with seeing the glacier :(.

After turning back and meeting up with Becca we made our way to the car and the drove back out of the park and around to the other entrance to get to Logan’s pass. This time Logan’s pass was PACKED. We ended up driving around the parking lot for an hour before we finally found a spot. The reason was both the hidden lake and highline trail were open today.

After parking we decided to do the hidden lake overlook trail. This trail was short but fun, there was a ton of snow you had to hike through and the view at the end was awesome!

After the lake we hiked back to Logan’s pass and decided to hike part of the highline trail since it was open.

We ended up hiking about halfway (3.5 miles) to created butte before finally turning back. The trail had amazing views and we even saw a big horn sheep right on the trail literally 10 feet from us!

After getting back to the car we drove back down to lake Macdonald for some well deserved ice cream! The we made our way out of the park, stopped for some dinner groceries and gas then made our way to the cabin (the same place we stayed originally) to grill our steaks.

Day 6

Today we woke up around 3:30am for our early flight just to find out that it was delayed until 9:40! With that news we decided to go back to sleep! Once at the airport the rest of the flights (to salt lake, Atlanta, and Savannah) went smoothly. We did end up getting back way later than originally planned (around 10:30).

Overall it was a super fun and exhausting trip! I think we averaged close to 20 miles a day and 4,000 feet of elevation gain! Looking forward to the next trip!

item.title: Ireland & Scotland 2021
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
So happy to write that my dad and I are FINALLY going on this trip! It's been quite the whirlwind and almost 2 years in the making. My dad and I were originally supposed to go on this trip back in April of 2020 (planning it at least 6 months before that). After about 3 reschedules, all due to Covid, we're finally able to go! Planning was quite the mess on this trip just because all of the golf courses had very limited availability we even ended up switching the trip so that we went to Ireland first instead of Scotland (per the original plan) just so that we'd be able to do everything we wanted.

item.title: Day 1 in Dublin
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Travel from Savannah to Chicago and then onto Dublin with United went off without a hitch. My dad arrived before me around 5:15am and got the rental car sorted. I arrived at 9a, my golf bag was literally the first bag out (off to a good start!). I quickly made my way through customs and met my dad right outside. We stopped at the car rental kiosk to get my drivers license scanned (since I’ll be doing most of the driving) and then walked to the car and packed the rest of my luggage.

Our car was a decent sized opel, we had to fold down the back seat to fit our clubs, but it was plenty big for the two of us. We got a manual (much cheaper than automatic), which I personally enjoy driving, but the other factor was the drivers side is reversed so not only are you driving on the opposite side but you’re also shifting with your opposite hand. That plus the lack of sleep and trying to navigate wasn’t a great combo. I definitely had a few close calls just getting out of the parking lot!

Nevertheless, after about a 20min drive (a little longer than it should be been since the roundabouts with the GPS were confusing and I missed an exit) we made it to our Airbnb just outside the city center. We were early so we decided to stop at a cafe down the block to get some hot chocolate, and I had to do a bit of work.

We stayed at the cafe until about 11:15 and then made our way back to the Airbnb, luckily our host was there and was happy to let us in early to drop our bags and have some tea and cookies (even though check in technically wasn’t until 3). Our hosts name was Dermont and he was super friendly!

After some tea we decided to walk (~15min) to the Guinness factory. It was a bit confusing to find the entrance since there were a few buildings (the tour entrance is at the storehouse). The tour was self-guided and basically you started at the bottom level and made your way up ~7 levels or so until you go to the top which was a bar whee you could try the beer and have great views of the city (it’s the highest bar in Dublin!). Overall it was pretty cool.

I had to jump on a few work calls while we hung out at the top (not a bad place to work actually). And then we made our way toward our next stop St Patrick’s cathedral. On the way we stopped at a small restaurant called tasty 8. I had a Chinese bbq chicken wrap and my dad had a chicken salad, both were tasty!

We stopped shortly at st Patrick’s cathedral, it was a pretty standard old church, nothing too unique, but it was still cool to see.

Next we walked another 10min or so to the Dublin “castle”. It really just looked like a building except for one section of it that had a stone tower. The castle ended up having free weekday admission till the end of 2021 which is great because I definitely wouldn’t have been happy if I paid for it (normally it’s $20). Essentially it was an art gallery with a bunch of old paintings and portraits (not really my thing). There was some really cool sand castles that were built in the courtyard.

After the castle we walked to trinity college. This one was also $20 to enter, we weren’t really sure what all there was to see inside besides a really old book, so we decided to skip it and grab some gelato instead. We ate at a nearby park. After we finished we walked down a famous pedestrian street called grafton street. It was filled with a bunch of shops and street performers. We ended up watching an Irish tap dancer guy for a couple minutes, he was actually pretty impressive.

At this point our phones were dying at we still needed to book our hotels for the next few days so we walked back about 45 min to our Airbnb, on the way back we walked past an escape room so we decided to stop in and check it out. Unfortunately they didn’t have any times available now but the lady was super friendly and convinced us to book the 8:45 time.

Once we got back to the Airbnb (around 4:30) we rested for a bit while we booked our hotels and also a golf course for tomorrow. We chatted with our host and I did a bit more work.

Around 7:45 we booked an Uber to the escape room. Before going in we stopped at a nearby “takeaway” restaurant. I got a diner kebab, which is always delicious and cheap! We ended up walking back over to the escape room and eating in the lobby before our game started.

The escape room itself was awesome. The room we choose (they have 3) was called “Game of Stones”, which for legal purposes has absolutely nothing to do with the similarly named HBO show Game of thrones :). The essential point of this room was to search the royal quarters and find a dragons egg.

The puzzles were really unique, I won’t give anything away but there were a lot of really cool ones, and only a few lock/combos. Although I wouldn’t recommend doing an escape room while be exhausted from a day of travel and lack of sleep, we still managed to find the dragon egg and escape! We got out with about 10 min to spare and the game master only gave us 3 hints. She said normally people finish with less than 5 minutes and need about 6-8 hints.

After the game we took another taxi back to the Airbnb and then pretty much immediately passed out (~10:30).

item.title: Day 2 Dublin to Blarney
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got up at 7. I slept really well after yesterday’s exhausting day. We ate at our Airbnb, our host had a spread laid out for us in the kitchen. I had eggs, toast, and a banana.

After eating we packed up and loaded into the car and made our way to Killeen golf course. This course was a steal for only 20 euros each. It was about 30 min away. It was a bit chilly to start the morning but the weather turned out to be amazing! All sun no rain, it was great! I didn’t play too well I ended up with an 89 but at least I had a few pars and a birdie. My dad played a little better than me with an 86. The wind was super strong. It was honestly kind of ridiculous at times, I think it was around 20 mph or more with gusts. Which was nice only when the wind was coming from behind you. besides the wind there were a ton of trees, I swear I’ve never hat to hit so many punch shots in my life!

After golf we ended up eating at the restaurant in the clubhouse. I had the fish and chips (aka fries), it was really delicious!

We finished eating around 12:30 or so and made our way south towards blarney, our first stop along the way was about an hour drive to the rock of Cashel. This was the ruins of an old cathedral on top of a hill. I think it’s famous for st Patrick baptizing people there. Anyway, it was really cool to see with great views of the countryside. And the best part was free entry again…thanks covid!

After the cathedral we made another quick stop at a castle 15min away called Cahir castle. This castle was tiny and probably could be skipped, but it was free so what the heck!

After the small castle we finished driving to blarney. Along the way we had a little snafu with the tool booth (I went in the wrong lane and had to back up and try to squeeze over to the other lane) and made it to the blarney castle at 4:20. This was perfect timing because the last entry is 4:30. This gave us an hour to see the castle and explore the grounds.

Our first stop was the castle. It was really cool with tons of rooms and of course at the top of the castle was the Blarney Stone which you can lean over and kiss for the gift of gab. It honestly surprised me they still let people do it with all the covid restrictions today. The best part was that we were the only ones in the whole place besides the two workers that make sure you don’t fall off when you kiss the stone (normally the wait can be longer than 90 minutes to kiss the stone!).

After the stone I walked to see the blarney house (dad ended up getting a hot chocolate and waiting for me). I’m not sure what the story is with it but apparently it’s a private residence and it’s super nice!

Finally we walked around the grounds and saw the “waterfall” which was little more than a few drops into a pond (guess it’s out of season). We also walked through the woods where the witches live. There’s a special staircase that if you walk down and then walk up backwards with your eyes closed and thinking of a wish it’ll come true, tbd on if it works…I’ll let you know.

After all that we made our way back out to the car right at 5:30 when they closed. We drove to our hotel which happened to be like 2 blocks from the castle parking lot. After we got to our room and settled, we went down the street to a restaurant called musketry arms. I had the bangers and mash, it was good!

After dinner we grabbed a gelato at the next door store and made our way back to the hotel to rest!

item.title: Day 3 Cork, Kinsale, & Old Head
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got up at 7 and went down for breakfast at 7:30. The hotel we stayed at had a nice spread and a menu to choose a main dish from. I had some cereal and the “full Irish breakfast” which consisted of egg, toast, sausage, bacon, and pudding. It was super filling!

After breakfast we hung out in the hotel and relaxed until 9:30. Then we packed back into the car and drove into Cork to a small castle called the black rock castle observatory. Luckily they weren’t doing tours today but allowed us to go in a climb up the castle by ourselves. It was super tiny but cool, and some nice views of the town/river. As a side note I’m getting much more adjusted with driving on the left and shifting with my left hand after driving through all these little towns.

After the castle we jumped back into the car and drove down to a place called Charles Fort just outside Kinsale. The fort was really cool, like a much nicer looking fort Pulaski. We walked around the perimeter and took some pictures. There were some good views of Kinsale just across the coast. Kinsale is apparently known as a fishing town and there were tons of sail boats in the harbor.

After the fort we drove over to old head golf course. We were originally supposed to play tomorrow morning at 7:45am, but the weather was so good, so we called the course and luckily we were able to play today instead at 12:45. We ended up getting to the course right around 11:45. The drive to the course was really beautiful. The course is on this little peninsula attached to the coast with shear cliffs, very picturesque.

We warmed up at the driving range and putting green. We ended up playing with two other guys, James and Ian, both were super nice and just out to have fun (not serious golfers). My Dad and I both played really well and took a ton of pictures! I shot an 81 and my Dad shot an 82 and I think we each had a birdie. Basically every hole you played was on the edge of a cliff with crazy tee shots and super large changes in elevation. There were so many fun shots to hit! By far the coolest course I’ve ever played.

We ended up taking 5hours to finish, which is really long for my dad and I (as a reference, yesterday took 3 hours), but it really didn’t seem that slow. After the round we hung out on the clubhouse patio and James and Ian showed up with a hurling stick as a souvenir for us. It was superr random, but apparently they’re both huge hurling players/fans and wanted us to have it! They explained the game to us, patently hurling is like a mix of lacrosse, field hockey, basketball, and baseball and is super popular in Ireland (one of the oldest traditional sports.

After hanging out we drove back to Kinsale ~15min away and checked into our b&b and then walked to dinner. We ate at a nearby pub called Kitty O Se’s bar. I had a Muphrys beer and the fish and chips, both were very good!

After dinner we were both tired so we walked back to the b&b to go to bed. One quirk about the place we’re staying is the shower is absolutely tiny you basically have to crouch in to use it. Tomorrow we’re heading up to Killarney national park to do some hiking, at least I’ll be doing some hiking while my dad takes a rest day.

item.title: Day 4 Killarney
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 6:45 and had “breakfast” at 7, which consisted of some cereal and questionable milk. Needless to say it wasn’t the greatest meal haha. After eating we packed up the car and drove about an hour and a half to our hotel in Killarney national park. We were way early but they were still able to get us checked in. After we got settled my dad decided to stay at the hotel and rest while I decided to go hike.

I drove about 25 mins to a place called Cronins yard and parked to hike a mountain called Carrauntoohil, the highest peak on the island of Ireland (includes Northern Ireland) at 3,407’. The mountain is actually privately owned but is free to access by the public. The hike was about 8 miles and 3,000’ elevation gain. The start was really flat and the weather was great. There were a ton of sheep grazing along the way all spray painted different colors (presumably to identify which farm they belong to).

After about 2 miles I got to the steep section called “the devils ladder” this part was super fun! Basically going straight up a rocky waterfall. At the top I had some good views of the valley below.

The only bad news was it poured rained for about 10 min so I was soaked and the wind was ripping. Also the peak was another 1,000’ and clearly the views weren’t going to be there since a cloud was engulfing the top of the mountain. I almost decided to turn around but I didn’t want to climb down the devils ladder and knew there was another way down on the other face of the mountain which I assumed would be easier. The rest of the way to the top wasn’t too bad. As expected the visibility was awful. There was a steel cross marking the peak but that was it.

On the way down it was really hard to find the trail (the whole hike the trail wasn’t very well marked you just kinda went in the general direction you needed to go). Luckily I had my GPS working and was able to find a path and started down. As I descended the ridge the wind was blasting me, I had to stop a few times to not get blown off the mountain! I later found out that this section is called “howling ridge”. Because of how windy it was I was rushing to get off the ridge and took what I thought was the right trail. It was a super steep gulley, even steeper than the devils ridge. I went slow and eventually made it out. As I came down I ran into a guide who told me that was the central gulley and is dangerous to go down…Whoops!

The rest of the way back was pretty uneventful. I made it back down to the car after about 3 hours 45 min. I ended up getting a sandwich and hot chocolate at the shop.

After eating I got back in the car and drove 15 minutes to a place called the gap of Dunlough. There were some great views of the mountains.

After enjoying the view for a few minutes I got back in the car and drove back to the hotel to pick up my dad. Our first stop was Castlelough Castle which was actually not the castle I was trying to go to, it was tiny ruins of a castle. Still cool I guess.

After the mishap we drove to Muckross house. I’m not sure why it’s so popular but it has over 6k reviews on google. Basically it’s a cool old mansion. We parked and walked around for some pictures.

Next stop was Torc waterfall. Google ended up trying to send us down a road that was closed. We ended up parking at a lot next to the gate. I walked the rest of the way the google directions had us going and then followed the trail signs to the waterfall. We’ll it ended up looping back right to the parking lot! Not sure how I missed the trail head haha. The waterfall was down about 10 minutes, it was cool, nothing too crazy. My dad was waiting in the car so I just took a few pictures and then made my way back to the car.

After the waterfall we drove back towards the city and stopped at Ross castle (this was the castle I meant to stop at the first time). It was cool we walked around but weren’t allowed in because of covid restrictions.

After the castle we drove back to the hotel. We made our way down to the pool for the hot tub and sauna. They ended up making us buy swim caps to use the pool lol.

Afterwards we drove to town for dinner to a place called Khao Asian street food. We both ordered the pad Thai. It wasn’t that great, I think I’ll stick to more Irish/English food while we’re here haha.

After dinner I got some ice cream at the store next door and then we went back to the hotel for bed.

item.title: Day 5 Lahinch
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Since we were able to fit in all the activities yesterday, we woke up early and had breakfast at 8am (right when they opened) after breakfast I went for a quick hot tub and sauna and then we loaded up and started the drive up to Lahinch (on the west coast of Ireland).

Our tee time was originally supposed to be at 2pm, but we were able to call at get an earlier time at 12:45. We arrived at the course around 11:45 and warmed up on the range and putting green. The weather was looking iffy. Right about when we started off the first tee the rain started. It was pretty rough, eventually everything soaked through which made it really difficult to grip and swing the clubs. Needless to say it was a challenging round. We played with two other people James and his wife loretti.

Besides the weather the course was really cool! It was a traditional links style course with lots of thick rough! There were some really cool holes with blind tee shots. One of the par 3 holes had a huge mound in front of the green so you couldn’t see it, so after you hit you had no idea if your ball was on the green or not.

Around 3p the weather finally cleared and it was sunny for the last 5 or so holes, though everything was still soaked it was nice to enjoy the sun. I ended up with a generous 88 for the round.

After we finished we drove up ~15 min to see the cliffs of Moher. We got there just in time for good weather, we could tell rain was coming in just off the coast. My dad and I hiked to a few view point for some pictures. I wanted roses the final view point on the other side, but my dad was tired so he decided to go back to the car and I went on by myself.

At the other viewpoint there was a trail that continued along the cliffs. It looked really cool so I figured I might as well walk it. After 10 minutes or so I could tell that the trail went way farther than I expected so I checked the map and saw it ended at a separate parking lot. I called my dad and he agreed to meet me there with the car (getting to experience a bit of driving in Ireland himself). Along the way it started raining again (luckily I had an umbrella so I stayed mostly dry). The trail ended near the ruins of a castle towering the cliff. There were some pretty cool views of the cliffs, cows, and even a rainbow after the rain died down again.

I met my dad at the parking lot and we drove to our hotel in Lahinch. We unpacked all our stuff into the room so we could pick everything up for our flight tomorrow. After settling in we went to the hotel restaurant for dinner. It was delicious! I had the steak sandwich and it was huge. We didn’t really eat lunch so I was pretty starving at this point (it was about 7pm).

After dinner we went back to the room to try and dry and pack everything up that we could.

item.title: Day 6 Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I was woken up at 2am when my dad decided to turn on all the lights to the room to go to the bathroom and then again at 4am 😡. We ended up actually getting up at 6:30 and got some breakfast at the hotel. After breakfast we tried to dry some stuff with the hairdryer one last time before packing everything and loading up the car for the 3 hour drive to Dublin airport.

The ride to the airport went off without a hitch. We returned the car rental and dropped our bags off. We were about an hour and a half early so we grabbed a quick sandwich for lunch at the gate. The flight was a quick 1 hour. Sadly the weather at Dublin when we left was perfect and sunny while the weather in Edinburgh was rainy and overcast.

Getting into the UK was super easy no one even asked us about Covid. Once we arrived we got our bags and then got picked up by a shuttle to take us to the rental car. Really no hassle which was nice because we were a little worried about getting into the UK. The drive to St. Andrews took about an hour.

The hotel we’re staying at is the historic old course hotel, commonly referred to as the “road hole” hotel that golfers must hit over on the 17th tee. The views from our view of the course were amazing!

After getting settled in we took a free cab to dinner at a place right next to the first tee and 18th green called hams hame (it was only a few minutes away). I had a burger with chili on top, it was pretty good! Apparently there’s a law in Scotland that you must cook beef well done. After dinner we went back to the hotel and went to bed.

item.title: Day 7 St Andrews Old Course
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was the old course day! Luckily we had Amazing weather! Almost 60 degrees and super sunny! We got up and had breakfast at the hotel (which was included). It was a buffet plus a menu that was really good! I had eggs Benedict and waffles. We met Scott (the guy who set up our golfing here in Scotland) at 9a to get a quick debrief of our itinerary and plans for our trip. After talking we went back up to the room and got ready for gold then met him back down at the lobby to go to the driving range.

The driving range is actually on the other side of the course. It was a really fancy range, every stall had a trackman that would tell you each shots ball speed, height, launch angle, carry, total distance, and a bunch of other cool stats.

After the range we drove over to the first tee to putt and get ready for our tee time. We were playing with a couple from Florida, George and Catherine, neither were very good, George almost missed and rolled one off the first tee 😂, but they were really nice.

My dad and I both had caddies, mine was Sam who was +1 golfer (really good). Apparently he’s caddie for a bunch of pros and celebrities, including Trump multiple times (he said he’s actually a really good golfer). My dad and I both played really well, I had 3 birdies and was 1 over going into 17th then doubled and bogied to end 4 over at 76.

After golfing we got a ride back to the hotel, then we went out and walked around St. Andrews town to see all the touristy sites including the castle, church, pro shop and jetty. The town is only about a half mile long so it wasn’t a whole lot of walking.

On our way back we stopped at Dunvegans, a famous pub with tons of pictures of pros and celebrities on the walls, for dinner. I ate about half of my burger and really didn’t feel well so I walked back to the hotel to get the car and then picked my dad up with the car. Back at the hotel I ended up puking a lot, not sure if it was something I ate but it was not fun! Needless to say we stayed in for the rest of the night

item.title: Day 8 Kingsbarns ⛳️
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I was feeling better than the day before but still pretty exhausted since I didn’t get great sleep last night. For breakfast I just ended up ordering room service (it was complimentary) I had some scrambled eggs, toast, and a banana. Nothing too crazy to start getting my stomach back to normal.

After eating I got ready for golf and we drove about 15min to kingsbarns golf course. Kingsbarns is known as the “Scottish pebble beach”. Our tee time was 9am, we got really lucky with good weather again! We played with two other people, Ian and Nicky. My dad had a caddie, Jim, who was very Scottish and apparently played pro in the older division.

The course was great! Not a single hole that had a bad view. Lots of hills and cool tee shots! I had one birdie and played okay overall. Ian, in our group actually got a hole in one on 15! We didn’t know it though because the pin was over a ridge so we couldn’t see it. It wasn’t until we were walking up that the group on the other hole was yelling and cheering (they had seen it go in).

We finally had a little drizzle on last hole, but it wasn’t bad at all. We were able to stay virtually completely dry. After golf we drove back to hotel after and I rested until dinner time. We went to dinner at the Jigger inn, which is basically attached to the hotel. I had a burger and fries, again nothing too crazy. After dinner we walked back And I went to bed. Jamie arrived late in St Andrews by train (from London) and stayed at an Airbnb a mile or two away so we’ll see her tomorrow.

item.title: Day 9 St. Andrews New Course & Pitlochry
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early and met Scott at the new course (right by old course) at 7:45. This was our final round in Scotland and for the trip! Weather was great again, just a little drizzle for a hole or two but really not much.

We didn’t have many people in front of us so we played fast and finished in 3 hours. The new course is similar to old course but a little tougher in my opinion (tighter fairways). After golf we picked up Jamie from the Airbnb went back to hotel to change out of our golf gear.

Jamie and I wanted to hike so we went to a town an hour and a half north called pitlochry. The town is just on the outskirts of the highlands, which has a lot more elevation (which is why we went there). In the town we stopped at small sandwich. They had a really good ham sandwich, however the horrible chocolate milkshake I ordered was awful, it kinda tasted like they just microwaved some chocolate ice cream and put it in a glass.

After we finished eating w went to a place just north of town (2min away) to do a hike called Ben verackie. It’s a 5.7 mile hike with 2,400’ elevation gain (so pretty much uphill the whole way). There were really nice views of the town to start then, probably halfway up, we go into the clouds so the visibility was nothing.

It really was not worth the second half of the hike with the poor visibility, but we finished anyway and got some wonderful pictures of the summit 😂.

The whole hike took just under 3 hours. Once back at the car we drove back to the hotel (about an hour and a half). Back at the hotel I stayed in and rested the rest of the day, the hike kinda wore me out. Dad and Jamie ended up walking around the town since she hadn’t seen it yet and then went to dinner.

item.title: Day 10 & 11 Edinburgh
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early and got all our clubs and stuff packed, then we took our at home covid tests for our return to the US (which we both passed). After the tests I went to down to check out the spa/hot tub area. Honestly I expected more from a fancy hotel, the hot tub was barely lukewarm. Jamie drove over from her Airbnb to have breakfast with us at the hotel. I had an omelet and waffles plus fruit. After eating I got packed up while dad and Jamie went to see the course and walk around the hotel. When they got back we loaded up the car and drove to downtown Edinburgh, a little over an hour away.

When we arrived we stopped and parked at the Airbnb which happened to be right next to Arthur’s seat (a hike overlooking the downtown). Jamie and I started hiking up while my dad decided to walk into the city. It was raining pretty steady so the hike wasn’t the best experience, but we had an umbrella so it could’ve been worse. The views on the way up and the top were great you could see the whole city.

After the top we walked back down and made our way to the royal mile to meet dad. We ended up stopping at an Italian restaurant called Gordon’s (it was recommended by Jim, my dads caddie from Kingsbarns). I got a calzone and it was HUGE. I ate maybe half of it.

After eating my dad wasn’t feeling great so he went back to the Airbnb while my sister and I walked around and explored the city. The royal mile is really cool, it looks like it’s straight out of Harry Potter (JK Rowling lived here), the architecture is awesome! We stopped at the Giles cathedral, the Scott’s monument, the castle, and the national museum.

After walking around we made our way to the meeting point for the Edinburgh underground tour. The tour took us under the streets of Edinburgh to the vaults which were originally built as store rooms for the shops above but later abandoned when they realized water would leak in when it rained and ruin anything in them. Also supposedly the vaults are haunted. The guide had a ton of ghost stories about the vaults and would jump out of places to scare everyone.

After the tour we walked back about a mile to the Airbnb to meet up with dad. We hung out at the Airbnb for a while then Jamie and I walked to a nearby Turkish restaurant for dinner. We had hummus and shish kebabs, it ended up being a ton more food than we expected, but it was really good! After dinner we went back and relaxed at the Airbnb before going to bed.

Day 11

The next morning I woke up early around 6:30. I drove with my sister to the airport so she could drop me off and then drop off the car. My flight was at 9 and the car rental opened at 8 and you weren’t allowed to drop the car off after hours for some reason. The Edinburgh airport was kind of a pain. They charged you to drop someone off and then took forever to check in and check my bag even though the airport was basically empty. The flight to Dublin was pretty uneventful everything went to plan and we landed on time…then the fun began.

So I had called United the day before to make sure my connection from dublin to Chicago was okay, it was only a 50 min layover and United actually called me twice saying I needed to call them back about my connection. Well the lady I talked with said it would be no issue, that was a lie. After landing in Dublin it turned out I couldn’t just walk to my next flight and check in. I had to exit through immigration and get my passport stamped, then go downstairs to check in at the United desk. At the desk they told me the boarding was closed, but luckily they gave me the tickets anyway and I sprinted through security and then through a second passport control and ran the rest of the way to my gate. I swear this was the farthest possible gate in the airport. Somehow I arrived justtt before they closed the gate and was able to get on the flight. Unfortunately, as I would find out later, my golf bag wasn’t so lucky.

My flight from Dublin to Chicago was smooth. I had a 4 hour layover in Chicago so my mom came and picked me up. We ended up getting lunch and hanging out at the house for a few hours before she took me back to the airport. I finally arrived in Savannah around 9:30pm.

Overall it was an awesome trip! I’m glad my dad and I were finally able to go! Looking forward to the next one!

item.title: Morocco 2021
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded: Another last minute trip! We were originally intending to go to Turkey for this trip, but due to some changes with our flights (they switched us to a 48 hour + travel time) we decided to call an audible and go to Morocco instead (Thanks again Covid)! Coincidentally my sister and her friends were already planning a trip to Morocco so we're joining up with them. The switch wasn't without it's own drama, less than 24 hours before our flight the government of Morocco suspended all flights from the UK, Germany, and Netherlands. This caused my sister and all her friends to have to rebook their flights so that they connected from Istanbul and Becca and I happened to be connecting in Amesterdam so we had to rebook our flight there too so that we had a layover in Paris instead...what a mess. Anyway... Here's the map of where we're going: [googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1tBheLb95qlDZ_OAVC8cFFGUrsSxU89_6&w=640&h=480] And our rough itinerary (the beginning part of the trip we're doing as a guided tour so that we don't have to drive) Day 0 Thursday Oct 21st Fly SAV to Casablanca depart ~2p EST Day 1 Friday Oct 22nd Arrive ~2:30pm local (Jack and Becca), ~11pm (Jamie) Explore the city: Hassan II Mosque & sacred heart cathedral Stay at Hotel Relax Airport, Casablanca Day 2 Saturday Oct 23rd Tour starts: Drive to Chefchaouen (5 hours) Explore Chefchaouen in afternoon (Known as the blue city) Stay Chefchaouen Day 3 Sunday Oct 24th Morning in Chefchaouen, Drive Fes (4 hours) Stops along the way: Volubilis & Meknes Stay Fes Day 4 Monday Oct 25th Day exploring Fes (guided tour included), See tanneries Stay Fes Day 5 Tuesday Oct 26th Drive to Merzouga Desert (8 hours) Stops along the way: Ifrane, Azrou, Midelt, Ziz Valley, Camel trekking in Sahara Stay Merzouga (Sahara Desert camp) Day 6 Wednesday Oct 27th Camel ride out of desert, drive to Dades Gorge (4 hours) Stops along the way:Tinghir Gorge, Todra Gorge, Dades Gorge- Stay Dades Valley Day 7 Thursday Oct 28th Leave Dades Valley, drive to Marrakech (6 hours) Stops: Rose City, Ouarzazate Stay Marrakech Airbnb Day 8 Friday Oct 29th Explore Marrakech, Hot Air Balloon Ride Food tour of market, Cooking class, tons of other nearby stuff Stay Marrakech Day 9 Saturday Oct 30th More Marrakech activities: Quad Biking, Walking tour Stay Marrakech Day 10 Sunday Oct 31st Fly home Marrakech 7am Arrive SAV ~11pm

item.title: Day 1 Casablanca Arrival
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We left Savannah Thursday after work connecting in Atlanta. On arrival at the airport we had to check in at the Delta desk because we booked the flight through KLM (it was randomly $100 cheaper to book through them instead of Delta). At the desk the agent told us our flight was cancelled, for some reason she thought we were still booked through Amsterdam, I guess they didn’t get the update from KLM that we changed it. It took like 30 min for the agent to get it all sorted out and confirm us through Paris. On top of that the security line was ridiculous! Luckily I have pre check and was able to get through in less than 5 min but Becca had to wait an hour to get through! Thankfully we got to the airport super early, Becca barely made it to the gate right when we were boarding.

The flight to Atlanta was uneventful and the flight from Atlanta to Paris was great we each had a complete row to ourselves and we’re able to lay out and get some good sleep. On arrival we had a small anxiety inducing moment when our KLM app said that our flight was cancelled!! We went to the Air France desk and they told us the flight was not cancelled but our booking was?? The agent had no clue why but he was able to put us back on the flight and since we had a long layover (arrived at 7:45 departing at 12:30) we had plenty of time to figure it all out and get to our gate. In short, the airlines need to get a better system!

The next flight Paris to Casablanca was a quick 2-3 hour flight. We also learned that my sister and her friends were denied getting on their flight because they didn’t have COVID PCR tests (supposedly the rules change that morning, however all of the government websites and even the airline website said no test was needed if you’re vaccinated…super frustrating!!). They ended up having to book a different flight and will be getting in a day later than us and will need to drive on their own to meet us in Chefchaouen. Once Becca and I arrived, we grabbed the free shuttle to our hotel ~5min from the airport. The room we got was HUGE it had a living room, bedroom, and 2 full bathrooms.

After we settled in we went back down to the lobby to catch a taxi to the airport. It was around 5pm and the drive to the city took about an hour. Our first stop was the old Medina, a covered market that sold random stuff clothes, jewelry, etc. we were both hungry, but the only food we could find was boiled snails which didn’t sound very appetizing.

We spent about 15 minutes wandering through the market, it was like a maze with tons of winding streets. We met back up with our taxi who took us to the Hassan II Mosque, this is the tallest mosque in the country named after one of the old kings. It was really impressive and built right on the coast.

We walked along the coast by the mosque and tried this fried potato sliced kebab thing as a snack, it was pretty good and only cost like 60 cents US. After walking around we got back to our taxi who took us to an area called la corniche, there wasn’t much to do where we stopped but there were some nice views of the beach/coast.
