Once back at the taxi we tried to ask about getting food somewhere, but he had no clue what I was talking about (I even tried to us the google translate app but had no luck). He just kept telling us something that sounded like “cover fee” and showing us the number 23?? Btw they speak mostly French and Arabic here, which neither of us know. We ended up making a final stop at the Morocco mall (apparently it’s a big attraction). There was this massive aquarium in the middle of it that had a bunch of sharks, fish, and whale ray swimming around in it.

We ended up finding some food, nothing amazing as it was mall food. I ended up grabbing a burger and fries and Becca had sushi. Then after we both got some ice cream. After the mall we drive back to the hotel. We were both exhausted so we passed out quickly.

item.title: Day 2 Chefchaouen the Blue City
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 6:45 to get get packed and ready. We had breakfast down stairs at the hotel. It was a buffet style but because of COVID you had to tell the waiter what you wanted. Breakfast was ok, afterwards we grabbed our stuff and met our driver and tour guide in the lobby to start our drive to Chefchaouen. The drive was almost 6 hours, the city is all the way up north right across the water from Spain. At least the van was massive and comfy, it even had usb charging ports at every spot.

Our tour guide, Said, was very friendly! The first thing he asked us was if we believe in COVID 😂. Not sure what exactly he meant by that (his English is a little rough). We stopped once on the way at a gas station. Becca and I watched a few episodes of an HBO documentary about a cult church in the neighborhood she grew up in and I read a bit.

We got to the city around 2:30, we also got word from my sister that they all had landed and made it into Casablanca! We checked into our hotel and they served us a welcome tea and showed us to our room. The hotel is a Riad which is like a big house with a court yard.

After settling in we went and ate some lunch at a nearby restaurant in the main square called Marisco. Becca and I both got the Tajine, which is like a pot roast served in a hot clay bowl.

The restaurant (and the city in general) has a ton of stray cats and there were a few surrounding our table trying to get some food. After eating we went across the square to the Kasbah, basically a small fortified castle. It cost $6 to enter and was kinda small, but it had a tower you could climb up to get views of the town.

The castle also had a little garden area in the center.

After the castle we decided to walk around the town and find all the recommended photo spots (there were a bunch of them). The whole city is painted blue and the town is like a little maze. It’s really cool!

There is also a bunch of elevation change in the city so not only are the streets winding all over but they’re also going up and down. After a few pictures of the streets we made our way to the top of the city and hiked to the atlas hotel which was on a hill just above the city. The views were okay but not as cool as the ones in the city.

After a few minutes we hiked back down to the city to take a few more pictures. On the way down we ran into a random herd of goats coming up the street.

One place we took a picture was a “paid set”. It only cost like $1 US so we decided we might as well do it.

After that we managed to somehow find our way back to the hotel (the GPS signal doesn’t work well in the narrow streets and half the streets don’t show up, so Google maps isn’t very helpful). There we took a little break before heading back out to hike to the Spanish mosque which was about 20 min away to watch the sunset and get some views of the city. On the way to the mosque we stopped at a crepería and I got a Nutella crepe, it was tasty!

We continued the hike up to the mosque. The sunset was nice and there were really good views of the city.

After the sunset we made our way back into town and explored (aka got lost) and eventually made it back to our hotel.

After changing (it was getting cold out) we went to the main square and found a cafe, hamas cafe, to get a snack and drinks. I had hummus and hot chocolate and Becca had tea and French fries. We sat in the very top of the cafe roof which had a nice view overlooking the square.

Right after we finished, around 9pm, Jamie and her friends all finally arrived! We met them all back at the hotel, they got unpacked, and then our guide met us and took us to dinner.

We went to a place a few minutes away called bab ssour , we all had different types of tajine and we also tried the goat cheese (what this town is known for, they’re also known for their hashsih according to Said 😂).

After dinner it was around 11pm, we made our way back to the hotel and went to sleep.

item.title: Day 3 Chefchaouen to Fes
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7:30, got dressed and ready then had breakfast downstairs in our riad. They gave us a ton of pastries and some tea, pudding, and egg omelet. It was pretty good!

After breakfast we walked around the city again with everyone so they could see it and get photos at all the cool spots. We took a bunch more photos and wandered around. Jamie and her friends are really into taking photos so we got a ton.

After exploring we hiked up to the Spanish mosque again then made our way back to the city to pack up and meet our tour guide to head to the next city, Fes.

We took a bus about an hour to a random restaurant for lunch. The food was good, I had grilled chicken and fries. They also had beer here which is uncommon because of the strong Islamic influence.

After eating we drove another hour to the volubilis ruins. These are ruins from the Roman Empire and supposedly are the largest Roman ruins outside of Europe. We spent some time walking through the ruins and taking pictures.

It was super hot and sunny out so we were glad when we got back to the air conditioned van. We drove another hour to a city called Mekenes. Here we stopped to see the Bab Mansour, which is essentially a really big gate to get into the palace

We also drove inside the outer walls of the gate and stopped at the Kara prison. The prison is a vast underground labyrinth that would hold 40,000 prisoners. They were fed by dropping food down the holes. You could look into the holes and see it was a long way down, at least 30-40’.

Supposedly if you could find your way out you gained your freedom, however it is thought that no one ever was able to escape. Apparently a group of French researchers tried to map out the prison in the 1990s and never made it back out.

We drove past the rest of the palace which was massive, according to our guide the King has at least one palace in every city and sometimes more than one. Also every palace prepares food for the king each day just in case he shows up. After getting past the palace we drove through the rest of the city and then continued on to the city of Fes.

We arrived at our Riad around 8pm and ended up getting dinner of the roof terrace. I had a meat and vegetable couscous that was really good.

After dinner we went back to our rooms to get some rest after another long day.

item.title: Day 4 Fes
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 8:20 and had breakfast at 8:30. It was similar to the previous day with a ton of pastries and an egg omelette. After eating we got ready and met in the lobby at 9 for our walking tour of Fes. Our tour guide was Jamal, who is from just outside of Fes, but randomly lived in Wisconsin so his English was really good and he had a tonnn of facts about the city and it’s history that he shared with us so I’ll try to include the few I remember.

For starters the medina was built to be economically diverse, the king did not want separate neighborhoods for rich and poor so they were mixed together. And in order to prevent people from flaunting their wealth no windows were allowed to the outside and no decorations, also when you opened the door to your house there must be a wall so that others can’t see inside so from the outside it’s impossible to tell the size of the house and this also makes all the streets/alleys (over 9,000 of them) look very similar making it very easy to get lost! There are 3 types of homes depending on size, a dar (smallest), a Riad, and a palace. Though the dars that we saw still looked huge!

After talking a bit in the lobby we went to the van and made a quick stop at the kings palace. There are 7 gold gates for the main entrance of the palace, but they’re really more for show. we also saw the old nearby Jewish street where they’ve been filming the new indiana Jones movie. This considered the moroccan bourbon street, this is outside of the Medina, hence all the windows.

Our next stop was up one of the nearby hills to a fort that had a nice panoramic view overlooking the city and the Medina. The medina is split into two parts by the river.

The next stop was a ceramic shop where they showed us how they make dishes and bowls out of clay. They also make clay tiles which they intricately cut, color, and create mosaics with.

Finally we made it to the Medina, our guide took us through the tight winding streets to show us a bunch of different districts of the Medina. There are no motorized vehicles in the Médina because of the small streets, so only donkeys and mules are used to bring stuff in and out. The districts are divided by what they produce, there’s a weaver district, carpentry, dying, jewelry, and tannery among others.

The first main area we walked through was the market which had all sorts of unique foods. They basically sell every part of an animal you could think of. They had a “Moroccan KFC” where you pick out which live chicken you want and they slaughter it and prepare it in front of you. They also sold goats and even camel meat!

After walking through the market we passed through the dying district and then went to a carpet co-op, this place was filled with all sorts of rugs it was pretty impressive. They also showed a demonstration of how they made the rugs. Of course after they tried to sell us rugs, no of us were interested but Alyssa was too nice and they really tried to get her to buy one.

After the rug shop we stopped to eat at another dar that was converted into a restaurant, the food was really pricey and it seemed like they took all the tourists here. I had the chicken pastilla, which was like a sugary pastry with meat inside. It was good but a little too sweet for me.

After lunch we walked to the weaver district. The girls were interested in getting scarfs which they had loads of. The shop keeper also tried to convince me to get one by showing how it could be used to make a cool turban 😂.

After getting the scarfs we walked to a madrassa, this is basically a religious high school with a mosque in the back. In order to get in you need to memorize the entire Quran! This madrasa used to be a trash dump actually but the prince decided to convert it into a beautiful madrasa. This was done to prove to people that “you can turn garbage dump into a beautiful mosque” (a common saying in Morocco). The reason he did this was because he had married a prostitute for one of his wives and wanted to convince people she was beautiful despite her past. Also randomly our guide also told us an in detail story about his circumcision when he was 5….it was really strange and not sure how it came up I guess it was something about the culture😂.

After the madrasa we walked to our last stop, the tannery. The tannery is just outside of the Médina. When you walk in they give you mint leaves because the smell is pretty bad (they use pigeon droppings for the ammoniac acid to clean the hides) after a while though you get used to it and it’s not that bad. They had all sorts of leather goods, apparently goat leather is the best type. We didn’t buy anything but of course they had us try on stuff and tried to sell us.

After the tannery we got back on the bus to make our way back to our palace hotel. We rested for about half an hour before heading out to the super market to get water and snacks for the next couple days. After that we went to a nearby restaurant our guide recommended called cinema diner. The food was decent, I tried the camel burger which really just tasted like a normal burger and I also had a milkshake which was pretty bad (it was really liquidy). After eating we drove back to our hotel and hang out on the balcony before going to bed around 10.

item.title: Day 5 Driving to the Desert
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up and had breakfast at 7:30. It was the same breakfast as the day before. After eating we got packed and loaded up into the van to start another longgg day of driving (8 hours in total). We drove for about an hour and a half before stopping in the town of ifran, which is a “Swiss themed town” it really wasn’t much. We basically just stopped for a quick bathroom break and then continued on.

The next stop was a little further along just on the side of the road there were tons of monkeys that you could feed peanuts to. They were really funny and really liked the peanuts!

After the monkeys we stopped in a town about halfway for lunch. There wasn’t much notable about the town. I had a “taco” for lunch but it was really more like a mix between a burrito and a panini. It tasted good though!

After lunch we continued on and made one final stop before our destination for another toilet break in the town of Edfu. Known as the gateway to the Sahara. We drove another hour from there to Merzouga where we proceeded on camel into the desert.

The desert was really cool with two MASSIVE dunes. We stopped the camels about halfway to camp to watch the sunset and sand board down the dune. The dune was tiny so the sand boarding wasn’t that great but it was still fun. We got a ton of cool pictures with the camels and the sunset.

After sunset we continued on the camels to the camp. We had some tea and snacks and then dropped our luggage off in our tents. The tents are really nice and all have their own bathrooms in them.

Afterwards we had dinner in the main dinning tent. It was a bunch of different dishes with the main one being chicken. After dinner we sat by the campfire while our hosts played a variety of drums and instruments. It was a good time they were all super into it and made us dance along. After the festivities we walked a little outside of camp to look at the stars. There was lighting in the distance which was added a cool effect.

After we went back to the tents to sleep!

item.title: Day 6 Merzouga to Dades Valley
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 7 and walked a few minutes outside of our camp to watch the sunrise at 7:30. The sunrise was really nice.

It was a bit chilly in the morning but was warming up quickly. After the sunrise we had breakfast in the dining tent, which consisted of a bunch of pastries and an omelet again. After eating we got packed up and then took the camels through the desert back to the car (about an hour away). Of course we took more pictures with the camels on the way. Jamie, myself, and Becca were on the back of the line and at one point along the way Jamie’s camel (along with ours) came detached from the group.

Back at the van we loaded up our luggage and then drove to another nearby town to ride dune buggies in the dunes. The ride was pretty fun but they made you follow the guide of course who went kind of slow. I got yelled at a few times to slow down going over the dunes. On the top of the dunes we took a bunch of pictures.

Becca drove for a little while to the top of another dune and then our buggy broke down. The whole tour you could tell it was struggling to stay running and it finally gave out on the side of a dune. They ended up having to call someone to bring us another buggy. They were definitely holding out on us because the replacement buggy was wayyyy nicer and more powerful.

After dune buggying we got back in the van and drove about an hour and a half to stop for lunch. The food was okay I had a chicken kebab, Becca had a chicken tagine that wasn’t very good.

After lunch we got back in the van again to continue on to our next stop the Tondra valley gorge. We stopped at two panorámica of the city that had really cool views of the belly that was lush with palm trees and other greenery.

After a few pictures we made our way into the canyon and we’re dropped off to walk through it. The walls of the gorge were huge and kind of reminded me of the narrows in Zion. Unfortunately the weather went from really sunny in the desert to raining so the walk was a little cold and wet. Near the end of the gorge there was a cool built in climbing trail up the rock face. I climbed a little way up but no one else wanted to go so I went back down.

After our little walk through the gorge we jumped back into the van and drove another hour to the dades gorge where we were staying the night. The drive was a bit slower, because of all the rain the roads were getting washed out by flash flooding. At a few points it was almost like we were driving through a river!

Our hotel had a nice view of The Valley. We had the customary tea and then got settled into our rooms. Dinner was around 8:30 and was a few courses consisting of soup with bread, meat rice and vegetable platter, and fruit. The meat was really good! After dinner we talked with Siad about the plans for tomorrow and then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 7 Dades Gorge to Marrakech
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7:30 and were greeted with a nice sunrise over The valley. We are a quick typical breakfast at 8:30 and then Jamie, Becca, and I drove up the road for a quick hike through the gorge. The other 3 in our group weren’t interested in hiking so they just slept in and waited at the hotel.

The hike was really fun, it was a really tight slot canyon/gorge that had some difficult parts you had to maneuver around. A few points you had to wedge yourself between the walls to avoid going through the shin deep water.

We made it about halfway down the gorge (which is a loop) and then turned around since we didn’t have enough time for the whole loop. On the way back we took a short cut and had to cross a river. Said ended up trying to build us a small rock bridge to help get us across without getting our shoes soaked 😂.

After crossing the river we climbed up to the van and then made our way back to the hotel to get the others and then continue on towards Marrakech. We drove for about an hour before stopping at the “Moroccan Hollywood” in Ourzazate. The place had tons of different movie sets where they filmed over 400 movies and TV shows including Gladiator, Game of Thrones, Cleopatra, Ben Hurr, and a ton more. The guide was really funny and even filmed some scenes for us 😂.

After the movie set we drove shortly to another stop to get some lunch just outside Ait Ben Haddou. For lunch I had kefta (basically a meatball with different meat mixed together). It was good!

After lunch we walked across the street to cost the kasbah, which is the term for a fortified village or castle. The village was perched on a hill in the middle of the oasis riverbed. The actually filmed a lot of the fighting scenes from gladiator right in front of the village.

After hiking back down we returned to the van again for another drive up through the Atlas Mountains to Marrakech. We made a stop at a nice panoramic vista at the top of the pass and then a final stop for the bathroom before finishing the drive to Marrakech.

Arriving in Marrakech we said our goodbyes to Said and our driver Ibrahim and then walked with our Airbnb host to our Riad inside the Medina. The Medina was very nice and modern. After settling in we decided to try and find a grocery store, unfortunately the first store we tried to get to with google maps didn’t exist so we ended up walking all the way across the maze of the Medina to a Carrefour where we got some groceries.

After making it back to our Riad we ate and went to bed. Another exhausting day!

item.title: Day 8 Marrakech
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 8 and made some scrambled eggs with cheese, tomato, and mushrooms for breakfast. After that we had a pretty relaxed morning in our Riad. We ended up leaving the Riad around 11 to go explore the Medina. Our first stop was Jemaa El fna, the main square in the Medina. To get there was about a 10 minute walk through the souks (markets where they sell various goods).

The square was pretty massive there were tons of stands selling juice or food. There were also people with monkeys and snake Charmers. We didn’t take any pictures with them because we heard they will aggressively hound you for money if you do. Jamie downloaded some information on the square and gave us a brief “tour” around the square.

The next stop was just down the road to the Koutoubia mosque. This is one of the oldest mosques in Marrakech with a huge minaret and some gardens around it. We couldn’t go in the mosque but we took some pictures and walked around.

Our next stop was the Saddiens tombs. These sounded cool but it was pretty underwhelming. Basically a courtyard with some intricate rooms you could look into and a bunch of graves scattered around. I would probably skip this in the future (I cost about 70 Dirhams to enter which is only ~$8 US but kind of a lot for Morocco).

After that we tried to navigate to the badii palace. A road was closed which threw us off but after some wandering around we were able to find it (the entrance was not obvious at all). These were more like ruins of a palace. We ended up looking inside the gate briefly and decided to skip it since there was another palace we wanted to see next that was supposed to be more beautiful and didn’t feel like paying the 80 dirham entrance fee.

Next we walked to the Bahia palace. Which was only a few blocks away (we had a much easier time finding the entrance). This palace was pretty expansive, but it’s not what you typically think of when you hear palace. Basically it was a bunch of big courtyards (I think 3) with rooms around them. It was okay nothing I would’ve been sad to miss.

After the palace we stopped for lunch, first we went to a place just outside the palace entrance, but while waiting to order we found another nearby place online that had a lot of good reviews so we decided to leave and try that one instead. The restaurant was called henna cafe and they had hummus surprisingly (we have struggled to find any here) and some gluten free options which is why Becca was excited to go. I ended up having the Moroccan version of a burrito which was good!

After lunch we walked back to our Riad. Jamie and her friends needed to get a PCR test for their flight (since they were connecting in Italy) so they left to go do that while Becca and I relaxed for a bit and then went for a quick walk to explore the area around our riad before they came back. I was able to somehow find my way around without a GPS this time!

When everyone was back we ended up cooking and eating dinner at the riad. Becca and I made a curry chicken with rice and the others had pizza in the oven. We all hung out on the rooftop terrace and played some uno. Becca and I went to bed early because we had to wake up early the next day. Overall a nice less hectic day!

item.title: Day 9/10 Marrakech and Home
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today Becca and I woke up at 5:30 and got picked up for a hot air balloon tour! They picked up another group and drove us ~30 minutes outside the city to a camp where they gave us some tea/coffee while we watched them inflate the balloons.

The balloons were inflated and we all loaded up. Our basket was fairly large and held ~16 people comfortably. We got up in the air just as the sun was rising. You could see the Atlas Mountains landscape and other hot air balloons flying around. It was really fun!

We ended up flying for an hour and getting up to 1,150 meters (the max is 1,500 so you don’t hit any airplanes landing at the nearby airport). We landed in an open field just off the road. They actually were able to maneuver the balloon when we got close to the ground and land it onto the truck trailer which was pretty impressive.

After jumping out they took us back to the camp for a quick breakfast and then drove us back to the Medina. We were originally supposed to pay by credit card but the tour guide reallyyy wanted us to pay another way. We ended up trying PayPal and that didn’t work. Eventually I just wired the money and he paid the fee (it was a bit of a pain). We walked back to our riad to meet the rest of our group. We had a quick lunch and then Becca and I walked to the tannery district (not as impressive as Fes) and to one of the main Medina gates (east of us) then we met back up with the others north of the medina at the Jardín Majorelle.

The garden was just that basically a big garden, it was cool but surprisingly expensive for Morocco (~$13 US). We walked around for 45 min and took some pictures. The place had lots of rave reviews on google and was a “not miss” but for me it was a bit overhyped.

After the garden (which was just outside the Medina gates) we walked across the street to the spa (also known as a hammam) that we booked the day before. hammams are very typical in Morocco basically every neighborhood has or had one. Usually they’re public and divided by gender but the one we went to was a bit fancier.

Becca and I ended up getting a traditional black sand scrub in a steam room and then getting a massage. The scrub was a bit awkward because they kept opening up the door to get in and out and the door led to the main hall which made us very visible to passerby’s. That said the scrub felt really good and it was kinda gross how much dead skin came off! The massage was also good, not as strong as I was hoping but they never are.

After the spa we walked back to the riad (it was about 1.4 miles away). At the riad I took my covid test which was negative (yay!). Becca and I had booked a food tour that met at 6 that in the main square so we walked there and met our tour guide, Abdul, and other member in our group who was a lady from Iceland (she was visiting her niece who married a Moroccan man and has 4 kids here!).

The food tour was really fun we had a bunch of stops. At the first stop we had tangia (different than tangine) and sheep head! The tangia was good! The sheep head was interesting…it all mostly just tasted chewy. We tried all the different parts of the head: the toungue, the cheek, and the eyeball! The eyeball was kinda gross because you had to dig it out with your finger and it was really slimy mushy, but it didn’t taste that bad though! We ate everything with just our hands, that’s the traditional Moroccan way, they don’t use silverware according to our guide. Also apparently they eat sheep head in Iceland because the lady we were with acted like it was no big deal and she really liked the tongue.

The second stop was an olive shop where we tried a bunch of different types of olives. I’m not a huge fan of olives but these tasted good. Our next stop was a soup and pancake shop. The soup was a tomato based soup with noodles that tasted really good. Then we got a pancake that was made with onions and spices that was also tasty. Unfortunately Becca couldn’t eat the soup or pancake.

Our next stop was a small little shop that had little meat patties and bread to make into a small sandwich. Our guide asked us to guess what the meat was, we had no idea we guessed basically every animal and it was all wrong. It turned out it was anchovies, never would’ve guessed it, but they were surprisingly good!

Next stop was a doughnut shop they make the dough 12 hours in advance and fry it and put honey on it. They were pretty good!

After that we went through a back alley to a “restaurant” that made corn based cuscous, the best in Marrakech according to our guide. It was really good! The restaurant has been run by the same lady for years, there are no signs, it’s not on a map or google, there’s no menu, you have to call in your order ahead of time and she’ll go get the ingredients in the morning and cook. She’s known as the mother of the Medina according to our guide.

After the couscous we continued walking through the Messina and made a stop in a random door to see where they heat up the public hammams. They keep the fire going all day to heat the water and steam and they also will cook the taginas here! Our guide said that this guy will burn anything for you if he likes you haha.

Continuing on we stopped in another small door and saw where they make a lot of the bread for the Medina. They have a huge oven and take dough from all the shops and cook it. They can tell who the bread is for based on the cloth and tray that the dough comes in.

Our next food stop was a small snail stand in the market. Snails are a typical cheap snack for Moroccans, we had seen them in some other cities too. You pull the snail out with a toothpick to eat it or you can suck it out. They were pretty slimy and salty but they weren’t too bad! Kind of reminded me of mussels but softer.

Our final stop was a pizza store. We didn’t have pizza here though just smoothies and cookies (some that Becca could eat). I had the mixed fruit smoothie with milk and Becca had the avocado smoothie which was surprisingly good. I don’t think they use ice for the smoothies so they were more like a juice consistency but still yummy.

The tour ended in the main square. Our guide helped set us up a ride to the airport for tomorrow and then we made our way back through the Medina to our riad. Jamie and co returned shortly from dinner we hung out for a bit and got all packed and ready for our trip home tomorrow.

Day 10

Today we woke up at 4:30, got ready and met our ride. They walked to meet us at our riad and then we walked with them to the car (parked a few blocks away since cars can’t fit in the streets by our riad). The aiport was ~15min away, getting through security to the gate was fairly easy. We spent the last of our Moroccan dirham on some snacks for the flight. Our first connection was Paris, we got there earlier enough to get on an earlier flight back to Atlanta. The ticket agent originally said Becca could switch for free but it was going to cost me $1,000 haha, obviously that was wrong and he eventually was able to switch us both to the earlier flight (arrived ~2.5 hours earlier in ATL) after about 30 minutes. The flight to Atlanta was also easy, it was a pretty empty flight so we had a ton of space. When we landed (just before 6) we were hoping to catch the earlier flight back to Savannah at 7:20p instead of 10:55p. Because I had global entry I was able to zip through passport control, switch my ticket to the earlier flight and make it through security again and all the way to the new gate in time....Becca however did not have global entry and it took her literally 2.5 hours to get to through the passport control line and to meet me at the gate!! So sadly we missed the early flight so we had an extra 3.5 hours at the airport. It was honestly lucky we got the early flight from Paris because if we didn't I'm not sure Becca would've made the 10:55 flight (last flight to Savannah for the day). We ended up making it back home around 12:30am, unpacked a little and then went straight to bed.

Overall it was a really fun trip! I highly recommend checking out Morocco, it's a really unique country filled with a huge variety of landscapes with tons of fun activities. As always I'm super grateful to be able to take these fun trips with my family and friends. Time to start planning the next one!

item.title: A Week in Cabo
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Little delay in posting this but better late than never! After hanging out with my Family for Christmas 2021 I went down and met Becca and her family in Cabo. Here’s a quick recap of the trip:

Day 1

Luckily I was feeling fine and tested negative for Covid twice after my sister tested positive for Covid on Christmas day and potentially being exposed. My dad drove me to the airport in the morning (it was somewhat busy, but with precheck I got through security in two minutes). The flight from Chicago to Cabo San Lucas was direct which was nice and only took about four hours and 45 minutes. Luckily the flight went off without a hitch, a ton of other flights were getting canceled because of airline employees coming down with Covid. I arrived in Cabo around 12:30 PM Becca was already down here with her family so she came and picked me up from the airport. She drove us about an hour back to the Airbnb in Todos Santos, north of Cabo. The Airbnb was really nice however we had to quarantine from everyone else because I was exposed. It ended up working out nicely because we got our own private room. At the Airbnb I took a quick dip in the pool which was really cold and then we walked to the beach which was literally 100 feet away.

At the beach I went for a quick 3 mile run to see the north end of the beach where there were a bunch of shops and surfers. On my run back I met back up with Becca and we walked back to the Airbnb. We then drove to a beach farther north that’s a popular surf spot for professionals we watched the surfers and the sunset and had a toast with Becca‘s family for our engagement. The sunset had some really great views.

After the sunset we drove back to the Airbnb and had leftover prime rib rice and green beans for dinner Becca‘s family had this for Christmas dinner The day before. After dinner we hung out in our room and then went to sleep.

Day 2

Woke up and went for early morning run on the beach, this time I ran south and the sand was thick! I ran for about 4 1/2 miles so I was really tired after. I took a quick dip in the pool at the Airbnb to cool off. After, we packed up the car to drive out to a hike. On the way we stopped at cafe elix for breakfast. I had a breakfast burrito strawberry smoothie it was really good.

We drove 10 min further north to hike Puerto Todos Los Santos, an old port and beach only accessible only by hiking. The hike was really fun it was probably about 5 miles in total along the way we saw some seals sunbathing on the rocks and barking. We also went a little off trail at certain points in scrambled up and down the rocks as a shortcut which was fun.

The beach was super secluded and a small scramble across rocks to get to. We were one of the only people there and the water was really nice. We hung out for about 20 minutes and then decided to hike back to the car.

On the way home we stopped at barracudas, A restaurant Becca sister recommended, for lunch. We got a ton of food: Tacos, burritos, chips and guac, ceviche, quesadillas.

After eating we drove back to the Airbnb. We hung out at the beach for a half hour and then got ready to go to a restaurant called El Mirador about 20 minutes away. You could actually see where we hiked from the restaurant. Becca and I were way too full to eat so we just had drinks and watched the sunset, unfortunately it was a cloudy day so the sunset was not very good, but there were still good views. After sunset we drove back to the Airbnb and hung out in our room before going to sleep.

Day 3

Today we slept in till around 8 AM Becca wasn’t feeling too great she thinks the sushi she ate a few nights ago cause her stomach to have problems. Plan was to do a snorkel with whale sharks and sea lions tour along with a picnic at Balandra beach. However it took some (a lot of) convincing to get Becca to go because she was feeling so bad, but eventually she caved and decided to give it a shot. We drove about an hour and a half to the city of La Paz which is on the opposite side of the Baja peninsula, the gulf side. When we arrived we parked near the La Paz marina and waited for our tour guide to arrive. The guide arrived a little later than planned around 11:15 and shortly after we were on the boat heading out at 11:30.

The boat ride out of whale sharks took a longgggg time, but the experience was worth it! We were so close to the whale sharks and they were huge, around 30 feet long, it was insane. We swam with them three separate times for probably about 5 to 10 minutes each time.

After snorkeling we got back onto the boat and drove again a long time to swim with the sea lions. All the sea lions hung out on one big rock that we snorkeled around there were a bunch sleeping in the water because they’re mostly nocturnal and there were others that were swimming around and some that were sunbathing on the rock itself. We were pretty close probably about 20 feet away but not nearly as close as we were to the whale sharks.

We also saw a bunch of fish and coral reef. After snorkeling around the small rock we got back in the boat and rode a short trip over to Balandra beach. This is considered one of the most beautiful beaches in all of Mexico. We also saw a famous mushroom rock that is what the beach is known for. On the beach we had a small picnic of tamales and chicken salad croissant. We hung out for probably about 30 minutes to an hour and got to explore a little bit of the beach and then got back on the boat and made our way back to the La Paz marina.

We returned around 4:30 PM and got back to our car and started to drive back to our Airbnb. For dinner we ended up eating some tamales that Caroline and Robbie picked up from the farmers market.

Day 4

Today was a pretty relaxed day. We woke up and went for a walk down to the north end of Cerritos Beach. We walked a little bit on the volcano rocks on the point. There were a ton of surfers in the water so we watch them a little bit from the point as well.

We made our way back to the Airbnb and hung out there for a little bit we saw a whale breaching which was really cool. For lunch we had leftover steak and cheese sandwich. After lunch we drove back up to the north end of the beach and rented a surfboard to try and surf. Apparently the lessons we took in El Salvador didn’t pay off because neither Becca nor I were able to stand up once lol. To be fair the waves were really rough and breaking really hard, also the board we had was much less stable than the normal boards we trained with. After surfing we stopped for a quick bite of ice cream on the way back to our car and went back to the Airbnb to get ready for dinner.

Before dinner we drove to a beach north of Todos Santos to watch them release baby sea turtles into the ocean. The sunset was really nice and then afterwards is when they let the sea turtles out. There was only maybe two dozen turtles and it was very dark so it was really hard to see them. Overall it was somewhat underwhelming.

After the sea turtles we went to a restaurant called Briquetta. The food was really good I had the short ribs and Becca had a grilled octopus. Also the restaurant was really cozy and interesting, there was a table inside a boat! The only problem was the portion size was really small.

After dinner we went to a an ice cream shop in Toso Santos that was next-door to the real, fake Hotel California. That’s right it has nothing to do with this song but the Eagles sued them because they were pretending to be the hotel the song is based on, in reality there is no hotel. Ice cream was really good I had brownie and chocolate peanut butter. Afterwards we drove back to the Airbnb and went to bed.

Day 5

Today we woke up kind of early for breakfast I had cereal avocado toast and eggs. After breakfast we packed up and got the car loaded and drove Becca‘s parents to the airport for their flight home. Becca and I were staying another two nights in Cabo. However we can check into the hotel until four so we decided to go do a bungee jump at a nearby extreme park. We almost didn’t do it at first because they wouldn’t give us the online discount since we were booking it at the park, but as we were about to leave they conveniently changed their mind and decided that they would give us the discount. The jump was really fun very similar to the one I did in Costa Rica where you jump from a gondola that is suspended above the canyon.

After jumping we drove downtown and tried to find a spot to park to do a hike that would take us to lovers Beach and the famous Cabo arch. However, we were unsuccessful in finding a parking spot so we ended up driving to the resort. We were about three hours early but the hotel let us check in anyway which was awesome. After we got settled in our room Becca and I went for a walk down the beach back towards the main marina. Speech is way more crowded and filled with people trying to sell you anything. On the way back we stopped at a restaurant called cocos you Camerons where we had some beef tacos for an early dinner.

After we ate we made our way back to the hotel as it started to rain. We ended up making some drinks at our room and hanging out in the hot tub for an hour or so. After the hot tub we went back to the room and hung out the remainder of the night (we’re lame) from our balcony we watched the show put on by the hotel (it was the greatest showman musical with a bunch of dancing). We barely made it to 10 local time to celebrate the Savannah new year and then promptly passed out!

Day 6

Today we woke up around 8, after lounging around the room for a bit we took our COVID tests. Of course there was an issue (this time with the test supposedly being expired), but after a minute of arguing the lady changed her mind and allowed me to use the test (it was negative). After we made our way down to the beach to take a water taxi over to lovers beach. After talking to the front desk we haggled the water taxi guy down from $20 to $12 and made the short hop across the bay. As a part of the shuttle service the boat driver gave us a quick tour showing us a few of the rock formations, most notably the famous arco (sea arch), and then dropped us off at lovers beach around 11:30.

Directly across from lovers beach (on the pacific side) is divorce beach (lol). We spent some time exploring, the beach was really nice with tons of grate views. Both beaches are really only accessible by boat but there is a way to climb over some rocks to get to a few of resorts further up divorce beach, so of course we climbed over them and walked down the beach.

This area looked way nicer and we kicked ourselves for not booking the resort we looked at that was on this beach. On the walk down the beach we also saw a baby sea turtle making its way into the ocean, super cool!

After exploring we climbed back over the rocks and had a snack on lovers beach.

After resting I wanted to explore a bit more we saw a “cave” and I also hiked up one of the rock faces onto a ridge that had good views of the beach. Unfortunately I couldn’t hike much farther on the ridge because there were a ton of signs saying private property and a barbed wire fence. After coming down from the ridge we hung out at the beach until our water taxi picked us back up.

The taxi was supposed to come at 3 but it ended up being closer to 4, luckily we weren’t in a hurry. After we got back we had dinner at the sports bar restaurant at the hotel and hung out in the hot tub before going to bed.

Day 7

Today we woke up early around 5:15 am to get packed and drive to the airport. After getting gas we left the car in the parking lot (per the instructions of the sketchy guy Becca rented the car from) and made our way to Savannah. Overall no issues getting home, we had one stop in Dallas and made it back to Savannah around. Another great trip to close out 2021 and kick off 2022, looking forward to what this next year brings!

item.title: Bolivia 2022 🇧🇴
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Heading out for another trip down to South America to visit Bolivia's famous salt flats and the worlds most dangerous road (aka Death Road)! Becca and I are traveling with Pat and Sarah again on this trip. Flights to Bolivia are not convenient at all, we have TWO overnights flights with a full day layover in Lima Peru. Here's the map and rough itinerary for our trip:

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1As0AeVY8HZBbxFDBmb-EFtjTRzi86SAc&ehbc=2E312F&w=640&h=480]

Itinerary:

Day 0 Friday March 25th
Depart for Bolivia
SAV-ATL-LIM Overnight Flight

Arrive in Lima 5:30am
Bike Tour
Paratrike (powered paraglider)
Walking tour
Huaca Pucllana ruins
Food tour or cooking class

Sagarnaga Street

Plaza Murillo
Jaen Street

Cable car tour
