item.title: Day 0/1 Lima, Peru
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today (Friday 2/25) we got everything packed and made our way to the Savannah airport for our flight at 8pm. At the check in desk we had an “exciting” start to the trip apparently they were required to physically see the credit card I used to book the flight. We’ll just my luck I used a card that I didn’t have with me… honestly I didn’t even know which card she was talking about. I should also point out that absolutely no where in the delta emails or anywhere that I could possibly find online did it say you needed to bring the credit card to check in…apparently I was “just supposed to know”. After frantically searching the various apps I figured out it was my fidelity card and logged in to show her the statement and even a virtual version of the actual card…and after all the it STILL wasn’t good enough 😫. The only option was to get the actual card or buy a new ticket. Luckily she was able to do a one for one trade and refund the one credit card while honoring the ticket price and charging the travel credit card I had with me. QUITE the ordeal and a whole lot of stress! Worst of all once again Becca was right in wanting to get to the airport way early than I did 😊.

We got through security and to the gate with no issue so I figured we were clear to go…false. I decided to call LATAM airlines (the company operating the flight from Lima to La Paz) to try and check in, delta wasn’t able to give us our tickets for that flight since they weren’t operating it. Well, shortly after talking to the LATAM agent on the phone he says “something looks weird”. It turns out they refunded my flight and never repurchased a new one! I was able to go to the gate agent and after more stress and 45 min on the phone everything was sorted out and Becca and I were checked into the Lima-la Paz flight…phew talk about a cluster! I hung up with the LATAM agent just as our plane started to board.

The first flight was a quick uneventful hop to Atlanta airport. We landed around 9 and had to go all the way to the opposite side of the airport for our next gate. Fortunately we had plenty of time. Our second flight (Atlanta to Lima) left at midnight. My seat was right next to the bathroom door and right in front of a bulkhead…not ideal. I was sitting next to people that were going to Peru as a big group of 120 from the same company. The flight was just over 6 hours, I got very little sleep

We landed around 5:30am. Getting into the country was a bit of a pain, apparently you needed a declaration form, no one told us, so we had to fill out this glitchy online form that took forever, but eventually we were able to make it into Peru.

We took a ~30min cab ride from the airport to the hostel we booked in Miraflores. Even though we weren’t staying the night we wanted a place to store our bags and take a nap, well worth it! since nothing was open we relaxed until 8:30 and then ate breakfast at the hostel. I had the pariwana breakfast and pancakes.

After eating we took a quick Cabify (Perus version of Uber) to a nearby ruins called Huaca Pucllana. Unfortunately because of COVID you needed a reservation to see the ruins. Luckily the gate guard let us in anyway to see the ruins (we just weren’t allowed to go up them.

After the ruins we walked ~1 mile to the coast to try paratriking, basically a tri-cycle with a big fan on the back attached to a parachute 😂. The place on google maps was wrong so we called an found out where they were flying today (~2.5 miles north). We jumped in another cabify and made it there for the flights.

It was a really cool experience! We each flew for about 10 min up and down the stunning coast.

After paratriking we took another cabify over to a main food court/shopping center area on the coast called Larcomar. We walked around and explored for a minute. The plan was originally to walk (~2 miles) to the old town of Barranco, however we were all tired so instead we took another cabify.

At Barranco we saw the bridge of sighs, which is apparently a really old bridge in Lima, not super impressive but the area was really cool. We also walked down to a mirador (lookout) to see the coast which was filled with surfers.

Next we walked back up slightly past the bridge to a restaurant called ayuhusca, which was recommended for it’s pisco sours (famous Peruvian drink). We all tried it except Pat who ended up trying Inca cola (another Peruvian staple) it’s a cola that tastes like bubble gum. The girls ended up wanting to eat there while pats and I decided to go to a Chinese restaurant closer by our hostel.

The Chinese restaurant was called chifa 8 dragones. It was pretty good and the server was super helpful even though he didn’t known much English. We also tried some chicha morada (a famous purple corn based drink) which wasn’t very good.

After eating we walked back through the park to our hostel to meet back up with the girls and nap. Along the way Pat saw some art he liked (and ended up going back and buying later) and we also ran into a show about saving Mother Earth. The show was cool because it was in a mini amphitheater and tailored to kids (meaning easy to understand Spanish).

Back at the hostel we napped for about 2 and a half hours until our cooking class guide came and got us at 6. We walked back across the park to the “kitchen” which was on the 7th floor of some apartment building at the south end of the park.

The cooking class was fun! It was just the four of us, the guide, and the chef. We ended up making was a potato dish (can’t recall the name) and lomo saltado.

After cooking and dinner we packed into a cabify with all our luggage (apparently cabify plus doesn’t mean anything besides an extra ~5sol charge) and drove ~40min to the airport. Getting through security was uneventful for Becca and I but apparently they were concerned Pat stole some significant artwork so they had to open up what he bought and verify that it was ok 😂. We ended up going to a random gate and resting.

Around 11:30 we woke up and made our way to the actual gate (it wasn’t assigned yet when we arrived). There they were checking everyone’s documents. We found out that you needed some special COVID insurance to board. Thankfully Becca was able to figure it out and buy some random COVID “insurance” online and we were able to board. We finally left around 1am…another rough night for sleeping!

item.title: Day 2 La Paz
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
The flight from Lima left around 1am and took ~2 hours plus and hour time change. I slept most of the flight (no one was in the middle seat next to me) and we arrived in La Paz around 4am. The immigration process took FOREVER they needed to scan a copy of our passports and itinerary before we were allowed to pay for the visa on arrival which was $160 USD. After finally getting out of the airport around 5:30am.

After a 30min cab ride to our hotel we unpacked and took a much deserved nap. We woke up around 10:30 and Becca and I decided have some coca tes upstairs on the deck of our hotel which had great views of the city. After we went for a short walk around the city to explore. The hotel is really central so we walked down the witches market and Calle srganara both were kinda dead since it was Sunday I guess.

We also walked to plaza mayor de San Francisco and saw the San Francisco basilica. There was a mass going on inside so we just popped in for a quick look.

After seeing the church we walked back up to the hotel and then head out again to meet a friend of a friend, Maria for some lunch at a restaurant called La tranquera. The food was really good we ordered two big plates of meat that had everything from steak, chicken, and pork to blood sausage, intestine, cow tit, and liver! We tried everything but I think the steak was my favorite.

Next Maria took us on an informal tour of the city. Because the city is so mountainous the easiest way to get around is to take the gondolas. They also give you a really nice view of the city.

We went from the centro area to calacoto which is much lower than the city. We walked around there and stopped at a local coffee shop before heading back up to the city to a restaurant near our hotel for some food and drinks.

I had a chicken burrito and a drink called te con te. It’s a popular drink here, basically tea with a brandy type liquor called singani. After dinner we walked back to the hotel for an early bedtime to catch up on some sleep.

item.title: Day 3 - La Paz
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 7 am and Becca and I went upstairs for breakfast a little after 8. Breakfast was eggs, fruit, and coca tea. After breakfast we made our way to a nearby tour shop to try and find some fun activities for the end of our trip, we decided on hiking and ice climbing.

After the tour shop we went back to the hotel to meet pats and Sarah to catch a taxi over to The Valley of the moon. It’s a cool area about 30 minutes away with a small hiking circuit and really cool rock formations. The whole loop took about an hour and we took a lot of stops for pictures.

While hiking we got a message back from one of the rock climbing tour guides so I called him and we were able to set up some climbing for today at a spot right by valley of the moon. It was going to take the guide 2 hours to get there so we ended up going to the nearby town, calacoto (close to where we were yesterday) for a quick bite to eat. We settled on another meat place. Along the way I tried a sáltena from a street stand (Bolivian version of the empeñada) it was delicious!

The restaurant was called boca y vaca, I had the trout and Becca had a steak, both were good.

We had to kinda rush to finish eating in order to make it to the rock climbing place at 1. We met Juve (our guide) and had to scale a fence to get to the rock.

We climbed about 4 routes in total of varying difficulties. I even was able to lead climb the easiest one. Overall it was a super fun day, we also learned that Becca is a really good climber!

Our guide was pretty tiny and had a difficult time belaying Pat 😂.

We finished climbing around 5pm and got a taxi back into town. We made a quick stop at the tour office to pay for our hiking and ice climbing and then walked ~10 minutes to do Urban Rush, basically rappelling face first down a 17 story building!

To start we got dressed in fun costumes, I was Superman Becca was Spider-Man and pat and Sarah were unicorns lol.

After some training on a practice wall we were ready for the real thing! The scariest part was the start when you have to lean forward face dirt and trust the the rope is going to hold you while you look straight down at the ground…nerve racking!

Once you were perpendicular to the wall you would sort of hop/jump while letting out the rope with your hand to progress down the building.

About halfway down the wall they had a free fall where you let go of the rope and jump while the guide catches you with the safety rope.

After the urban rush, we rushed back to our hotel to pack, shower, checkout, and taxi over to the bus station for our overnight bus to the salt flats. We ended up getting to the station at 8pm (per the request of the guy from the company), turns out the bus wasn’t leaving until 9pm so we had some time to kill. Loading the bus was an ordeal to we probably didn’t leave La Paz until 10pm. The bus itself was really nice though! Dinner, good legroom, the seat lean wayyyyy back!

item.title: Day 4 Uyuni Salt Flats
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
The overnight bus was pretty nice, not the best sleep but at least 10x better than an airplane. We arrived in Uyuni around 7 am and met a guide who took us to a nearby breakfast restaurant called nonis. I had the americano breakfast it was pretty basic, toast, eggs, and ham. After breakfast we went tot the tour office to pay for the tour and start the tour. We ended up paying in both USD and Bolivianos since we were able to pay for the travel visa with credit card. However they rejected some of the USD because they were imperfect (small tears, etc)

Apparently the tour wasn’t going to start for another two hours so we walked around the city to pick up some water. The city is super small and I think only exists because of the salt flats. The tour wasn’t very good at communicating not only was there a bit of a delay to the start of our tour but also we were told we needed to consolidate our luggage because “it would be too heavy”? So Becca and I combined into her pack, which is massive. Honestly the few clothes we took out wasn’t even close to the amount of weight we added in water.

Anyway, we finally start the tour 30 minutes later than we were told and the first stop was the Uyuni train graveyard. Basically a big area where all the old trains were left to rust away. Because of this you’re able to climb all over the trains and take a bunch of fun pictures. We hung out there for about 45 minutes and had a good time taking lots of pictures.

After the train graveyard we made a quick stop to try on boots (I needed the largest pair they had available of course). There were a bunch of cute puppets hanging out while we tried on the boots.

After getting the boots we loaded up the car and made our way to colcahni, the town is the entrance to the salt flats and had a bunch of shops and things. Becca and I ended up getting an ornament made of salt that was in the shape of the salt flats. Also basically everything here is made of salt the buildings, chairs, etc all salt.

After 30 minutes we made our way back into the car and finally drove out onto the salt flats!! This was seriously one of the coolest places I’ve seen. The salt flats are soooo huge, it’s literally a dried up lake. It almost looks like you’re in a tundra of snow but instead of snow it’s all salt…all of it. Our first stop was a little water hole in the salt that was bubbling up, looking at it, you’d think it was hot but it was actually really cold. We sat around it and soaked our feet in the cold salt water for ~15min. Apparently it’s good for you.

Next we drove to the Dakar monument…we’ll almost there. Our guides stopped short and had us walk about 15 minutes so they could drive ahead and set up lunch, kinda weird but whatever, hiking in the salty desert was kinda cool. The Dakar monument is a big monument I think for some race they do on the salt flats (our guide was more of a driver and didn’t tell us much). It was a cool looking monument though! There were also a bunch of flags in the ground, but sadly no American flag. After taking a few pictures we had a picnic lunch with everyone in our group (two cars with 6 people each).

Lunch wasn’t great there was some kind of beef that was superrrrr dry (I had to dip it in ketchup). There was also a veggie pasta, quinoa, and an omelet. I also tried one of the Uyuni beers I picked up in town, it was pretty good.

After eating we took some time to take some perspective pictures. We literally took hundreds of pictures today. This area was dry Salt on the ground (as opposed to a small layer water). Here are just a few of the pictures we took.

After taking pictures we drove out further, to a better more remote spot to take even more pictures.

Our guide also helped direct us for a bunch of funny group pictures.

The next stop was to the flooded area of the salt flats where the water is a few inches deep which causes a really cool reflection and even more good photo opportunities. We took a bunch more photos here.

The guides set up the picnic tables with wine and some snacks to watch the sunset. It was legitimately the best sunset I’ve seen, really cool colors.

After the sun went down we made our way back to colchani to get to our salt hotel. On the way the guide stopped and let us take some pictures of the stars. The salt hotel is pretty cool, again literally everything is made of salt from the floor to the walls, beds, etc. Becca and I took a quick shower and then went to get dinner with everyone. Dinner was much better than Lunch, it was salchipapas basically cut up hotdogs with fries and some other sauce and toppings. After dinner we went outside to stargaze some more then made our way to bed after a long exhausting day.

item.title: Day 6 Hot Springs, Rocks, & Canyons
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up super early to leave at 4am. It didn’t help that I had some stomach issues (from the spaghetti?) and woke up at like 11:30pm. Also I checked my blood oxygen level with my watch and hit a new record 79% 😧 (we were at ~15k feet) Anyway, we drove around 45 minutes to the sol de mañana geysers. They’re called geysers but they were really more like steam vents.

They were cool to see, we took a few pictures and made our way another 30 minutes to the next stop the auguas termales de polques (a hot spring). It was around 5am and it was still dark so the stars were out in full force and it was awesome to see. We hung out in the hot spring for around and hour and a half to watch the sunrise.

After the hot springs we changed and went to the nearby building for breakfast. Today was pancakes they were pretty decent.

After breakfast we waited a bit longer, Pat, Sarah, Becca, and I played a quick board game. Then we loaded up the car (around 9am) to head towards our next stop.

We drove about an hour and a half, passing out through the park checkpoint, to get to the green lagoon. The lagoon looked mostly white near us but farther off you could see it looked really green. Apparently when it’s windy it’s looks more green. The reason the water is green because it contains arsenic, copper, and silver…don’t drink it!

After pictures we loaded up for our next stop. We stopped at a town called mallku for lunch. There were a bunch of lamas around the town. Lunch was pretty bad it consisted of rice, canned corn, and the most un appetizing fish I’ve ever seen. When we asked what type of fish our guide said “normal” lol. We joked and asked if it came from one of the nearby lakes (they’re all filled with metals and other nasty chemicals) and our guide said maybe hah! I had some stomach issues the night before so I didn’t have any, but Becca was brave enough to try some. I think the guide realized we didn’t like the fish so he got us some ham and bread to eat sandwiches. After dinner the guide also brought us some beer for “dessert” and then we loaded up the car and left for our next stop around 12:45

The next stop was a rock formation that looked like a camel. The resemblance was actually pretty good! We were able to climb on top of the camel rock and take some cool pictures before driving another 10 minutes to the next stop.

This stop was called “Italians lost” it was a bunch of tall rock formations that were fun to climb. It got its name when two Italians went climbing here and lost their passports so they went to the nearby village for help and the whole village came and helped them find their passports. We ended up climbing one of the bigger formations, it was a really fun and easy climb! We left around 2 pm to head to our next stop.

We drove for around 30 minutes to the trailhead of hidden lake. The hike to the lake was only like 10 min and then at the lake there were more rocks that formed a sort of canyon around the lake that was really fun to climb around! There were a bunch of lamas on one end on the lake on the grass.

After hanging out at the lake we loaded up in the car and drove to a canyon called the anaconda canyon because the river that runs through it looks like an anaconda. We walked out on one of the rocks, took some good pictures of the canyon, and enjoyed the views.

We loaded up the car again to head back to Uyuni to catch our night bus back to La Paz. On the way we made a quick pit stop again in San Cristóbal. We arrived in Uyuni around 7pm, we picked up the bags we left at the tour office and then went across the street to a restaurant that had showers. We quickly showered, repacked and walked about 3 blocks to the bus station. I was finally able to catch up on most of my blogs (the reception was terrible on the tour) and then we made our way back to La Paz leaving a little after 8pm.

item.title: Day 5 Laguna Colorado and more!
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 6 to get breakfast, turns out breakfast was actually at 6:30 (our guide has trouble keeping time lol). Breakfast consisted of toast m, eggs, fruit, and tea. Pretty basic but we weren’t expecting much. After breakfast we showered, got all packed and ready to go (we were supposed to leave at 7 but ended up leaving at 7:30). We made a quick pit stop back in Uyuni for the drivers to pick up our lunch and then started our drive south.

The first stop was about 1.5 hours away called San Cristóbal, we basically just here to pee and there was a market if you wanted a snack or something. I did find a cute dog to pet so that made it worth it. Then we drove another hour or so in the car to a place called valle de las rocas. It was a huge area with tons of volcanic rock scattered everywhere from the nearby volcano. It was a really unique landscape and we had about 30 minutes to explore and climb the rocks. The rocks were really grippy and fun to climb, we took a bunch of pictures.

After climbing we loaded back into the car and drove another hour to a lake nestled in the mountains called lake cunyapa. It was cool because it had a bunch of pink flamingos in it.

We stayed for about 15 min before getting back into the car and driving another 30 minutes to stinky lake (thats literally what it’s called lol) to eat lunch. We arrived around 2pm This lake was also surrounded by mountains and had a ton more flamingos! Probably like 1000 of them and apparently the lake is stinky because of all the flamingo poop.

Lunch consisted of some chicken, pasta, veggies, and an orange. After eating we hung out and enjoyed the view for a bit before getting into the car and driving 20 min to deep lake

Apparently it’s actually not a deep lake but it’s called that because it’s lower in elevation than the surrounding lakes. We also learned that the white stuff in the lakes is actually borox.

After some pictures we drove 45 minutes to stop at the Solie desert. It’s the highest and driest desert in the world. Apparently it only rains once or twice a year, I decided to help out and water the plants 😁. It was super windy so we didn’t stay long just some pictures before getting back in the car.

We continued driving through the desert and made a stop to feed the viscasheta, basically desert bunnies with long tails. They like cookies so we feed them a few and got some cute pictures.

Our next stop was the stone tree, a really cool rock formation. We stopped for some pictures and climbed a few of the rocks (it was prohibited to climb the stone tree rock). It was super windy here as well.

We got back in the car yet again and made our way about 45 minutes to the border of the national park where the laguna colorada is at around 5:30pm. We had to pay the 150 boliviano entry fee and have our passports checked to enter the park. We drove a little ways past the entrance to see the laguna colorada (colored lagoon), the lake gets its red color from micro-organisms that live in the lake.

After the lake we drove to our hotel around 20 minutes away. It was a pretty basic accommodation, the shower didn’t work quite right but at least our bed was comfy. For dinner we had a spaghetti without meat, it had a mushroom tomato sauce. We also had a soup that was pretty good. After dinner we went outside to look at the stars, with such little light pollution you could see everything, it was awesome! We went to bed pretty early since we decided to start early tomorrow (at 4am).

item.title: Day 7 Death Road Mountain Biking
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Sorry for the delayed posts, wordpress decided to run out of space with it's free version, I guess it was bound to happen after nearly 200 posts filled with tons of pictures. The paid version of wordpress is now like $200 a year :(. Luckily I ended up figuring out a work around when I got home, it involves hosting the photos on imgur and linking them to wordpress to save space (it's a bit of a pain with the extra step, but better than paying $200 a year!).

The overnight bus from Uyuni arrived super early at the La Paz station (4:45am instead of 6:30am). We were originally supposed to be picked up for our bike tour directly from the bus station, but because we had so much time we decided to take a cab 5 min to our hotel instead (staying at the Quantu hotel again) to drop our bags off and got some sleep. We were able to get a quick nap in, woke up around 7, and were picked up by our tour guide in the lobby at 7:10.

Our tour guide, Nelson aka Nel, was super energetic and fun. If you ever go to ride the death road I highly recommend him (he works for Altitude). Our group was the 4 of us, a Brit named Thomas, a German guy (who already rode the death road 20 years prior), and A girl who just graduated named kiara, they were all super nice and good company and lots of random funny and deep conversations. We made our way by bus about an hour and a half up into the mountains north of La Paz to the start of the tour (almost 5000m elevation). We got suited up with all our gear, took some pictures, and got the safety explanation from Nel.

The first part of the road was the new road which was paved and had a decent amount of traffic. We were able to go pretty fast in this part because the road, for the most part, was smooth and well maintained. I believe this section was about 30km total which we broke up into multiple stops so the group didn’t spread out too much. At this altitude riding was actually kinda cold, and between stops I had to try to warm up my hands because they were freezing! One thing I really appreciated was they didn’t make us all ride together in one group, everyone was able to ride at the pace they wanted/were comfortable with and meet up at each stop.

After the paved section of the road we ended at a tunnel which had a small paved detour rode around it to get a taste of how the bikes handle on a much much bumpier road (what we were about to be riding on exclusively). Then we loaded up the bikes and drove to the real death road about 10 minutes away. On the way there our guide played the song highway to hell 😅.

Once at the start of the roads we unloaded the bikes again and got another safety explanation and a small history lesson. Bolivia has been in 3 wars, all of which they lost (Brazil, Chile, and Paraguay I think). During their war with Paraguay they had a lot of prisoners of war which they put to work to build the road which, according to our guide, is why the road is so shitty haha. This part of the road was much tighter and way more bumpy than the new road (as expected).

This section of the road was also much longer, I have no clue how long it was, but we broke it up into much more sections than the paved road. There were a few scary parts on the ride down, Sarah ended up riding in the van for a bit (which was following us) because she wasn’t comfortable biking (honestly though the van was probably scarier than the bikes!). There were a lot of cool stops with good views. Unfortunately at the higher altitudes it was much more foggy and difficult to see but as we got lower and lower the clouds disappeared and the temperature got way warmer.

We ended up biking through waterfalls and rivers which was fun. I ended up riding up front with the guide and we were whipping down the mountain fast, it was a blast! At one point we had to stop to remove some boulders from the road so our van (which was trailing us) could make it past.

We stopped at the San Juan falls and saw the memorial for the last accident on the death road, it was a tour bus filled with Israeli tourists that fell off the cliff (which is why the memorial is in Hebrew.

Our next stop was for a snack at a small viewpoint/hut. Thomas had a drone and was able to take some cool pictures and video with it. The hut was right by a part of the road that had been “washed away” by an avalanche. It was a little too rough to ride so we ended up walking that section.

There was another section called tooth breaker that was steep and known for people braking too hard and flying over their handlebars and breaking their teeth. I didn’t think it was that steep to be honest, but it was still fun to ride. Throughout the whole day Thomas ended up popping 3 tires and our guide Nell popped one also!

We finally made it to the very end of the road around 3pm and celebrated. Definitely sore wrists and forearms from bouncing around on the bikes. Nel told us some of the crazy stories he’s had while giving tours in the death road. Afterwards they drove us to a nearby hotel called Dos Rios for a “buffet” lunch, however it wasn’t really buffet because the lady was super stingy with giving out the meat (chicken and beef). Overall the lunch was good After lunch we made the long ~2.5 hour drive back to La Paz to get dropped off at our hotel.

Back at the hotel we showered and ended up eating a quick dinner at the upstairs restaurant. I had a burger and salchipapas (Bolivia version of poutine).

item.title: Day 8 Pico de Austria
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7am, grabbed some food from the breakfast buffet, and met our guide and driver in the hotel lobby at 7:30. We left La Paz and drove about 2.5 hours into the mountains north of the city in an area known as Condoriri (named because the mountains resemble a condor). At least half of the drive was on a super bumpy dirt road out into the mountains.

When we finally arrived, the area was very picturesque and had lots of wild life, alpacas, lamas, donkeys, and rabbits. The hike was basically all uphill but the views were fantastic. We passed by some small waterfalls early in the hike.

After about 45 minutes we made a quick stop at a small refugee next to a lake that our guide told us had a bunch of trout and salmon in it. We took a quick break for some coca tea and then continued on the hike.

As we hiked higher up the mountain the terrain became less dirt/plants and more shale rocks. It took us around 4 hours to reach the summit at 5,350 m or 17,552 feet. Becca some had stomach issues on the way, but was able to push through it and make it to the summit a few minutes behind me. The views from the top were awesome we could see the whole valley from where we parked all the way to lake Titicaca. Becca and I had went ahead of Pat and Sarah so we waited at the summit for ~30 minutes until Pat and Sarah arrived. We took some more pictures as a group and enjoyed the views for a few minutes before starting our descent back down the mountain.

Becca and I descended faster so we arrived back to the refugee first. At the refugee we had lunch finally, it consisted of guacamole (which was delicious), pita bread, tuna, cheese, juice, and coca tea. After we finished eating we walked the rest of the way down back to the van, we made it just as the sun set and the temperature started to drop. There were some little kids from the nearby community by our van so we gave them some candy, they were really shy but grateful. By the time we left it was dark. There were some stubborn llamas sleeping in the road on our way out and the driver had to get out and shoo them off the road so we could continue.

We finally arrived back at the hotel around 9pm, we ended up eating some dinner at the upstairs restaurant again since we were too tired to go out and get something else. Pat and Sarah took their COVID tests since they were leaving tomorrow (a day earlier than us). We said goodbye to them and went to bed.

item.title: Day 9 Ice Climbing & Cholitas
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7am to get ready and went upstairs at around 7:30 to eat breakfast. We ate the typical eggs and toast again (breakfast was free with the hotel). After breakfast we walked down to the tour agency shop to get fitted for ice climbing gear. The tour shop was not open when we arrived (at 8am), our friend Maria was joining us for the climbing and was at the café next door to the tour agency so we met her over there. After ~30 minutes we were able to connect with the tour company and get our gear all sorted out before loading up into the car for another car ride.

The ride out to the mountain, Huyana potosi took forever. We left the city around 9am and didn’t get to the base camp until almost ~12. It didn’t help that we had to wait at least 30 minutes for our guide to 'pick up food for us' (He claimed it was difficult to find gluten free food). It also didn’t help that our van got stuck on one of the muddy roads on our way out to the mountain 😂.

Our driver seemingly had no idea what to do when your car gets stuck in the mud. He decided that the best course of action would be to try and keep revving the car and spinning the wheels as much as possible to try to get us out (of course this just made the van get more stuck). Finally he listened to me and we put a bunch of rocks and whatever else we could find under the wheel while us (and some passerby's who stopped to help us) pushed the car out of the mud.

Near the base of the mountain we stopped at a famous cemetery for miners and there families. Apparently there was a pretty big mine out here that had an accident and killed a lot of the workers.

We finally made it! At the base camp we opted to postpone lunch in order to get more climbing in (we were tight on time trying to make it to the cholitas wrestling at 4:30). We geared up in the base camp and started hiking out to the glacier.

The hike took about 45 minutes and at the glacier we put in crampons and learned to walk on the glacier with them. I had done this before during Cotopaxi but it was the first time for Becca and Maria.

After hiking up the glacier in crampons we made it to the ice wall to climb. Our guide first gave us a demonstration at a less steep area before we trained the more vertical wall.

The climbing itself was really fun! We all scaled the wall a couple times before it was time to head back to base camp.

We ended up leaving around 3:30 to try and make it back to La Paz in time for the cholitas wrestling show. The cholitas are the Andean women who dress in traditional clothes, they are usually in the street shops selling their goods (you can't mistake them). The wrestling match was basically a knock-off WWE show. It was hilarious and a bit hard to follow, but basically 5 cholitas were in the ring at one time all “fighting” each other. At a few points they even got out of the ring and were fighting each other in the stands!

After the show we were able to get some pictures with a few of the cholitas wrestlers.

Our driver drove us back to our hotel after the show. We dropped off our bags and then walked down to the cafe we were at earlier for dinner. It was a really neat restaurant with foods from all over the world. I had the Bali bowl and it was really good! After dinner we made our way back to the hotel to take our Covid tests. Of course there were issues with emed, but I was able to work around them and both of our tests came back negative :). We packed up our stuff and went to bed.

Day 10 Flight Home

We woke up just after 2am to catch a taxi (pre-arranged) to take us to the airport. We had no issues catching our 5 am flight to Lima. After a short layover in Lima our flight to Atlanta left on time. We knew there was an earlier flight from Atlanta to Savannah so when we landed we hurried to the Delta desk and they were able to get us on the earlier flight...or so we thought. It turns out we were just on standby for the early flight and after everyone boarded only Becca was cleared (there was only 1 seat left). So we ended up both staying and getting dinner together at buffalo wild wings before our later flight (about 3 hours later). We finally made it back to Savannah and back home around 11:30 pm, talk about a long travel day!

As always I'm forever grateful of the amazing travel opportunities and experiences I'm able to have with such awesome people. Definitely wish we had more time to explore Bolivia, but I think we were able to fit about as much as possible (and some!). For now, I need another vacation to rest! Until next time.

item.title: Acadia National Park 2022
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Here’s the quick overview of our long weekend trip to Acadia national park with Clint and Kate.

Day 0 (Thursday)

We left after work and got to the Savannah airport around 4:30. Everything was going smoothly, our flight arrived to Savannah on time and we even finished boarding early! We were all ready to leave…That’s when thunderstorms decided to pop up, localized literally right over the airport. At first I wasn’t worried because Savannah in the summer is notorious for quick afternoon storms and I figured it would blow over in 20-30 minutes tops (which happened the day before). Unfortunately today the thunderstorm lingered over Savannah and we didn’t end up leaving for 2 hours! Also after the weather had finally subsided our first attempt to take off was aborted! The pilots told us they had received some warning messages on the takeoff roll so they ‘debugged’ the issue on the taxiway. Takeoff attempt number 2 was successful! Unfortunately all of these delays compounded and we completely missed our connecting flight from Philadelphia to Bangor.

When we arrived in Philly (around 10:30pm) we had to assertively talk with customer service manager to get us a hotel voucher. After some back and forth (Becca was told on the phone by American customer service that they’d get us a hotel in Philly while the manager at the service desk in Philly told us they will not do that for a weather delay) she eventually relented and was able to get us a hotel that was about 10 minutes from the airport via shuttle. The hotel itself was pretty dumpy (0/10 would not recommend) but we were happy to have a bed to sleep in! We ended up finally getting to sleep around midnight

Day 1ish

Today we had some time to kill in Philadelphia before our flight to Bangor (at 1:30 pm) so Becca and I took a taxi to the city to see the sites in Philadelphia. I had previously visited for a wedding around 4 years ago but Becca had never been. Our first stop was breakfast near Washington square. I had bagels (which for some reason are really good in PA) at a small store called Knead’s bagels. I had a bacon, egg, and cheese everything bagel and a cinnamon cream cheese flaxseed bagel, both were delicious! Becca of course wasn’t able to eat bagels so she went to a restaurant across the street called pain quotidian to have an omelet.

After breakfast we walked over to the Independence hall to get a tour of the East wing Assembly room which is where they signed the constitution. The guide was actually really good and told the story leading up to the American independence, very inspirational!

After the tour we walked across the street to make a quick stop to see the liberty bell. It’s funny how small it is in real life.

Then we got a ride over to the Eastern penitentiary, which was the first penitentiary in the world (over 300 prisons were modeled after its system). Named penitentiary as the inmates were supposed to seek pentenance and become reformed after serving their sentence of solitude. The entrance came with a free audio tour and we spent about 30 minutes exploring the large complex. The penitentiary was huge and really interesting, it even held Al Capone for a period of time.

After the penitentiary we walked about a half mile to the famous Rocky Steps. Of course I ran up them and did the obligatory Rocky celebration. Becca wasn’t quite as enthusiastic and walked up the steps.

We were planning to check out Reading terminal next and grab some food, however we were running a bit short on time and were tired of lugging our bags around so we ended up taking an Uber to the airport (about 25 minutes away). Our driver was actually from Ecuador so we talked to him in Spanish on our way.

We got through security quickly and luckily our flight was on time and we made the short ~1 hour trip to Bangor where Clint and Kate picked us up from the airport. The drive from the airport to Acadia was ~1.5
hours. We stopped at Clint and Kates hotel so that they could check in
and then we drove into the park to the beehive trailhead to hike.

The hike was really fun! It was a short 1.5 miles and lots of scrambling and sections you had to climb iron rung ladders.

We rested at the top for a drink and to take in the views and then made our way down to the lake.

We continued the loop back to the car and then drove down to otter overlook which was at the point of the peninsula. We hung out there for a minute and then tried to drive back up to see the thunder hole only to realize that the road was a one way! So we had to drive all the way back around the park. We should have gotten the hint as the road was named park loop road. We ended up going back and parking in bar harbor. Since it was low tide we were able to walk across the land bridge to bar island that is inaccessible when the tide is high. While walking across to the island we saw a deer bolt down the sand bar as he was being chased by a small dog.

The others were hungry so they went back to the city while I hiked the bar island summit trail. It was a super short trail and the views from the summit weren’t great. I did see some more deer grazing in a milkweed field though which was cool.

I made my way back and met up with everyone in the park next to Geddy’s restaurant (there was a wait). We watched the sunset until they were ready for us.

Dinner was good we all had the lobster rolls (which was pricey $$). It was good, but overpriced for what it is in my opinion. After dinner we went to the desert mountain ice cream shop. The line was superrrr long (reminded me of Leopolds in Savannah). I had the sugar pill and Maine cream, it was really good. We finished our ice cream in the park across the street and then went to our airbnb to sleep

Day 2

Today we woke up around 6:30 to get ready. We ate breakfast at our B&B at 7 which consisted of a bagel, yogurt, and fruit.

After breakfast we got picked up by Clint and Kate and drove over to the east side (also know as the “quiet side” of the island. We started at Echo lake and hiked the Beech cliffs and Canada Cliffs trail. There were a few small iron rung sections but nothing too crazy. At the top the views of the lake were great, the whole hike took us just over an hour.

On the way back down the mountain we stopped at the lake to see the view from a different perspective. Echo lake is actually one of the few lakes that you’re allowed to swim in in the park. The others are restricted because the water is used to supply the town.

Next we went slightly up the road to the Acadia mountain trail head. This hike was another short summit. At the top we found some blueberries which we confirmed were edible with the other hikers on the trail, they were tiny but delicious! The views at the top of the mountain were again great.

On our descent the trail split in two, one to go back to the car the other to summit mount St. Sauveur. Becca and I still wanted to hike so we continued to the next summit while Clint and Kate took the path back to the car. More nice views at the top, this trail was also very lightly trafficked so we didn’t run into many other hikers.

Clint and Kate ended up driving to meet us at the flying mountain trailhead (where our trail ended). From there we drove a bit further down the east side to a lobster lunch spot called Thurston’s. It was a really cool spot on the water and you could tell the lobsters were fresh because you actually got to pick them out of the water tank!

Becca ended up getting the full lobster and I had the lobster melt, both were delicious. After the main course we shared some blueberry ice cream (Apparently Maine is also know for its blueberries).

After Lunch we went to the Bass Harbor head light house (a famous picturesque light house). It was right off the parking lot so no hiking required.

Next we made another quick stop up the coast to hike the ship harbor trail. It was a really flat coastal trail that was very flat and only about a mile long. There were some nice views of the water and some rocky pebble beaches.

Next we drove up to Long Pond to hike Mansell mountain. Clint and Kate were tired and ended up relaxing and waiting for us at the pond. The first summit was only about a mile.

The trail continued to another summit called litte Notch, more views of the lake.

There was a 3rd summit just off the trail, Becca didn’t want to hike up more so she waited while I hike ~0.4 miles up to the Bernard mountain summit.

There wasn’t much of a view from the top, but there was a log book that i signed. I hiked back down and met up with Becca and we continued down the mountain back to the pond to meet back with Clint and Kate.

Next we drove back to Bar Harbor. We walked to get drinks at a place called the Ivy Manor inn, it had an outdoor spot with Adirondack chairs and fire pits which were perfect to relax in after a long day of hiking (10/10 would recommend).

After a drink there we went across the street to a Mexican restaurant called Jalepenos to try their blueberry margaritas, they were surprisingly good! We also we to a place that we thought was a bar that was known for a large rocking horse…it turned out it was just a gift shop with tons of wood things and a giant wooden rocking horse :D.

Finally we made our way to a dinner spot called Aloha poke bowl. I got the house poke bowl and another blueberry drink. It was ok, definitely not the best poke I’ve had. After dinner we went down to the land bridge/sandbar again to watch the sunset. After sunset we went back to our B&B to go to bed, we have an early day tomorrow!

Day 3

Woke up early at 4:20 to go see the sunrise on Cadallac mountain. Clint and Kate picked us up and drove to top. There were tons of people at the top so we only stayed for 20 min, enough to see the sunrise.

The weather was good and we were already awake so we decided to go and do an actual hike. This hike was near the Jordan Pond called bubble rock. There were actually two peaks (north and south) and a large boulder which we assumed was ‘the bubble’ perched precariously on the edge of the mountain. Of course I had to climb it, but it took some help from Clint to get up.

After the hike we drove back to inn, on the way back we stopped at the Acadia national park sign for the obligatory picture.

We also made a stop at Jordan’s restaurant, a small breakfast place, fairly close to our inn. It was pretty good, but pricey.

After eating we got back to our inn and took a much deserved nap. We then ate second breakfast at 8:45 :D. This breakfast was smaller (and free) it consisted of bacon, egg, cheese on English muffin.

After eating we were picked up by Clint and Kate, they were tired from all the morning hiking so they decided they would explore the city and dropped us off at the trailhead for Champlain mountain. The hike was great, the trail was much less wooded so the views were awesome, the only downside was the sun was HOT. Unfortunately, one of the really cool iron rung trails that we wanted to hike, precipice trail, was closed due to peregrine falcon nesting season.

We hiked down the other side of the mountain (towards beehive) we were through hiking (instead of looping back) and planning to meet back up with Clint and Kate at sand beach.

We wanted to keep hiking a bit more and since we enjoyed the beehive hike we ended up doing it again. This time it was much more crowded. We ended up going up and back down the iron rung route (since it was quicker and more fun than hiking down the backside of the mountain).

Once we got down to the bottom of the beehive trail we walked a block down the road to the sand beach parking lot. We realized that we didn’t have any reception here and the place was packed. We figured Clint and Kate were hanging on the beach so we walked along the shore to try and find them without any luck. We ended up hiking up the road a ways to get reception and were finally able to get a hold of them. It had turned out that they weren’t able to find a parking spot so they drove around the island and back to the town to explore.

We ended up finding and saving a parking spot for them and they drove back to sand beach to meet us and hang out. We spent a few hours relaxing on the beach. I took a dip in the water…it was absolutely freezing cold!

After the beach we drove a few miles up the road to a place named ‘thunder hole’, which was supposed to be a natural blow hole in the rocks, however it wasn’t very active when we saw it unfortunately. It was still a fun place to climb around the rocks though!

Becca and I wanted to do one last hike so Clint and Kate ended up dropping us off at the nearby trailhead for Gorham mountain. The hike was a short 1 mile ~500’ of elevation trail. There was some fun scrambling and hiking under boulders on the way up. The whole hike there and back only took about 45min.

After the hike we met Clint and Kate back down at boulder beach (just a short walk from the trailhead). It was a cool beach with a ton of small boulders/large pebbles.

After hanging out for a minute we got back in the car and drove back up to Jordon pond for popovers - basically a muffin with ice cream in it. Becca wasn’t able to have one, because gluten, but she did eat some of the ice cream. Overall the popover was really expensive and I was unimpressed.

After the popovers we drove back to Bar harbor, changed and showered and then went to side street cafe for dinner. I ended up having a burger (I was over lobster at this point) and Becca had a GF lobster melt and we all had margaritas.

After eating we went back to the ivy manor again for drinks and to relax in the Adirondack chairs. When it was time for sunset we walked back up to the dock to watch.

Finally after a long day of hiking (I was exhausted just typing everything we did!) we made our way back to the inn and went to sleep.

Day 4

Today we slept in and ate breakfast at 8:45 - Finnish pancakes (basically an apple pancake) and bacon. It was delicious. We walked down in the town to some of the shops to find a Christmas ornament. We ended up getting a lobster. When we got back to the inn we packed and got picked up by Clint and Kate to drive to airport.

On our way to the airport we found out that our connecting flight from DC to Savannah was cancelled :(. We ended up talking to the gate agent in Bangor and he was able to get us a flight to Charlotte from DC and then a flight to Savannah. We boarded our plane confident we would make it back. Unfortunately the airlines had different plans. It turns out the flight from DC to Charlotte was going to be late because of airplane availability so there was no way we would make the connecting flight to Savannah and we would end up stuck in charlotte….not cool. We ended up talking to another gate agent in DC and he was able to get us on a flight from DC to Charleston and then American Airlines gave us a voucher to take a taxi from Charleston all the way to Savannah! (In case you don’t know its ~2.5 hour drive. I’d personally never heard of an airline doing that before, but I was just happy to be getting back to Savannah that night. In the end we made it back home around 9pm (only a few hours later than our original plan).

Unfortunately Clint and Kate were not so lucky (they flew Delta) and ended up getting stuck in Maine with the only available flight to Savannah from Portland (~2 hours from Bangor) the NEXT day. So they had to rent a car, drive to Portland, get a hotel, and then get back to Savannah a day later than planned!

Besides all of the travel hangups it was a great trip! We really enjoyed the hiking and hanging out with Clint and Kate. As far as national parks Acadia is a unique spot and small enough that you can really see the majority of the park in a short time. As always looking forward to the next trip!

item.title: Day 0/1 - Castle, Lichtenstein, & Austria
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We went tot the airport after work to catch a quick flight over to Atlanta and then onto Munich. of course it wasn’t as smooth as we hoped (flying never seems to be now). Our plane was delayed about 45 min, getting in late from wherever it was coming from. We boarded quickly and taxi out to the runway when our pilot said we needed to wait for the weather to blow through. Well that took at least 30 min so now our super cushy 2 hour connection became a “sprint through the airport as fast as you can and hope you make it before the doors close” connection. We ended up landing around 5:20 and our connection was supposed to leave at 5:50 (with doors usually closing 15 min before that).

Delta had already anticipated we weren’t going to make it and pre-switched us to another (worse) flight with a connection. We sprinted through the airport from A terminal all the way to the international terminal. I arrived at the gate around 5:40 to see the door closed :(. However, when I got to the desk I was told the flight was delayed and they hadn’t started boarding yet! (Would’ve been nice to know about that delta!). So thankfully we made our original flight, which was surprisingly empty, Becca and I each got a whole row to ourselves!

I mostly slept during the flight, we landed around 9:30am. Becca and I made our way out of the airport and picked up the car rental and then started driving to our first stop Neuschwanstein castle.

The drive took about 2 hours with some parts and the No speed limit section of the autobahn (I was able to get up to ~215 kph) which was fun. We arrived and found some parking and then hiked up to the famous bridge and viewpoint of the castle.

The castle and area in general was super picturesque and nice. The only issue was there were tonsss of people. We were already warned by our Italian friend that this week was a super busy holiday weekend in Europe.

On the way back to the car we stopped for a quick bratwurst snack and a quick picture of the lake and another castle.

After walking back to the car we hit the road again. We were originally planning to see linderhof palace, but because the traffic was bad we decided to skip it and head directly to Lichtenstein. It was only about an hour and a half away so we figured we might as well see it. Plus on the way there was a via ferrata (basically a rock climbing route with iron rungs you clip into).

The via ferrata (also know in German as klettersteig) was in a town of the boarder called Bergenz. The route was called Kanzle Klettersteig. We had some difficulty finding the start of the route but eventually followed some people and found it. We decided to do the easier route since it was our first one. It was so much fun! Climbing up the sheer cliff with awesome views of the city. There was a beach volleyball tournament going on in the city just across the river from us, too bad we didn’t have time otherwise I would have checked it out.

We made it through the hike/climb in around 1.5 hours and drove down to Lichtenstein. Originally we were planning to drove through Switzerland (because it was faste) but we learned the toll sticker required to drive in Switzerland cost ~$40! No thanks. In Lichtenstein we saw the capital of Vaduz and saw the church of st Florin, the castle, and the red house.

We ate an overpriced dinner at a place called the Burg. Si had a cáprese burger and a beer (the burger was actually pretty good).

I was hoping to do a short little hike to a view point and some castle ruins but we were running out of daylight and decided to start the drive to Imst, a town in Austria we were staying the night in. The drive took about 1.5 hours and went through some superrrr long tunnels. I was impressed by how extensive the tunnel systems are, I guess it’s easier then driving to build roads around them.

We made it to our hotel around 9:30 and unpacked then passed out for the night!

item.title: Day 2 - Austria to Italy
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7am, got ready and then had breakfast at the hotel. The breakfast was really good! All you could eat and they had a really fancy coffee machine that made delicious hot chocolate, seriously some of the best I’ve had. We stepped outside to enjoy the amazing views of the mountains while we drank.

After eating we got ready, packed the car, and drove about 30 minutes to another kletterstieg called Crazy Eddy. This one was a bit more difficult with some fun features including a wire bridge, spider chains, and of course great views the whole time! I forgot my gloves in the car and decided to not go back and get them (definitely don’t do that, the gloves are immensely helpful when gripping the cable).

We completed the route in about two hours. We drove a bit into the town and stopped to get some gas and snacks before driving onto Innsbruck to pick up Pat and Sarah. They had flown into Munich and then took the train to meet up with us.

From Innsbruck we headed south towards Italy. It was funny, crossing the boarded you had to pay a toll but included with your toll apparently were apples and water. The apples were very tasty! 10/10 would recommend Italian tolls.

The drive to our next stop, Orteisei (a small town), was about 1.5 hours. We attempted to find parking for the gondola to see Secceda ridge, after some trial and error we managed to find the right spot and took the gondola up to the top (the gondola was v expensive but worth saving 3 hours of hiking). The views of the ridge were amazing! No matter with way you turned you saw impressive mountains and cliff jutting out of the earth.

We hung out and hiked around the ridge a bit, I ended up climbing up to one of the peaks. On the way up I ran into a chill goat hanging out on the trail.

We spent probably an hour and a half at the top before heading back down to the car. It was around 4pm so we decided to drive about an hour to lago di carrezza, a “rainbow” lake with tons of myths and legends related to it. The lake was a bit underwhelming, I wouldn’t recommend going out of your way to see it.

We walked the small path around the lake and then had some gelato to relax before heading back to ortesei and our hotel. We checked in and dropped off our bags before heading to the restaurant next door called “tennis pizza”. Fittingly It was a restaurant with a bunch of tennis courts. The pizza was amazing. I had the “Vesuvius” pizza which had cheese, pepperoni, and a over easy egg! It was so delicious. They even had gluten free pizza for Becca! Pat ended up ordering a cheese pizza with pepperoni, apparently pepperoni is called “spicy sausage” in italy, and our waiter thought he wanted peppers 😂.

After dinner we went back to the hotel and played a scuba board game and then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 3 - Lagazoui Tunnels and Ferratas
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I worke up early, around 2am I guess the jet lag finally hit me :(. The plus side is I was able to catch up on my blog we ended up getting up around 5:40 to load the car and eat breakfast at the hotel.

The breakfast was an assortment of pastries, eggs, yogurt, fruit, and
delicious hot chocolate. After breakfast we drove about 30 minutes to the falzarego pass to park for our hike. The hike we were doing was called Lagazoui (pronounced “La-Gat-zz-why”). Luckily we ended up getting a spot on the side of the road right by the trailhead! (It did involve a tight squeeze and almost driving the car off the road into the gully).

We started up the mountain to the tunnels, on the way up we were a little confused about which way to head up as there were two different paths and we were trying to decipher a German website. Eventually we figured it out and made the right choice. About 30 minutes up the mountain through some switchbacks and we made it to the first set of tunnels.

The tunnels were super long, apparently they were built during WWI
when the Italians and the Austrians were fighting. They would mine tunnels into the mountain, hit daylight and course correct, which is why there are tons of holes poking out of the mountain in random places.

The tunnels were a super long labyrinth with small lookouts (where they mined the wrong direction), utility rooms, etc. It was super dark so we had to use headlamps the whole way.

We made our way to the summit and enjoyed the views. There was a
Refugio at the top where we had some food (I had a panini and apple strudle). Becca and I hiked to the summit (a short 10 minute hike from the Refugio) while Pat and Sarah rested.

After we got back we hiked down most of the way and then cut across the mountain over to the base of a via ferrata called Delgi Alpini. The hike down was a lot of steep shale and which was a pain, lots of slipping and falling. Becca, Pat, and I did the feratta while Sarah waited behind (she was tired from all the hiking and the difficulty of this feratta was fairly high). There was a slow group in front of us to start which took them forever.

The Ferrata took foreverrr, but was really fun, there were tons of scary
climbs and great views. We finally made it to the summit. We enjoyed
the views again and took some more pictures before making our way
back down to reunite with Sarah.

We hiked the rest of the way back down to the car, we got water which
was key because we were all out from hiking all day. From there we drove to our next airbnb (about 30 minutes away) in a town called cortina di ampezo. The parking was atrocious the airbnb host definitely lied about the onsite parking. We ended up parking in front of the dumpster. The airbnb was very 'authentic everything was super outdated and it smelled a little strange. Also the ceilings were super low. The good thing was it was only a block away from the Main Street of the town.

After we got settled in we walked into town to get some groceries. Becca and I ended up making some pasta (gluten free of course) with veggies and meat and some gelato for dessert. After eating we went to bed.

item.title: Day 4 - Tre Cime di Lavaredo
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early at 5am to get to Tre Cime di Lavaredo and hike. The weather forecast was looking bad, so we debated wether or not to postpone the hike till tomorrow but we ended up deciding to risk the weather in order to have more time tomorrow getting to Slovenia.

The drive took about 40 minutes to get to the park. The entrance fee was 30 Euro (a bit steep, but not bad split 4 ways). We drove into the park and up right next to the 3 peaks, there was a parking lot right next to the Refugio Auronzo. The trailhead to get to the other side of the peaks started right there and wrapped around them to the right. We hiked about 20 minutes before catching our first glance at the peaks.

We continued to hike up along the ridgeline heading towards the summit of Monte Paternokofel. It wasn’t long before we reached another set of tunnels and Klettersteig wire (we were loosely following this route). The views along the way were great, we were lucky the clouds and bad weather was holding off.

There was a steeper section of the feratta that involved some climbing that led us up to the summit of paternokofel. There was a cross at the peak as per usual. We were in the clouds while climbing up, but they cleared again when we reached the top and gave us some good views of The Valley below but unfortunately the 3 peaks were covered.

After resting and enjoying the views we made our way back down the other ridge of the mountain.

Sarah and Becca ended up following the correct path down through some tunnels and ferattas while Pat and I ‘created’ our own off piste route down the gulley of the mountain. It was a fun hike down but filled with tons of loose shale that would create mini rockslides as you rocked. Probably not the smartest route down, but we survived.

Pat and I stopped for a break at the bottom on a small crest near the second Refugio called locatelli to do some droning.

After droning we made our way to the Refugio to meet up with the girls. We had some sandwiches and hot chocolate while relaxing and enjoying the view.

After our break we started to make our way back to our car, this time we took the route around the north side of the mountain, which had more views of the peaks and the surrounding landscape.

We made it to the car about an hour later, we passed by a field filled with a ton of cows. After loading up we drove back to our airbnb in Cortina and walked around the town. We walked all the way up and down the Main Street, mostly window shopping. We found a place to eat but the kitchen didn’t open until 7pm so we sat and played a small board game while having a drink.

When the kitchen opened we got dinner, we all tried Spatzle and Candederli (basically dumplings) as an apetizer (they were recommended to us by our Italian friend Maria). I also had another pizza…when in Italy! Everything was really tasty!

After dinner we went back to the airbnb to hang out and then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 5 - Slovenia & Stoeska Vintgar 🇸🇮
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up relatively early and left our place in Cortina around 8am. We drove about 2.5 hours and made a stop at a granite pit off the main motorway to hike a via feratta called Ferrante di Ruffano. We were able to park right near the start of the feratta (only ~5min walk). There were some rock climbers climbing that were climbing near the start.

The Feratta was really difficult, Sarah and Becca both quit after the first pitch (and it’s a good thing they did, it got significantly harder!). Pat and I continued on. It was super hot and the rock face was extremely exposed so I ended up climbing fast to get to the shady spot and wait for pat.

The feratta ending up taking around 1 and a half hours, Pat and I made it back down and met up with the girls in the dry river bed below to have some snacks and do some more droning before heading back on the road.

We drove another hour to try and go to another via feratta, but it turned out you had to pay 20 euros to get in so we decided against it (we were only planning to stay for a short time anyway).

We continued on in the car and made a stop along the motorway for food for Pat and Sarah at a place called Maria’s diner. It was an American themed diner from 50’s and they had just about every typical American dish you could think of.

After they ate we got back in the car and drove to Stoeska Vintgar, known as the Grand Canyon of Slovenia. We didn’t pre-book tickets (we didn’t know you needed to) but luckily we were able to get online and get some last minute tickets so we could do the hike. Also we were able to get a good parking spot right near the start of the trail. It was surprisingly crowded, but since it was the end of the day I think we missed the main rush of people.

The trail was really nice and had a path built on the side of the canyon wall that followed the river. The views were great and there was a nice cool breeze through the canyon.

We stopped for drinks near the top of the waterfall. I tried the local crazy duck beer and a pastry. After resting we went to the bottom of the falls for a quick photo.

After seeing the falls we walked back above the gorge (they don’t allow you to take the same path back. Also the path back is mostly uphill so they try and get you to pay for a shuttle ride back to the entrance.

Once we got back to the car, we drove another 10 minutes to the hotel we’re staying at (in lake bled) called Villa Ana. The villa was a super old house (I think our host said the 6th one built on the late) so it was like living in a historical house with all the old furniture and everything.

After checking in we stopped at the bakery across the street, I tried this chocolate coconut ball that was really good. We walked to the grocery store to pick up things for breakfast and some snacks before going back to the villa.

Becca and I walked down to the lake and hung out on one of the small boats at the dock until Pat and Sarah met up with us. The four of us went to dinner on the main road at a restaurant called Central Bled house.

The food was good! I had the ‘Central Plate’ which was a variety of meat and dumplings and also tried the local beer.

After dinner we stopped at the nearby gelato store and then went back to the hotel for bed.

item.title: Day 6 - Lake Bled
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in for a rest day (Pat’s favorite type of day) and woke up around 8am to cook and eat breakfast in the hotel I had cereal, yoghurt, and bread with jam. After eating I went downstairs to check on pat and Sarah who were surprisingly also awake. Pat and I took the drone for a quick spin around the hotel (called villa Anna and one of the oldest on the lake).

After getting ready we slowly made our way down to the lake to walk clockwise around the lake ~6km. We walked a little ways and came across a boat rental shop. We rented an oar boat for a bit over an hour to paddle out to the island in the middle of the lake (Slovenia’s only official island).

The ride took about 20 min (i rowed). Pat took some cool drone footage of us on the lake. We docked at the small island and made our way up to the church (the only thing on the island). There’s an old myth that if you can carry your bride up the 99 stairs to the church then you will have a blessed marriage and fertility. Of course pat and I decided to not only carry Becca and Sarah on our backs but also race up the steps. It was a run race, we both made it to the top, I barely beat pat. People were cheering us, it was a fun time!

After running up the steps we took a quick and we’ll deserved dip in the lake. The water is super blue and refreshing!

We got back on the boat and circumnavigated the island before making our way back to the dock. I stopped and jumped in the water on the way back for another quick dip (rowing is exhausting and difficult!).

After getting off the boat we continued around the lake. We saw some people jumping and rope swinging off a tree into the lake so of course I had to try.

Next we made our way to a small beach that is know for its vista of the lake. We took some pictures of course.

After dipping in we hiked up to mala osjenica (a small mountain with a nice elevated view of the lake). The hike itself took about 30 min to get to the top and an uncountable amount of complaints from Pat about hiking during our rest day :). In my opinion the view from the top was well worth it!

We made our way down it was a bit less steep and more stairs than the hike up. We walked along the boardwalk of the lake and stopped at a nearby “beach” we laid out on the grass and took a refreshing dip in the lake.

We hung out for a while before going to the nearby restaurant. I had a blesjko pizza (lots of meat, veggies, and an egg) it was really delicious!

After lunch we continued walking down the lake and decided to hike up to the castle that’s on the lake the hike was quick and had some good views at the top (Pat was upset with all the hiking on our rest day). The castle cost 13 euro to enter and Becca and I weren’t that interested so we ended up walking back down to the lake to swim and relax while we waited for pat and Sarah to tour the castle.

When they got back we hung out at the lake some more and then eventually made our way to dinner. We went to a Thai place, I had the pad Thai and also tried the Slovenian cream cake (a “must try”) both were good!

After dinner we made our way back to the hotel, played a quick board game and then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 7 - Austrian Sky Ladder
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early, around 6 am, ate breakfast in the hotel. I had cereal and a yoghurt. We loaded up the car and left around 7am making our way to Austria to do the famous sky ladder klettersteig called Donnerkogel.

The drive took around 3 hours. We parked at a parking lot near the gondola and took it up to the hut (it saved at least an hour of hiking). Sarah decided she wasn’t going to do the feratta, so instead she did the hike on the back of the mountain to meet us at the summit.

Getting to the ladder wasn’t too difficult just long, it took us the better part of two hours on the via feratta (on mostly A, B, & B/C difficulty). There were some other people right at the start, luckily we were able to get on before them. We also passed a couple on the way up who were going really slow.

When we made it to the ladder I decided to go first, it was really fun! Unfortunately Pat wasn’t able to get the drone working while I went but Becca still got some good photos.

I ended up hiking back down (an alternate route) to take photos and drone footage (it worked this time) of Becca and Pat. The drone footage turned out really good! Unfortunately by the time pat made it up the ladder a huge group of people arrived so I decided not to do the ladder again. Also weather looked like it was moving in and we didn’t want to get stuck on the ridge during a rain storm.

After the ladder the feratta got a bit more difficult but we were nearly at the top. It took maybe a other 20 minutes to reach the summit where we met up with Sarah.

At the summit we took a break to snack and enjoy the view (the weather looked like it cleared up a bit). We took a couple of group photos and then started our way back down the mountain.

The hike back down was a bit of a pain. It took us about an hour to make it dow to the hut. Becca and I made it back just before it started to downpour. Unfortunately pat and Sarah descended a bit slower than us and had to hike a good 15-20 minutes in the rain.

At the hut Becca had a sprite and cappuccino while I had a winter schintzle and hot chocolate. Once pat and Sarah got back we hung out for about half an hour till the rain subsided and made our way back to the gondola to head down.

Back at the base of the mountain we walked over to the lake (only a few hundred feet away) and went to do another via feratta called Laserer Alpine Steig.

This one was short, but fun. We were directly above the lake for about half of it and there was another 2 wire horizontal ladder that was fun and of course great views of the surrounding area.

I hiked ahead a bit to get some drone footage of everyone else making the climb. Once we all finished we went back to the car and drove about 45 minutes to strobe to check into our Airbnb.

We ended up parking the car in an electric vehicle spot (per our hosts instructions); parking seems to be an issue with all our accommodations lol. We showered and did a quick drone of the area before heading into town for dinner.

The town is small and quaint but apparently there was a “summer in Strobl” festival taking place so there were tons of people at the lake shore. They were doing a water skiing demonstration that was pretty impressive. One guy water skied on top of 3 chairs and another guy was doing all sorts of flips.

We ended up getting dinner at a place near the lake called kitchenwrit. I had the boiled “special beef” it was good!

After eating we went for some gelato and then watched the band perform on stage. It was funny because there were a lot of recognizable American songs but some of them were sung in German. My favorite was “the devil went down to Georgia” sung in German 😂.

After the concert we walked back to our place and then went to bed.

item.title: Day 8 - Strobl & Klettersteigs
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was another slow morning. We woke up around ate and went downstairs to try and get breakfast at the cafe. The host was super rude to us again so we ended up walking across the street to get breakfast groceries and snacks to eat in our apartment instead.

After breakfast I spent some time catching up on the blog while the others rested and relaxed. Around 11:30 we made our way 30 minutes by car to do some more klettersteigs.

The two we were doing are called Mein Land Dien Land and Leadership. They’re both on the same cliff so we figured they would be easy to find… that was wrong!

We parked the car in a parking lot near a hotel and followed the topographic map to the best of our ability to try and find the start of the first Klettersteig. We made a few wrong turns and had to climb off trail (there really weren’t great trails to start). We eventually ran into a big group of Germans that were also going to the Klettersteig, so we followed them to the start.

This Klettersteig was really cool! It started in a slot canyon and made it’s way up and out onto the cliff face. There was another 2-wire bridge and a horizontal ladder on the route which were both fun.

The whole rout was pretty short so we finished it quickly. Pat and Sarah were slow to get their gear on and were stuck behind the large group so Becca and I decided to try and get back to the beginning of the Klettersteig. That was a bad idea, we ended up on the side of the mountain that was really steep and hard to traverse.

We eventually made it to the start and did the run again. By the time we were done Becca was tired and didn’t want to do the second Klettersteig. Also it started to rain a bit :(. Becca waited at the top under the trees while I hiked down and across to try and find the second Klettersteig. Luckily Pat had followed the German group and was able to send me his location. I had to do some more scrambling and off trail hiking but I eventually made it.

The route was short but fun and had another small slot canyon type segment. It was raining harder the whole time which wasn’t as fun. I didn’t take any photos of this one because of the rain but I didn’t get GoPro video. I met back up with everyone at the top of the route and we hiked back down to the car.

We drove back to the apartment and hung out for a bit. Everyone was tired so rest was needed! Around 6:30 we walked into town and went to dinner at the same restaurant we ate at the night before. This time I had the pork schnitzle, which was really good.

After dinner we went back and played a card game called lock pick and then watched some Netflix and went to bed.

item.title: Day 9 - Salzburg, Eagles Nest, & Munich
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7:30 and had breakfast in the apartment. The first stop was to the other side of the lake which took about 45 minutes to drive to. We were planning to try and do some cliff jumping, but by the time we got there it was pouring rain and we still had to hike from the parking to the jump spot (which we only had a general idea of where it was). So with all that we decided to pass on the cliff jumping and continue on.

Our next stop was another 45 minutes away to Berchtesgaden Germany. Or more commonly know as the eagles nest, basically Hitler’s evil secret hideout that’s built into and on top of a mountain.

We had to park at the bottom of the mountain and then take a bus up. It’s possible to hike but it takes like 3 hours one way and we were short in time so we paid the outrageous ($25 bus price each).
