The bus dropped us off at the top and then we walked through a tunnel into the mountain and then got on an elevator that took us straight up into the kehlsteinhaus (the eagles nest).

That house itself wasn’t that interesting. It had a small museum type section but the rest of it was converted into a restaurant.

We went outside for a bit to walk along the mountain ridge. The foggy weather cleared just long enough for us to see some views and get a few pictures before obscuring again.

We went back in and had lunch. I had a brawtwurst, it wasn’t very good and kind of expensive, I wouldn’t recommend.

After eating we took the elevator back down and then took the bus back to our car. We got back in and drove about an hour to our next stop, Salzburg (back in Austria).

Salzburg was a cool town, built right on a river and famous for being the birthplace and home of Mozart. When we first drove in there was a ton of traffic and we couldn’t find parking anywhere. We thought we had found a spot, but upon further inspection and translation of the sign it turned out it was for residents only.

Since the rain seemed pretty light we decided to head over to the city wall klettersteig. It’s a klettersteig that ascends the old wall of the city! Luckily we were able to find some street parking close by. The girls were tired of klettersteigs and weren’t a fan of the rain so just Pat and I went.

The route was short but really fun! The wall was pretty slick from all the rain but we made it to the top without falling ha! The top had some good views of the city.

There was a path back down but we had no idea where it went so we opted to climb back down instead (this time on the easier route).

After we finished we met the girls at a nearby coffee shop for some hot chocolate. We ended up walking from there to explore the city. We went through a few of the main squares (called platz). We also saw Mozarts birthplace and residence, walked the main shopping street, crossed the river bridge, saw a small market, and saw the Mirabell palace.

After exploring the city we made our way back to the car for another two hour ride back to Munich. Pat and Sarah weren’t able to get a room at the same place as us (pat waited too long to book). So we dropped them off and then went to our hotel to check in.

Apparently there’s some sort of huge music festival and also the Europe games going on in Munich right now so the city was packed. We just ended up going to an Indian restaurant by our hotel that was sooo delicious, seriously the best chicken tikka masala I’ve had (and I’ve had a lot).

After dinner we ended up taking an electric scooter back (we were only a few blacks from the hotel. Becca had never been on one before and I’m not sure she enjoyed it haha. At least we didn’t crash like my sister and I when we tried to share a scooter. Back at the hotel we got packed and went to bed.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: WHY DIDN'T YOU JUST GET SEPARATE SCOOTERS THIS TIME

item.title: Yosemite & Sequoia NPs
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We’re married!!

We got extremely lucky with the weather, hurricane Ian missed us completely and left us with amazing weather all day Saturday. We had an amazing time with all of our close family and friends celebrating the weekend. Which brings us to now, our mini honeymoon.

We put our names in the lottery to hike half dome (a popular hike in Yosemite national park) and my name got picked! This spurred planning and that’s how we ended up with this mini-honeymoon trip after our wedding to Yosemite and Sequoia national parks in Northern California.

Day 0 - Monday

After saying goodbye to our family and friends on Sunday, we woke up early to catch our 7am flight from Savannah to Charlotte and then from Charlotte to San Francisco. All the flights went super smoothly, we made it to SFO ahead of schedule and picked up our car from the airport.

We were hungry from flying all day so we made a quick stop at in-n-out for some animal style burgers and fries and then continued the 4.5 hour drive to Yosemite.

We made it Curry village (in The Valley of Yosemite) around 5:30pm to check in to our heated tent :). We settled into our tent then explored the village for a bit before showering and getting ready for bed (we were exhausted).

Day 1 - Tuesday Half Dome

Today we woke up early 5am to get ready for our hike. We cooked freeze dried camping meals with hot water for breakfast and then made our way from our tent to the trail around 5:45am.

The start of the hike was dark so we had our head lamps on. The first interesting site was Vernal falls (on the mist trail which we got on right before they closed for contstruction for the day).

We continued up to Nevada falls and the sun started to rise.

We finally made it to the ranger at the base of half dome’s “sub-dome” around 9:30am. After checking our permit we continued another steep section to the top of the sub dome.

Then started the famous “cable section” of half dome.

The hike itself was really short, but it was steep and somewhat slippery, there was a bit of a traffic jam (so many out of shape people hiking) so I decided to hike on the outside of the cable to pass everyone. At the top we rested and enjoyed the views. We had some snacks, explored, took some really cool photos. I also was able to hit the turtle back repeater (about 9 miles away) with my handheld radio and talk to a few radio nerds (I might be one myself).

After we rested we made our way back down the cables taking more pictures on the way down. We reached the bottom around 11:30am.

We continued hiking most of the way down until the fork in the trail. I decided I wanted to do the clouds rest peak trail (which added about 8 miles and 3,000’) Becca decided she wanted to head back down to the river and rest. We each had Walkie-Talkies and somewhat surprisingly we were able to talk to each other the whole way (we were at least 8 miles apart).

The hike to clouds rest was EXHAUSTING the heat of the day was in full force. It took me around 2 hours to hike up to the top and I was rewarded with amazing views of The Valley and half dome. I rested at the top of clouds rest for about 15 minutes and had some snacks.

I hiked back down to Becca at Merced river, which took about 2 hours. I thought I lost contact with Becca on the radio but it turned out that she inadvertently switched the frequency on her radio lol.

After we reunited we continued down taking some more pictures along the way of Nevada and Vernal falls. We stopped emerald pool (which feeds the falls) to dip our legs in the cold water…it felt sooo good to rest. While we were there Becca spotted a mama bear with her 3 cubs across the water!

We continued hiking down and finally reached the village around 5:45. 12 hours of hiking for the day! I ended up with about 25 miles and 7,000’ elevation gain. We were both exhausted. We made some more freeze dried camp dinners with hot water (some sort of masala). It was really good but there was a ton of food.

We went to the grocery store to pick up some ice cream, beer, and snacks for tomorrow. After eating we got ready for bed and another early day tomorrow.

Day 2 - Wednesday - El Capitan

Today we woke up around 5:15, got dressed and ate some more egg and sausage skillet. Once we were ready we loaded up in the car and drove about 2 miles further down and on the other side of The Valley to start our hike.

We started hiking around 6:15. This route had a lot of switchbacks up. On the way we ran into a small bear! (Unfortunately no pictures) Becca got the closest to it only a few feet away!

Once we got to the top of the ridge we hiked over to the to of El Capitan (the famous wall that lots of rock climbers climb). The views from the top were nice, Lots of good views of half dome and further down The Valley. It was around 10:30 at the top, we rested for a bit and ate some snacks before making our way back across the ridge to the next stop.

There was another peak only about 0.3 miles off our trail, Becca was tired so I ended up hiking it myself. Eagle peak was really cool and in my opinion better views and more fun than El Capitan. There were some boulders you could scramble and climb on.

After taking in the views I rushed back to catch up to Becca who was on her way to our next stop, Yosemite falls. We had already caught some glimpses of the falls on the way up (there wasn’t much water, it was mostly mist).

The top of the falls was really cool! Nice views and there was a little river with some pools. We ended up relaxing at the top near the pools. I ended up taking a dip in the water, it was freezing, but refreshing! Also while laying out to dry/warm up I accidentally dropped my phone in the water. Luckily it was super clear and not that deep I was able to retrieve it without an issue and the phone was fine.

After relaxing for a while we made our way to our final stop on, Yosemite point. This was only about 0.8 miles away from the falls and not that much higher so it was a quick hike. This point had the best views of half dome in my opinion and there were some cool rocks you could climb. We took some good photos and then started the long journey back down to The Valley.

We made it back down to The Valley around 4:30 and took a short break at the car. We hiked about 11 hours today and around 21 miles with over 5,000’ of elevation gain…soooo exhausted!

We drove a little further down the road and stopped at a small river near the base of El Capitan to relax. The view of el capitan from the base was really cool, the wall is so shear and tall. You could even see some rock climbers on the face of it!

After relaxing there we drove back towards our tent making a quick stop at a place called swinging bridge, spoiler alert it’s a normal bridge that doesn’t swing.

After we got back to our tent we showered and then called it a night as we were both completely spent!

Day 3 - Yosemite and on to Sequoia

Today we slept in till 8, had some breakfast and got everything packed up in the car to check out. We did a really short hike to mirror lake. Unfortunately the lake was basically completely dried out, but there were some really good views of half dome.

We got back to Yosemite village and drove to the Yosemite village store and walked to the museum. The museum was cool, the most interesting section to me was how the granite formed (it was pushed up out of the ground over time by volcanic activity) and also the section on rock climbing. After the museum we made a quick stop at the ansel Adam photo house (right next door) and then picked up a few snacks from the store and Becca got herself a Yosemite hat.

Next we drove down The Valley to the El Capitan viewing turnoff and walked the short walk over to the wall. Seeing it up close was impressive, I can’t imagine how difficult it would be to climb the whole thing (Becca and I downloaded the free solo movie to watch later about the guy who climbed it, all 3,000’, without any rope or aid).

After marveling at all the climbers on the wall we got back to the car and made our way south towards Sequoia. We attempted to stop at bridveil falls on our way out but sadly it was closed.

The drive to Sequoia took us through Fresno where we stopped at a grocery store to get some lunch and breakfast supplies and some more (cheaper) snacks. We also filled up the car before heading the 1 hour east of Fresno towards the park.

Sequoia is actually a national Forrest but it is essentially combined with another park called King’s Canyon (we drove through King’s Canyon but didn’t stop anywhere).

Since we had some time before sunset we stopped to see the General Sherman tree. This is the largest tree, by volume, in the world. The hike from the parking lot was only 0.6 miles. The tree itself was pretty massive. Apparently it’s over 2,200 years old!

We walked around near the general Sherman and saw some other pretty massive trees.

After seeing the trees we made another stop at Moro rock. This is a really cool rock that overlooks the sierra mountains. It was another short but steep hike to the top, but the views were totally worth it. There wer some ‘influencers’ at the top filming a review for social media, Becca and I secretly judged them while waiting our turn to take pictures.

We made one final stop at the tree tunnel before leaving. It’s literally a tunnel through a tree that fell on the road that you can drive through and take pictures. We took a bunch of pictures and climbed on the tree, it was a fun time.

We finally drove the 45 minutes back down, this time out the south exit of the park to our airbnb, only 5 minutes from the park entrance. We went across the street for dinner (at Totem’s). I had a BBQ sandwhich that was delicious, probably the most meat I’ve seen on a sandwhich. After dinner we chilled in our room and watched free solo before falling asleep.

Day 4 - Sequoia

Today we slept in again, we had free breakfast coupons for Totem’s (I think the own our airbnb) so we stopped there at 8am. The breakfast was really good, I had the cowboy burrito. Becca met a friendly old guy who gave us some hiking recommendations for the day and showed us pictures of a lot of the hikes in the park so we could decide what we wanted to do.

After eating we got back in the car and made our way into the park to our first hike. Getting in and out of the park is a bit of a pain because it’s a one lane road through the mountains for ~20 miles, inevitably you get stuck behind someone driving really slow. Our first hike was to a place called the watch tower.

The hike was about 4.5 miles out through the Forrest until we reached a rocky outcrop that overlooked a valley (known as the watch tower). It was a really cool location. We took some pictures and then I continued on another mile to an Alpine lake called Heather lake while Becca waited for me.

The lake was really cool, super calm and peaceful. There were some people fly fishing. I took some pictures and hung out for a minute before heading back and meeting up with Becca.

We hiked back to the car and then drove to our next stop (through the tunnel log again) to hike in the giant grove Forrest. We only hiked ~3 miles in the Forrest. There were a ton of huge trees! It was also interesting to see the different effects of the fire, a bunch of the trees were damaged or had completely fallen.

After hiking through the grove we drove to a super short hike called hanging rock. Becca wanted to rest so she waited for me in the car. The hike was only 0.1 miles each way to a rock held precariously on a ledge. Of course I climbed on it and took a few pictures before heading back.

While Becca waited for me in the car she saw another bear! This time she was able to get some pictures of it before it ran off into the woods.

Afterwards we made our way back out of the park, making three short stops on the way. Hospital rock, know for the Pictograms from the native Americans (it was really hard to see what it was). Tunnel rock, park of the old road into the park, basically a big rock that was a small tunnel. Finally, the Sequoia park sign.

Once we made it out of the park we stopped at Totem’s again for some BBQ to go and then went another 5 minutes down the road to Reimers for some ice cream. We drove back to our place to each outside and enjoy the sunset. We relaxed the rest of the night before going to bed.

Day 5 - The Coast

Today was a pretty open day, our original flight changed by a day so we basically had a free day to do whatever we wanted. We decided instead of driving directly to San Jose (where we were flying out of) we drove due west to the coast to drive up the famous highway 1.

Our first stop on the highway was the elephant seal beach, there were a surprising amount of elephant seals there sleeping, swimming, fighting, and barking. It was actually really cool!

We continued up the the road stopping at various vistas and pull offs.

We drove all the way up the coast until we hit Monterey and the famous 17 mile drive. We stopped for a short break at caramel beach. I walked down the coast near the 9th and 10th holes of Pebble beach golf course. The weather was extremely foggy so we didn’t hang out too long.

After the beach we drove up 17 mile drive to stop for lunch at Roy’s (on the Spanish bay golf course). We both had the butterfish which was delicious. After lunch we drove up to San Jose to our hotel.

We rested at the hotel and eventually had dinner at a nearby taqueria before getting packed up a going to bed (we had an early flight back home the next day).

Day 6 - Home

We woke up super early to drop off the car and catch our flight back to Savannah. It was an unremarkable trip back with a quick layover in Dallas before getting back to Savannah later afternoon.

Another successful trip in the books! As always I’m grateful for all the amazing experiences and am looking forward to our next trip (the real honeymoon) to New Zealand and Bora Bora next February!

item.title: New Zealand 2023
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Starting the year off right with a two week trip down to New Zealand and the French Polynesia for our honeymoon. Technically we had a mini-honeymoon right after our wedding but that was mostly hiking so it didn't count.

Here's the high level itinerary and Google map of what were planning to cover

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=16N380suTCtX4qlwJbiUv9Yjv_3QoVwpm&ehbc=2E312F&w=640&h=480]

Days 1-5 North Island

Flying into Auckland seeing the Watimo caves, Hobbiton. Then heading to Rotorura to see the geothermal reserves/pools and the kiwi hatchery. We make a stop in Tongariro national park to hike "Mount Doom" from lord of the rings and then drive down to Wellington for a quick look before flying to the south island.

Days 6-13 South Island

We fly into Queenstown and spend some time there doing the adventure activities and then take a quick trip over to milford sound for a cruise and kayak. After queenstown we drive up to Franz Joesef (with a quick stop in wanaka) to do some heli hiking and skydiving! After the Glacier we make our way to Christchurch before flying out.

Days 14-17 Bora Bora

We end the trip relaxing on the beaches in Bora Bora (an island in the French Polynesia)!

Our flight from Dallas to NZ is 15-16 hours! Probably the longest flight I've ever taken.

item.title: Auckland Day 1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
After an arduous day/night of travel we finally made it to Auckland New Zealand! The journey here we flew from Savannah to Dallas (~3 hours) and then after a ~2 hour layover we flew from Dallas to Auckland, which ended up being a 15.5 hour flight! We flew in a 787-9 which is a newer airplane, but the seats still seemed tiny. The plane does has really cool tint-able windows instead of pull down shades.

We watched the entirety of season 1 of white lotus (HBO show) wouldn’t recommend, a few other random movies, and listened to an audio book. Unfortunately I didn’t get much sleep but Becca was able to. After we landed passport control/ customs was super smooth. It took us some time to figure out how to get to the enterprise rent a car (needed to take a shuttle).

After getting our car we drove to the Victoria street parking garage downtown (about 20min away) to explore the city and fight the jet lag. Our first stop was Albert park, fairly small but it was right next to the parking lot. Next we walked down to the ferry port area.

We ended up stopping at a place on the water called the good luck coconut for some fish and chips (they were gluten free so Becca was able to eat them!).

After lunch we made a quick stop at the nearby silo park. Which is exactly what it sounds like, a park built around a few old silos. Not sure who came up with that one.

Next we made our way to the Auckland sky tower. We actually weren’t planning on seeing this but then decided we might as well since we’re here. We signed up to jump off the top of it (the big needle building in the first picture).

We had about an hour to kill before jumping so we went up to the sky deck to get a view of the city and a little preview of where we’d be jumping from. the views of the city were great!

After exploring the two viewing decks we made our way back down to the basement to meet up for the sky jump.

The jump itself was fun! The most nerve wracking part was the wait. They want to charge 70 NZD for video and pictures which seemed outrageous so we took a a few pictures of the preview photos with our phones, hence the watermark 😂.

After jumping we made our way back to the car and then drove to the hotel to check in. After a much needed shower we walked to a nearby shopping/market area and got some gelato.

After the gelato we walked to a hill that was also fairly close that had the Auckland war museum on top the museum was closed but there were some nice views on the top.

After we walked back to the mall to pick up some breakfast for tomorrow and then stopped at a restaurant on the rooftop called baha Betty’s. The food was delicious, I had the chicken and waffles and Becca had tacos.

After eating we walked back to the hotel to relax and get some much needed rest. We have a pretty loaded day of activities tomorrow!

item.title: Glow worm Caves & Hobbiton Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We got up at ~6am after some much needed rest. It was surprisingly easy to switch time zones, probably because I was so exhausted. We ate a quick breakfast in the hotel and then loaded up to drive south to visit the waitomo glowworm caves (about 2 hrs away).

We got to the meet point around 8:30 to check in and ate some snacks before being shuttled to the gate location to get our wetsuits and harnesses.

To start the tour, after some instruction, we abseiled (rappelled) off a platform about 100 feet under ground through a tiny hole, super fun! I’ve abseiled before but this time was with a unique device called a 5 bar break bar

After the rappelling we made our way through the dark cave by zip lining, crawling, swimming, and even tubing! The really cool thing about the cave is the glow worms. Basically these little worms that grow all over the walls of the cave and glow light blue. Pictures didn’t do it Justice but it was really cool to see! Fun fact the glow is called bioluminescence and is actually their poo being processed 😂. Their light attracts bugs that they eat.

The full tour took about 5 hours to make it all the way through the cave. Overall we had a great time, our tour guides max and Astrid were awesome! I’d highly recommend the tour if you’re near Auckland.

After the tour finished we had to rush to our car in order to get to our hobbiton tour on time. Hobbiton was ~1 hour away. Thankfully along the way we were able to call and shift our tour from the 3:10p to 3:30 which gave us plenty of time to make it there.

Pat and Sarah got to Auckland in the morning so they weren’t able to make it to the cave tour with us but they were able meet us for the hobbiton tour. While we waited for our tour we had a small snack, muffins and a beef pot pie. There were some very friendly/daring birds that were happy to try and eat your food so you had to be careful!

None of us are super huge lord of the rings fans, but since it was so close by we had to make the stop. The tour drives you from the entrance of the farm to the main village. There are something like 47 hobbit holes in the village. Interestingly some doors are small and others are large, they do this to create the illusion the hobbits are small while others (like wizards) are tall.

I’m not sure how much money was spent putting the village together but it had to be a lot. The level of detail they went to was seriously impressive. There is a massive tree on top of bag end (bilbos house) that was built specifically for the movie, I guess they couldn’t find any other trees they liked so they built one.

After walking through the village we crossed the bridge and ended at the green dragon where we got a complimentary drink before getting back on the tour bus.

The tour was really cool, definitely a zoo of tourists, but it seems like they have a fairly good system in place to shuttle everyone through. After the tour we drove another hour to Rotorua, a volcanic lake. We made a quick stop to drop off pat and Sarah’s car and then grabbed dinner at a small pizza place by the lake called capiazza.

The pizza was actually really good I had the meat lovers. One thing we’ve all noticed about New Zealand is that they seem to have all the American chains/brands, if it wasn’t for the accents and left had driving you’d think you were in the US. After eating we made our way to our Airbnb which literally was right on the lake and had an awesome view.

After getting settled we decided to go to this thing called the redwoods night tree walk. Apparently New Zealand and California are the only two places in the world that have redwoods. The ones in New Zealand aren’t quite as big as they were only planted about 120 years ago during an experiment to see what types of trees would grow here.

The line for the tree walk was pretty ridiculous but we decided to wait it out. There walk itself was super cool - basically a bunch of suspension bridges between trees with lights and lasers lighting everything up.

The whole walk only took about 30 minutes, but was worth the wait, the pictures don’t really do it Justice since it was so dark it was hard to get a good shot. After the tour we made our way back to the Airbnb and took a quick dip in the hot tub before going to sleep.

item.title: Rotorua Day 3
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up early so I decided to go for a quick run. There was a really cool trail right by our Airbnb that went by the airport and the lake.

After running Becca, Sarah and I made a quick trip to the grocery store to get some snacks and breakfast. We made some scrambled eggs and yoghurt for breakfast and then loaded up the car again to head to a place to try zorbing at 9am.

I wasn’t expecting much but the zorbing was actually a ton of fun! We ended up doing all 4 runs two were straight down and two were very curvy. We did both solo and double. The double was definitely crazy, you’re not allowed to stand up for the double and for good reason, you’d probably fall on top of each other.

I was even able to take out the drone a get some cool videos chasing the sorbs down the hill!

After an hour of zorbing we finished just in time to run next door to the kiwi hatchery for our 10 am tour. The tour itself was okay we got to see a baby kiwi get its daily health checkup and I must admit they are super cute. Our tour guide however was very obnoxious making sure we knew she got to name the kiwi we saw. We did get a few interesting facts. One weird fact is that the kiwi has the smallest beak of any bird, this is because they define beak as the tip of the nose to the nostril, the rest is considered the bill so the kiwis have a tiny “beak” but a really long bill.

We also got to see a more grown up kiwi running around in the terrarium. Unfortunately no pictures were allowed. This is the only picture we took.

We finished the tour in about 30 minutes and since we had some extra time we decided to make a quick stop at the downhill luge, also next door.

I swear New Zealand has all the coolest activities. The luge was a ton of fun! We only had time for one run but I totally would’ve done more. It’s basically like down hill Mario kart and the best part is there are no rules you can bump into each other as much as you want and go as fast as you want. There were quite a few times I almost flipped the cart or spun out of control.

After the luge we took the gondola back down and then drove to a thermal spring called hells gate. Most of the lakes in this region are old volcanoes whose craters were filled with water after they erupted, due to all the volcanic activity there are a lot of these thermal springs in the area. Hells gate had a ton of muddy thermal springs and about a 2km walk.

We took a bunch of pictures, the smell was overwhelmingly bad, sulfur - aka smelly eggs. After the walk we did a complimentary wood carving station, it was super random but a ton of fun. Becca and I both carved kiwis.

After carving we got to do the “mud bath”. The bath wasn’t what I expected. Instead of thick mud it was bath of dirty looking water with mud on the floor that you could pick up and smear in your skin. I guess it’s supposed to be good for you.

After the mud bath we went to the normal hot bath and then showered. We drove about 2 hours to our next Airbnb near lake taupo. After unpacking we went to the grocery store to pick up some lunch and breakfast for tomorrow. After grocery shopping we had some dinner at a place called the tongariro grill. The food wasn’t very good but there was a lot of it.

After dinner we went back to the apartment had some dessert, played a game of 9tiles panic (I won), watched some tv, and then went to sleep. We have an early day with lots of hiking tomorrow!

item.title: Tongariro Crossing & Mt Doom Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 5 to eat and get ready for our big hike. We left the apartment at 5:45 and drove to the north end of the tongariro national park to meet our shuttle. How it works is everyone parks at the north end of the park and then takes a shuttle to the south starting point of the hike and through hikes back to their car. The hike is about 12 miles from start to finish with some optional summits, which of course I did.

Once on the bus the ride to the starting point took about 30 min so we started hiking right about 7am. The one problem with this shuttle system is it causes a ton of people to start at the exact same time (there’s only one shuttle time option) so the trail gets filled with tons of people and no one is spread out in the beginning. We started with a pretty good pace which got us away from most of the crowds. Initially the weather was foggy/cloudy but it quickly burnt off as the sun rose.

After about 4 miles into the hike we hit the split for the first summit option. The first summit was Mt Ngauruhoe (aka mt doom from lord of the rings). Of course a summit with such a menacing name would not be an easy hike. Somehow I managed to convince Pat to make a go at it with me while the girls waited for us.

The start was steep and only got steeper as we went up. This was compounded with the fact that there was no path and the mountainside was basically all scree/shale (loose rock) so it was essentially like climbing up a massive sand dune…super tiring. After some climbing we found a more rigid section of rock with more stable footing that made the ascent easier, more of a scramble/climb.

After about an hour Pat couldn’t take it anymore so he decided to wait while I made the last push to the summit. The top segment was not quite as steep and was much easier to hike. I ended up pulling out the drone and taking some epic shots at the summit before making my way back down. The coolest thing (besides the views) was I was the only person up there!

Heading back down was significantly easier. The shale allows you to almost run down the mountain (like a sand dune). I made it back down to the girls after only about 20 minutes.

Once we rejoined we continued the trek across a dry desert looking basin and up onto another ridge.

Here there was the spilt for the second summit. This one was significantly easier so Becca came with for most of the way. I finished the second summit, did some more droning and then met back up with Becca to get some drone shots together with Mt Doom in the background and one of the alpine lakes.

We continued on the path passing by the red crater (named for its color caused by extreme heat oxidizing the iron in the ground).

We continued down some more shale past some sulfur lakes and then slightly back up again to the alpine lake where we met up with pat and Sarah for a quick lunch break.

After eating we continued down the last 6 miles or so back to the car. The end of the hike wasn’t nearly as epic as the beginning but still good views!

At the bottom of the hike there’s about a mile long road to the car, I decided to run the last mile and get the car to pick everyone up to save them the extra mile of hiking.

Pat ended up getting down about 30 minutes after us. After loading up we drove back to the Airbnb. We rested and went to the hot tub. The hot tubs are very strange here. They’re a part of a community of houses but they are private so you reserve them to use it.

After the hot tub we grabbed some pizza for dinner across the street and then watched some tv before going to sleep.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Can you come pick me up at the end of the hike too

item.title: Wellington to Queenstown Day 5
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 5am, ate a quick breakfast and then hit the road. The drive to Wellington was about 4 hours. Unfortunately we had to go to Wellington because there wasn’t any closer airports besides Rotorua (2.5hrs) however Rotorua didn’t have an enterprise car rental so we were stuck with Wellington.

The drive was long but the views were scenic. I was pretty exhausted, the bed in our Airbnb was terrible so I didn’t get much rest.

We arrived in Wellington around 9:45a. We passed by the New Zealand parliament building (its a circular looking building not that special) and made our way to mount Victoria lookout which had some great views of the city as well as the airport.

After some pictures we drove down to Weta cave. Weta is a famous workshop in New Zealand that builds lots of movie props, costumes, and sets. They are basically the best movie prop creation company and have been used by tons of massively popular films. Unfortunately all the tours of the actual workshop were sold out so we just stopped at the “cave” where they had a mini museum with lots of movie memorabilia.

Next we drove to a brewery called parrot dog (Wellington us known for its craft beer). Unfortunately the brewery was closed so we walked down to the coast where there was a dog beach and surfers. After walking down the beach we stopped at a cafe called the spruce goose. I had a chocolate milkshake. We watched some airplanes land and take off until it was time to drive to the airport.

Unfortunately after dropping off the car I realized I had left my sunglasses in the car. I ran back quickly to try and get them but the car was gone and no one from enterprise was around or answering the phone :(. Luckily the glasses were super old. We took our air New Zealand flight to queenstown and landed around 3:30. We got the car and drove about 15 min to our Airbnb.

It just so happened that Nate and Jamie were staying in Queenstown the same time as us and I had no clue until the day before. Jamie has been traveling for a few weeks before returning to work in the US.

We ended up meeting up with Jamie and Nate around 5p after getting settled in our Airbnb. Since our Airbnb had frisbees we decided to try out the local disc golf course. The course was fun and on a peninsula in the lake which meant good views but also that it was super windy! Even though most holes were 100m or less it was really difficult with the wind…or at least that’s my excuse! We ended up playing 11 holes before deciding to call it quits and get some dinner.

We went to a “famous” burger place called Fergburger. The line was super long we had to put our order in (I got the ferg deluxe) and then wait ~20 min. Once we all got our burgers we walked back toward the pier and sat down to eat. The burgers definitely lived up to the hype! They were delicious!

After dinner we had some ice cream at a nearby shop for Becca’s birthday today! and then we went back to our Airbnb to play some board games with everyone. We played some 9 tiles panic (highly recommend) then a new game called floatsam (not that fun), and finally a game called cat in a box (pat didn’t remember all the rules so we didn’t really play this one so tbd if it’s good). Overall we had a great day, it was really fun to catch up with Nate and Jamie!

item.title: Queenstown Day 6
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6a. Jamie messaged me to see if I wanted to do a quick hike with her and Nate before they left. Everyone was asleep so I went by myself to meet them at the trailhead (which was only about a 10 min walk from our Airbnb).

The hike was the Queenstown hill walkway hike and took about 40 minutes to get up to the “basket of dreams” (a weird sculpture thing). The view was pretty nice from there of the lake. We hiked back down and then Jamie and Nate drove me back to the Airbnb since I had to leave shortly for our bungy jump.

After meeting back up with Becca, Pat, and Sarah I had a quick breakfast and then got ready. We left around 8:30 to go bungy jumping! We went to the Kuwarau river bridge for the jump. It’s a super picturesque bridge with a 43m jump. Becca and I decided to jump tandem (which we’ve never done before).

The jump was a blast! Not as scary as the others I’ve done (probably because it was shorter and over water but nevertheless thrilling! We wanted to get our heads dunked but I guess the bungee was new so they weren’t failed in to getting the settings right and we ended up about a half meter above the water at our lowest.

After the jump we decided to do the “swing” which was another thrill seeking activity with the same company (also the same ones who did the Auckland sky tower jump). The swing is a 300m swing that is strung across a valley in Nevis. We took an off-road shuttle bus about 15min to get there.

That swing was a blast! Not scary at all but a ton of fun. After swinging we got out of the harnesses and bussed back down to the bridge where are car was parked.

At the car I did a little bit of droning to get some cool arial shots before we loaded back up.

We drove the car to the airport, I had to drop off our rental and pick up our other car rental. The short story is I messed up the booking dates and it ended up being cheaper to book a one day rental than add a day to my other rental, it was a pain but it worked out smoothly and the newer rental was nicer!

After swapping cars we were able to get a last minute spot for the shot over jet boat tour so we drove over there around 1:15 and got checked in for our 1:30 tour.

The jet boat was a ton of fun! Basically it’s a super charged boat with 2 massive engines putting out 700 Ho with a very flat hill that allows it to glide and spin across the water. It’s highly maneuverable and super fast. The tour took up through the tight shot over canyon barely missing rocks and walls and doing 360s! Lots of fun, would recommend if you’re in the area.

After the jet boat tour we stopped at the brewery next door for a drink and snack. The beer was actually surprisingly good and the appetizer, a lamb sweetbread was delicious! After eating we went back to the car and I threw the drone up for some cool shots.

We drove back to our Airbnb and then went to get some much needed food. We stopped at a place called Erik’s fish and chips, it’s owned by someone with celiac disease so everything was gluten free, Becca’s dream!

The food was good! After eating we decided to walk to the gondola and take the lift up to do the Queenstown luge (since we had so much fun at Rotorua). This luge only had two tracks, they were much shorter than rotura but still fun! The one track had some pretty steep drops!

After the luge (we did 3 runs) we took the gondola back down and walked back to our Airbnb. Becca wanted to do an ice bar so we decided to check it out, there are 3 ice bars in Queenstown, I have no idea why, but I would not recommend, they are Very gimicky.

Regardless we still had a fun time. After the ice bar we stopped to pick up some groceries then went back to the Airbnb to watch some tv and then sleep.

item.title: Remarkables & Te Anau Day 7
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in and took it easy. We ate breakfast at the Airbnb and then cleaned and packed up before heading out. Today the weather was perfectly clear, not a cloud in sight! Perfect for hiking up mountains.

We left the Airbnb around 10a, the drive up to the remarkables took about 45 minutes, the drive itself had great views of the city and surrounding area. We parked at the lot for the ski area, currently closed for the summer - though there was snow it wasn’t nearly enough to ski.

The hike up to Alta lake took about 30min and was around a mile. Apparently the lake was one of the film locations for LOTR. The lake was really nice and had great views of the peaks surrounding it.

At the lake the other decided to hang out while I decided to attempt to hike to the top of one of the double cones (the name given to the two peaks).

The hike up was very rough lots of scree (big loos boulders), no clear path, and snow. The snowy scree was very difficult to traverse. My shoes are pretty old and had no grip on the snow.

After a certain point (probably 20/30 min) I hit the ridge of the peak. There was less snow because it was steep and require a scramble/climb up. It was really fun, I ended up making it about 10m from the final summit which required some climbing that was too sketchy for me.

Also the wind on the ridge was ripping and I was start to get cold. I took out the drone for some quick photos and videos (I tried to cicle the peak and lost signal with the drone, thankfully it was able to return to home automatically but it freaked me out for a minute!).

After I successfully got the drone back I decided to hike down. The hike down was much faster. However I went a little too quick and my foot slipped on some snowy scree and I got a nearly gash on my ankle. I was able to hike down the rest ok and Becca was able to patch me up with my mini first aid kit (glad I always carry it!).

I ate a quick sandwich at the lake and then we hiked back down to the car. After loading up we made the ~2 hour drive to our next stop, te Anau. Te Anau is basically a stop over town on the way to the famous Milford sound.

We arrived at our Airbnb around 4p and got unpacked. The Airbnb layout was really strange. After getting settled we walked into town. I made a quick stop at the gas station and got some cheap replacement sunglasses then we walked down the main strip to the lake.

On the way down we saw an escape game so we booked a time for 7p. We made another stop at the grocery store for breakfast and lunch tomorrow and then brought everything back to the Airbnb (we’re only 5min walk from the town). We rested for a bit before heading back to do the escape game.

The game was actually really cool, the theme was moose hunt we had to collect evidence that moose still exist in NZ and then escape (apparently it’s based on a true story where they brought moose to the island and then tracked them).

We made it out in 48 minutes without any help or clues! All the puzzles were really unique and fun so we decided to reserve the second room for tomorrow (apparently it’s more difficult).

After the game we stopped at an Asian fusion restaurant called ditto. I had the spicy tuna sushi bowl and a bao bun. Both were delicious! We got the food to go and ate it at the Airbnb.

After eating we watched the end of white lotus season 2 (just as strange as season 1) and then went to sleep.

item.title: Milford Sound Day 8
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 6a and ate some breakfast at the Airbnb. We loaded up the car and hit the road for Milford sound at 7. The drive out took about an hour and a half. It’s a two lane road the whole way with little passing opportunities which made it slower but we still made good time.

We arrived at 8:30 and parked, our boat tour was at 10:45 so we had some time to walk around and explore. Becca and I did the viewpoint hike, which wasn’t much of a view 😂.

There was a random rope which we thought would go somewhere to a better view but ended up going nowhere.

Then we did the peninsula hike. The peninsula hike was really cool because the tide was low we were able to go way out on the rocks and get some cool pictures as well as watch the planes and helicopters land (there must have been like 20 or more of them, probably all returning from the tour loop).

After hiking around we went to the dock and waited to board our cruise.

When we originally planned this part of the trip we booked a kayak and cruise tour, however two days before the tour we got an email saying they canceled the kayak part of the trip because the guide got sick :(. The nice part was we got. Free cruise (usually $100/person) but we didn’t get to kayak.

The cruise itself was ok. The weather was great and the views were spectacular but it was very touristy and not super adventurous:). The drive did pull the boat up to a couple of waterfalls and soaked everyone who was on the front deck of the ship.

Luckily Becca and I managed to stay relatively dry. Some fun facts about Milford sound - it’s not actually a sound it’s a fjord, the main difference being that a fjord is carved out by glaciers instead of rivers.

We travelled all the way through the sound to the outlet at the Tasman sea and the returned back through the sound. Besides the waterfalls and fjords we also saw penguins, dolphins, and seals. Overall a fun tour but I’m glad it was free!

After the tour we decided to stop by the airport and we’re able to book a helicopter tour through the fjords on top of one of the glaciers!

We had about an hour to kill before the flight so we went back by the water and had lunch. We met back at the airport at 2:30 for our tour. It was my first helicopter ride and it was awesome! It felt like droning but in real life instead of a screen. The pilot, Andrew, took us up through the fjords and around some of the alpine lakes before landing us on the Tutoko glacier.

We spent some time in the glacier taking pictures and hiking up a little before jumping back in the Heli and returning to the airport. Definitely makes me want to learn to fly a helicopter!

After the flight we drove ~1.5 hours back to Te Anau. We stopped at the Airbnb for a while before heading to do the second escape room at 6pm. This room was about the digging of the hormel tunnel and was just as good as the first room. We didn’t use any hints or clues and got our in just over 45 minutes! I won’t spoil any puzzles but I definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in the area. We met the owner who designed and built the rooms as a side/passion project.

After the room we walked back down the main strip and decided to get dinner at an Indian restaurant cleverly named Thai Anau. I had the butter chicken and garlic naan. Both were good!

After eating we got back to the Airbnb and decided to book a canyoning trip for tomorrow in Wanaka. This meant we have to wake up early so we got everything we could prepacked so we can eat and leave quickly tomorrow morning.

item.title: Wanaka Canyoning Day 9
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today, since we decided to book the canyoning tour, we had to wake up early to get to Wanaka by 9am. We woke up at 5a, ate a quick breakfast and hit the road. We ended up making great time and arrived at Wanaka around 8a. Since we had some time to spare we decided to take a short walk to “that one Wanaka tree”. Basically a lone tree in the middle of the lake.

The walk there only took 10 min and after taking some pictures we walked back to the car and drove to the meeting point for our tour.

We met our guide, Robin, and one other person who booked the tour before getting in the tour van and heading to the canyon. The drive to the canyon took about an hour and a half. We did the intermediate trip which was a bit longer and more difficult. The canyon we were exploring is called Robinsons creek.

Once we got to the canyon we got suited up in our wetsuits, harnesses and other canyoning gear. We had to hike from the van about 20 minutes up to the start point. The hike was really cool very mossy and looked like a fairyland if that makes sense lol.

The water was super cold but the trip down the canyon was a blast! Lots of jumps from 8 m high to 2 m high and lots of rappels/abseils.

Pat had his GoPro but the battery didn’t last very long so we only had a few pictures from the trip. Unfortunately we didn’t get a good video of the biggest jump either because Pat was too scared to go first 😂.

The coolest abseil was like 100’ into a big cavern!

The whole trip lasted a few hours. After we got out of the canyon we ended right at the van. We changed into some warm clothes and drove about 20 minutes to a lunch picnic spot.

The lunch was okay, it was sandwich’s but all veggies and no meat so it was lacking a bit of protein.

After eating we drove back into town and got back around 4. Overall the tour was a blast and our guide was great! Would recommend if you’re near wanaka check out deep canyon tours.

Wanaka is a super quaint lake front town surrounded by mountains. Much less touristy than Queenstown and a really cool vibe. After we got to the car we checked into our Airbnb and then walked down to the lake to relax.

We hung out at the beach for an hour and a half soaking in the sun and people watching. There’s a ton of things you can rent at the lake if you want to (paddle boats, sail boats, jet skis etc) there’s also a pier you can jump off of. We didn’t bring suits so I only went in knee deep to feel the water.

After hanging out in the beach we made our way to a craft brewery bar called Kai Whakapai (right next to the lake). Apparently Wanaka has the most breweries per capita than any other NZ town. I had the hazy IPA which was really good!

After a beer the girls went to get food from a food truck place while pat and I decided to hike the mount iron cross (surprisingly Pat suggested hiking as he’s trying to lose 1kg so he weighs less than 100kg and doesn’t have to pay extra to skydive).

The hike was about a mile from our Airbnb. We made a quick stop there to change shoes and then walked to the trailhead.

At the trailhead there was really ominous signs posted about “random nightly shootings” occurring.

At least the police are aware? We weren’t really sure what it meant but it was about 7:20 when we started the hike so we had about an hour and a half before sunset to complete the hike and avoid being shot 😂.

The hike was fairly quick about 2 miles. It took us about 30-40 min up. I did some droning and we took some pictures at the top (there were great views of the town and lake). The wind was really strong but the drone did well.

After the hike we met the girls back at the Airbnb. Becca got me a lamb should from one of the food trucks, it was delicious. After eating We watched some tv before going to bed.

item.title: Fox Glacier Day 10
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was an early day, we woke up at 4a and had a 3 hour drive to get to the town of fox glacier for our tour. The drive was dark most of the way which is apparently a bad time to drive as I had at least 4 rabbits run out in front of me :(. We ended up making it in early, around 7am. We waited in the parking lot for a bit before going into the tour shop and checking in around 7:45.

We met our guide Hector (from Brazil) and got suited up with our climbing boots and cold gear. Our tour was a glacier ice climbing tour! Becca and I did ice climbing once before in Bolivia and really enjoyed it (though we didn’t get to do much climbing).

Once we were geared up we shuttled a short distance to the helipad and took the quick 5min flight up to the fox glacier (I tracked it on ForeFlight). The Heli flight was cool but definitely not as cool as the one we took in Milford sound. You can tell they really shuttle people back and forth to this glacier. They had a mini helipad set up and helicopters landing every few minutes.

There are 3 main glaciers in the southern alps - mt cook, fox, and Franz Josef. The reason we actually ended up choosing fox glacier was because it was the only one we could get a ice climbing tour on the day we would be there. The other only had the Heli hikes which were clearly more common/popular because they cater to a wider audience (less physically demanding).

Once we arrived on the glacier we got our crampons on and then started hiking on the glacier. There were tons of crevasses some were super deep. We walked a short distance to a small incline wall to learn some fundamentals and practice our crampon work before walking another 15 minutes or so to a bigger ice wall.

Once at the wall we practiced some drills with our ice picks while hector set up the top ropes for our climbing. Hector took a fairly long time to get everything set up. Once the lines were up hector checked us all out on belaying and then let us climb!

We started on the easier walls (less vertical) the moved to the more difficult routes (with small overhang). We did quite a few climbs before taking a break and eating our lunches.

We ate while hector packed up the lines and then we walked further down the glacier to a super large crevasse. hector was super overly precautious the whole trip and took forever to set everything up, he even put up fixed lines to cross a small crevasse. Once he was finally set up he lowered us down into the crevasse, it must’ve been 100 feet and then let us climb back up out of the canyon.

It was really cool, I did it twice and everyone else did it once. After climbing the crevasse we made our way back to the helipad and made the quick flight back to fox glacier. We took the bus back to the tour office and took off all our gear.

After leaving the tour office we drove a short distance to hike to lake matheisen, we didn’t do the full loop, we decided when we got to the lake to turn back because we were hungry. We stopped at a restaurant in town called Betsy jane (recommended by our guide). The food was really good! I had the ribeye.

After eating we drove to our Airbnb about 30 minutes away in Franz josef, it was like a little village, a guy with a bunch of land built like 10 small houses on it to Airbnb, there aren’t many options to stay here.

There Airbnb had a hot tub Becca and I checked out and then we played a game of cat in the box (with the correct rules this time), then went to sleep.

item.title: Franz Josef Glacier Day 11
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we didn’t have to wake up quite as early. We had breakfast at the Airbnb and then got the car loaded and over to the meeting point for our sky dive!

Sarah had changed her mind overnight and decided she didn’t want to go. The guy at the checkin counter did his best to try and convince her but she ended up staying with her decision not to go. After we were all checked in we ended up driving ourselves to the Franz Josef airport (the shuttle was too full) and then getting geared up for our dive. They made us wear these jump suits and silly padded helmets that looked like rugby helmets.

Fortunately Becca and I were on the first plane up while Pat ended up having to wait for the 4th plane. The flight up to 13,500’ (our jump altitude) was quick. The weather today was perfect! Very little clouds which meant great views of the mountains and the sea. Becca was the first jumper out of the plane while I followed her shortly after.

The jump was awesome! Really makes me want to learn more about the sport. The free fall lasted around a minute, we did some turns/spins. I was surprisingly not scared at all on this jump (I guess I’ve become desensitized). After the minute free fall the instructor pulled the chute and then let me do some canopy flying, steep turns left and right and flares. As we got closer to the landing site he took over and we landed on our butts.

Since I was heavier we landed shortly before Becca so I got to see her landing. After we were back on the ground we got all our gear off.

We realized it was going to take a while for Pat to jump so Becca and I decided to go do the gorge and tunnel hike which wasn’t far.

We did the gorge hike which was about two miles. There was a cool suspension bridge over the river and a path down so you could get to the water, it was very cold!

Since we still hadn’t heard from pat, After the gorge we did the tartare tunnel hike. The hike is connected to the gorge hike and is another 2 miles hike. The hike took us to an old tunnel that was used to transport fresh water to the town.

The tunnel was cool but was filled with ankle deep water. I went a good ways into it (not sure if it ends somewhere) and my feet were pretty soaked so I turned back.

After the tunnel we hiked back to the car and finally heard back from pat that he survived his jump so we went and picked them up.

We decided to do another slightly longer (6.5 mile) hike called Robert’s point with pat and Sarah. The hike was pretty cool, lots of long suspension bridges and very steep! Becca wasn’t feeling great and I was the only one who made it to the end of the trail. Unfortunately the clouds had rolled in so you could barely see the glacier.

I ran into pat and Sarah on my way back to Becca and showed them the pictures of the end of the hike and they decided to turn back with me because it wasn’t worth it.

We got back to the car after about 3.5 hours and we to a restaurant called snakebite for dinner. I had the BBQ ribs. The food was really good, I was impressed for such a small town.

After dinner we went back to the Airbnb and did the hot tub again and then played a board game before going to bed.

item.title: Christchurch Day 12
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we had a slower morning. We ate breakfast at the Airbnb before packing up the car and heading our around 9am. We said goodbye to Frankie, the dog that lives on the property.

We had almost a 5 hour drive from the west coast of the island to the east coast to get to Christchurch.

We drove for about 3 hours and listened to a book called red rising, very good! We made a stop at a place called castle hill, known for its interesting looking boulders.

We went and hiked up from the parking lot to the boulders. Pat and I tried to climb up the front before realizing there was a much easier way up if we walked around the back.

The top of the boulders had a nice view of the landscape. I forgot to bring my backpack and drone so I ran back to the car and did some droning while everyone else was still on the boulders.

We spent about 1 hour there hiking around. Then we finished up the 2ish hour drive to Christchurch and made it to our Airbnb. Our Airbnb was close to downtown and also had a hot tub in the backyard.

We settled in and then decided to go do another escape room since we didn’t have much else to see in the city. We did the room called Nikola where you try and recover the designs from nikola tesla. The room was cool, very high production value but the clues weren’t very unique. We would have finished without any clues but one of the items wasn’t working correctly and needed some excessive force to activate. We ended up finishing in 46 minutes, but would have been much quicker if we didn’t get stuck on that one item.

After the finishing the escape game we decided to get some food at a nearby restaurant. We ended up landing in a fancy Mexican place. The food there was very tasty!

After dinner we went back to the Airbnb and hung out before bed. Tomorrow we leave for the French Polynesia!

item.title: Bora Bora Day 13-17
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We left Christchurch for Tahiti. We got to the airport early and left at 12 for a 1.5 hour flight to Auckland. In Auckland we had to walk pretty far to get to the international terminal and then go through security and everything again which was a pain. We made it to the gate about 10 minutes before boarding. We had some extra NZ cash so I got some food before the flight. There was nothing but McDonald’s close so I ended up getting a Big Mac (it’s been years since I’ve had McDonald’s).

The flight to Tahiti took about 5 hours. Becca and I had no one in between us which was nice! However we did have some crazies sitting behind us. Right when we got up to cruising altitude I reclined my chair, as I always do, and moments later the person behind me tapped my shoulder and asked me to not recline my chair. I politely told her no I wanted to recline. Throughout the flight they kept kicking our chairs and eventually culminating in the guy getting up to go to the bathroom and forcefully slamming my chair forward. Needless to say I was in shock, I let the chief flight attendant know who unfortunately decided not to do anything since there was only an hour left in the flight.

We arrived in Papeete around 8:30pm the day before we took off (we time travelled since French polynesia is 23 hours behind NZ). We got a shuttle to the nearby Hilton hotel. We stayed there for the night. The hotel looked really nice actually! Unfortunately we had an early flight so we didn’t get a chance to enjoy it.

We dropped our bags in the room and then explored the hotel quickly before getting to bed.

Day 14

We got an early shuttle back to the airport to catch our 6:45am flight to Bora Bora! The flight was super quick (45 min) on an ATR 72. Once we landed we grabbed our bags and immediately took a boat to our resort. We got a great deal from Costco and are staying at the four seasons in an overwater bungalow! Pat and Sarah weren’t able to book as early as we did and ended up booking at the St Regis (a neighboring resort).

From the airport you travel by boat to the resort (there are no roads to the airport). The boat ride only took about 20 minutes and had nice views of the main island on the way.

We got to the Four Seasons around 8:30am. We were greeted with the traditional lei during check in (we've gotten about four of these now, literally everywhere gives them to you). Unfortunately since we were so early our room wasn’t ready, but we were able to go hang out at the beach until it was.

Fortunately they were able to get our room ready fairly quick (around 11). Our room is incredible! We have a Mountain View (which I’m pretty sure we weren’t supposed to have) we’re on the west most “branch” of the overwater bungalows which is closest to the beach and all the restaurants. Also the room is massive!

Since it was our honeymoon the gave us a free bottle of champagne and some fruit in the room.

We spent the rest day exploring the resort - hanging out at the beach, stand up paddle boarding around the bungalows, and snorkeling at the on resort lagoon. The resort lagoon has tons of coral reef and lots of fish swimming around, my favorite was the puffer fish.

They also had a free shell necklace and bracelet making class so Becca made a necklace and I made a bracelet.

My bracelet turned out really cool! We ended up eating lunch at the beach restaurant, I had the Mahi burger, it was delicious.

We ended the night with dinner at the Asian fusion restaurant called Vaimiti. The dinner was very good and they were super accommodating to adjust dishes to be gluten free for Becca.

Day 15

Day two at Bora Bora started with a massive breakfast at the buffet and then did a free morning yoga class. Then it was more of the same - hanging out at the pool, relaxing, paddle boarding. I flew the drone around for a bit and got some cool shots of the room and Becca on the paddle board.

We also had a ton of fun jumping and diving off of our dock!

We ended the night with dinner at the Terre Nui restaurant which was like a 3 course meal. It was really good, but I liked the first restaurant the best. While at dinner we were also able to see a private fire show that someone had arranged on the mini island just off the beach. Even though it was kind of far it was impressive to watch!

Day 16

Day 3 in Bora Bora we started again with a really big brunch. Then we got picked up at the dock for our scuba diving trip! Our first dive was inside the lagoon area at a cleaning station for eagle rays. This was probably the coolest dive I've ever done we saw at least a dozen eagle rays (basically massive sting rays) that passed by us within an arms reach, they were sooo close! Unfortunately we didn't have any underwater cameras with us :( but the experience was amazing. Our second dive was just outside the lagoon and was nearly as cool as the first. This dive was saw dozens of white tipped sharks. At one point there was probably 40 of them, the reason is the snorkel boats will feed them which, needless to say, draws a ton of them over!

We got back to the resort around 12:30 and did some more paddle boarding and relaxing at the pool and the beach. For dinner we tried the final restaurant, Aria Moana, it had a Mediterranean theme and was really good!

Day 17

Our final full day in Bora Bora :(. After our massive brunch buffet we basically did everything the resort had to offer again: yoga, volleyball (only 1 v 1), ping-pong, lagoon snorkeling, droning, and of course relaxing at the pool/beach/room.

We ended the day with dinner at Vaimiti (our favorite of all the restaurants).

Day 18

Unfortunately today was the day we had to leave :(. We had an awesome time at the resort and after another big brunch we packed up and started the long journey back. The weather today was really bad, overcast and raining, which made it a little easier to leave.

We boarded the boat around 10:30 to make our way back to the Bora Bora aiport.

It was another quick hop back to the main island on an ATR-72. This time around we had some really nice views of the island as we flew back.

Unfortunately there was no really good way to get back and we ended up having a super long layover at the Papeete airport. The airport is a typical island airport so no air conditioning and wifi unfortunately. On the plus side I met a really cute puppy at the airport (I think he just wanted me beef jerky).

We were on the same flight back stopping in Dallas as Pat and Sarah and barely missed an earlier connection before finally getting back to Savannah late at night.

Another epic trip is in the books! I was too lazy to post this right away when we got back, hence the delay, but I had to get it posted before we set off on our next trip, Colombia! As always looking forward to exploring the world on the next adventures 2023 has to offer.

item.title: Colombia 2023
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Time for another trip! This time Becca and I are heading south to Colombia to explore the country, hike, and relax at the beach! Here is a google map of all the spots we plan to hit.

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1vp7zgvnQcaZTe8zAa-d3BqTsu03jxSM&ehbc=2E312F&w=640&h=480]

Here’s our rough itinerary:

Day 0 Thursday May 11
Drive Sav to Jax
Fly Jax to Miami to Bogota (Depart KJAX 8pm)
Arrive 1:10 am
Stay Bogota - Cranky Croc Hostel

Day 1 Friday May 12
Bogota Activities (8,600’)
Walking tour - La Candelaria Barrio: Museo del Oro, Museo Botero, Plaza Bolivar, Graffiti on Calle de Escudo
Food Tour - ajiaco (soup), chocolate santafreño (hot choc w/cheese), chica (fermented corn drink), Plaza de Mercado la Concordia
Hike Mt Monserrate- 3.2 miles, 2637 ft elevation gain
Dinner @ Puerta Falsa (anthony bourdain, open since 1816)

Day 2 Saturday May 13
Fly Bogota to Medellin 6:30a
Fruit Tour 10 am
4:30pm Comuna 13 Tour
To See: Plaza Botero, Parque Lleras, Palacio de Cultura Uribe Uribe, Parque de la Luces, Plaza Minorista market

Day 3 Sunday May 14

Stay Medellin - Los Patios Hostel

Day 4 Monday May 15

Day 5 Tuesday May 16

4 hours day trek, 6.8 km/4.2 miles

Day 6 Wednesday May 17

Day 8 Friday May 19
