Excited to explore another new country! Stay tuned for updates!

item.title: Bogota Day 0/1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I worked from home while Becca had the day off. We left Savannah around 3:30/4 and drove about 2 hours to Jacksonville airport. The flights were much better and cheaper from Jacksonville so it was worth it.

We ended up getting to the airport really early. We used spothero to get a covered parking spot for $7/day at a place called Wally park. Security at the airport was super quick. We got to the gate early and were lucky enough to get an earlier flight out of Jacksonville to Miami at 6:30 instead of 8pm. However, we weren’t as lucky in Miami, instead of leaving at 10:30p our flight left closer to 11:30 which meant we didn’t arrive in Bogota until ~2am 😩. We had a prearranged ride to our hostel which was super nice, we ended up getting to bed around 2:30. We are staying at the Cranky Croc hostel located in the historic central area of Bogota.

Even though we went to be really late I still woke up around 7am with a lot of energy. We ended up eating breakfast at the hostel at 8am. I had the Colombian breakfast and (even though I’m not a coffee drinker) a latte, both were really good!

After breakfast we got ready for the day and then walked ~2 blocks to our first stop- the museum of gold. We spent way too long trying to find the entrance (people were telling us different things!). We finally figured it out and started exploring the museum around 9. The museum was pretty big, 3 stories and of course filled with all kinds of gold treasures and trinkets. Overall it was cool to see but wouldn’t recommend going out of your way for it, but if you’re in Bogota the entry fee is only $1/person so you might as well go.

We got out of the gold museum after about an hour, just in time to meet up for our walking tour (which was conveniently meeting right outside of the museum).

The tour was really interesting but long! We walked around the city from 10a-1p. We learned a lot about Colombian history and some interesting stories, here’s my summary of the stops and most interesting things I took away.

The main reason for the city of Bogota was gold exploration, Spanish explorers took a wrong turn on the river and ended up in Bogota. The higher altitude of Bogota lends itself to nice weather and no mosquitos making it a popular place to live. Colombia used to be one large country consisting of Ecuador, Venezuela, and Panama when it first split from Spain. However, after many power struggles the countries split up into what we know them today.

On the walking tour we walked around an area called La Candelaria. There is a ton of really cool graffiti in this city which has a story behind it. To make it short a kid who was graffitiing was shot and killed by the police which caused a lot of protest and then shortly after Justin Bieber (who was on tour) decided he wanted to graffiti a building and while doing so was being watched by the police in his entourage who didn’t do anything to stop him. This led to the decriminalization of graffiti. Finally, to avoid their buildings being “tagged” by less talented graffiti “artists”, many building owners paid talented graffiti artists to graffiti their buildings.

On the tour we stopped for a quick break at La Mercado Concordia. Becca and I grabbed a strawberries and cream (like an ice cream) and some empanadas. We also got to try Chicha which is basically Colombian moonshine made from fermented corn, it tasted very sour!

We looped back to the plaza Bolivar, one of the main squares where the president lives and the congress building (btw Bogota is the capital of Colombia).

We finished the tour at 1 and decided to stop at a restaurant that Becca heard about called La puerta falsa (the false door). Apparently Anthony bourdain ate here. We had the popular chocolate sanatferrano which is hot chocolate with cheese, it sounds weird but it’s actually really good! It came with almojábana which is a tapioca bread (that Becca can eat!) and we also split a tamal, a rice and chicken dish cooked in plantain leaves. The food was good and the restaurant was really unique, very tiny.

After eating we walked back to the museum of gold to catch our food tour (lots of tours today!). The first stop on the tour was a fruit stand where we tried 3 different fruits: sweet mango, mangosteen, and rambutan.

The next stop was on the way towards plaza bolivar at an empanada and arepas shop. We had the meat empanada (called empanada casera - empanada of the house) and the arepa con huevo (egg arepa) both of which were very good!

The next stop was plaza bolivar where we had grilled corn on the cob, a traditional snack for colombianos.

Next spot was an indoor restaurant where we tried ajico - a chicken and potato soup, barbecue - one veal and the other capybara (a rodent), patacones - flattened and fried plantain, Colombian beer, and a coconut lemonade. All of it was really good, yes even the rat (the had a small stuffed capybara nearby so you could see exactly what you were eating 😂). I was most surprised by the coconut lemonade it was really good and tasted kind of like key lime pie, but better.

It started pouring rain while we were in the restaurant, lucky. We waited about 10 minutes before stopping at a street vendor to try a desert called oblesa. Basically two thin waffles sandwiched with your choice of filling, I went for the condensed milk and black berry our guide recommended. Very delicious!

Becca and I decided to end the tour early after this stop, the next stop was hot chocolate with cheese and then coffee which we already had tried. Instead we stopped at the Botero museum, he’s a famous artist who apparently really likes painting fat naked people. He even had a fat version of the Mona Lisa, super random! Botero donated a ton of his paintings to the government on the condition that the museum would be free to the public.

After the museum we walked back to our hostel only to find that the massive rain storm that hit completely flooded the floor of our room! Thankfully only some of Becca’s packed clothes were in the ground that got wet.

While the hostel worked on drying the room and Becca’s clothes, we walked up the hill to the teleférico to see Monserrat- a church on the mountain boarding bogota. You can hike up to Monserrate but Becca and I opted to take the cable car (~$6 each). The views at the top were awesome. I started to fly my drone but only got a few pictures before the security said I had to land, there weren’t any no droning signs around so I didn’t think it would be a problem.

After enjoying the views of the city we made our way back down and walked back to the hostel. Along the way we picked up some empanadas and arepas to eat at the hostel.

Back at the room (which was now dry thankfully) we ate and watched some of the movie El Dorado on nextflix before passing out. El dorado is a myth about a city of gold which was supposedly very near to bogota.

item.title: Medellin Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was an early day. We woke up at 4:15am to get a taxi to the airport to catch our 6:30am flight. We got to the airport and through security without issue and had a small breakfast of some pastries and hot chocolate before boarding. Very delish!

The flight to Medellin was a super short hop, a bit over 100 nautical miles. However, driving through the mountains would have taken over 8 hours! The 30 minute flight was smooth. We arrived in Medellin a little after 7. Unfortunately we weren’t able to connect with our scheduled ride, but we were able to quickly get a taxi which actually ended up being a few dollars cheaper.

We arrived at our hostel, Los Patios, in La poblana barrio which is a very trendy area popular for tourists. We checked in and dropped off our bags (our room wasn’t ready). We explored the hostel and the surrounding area. After the quick walk we hung out in the hostel lobby until our 10am fruit tour.

The fruit tour was us, our guide Marcela, and one other person, Rodrigo, who was also from the US but originally from Mexico. We drove about 20 minutes to the plaza Minorista market. Along the way we learned a little about our guide. She was leaving after our tour to go live in New York with her husband who she “spiritually married” (no idea what that means). Needless to say a little strange, but otherwise very nice!

Our first stop in plaza Minorista was a small restaurant that was one of the first in the plaza. There we had the traditional drink calledAgua de panella also called guandolo- a sugarcane drink infused with passion fruit.

While drinking our agua de panella our guide showed us flash cards of all the fruits we would be looking for and trying today. It was a really fun tour we ended up roaming around the market searching for the foods on the cards and learning about them. Our guide kept telling us about how clean the market was, but to me it looked kind of dirty 😁.

After an hour or so we had collected all the fruit we were looking for, and went upstairs to start tasting them. Along with the fruit we also tasted a few juices. One was guanoabana with milk (a big spikey fruit) and the other was lulo juice.

The fruit was all really good: a variety of passion fruits, lychees, mangos. My favorite was the mangostine.

After the fruit tour we said goodbye to our guide, and then our driver took us for a quick stop at plaza botero. On the way there we passed different street markets and some very sketchy streets where people were openly using drugs. It was very shocking- on one street segment there was about 12 people either shooting heroin or smoking crackpipes. We stopped at plaza botero for ~10minutes enough to walked around and take some pictures with the fat statues 😂.

We got back in the car and made our way back to the hostel. Apparently our room still wasn’t ready so we hung out in the lobby. Around 3 we got in the room, moved our bags, and left the hostel to take the metro to meet our tour at Comuna 13. The metro was packed! Luckily we were only on for a few stops before switching lines.

We arrived at the meeting point a bit early so we stopped at an ATM to get more cash and then some street food. Becca had and empanada and I had a chorizo on a stick and a bunello.

After eating we met our tour group at the subway station to begin our tour of comuna 13. There is so much history behind comuna 13- they made a few documentaries about it. Basically it was a really bad neighborhood because it was the access point between Medellin and the coast and jungle (where all the drugs were being farmed). Therefore whoever controlled the comuna controlled all trade and drug traffic - this made it a highly contested area between the guerrillas (various groups of political soldiers), paramilitary (private military), and the government. The government left the area mostly alone until Pablo Escobar was gone and they finally had the resources to try and “clean up” the city. These government operations ended up killing a lot of innocent people, specifically the Orión mission.

In order to make amends the government invested in a lot of social projects like schools for the comuna. However, the one that proved to be the best for the comuna was the escalators (the comuna is on a mountain). The escaltors facilitated the movement but also had the unintended consequence of bringing lots of tourists to the area which was a major boon for the local economy.

Our tour guide Christian was awesome. He took us all throughout the comuna showing us different types of graffiti and street art and the maze of alleys in the unplanned city. He is from the comuna and is also a teacher. He told us a crazy story about how his dad was shot in the face 3 times (being accused of being a guerrilla) and survived!

We ended the tour at a rooftop bar where we got to make our own graffiti. It’s a lot more difficult than it looks!

After the tour we walked back and took the metro home (it was much less crowded). Before going to the hostel we stopped at an Argentinian steakhouse restaurant called Malevo. Becca and I each got massive steaks and the whole dinner only cost $29 total! Insane.

After eating we went back to the hostel to sleep! Another long but fun day exploring.

item.title: Guatape Day 3
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we had a relatively late start and woke up around 6:30am for our 7am pickup for a day tour to guatape. We took a large tour bus with ~30 people. The guide was very punctual which I liked! Our first stop was a cafe called Delicias de la Abuela where we ate breakfast - empanada, scrambled eggs, arepa with cheese, and hot chocolate. It was really good!

Our first stop was the town of Peñol. It was a pretty small basic town, the only notable thing was they had a church that was built into the side of a rock that looked similar to the famous piedra (stone) but smaller.

Our next was the famous piedra. It’s basically a big rock in the middle of a man made lake. It was extremely crowded (likely because it was a weekend). The hike up was about 700 steps and at the top there was a lookout with great views and some shops/restaurants.

I flew the drone around a bit at the top and we took some cool pictures of the landscape before stopping at one of the shops to try a weird popsicle in a cup. I had the passion fruit (called maracuyá) it was hard to eat but good.

We hung out in top of the rock for a bit, we saw a really cool powered hang glider boat fly around the rock.

The way down from the top took longer than the way up! There were a bunch of out of shape people in front of us who were going extremely slow and there was no room to pass (unlike the stairs going up).

We eventually made it down and met at the meeting point, the rooftop of a restaurant near the base of the rock. The next stop was in the town of Guatape. We walked around the town there was an old church with the inside made all of wood, an umbrella street, and a boardwalk.

After exploring and taking some pictures we got some ice cream and then a few snacks from the grocery store before getting a beer and hanging out at a restaurant near the meeting point.

Our next stop was the replica of the old Peñol town. As mentioned the lake was man made. It was made with a hydroelectric damn and in doing so it completely submerged the old town under water so they decided to make a replica of the town.

We had lunch in the old town. It was soup, beef, rice, salad, and a plantain. Not too bad, there was a super cute pup there who begged us for a bite so we obliged.

After lunch we walked around the town to get a few pictures and then made our way down to the boat for a quick tour of the lake.

The tour of the lake was okay, I could’ve done without it, but we got another view of the piedra and a couple mansions. One peninsula had 3 mansions next to each other one was a famous soccer player the other was his teammate and the third was his ex wife’s (which was the biggest lol!). We also saw the ruins of one of Pablo Escobars mansions.

After the boat tour we took the bus back to the hostel. We rested at the hostel for a bit before going out to grab some dinner. We ended up at a nearby taco shop and ordered like eight tacos and some elote to share. It was all really good!

After dinner we went back to the hostel and went to sleep for another early morning tomorrow.

item.title: Santa Marta & Tayrona National Park Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we had another very early day, we woke up around 3:30am to catch our ride to the airport for our 6am flight to Santa Marta. When trying to get cash from the ATM I found out that my card was locked - after calling the bank they said there were some fraudulent charges and they had to lock out the card so now I have no way to get cash out :(. Lucky Becca’s card still works though so we’ll be fine.

At the gate we got a small breakfast from one of the shops - it was pretty bad. The flight to Santa Marta was another short hop ~55 minutes. When we arrived we grabbed a taxi from the airport to our hostel, the Masaya hostel. One of the roads was closed and our driver ended up driving reverse for like 4 blocks down a tight one way street to get us there 😂.

Since our room wasn’t ready, we checked our bags and hung out in the lobby area by the pool. The hostel has two pools! Around 9am we walked to the Marina for our sailing trip. Our original trip was cancelled on us the night before, but luckily we were able to rebook with another company (Tayrona sailing) last minute.

We met the tour operator at the dock and then waited for everyone to arrive. We got in the boat and started sailing around 10 to tayrona.

We sailed for about an hour until we arrived at conch bay - a secluded beach. We hung out and relaxed at the beach.

Becca and I walked down the beach to the other end, the crowded end, to explore. There was a sign, some shops, and a bunch more people swimming. (We definitely had the better location).

When we got back to our spot I tried paddle boarding - our boat brought one with, however it was missing the bottom fins which made it almost impossible to steer. After one lap around the boat I was done.

I also took the drone out to get cool shots of the beach from above. The little kids working at the beach were super interested in the drone so I showed them how it worked and let the one kid fly it for a little. I ended up making friends with two of the kids named Hannes (sp?) and Diego both are 13 and from the area. They each walk 3 hours to get to the beach!

We also ate lunch on the beach, we had fish, salad, rice, and plantains. It was pretty good!

After lunch we hung out in the water and on the beach. I played some paddle ball with Diego.

We left the beach around 3pm to sail back to Santa marta. The ride back took twice as long, I think the captain was trying to mostly use the sail, which is why it took longer. Along the way back we passed by a random island that had a bunch of goats on the top - I have no idea how they got there.

Once we were back on land we walked back to our hostel. Our room was finally ready so we moved our bags unpacked and showered. After getting settled in we went to the downtown Santa Marta area for food. It turned out there was some sort of burger competition going on called burgermastsers that a bunch of the restaurants were competing in and each restaurant involved was serving only one item, their best burger. We stopped at one of the restaurants and got their burger (the used lettuce instead of a bun for Becca). It was really good! It had a delicious sauce and pulled pork on it.

After dinner we made a stop for some gelato ice cream. It was delicious!

After ice cream we made our way back to the hostel to get ready for the hike tomorrow and to sleep!

item.title: Day 5 The Lost City Hike Day 1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6:30am and got everything ready for the hike. Becca and I went to a nearby cafe for breakfast. We had omelets and a big bowl of fruit and hot chocolate.

Becca was not feeling great so she decided to not do the hike and go to the beach resort instead while I did the lost city hike. I walked down to the tour office at 8:30 to pay and meet up with the tour. After paying we got loaded up in the cars around 9 and drove about 2 hours to the town of mamey to start the hike.

There were 8 other people on my tour and one guide (Antonio) and one translator (Pilar). Two were an older couple from Germany (Evelyn & Christian), two Dutch friends (Ann Marleen & Marlijn), two English friends (Amanda & Darren), and a young English couple (Bea & Tom). Everyone was super nice and friendly!

We started with a quick lunch in Mamey that was chicken rice and then our guide, Antonio explained us the plan for the hike (in Spanish) which our translator, Pilar, translated for us.

The basic plan is a four day hike where we reach the lost city on day 3 and then hike all the way back to the start. The total hike is just under 30 miles and over 8,000’ of elevation gain. It’s a lot but over 4 days should be no problem. After the brief explanation we grabbed all our bags and started! This was only the second serious multi day hike I had done and the first where I had to carry my own gear (the Kilimanjaro hike we had porters to carry everything!).

The first part of the hike is in the farmerlands. The trail was a fairly wide rode and we frequently were passed by motorbikes and mules transporting people and various supplies.

We hiked for about 3 hours with a few short stops one notable stop was at the banderas (flags) which was the highest point of todays hike. I was in the front of the group, luckily the translator liked to hike fast so I stuck behind her while the others went at a slower pace.

We also had one stop at a little shop for some watermelon, it was very delicious.

To my pleasant surprise there were a ton of dogs on the trail! So of course I had to pet them all.

We ended the day at camp Adan just across the buritaca river. The hike today was only about 4 miles, mostly uphill, but overall not too bad. When we arrived at camp we got our beds (bunk beds) and then went for a swim in the river. It was a little pool with a ~12ft cliff jump. It was super refreshing!

After showering we had dinner which was fish and rice, pretty good! We hung out for a while and our guide told us some of the history of the area and the tribes that live here.

There are two tribes that will be seeing the Kogi and wiwa and there are four tribes total in the area. After the explanation we went to bed around 8 for an early start tomorrow at 6am.

item.title: Day 7 Lost City Hike Day 3
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We had an early breakfast at 5:30 and then began our hike to see the lost city!

Since we were stopping back at this camp for lunch we were able to leave some of our things here and have a lighter pack for the climb. My pack was still pretty heavy since I was carrying the drone but it was nice not to have to carry all of my clothes (I was able to leave some out to dry while we hiked). One thing I forgot to mention is that it is hot here! Like seriously hot. I've been hiking at a pretty quick pace which hasn't helped which leaves me drenched after hiking - so getting the clothes to dry is great. A few people in our group didn't bring fresh clothes for each day and I seriously don't know how they do it.

The start of the hike was relatively flat we crossed the river a few times. The last time we crossed the natural bridge that had been there had washed away so we had to take our shoes off and cross. It wasn't too bad, the water was knee deep at the worst and the current was relatively mild.

After the river began the stairs. Since we were the last group to leave camp in the morning there were a lot of other people in front of us. That didn't stop our guide and me from quickly ascending the 1200 steps passing people on the side of the stairs. As usual we were the first of our group to the top (the first part of the lost city). I flew my drone around a bit to get some cool pictures while I waited.

Once the rest of the group arrived our guide told us a little bit about the lost city. At first I thought that what we were seeing was it, which if I was honest was a little underwhelming after all the hiking and effort it took to get here. I was excited to find out that there were hundreds of these circles and that this was only the first section of the lost city. Some other interesting bits of information, all the circles used to be houses (there is another area where some of the tribe now lives), the city was built over 1,000 years ago and was "lost" - when it was abandoned by the Tairona people during the Spanish colonization - until it was discovered in the 1970s by treasure hunters. Since then the government took steps to protect the city.

Since our group was the last to leave in the morning we had the benefit of being the last ones in the lost city which meant there was no one else but us when we left each section. The lost city is often described as the Machu Picchu of Colombia - I think Machu Picchu is just as "grand" if not more so however the difference is there are way more people at Machu Picchu (since they are literally buses up there). The isolation and solitude of the lost city was super cool and in my opinion makes it better than Machu Picchu.

After exploring the first section and taking some pictures we continued onward and upward to the main part of the lost city. Of course I had to take some cool drone shots at the main area.

After walking through the main area we got to the main vista - which if you didn't have a drone would be the best spot for photos. We waited for a bit while our guides went and prepared a snack plate for us. Again we were the last group left so we had the vista to ourselves.

After taking pictures our guide gave us some more information about the lost city. I learned (and already knew from my sister) that the city is closed to tourists in September so they can cleanse the city of any bad spirits and for more restoration and cleaning.

After we finished the snack plate. which was delicious. We started to make our way to another part of the city when we ran into the Mamo (basically the leader of the tribe). Apparently our guide knows him and I guess he's kind of a big deal since he's on the 50,000 peso bill.

We bought bracelets from the Mamo which support the tribe (they were donation based but it's suggested 2 pesos which is like 50 cents USD). Our guide is in the process of helping film a documentary so we also saw the Mamo sign some sort of permission agreement for the film.

After talking to the mamo we continued to the next part of the city, where the current tribe actually lives. We also got to peak inside one of the huts which apparently doesn't happen often (our translator who has done the hike 20 times had never seen inside before). I don't have picture but basically just a hut with some furniture and a fire smoking in the middle (which helps keep the bugs away).

We continued on looping back past a ton more circles until we got back to the top of the steps.

We made our way back down the steps, across the river and back to our camp. We took a break there to swim in the river and to eat lunch which was chicken rice and beans.

After eating we packed all of our stuff back up and started the trek back. We made it through the muddy trail and stopped again at the fruit stop, where we saw the Mamo again at the shop (at least I swear it was him in the shop, if not it looked exactly like him).

We did the "happy hour" part of the hike in reverse. The translator was running down the happy hour trail so of course I tried to follow running with my massive pack. We ended up getting to camp well before the rest of the group so I took a dip in the river to cool off.

After relaxing in the river I hung clothes out to dry and had some hot chocolate. We played some more of the Tuepen card game and ate popcorn before having dinner. We also learned a sad story about our translator - apparently she was in a car wreck with her family and was the only one to survive - she was in a coma and had broke both her legs. She loves hiking the trail because at one point she thought she'd never be able to walk again, crazy.

After eating we went to our beds, it started raining slightly so there were a bunch of frogs under our beds, I guess because it was dry? So I we to sleep to the sound of ribbits.

item.title: Day 8 Lost city Hike Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
The final day of the hike! I was ready to get back and see Becca! We woke up and had breakfast which was eggs bread and fruit.

After breakfast we packed up our things before starting the trail back. We hiked back past the Kogi and Wiwa village and made a stop at for watermelon after about 30 minutes. The guide decided to lead the first part of the hike today so we were going a much slower pace. However, after the fruit stop he allowed Pilar to lead and she along with a translator from another group decided to run the trail back, so of course I followed. It was a fun trail run, tough with my large pack but it wasn't too bad.

We made it to the first camp we stayed at in record time. Since we got there so early I decided to jump into the swimming spot, I was drenched in sweat anyway so I didn't really care if I dried. We had a quick snack of chocolate cake and filled up on water before finishing the rest of the hike (I didn't run the final bit).

On the way back a younger dutch guy, Lars, from one of the other groups caught up to us and I talked to him for most of the hike back to the village. He was most surprised to hear about how little vacation we get in the US (he had been traveling for over a month).

We finally ended back at the same restaurant that we started at. I took a quick shower and then waited for the rest of the group to arrive (they weren't that far behind us). We ate some lunch which we had picked on day one. I had beef which was delicious.

After eating the cars came and picked us up. I said bye to half of the group (that was in the other car) and then we drove the 40 minutes to get out of the mountains to the main coastal road. At the road a driver from the beach hotel Becca was staying at met our car and drove me back to the beach resort to reunite with Becca! It was only about a 15min drive.

Once I met back up with Becca she informed me of how bad my bag smelled and made me put everything outside to air out before showing me the resort. There was a nice pool and it there was also direct access to the beach.

We took a look at the beach and then hung out at the pool and relaxed.

Becca got some food for lunch, I had an ice cream since I already ate. I had a taste of Becca's food, chicken curry, and it was delicious.

After lunch we hung out in the hammocks by the beach.

We ate dinner at the resort (there really isn't anywhere else to eat unless you drive somewhere I guess). The food was really good, I had the stir fry.

After dinner we went to bed, unfortunately no air conditioning here but the bed was really comfy and it was nice to have a lot of space finally!

item.title: Day 6 Lost City Hike Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 5a for an early breakfast of eggs an arepa before getting packed and ready to start hiking again.

The first part of the hike was still in the farmer land. We hiked mostly uphill for about an hour till we got to the end of the farmer land and had a break for some watermelon.

After a short break we continued hiking another 30 minutes mostly downhill and “Colombian flat”, which means lots of ups and downs but no elevation gain at the end 😂. Before arriving at our first indigenous village of the wiwa.

At the village one of the tribesmen gave us a demonstration and told us about the culture of his tribe. One of the scared items they have is called a poporo, it’s a dried out gourd that they give to boys when they become a man. They fill the poporo with crushed sea shells. The man will then chew coca leaf and use his spit and the crushed shells to create a plaster like coating on the outside of the poporo. You can tell how “wise” someone is by the size of their poporo.

After the village we walked further to a Kogi village (one of the other tribes. The way to tell them apart is that the kogi’s live in Round houses while the Wiwas live in rectangular ones. There was on rectangular house in the village because a wiwa married a kogi.

We continued walking until we reached the lunch camp. Lunch was good it was soup, chicken, and rice. This is the camp we stay at tomorrow on our way back from the lost city. We ate and rested here until about 11:45 when we started the second half of the hike for today.

This part of the hike was called “happy hour” because you hike uphill for one hour in two sections after a flat section in between (2 for one deal!). We took a short break on the ridge near some houses. I took out the drone and took some videos and photos.

After resting we continued about 15 minutes uphill for our fruit stop. This time we had pineapple and oranges. Very good. There were a ton more cute dogs on the trail and at the camps.

After the fruit stop it was another hour approximately to get to the camp (near the base of the lost city). It was a very muddy hike to the camp.

When I got there I showered and threw my clothes on a line to dry and dry. It’s super hot here so very sweaty hiking!

I got into my swimsuit and went for a quick dip in the river next to camp. It was super refreshing!

After the river we hung out and learned how to play a Dutch card game called toepen (pronounced two pen). It was a really fun game and good to play with a lot of people! They brought us popcorn and hot chocolate while we played.

We ended up having dinner around 5:30. It was pasta with meat and bread, not too bad for being in the middle of nowhere. After eating we all hung out for a while before getting ready and going to bed around 7:30

item.title: Day 9 Buritaca to Cartagena
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in and had breakfast at the hotel. I had pancakes! They were great!

After eating we hung out in the room until our drive came to pick us up and take us to Cartegena. We decided to get a driver because we needed one regardless to get back to Santa Marta and an airplane would have cost more and likely not saved anytime (4 hour drive) and no direct flights. Also the bus would have cost only slightly less total.

Unfortunately we ran into some bad traffic on road which according to our driver was due to protests. We were dead stopped in traffic and it was a somewhat sketchy area. In typical fashion Becca really had to pee so she went to a small shop near the road. The drive ended up taking 5 hours which I still think was faster than flying, but we basically spent an hour sitting completely stopped in traffic. We finally made it to our hotel to check in at 3:30. The best part about the hotel was that it had air conditiong!

We relaxed in the room and got some Powerade's and snacks from a nearby store. After relaxing we took a cab downtown (about 15 minute drive) and ate dinner at cafe Del Mar a restaurant on the city wall known for its great sunsets. Unfortunately it was cloudy so the sunset wasn't great but it was still a good spot to eat.

After dinner we walked around for a bit to explore. The restaurant is in a very touristy area called the old city with tons of old shops, curches, and squares. This part of the city is completely surrounded by walls (cafe del mar is on top of a corner of the wall).

After some exploring we took a cab back and enjoyed a nice cold night of sleep at the hotel.

item.title: Day 10 & 11 Cartagena
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was a lazy day, we slept in and had the buffet breakfast at the hotel - it was delicious. They had so much food! After eating we hung out in the room and then down at the pool. Our hotel is on the beach so you can walk from the pool directly out onto the beach.

At 12 I walked to meet my kiteboarding instructor. I had learned a little bit about kiteboarding from a friend/coworker previously and wanted to learn more (lessons here are super cheap relative to the US). My instructor was the "english speaking" instructor, however his english was very basic - which I actually think was good, he explained things to me in the simplest way possible.

We practiced flying the kite on the beach to start and then made our way into the water to practice body dragging. Unfortunately after about two hours it started storming so we had to stop. Originally I planned for 5 hours (since the lessons are so much cheaper here than in the us).

After paying Becca and I hung out in our hotel room during the storm. The rain was supposed to let up around 4 so we decided to book a free walking tour in downtown Cartagena at 4pm (free walking tours are great by the way and most major cities have them). We took another taxi from our hotel to downtown, the roads were flooded driving there but luckily the rain completely stopped when we arrived.

Before the tour we made a quick stop for some ice cream and then met the tour group, it was only two other people besides Becca and I. The tour explored most of the old city of Cartagena we started on the walls and then made our way to the plazas and churches. The old city area is relatively small maybe a mile by a mile so we were able to see almost all of it on foot.

After the tour we decided to walk to another nearby neighborhood called Getsamani. This neighborhood is know for it's graffiti and it also had a sloth park. Unfortunately we didn't see any sloths when we walked through it.

We walked through the neighborhood through one of the main squares and through the "flag street" before finding a place to eat dinner. We ended up stopping at an Italian restaurant. I had a baked zitti dish and Becca had a steak. The food was really good!

After eating we walked through the "umbrella" street (I swear they have these everywhere) and then we made our way back to the gate of the old city.

Umbrella street

Gate back into the old city with the clock tower

After walking through the old city again we made our way out to the main road and took a taxi back to our hotel to sleep.

Day 11

Final day in Colombia! I did some work in the morning and then we had a big breakfast at the hotel buffet.

We decided to hang out at the hotel all day, we grabbed some snacks at the nearby grocery store and went to the pool for a few hours.

After the pool we went back to our room and packed up our stuff. My shoes were basically destroyed from the hike so I ended up leaving them. We took a quick cab ride from our hotel to the airport. Our flight was at 3pm and went to Miami. Becca got flagged for extra screening for some reason. The Cartagena airport is pretty terrible, no a/c and one small terminal for all the international flights which was jam packed while we were there. I had a quick snack from the one food shop which took about 20 minutes to get because of the long line.

We landed in Miami on time and decided to eat at an Irish pub for dinner.

Our flight to Jacksonville was at 10:30pm - very late. Luckily we got bumped up to first class for some reason, which was nice even though it's only a 45 minute flight. I was actually able to sleep on the plane. We arrived 12:30 and hustled to catch our shuttle which was a quick 10 minute ride to our car. We then made the 2 hour drive home and reunited with the dogs and then finally go to sleep! Unfortunately I had work the next day, Becca was smart and had the day off.

Overall a super fun trip and as always excited for the next adventure!

item.title: Olympic & Rainer National Park
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Here's a quick re-cap of our annual national park hiking weekend trip.

Day 0 - Thursday

Becca had the day off and I worked from home until ~1:30 when we loaded up the car and drove up to Charleston airport (we got a cheap direct flight to Seattle in Alaskan Air). The drive up took about 2 hours and by the time we got through security they were starting to board. The flight took about 5.5 hours and we arrived at 7:30 pm. There were some great views of Mount Adam’s and Mount Rainer on our approach into SeaTac.

Once we arrived we grabbed our car rental (a Ford Bronco) and drove another ~2 hours to our Airbnb in Sequim (pronounced “swim”). We arrived around 10 pm and went to bed.

We were originally hoping to stay with and visit Becca’s sister, however they ended up moving to North Carolina like a month before our trip! :(

Day 1

Today we woke up pretty early (3 hour time zone difference helps). I made a quick trip to Walmart to pick up some snacks and breakfast food while Becca napped. We cooked eggs, sausages, and bagels for breakfast. We got ready and had a bit of time to spare so we played a Sequim version of monopoly our Airbnb had before heading out around 8:40. We didn't get to finish the game but it's basically the same as monopoly just themed for Sequim.

We drove about 10 min to the Sequim valley airport where I was going to do the wing walking! Wing walking is pretty much exactly what it sounds - you get to walk on the wing of an airplane while it's flying and then do a bunch of aerobatic maneuvers. I think saw it online somewhere and when I found out they did it in Seattle I couldn't pass up the opportunity. Luckily I have an awesome supportive wife who was happy to let me do it (as long as my life insurance was up to date). Once we arrived we met Marlyin (the owner) and her daughter at the airplanes to sign all the paper work and then start training. It's a small family run operation and they were super personable and friendly.

The training consisted of lots of practice knowing where to step, how to climb up, and how to use the buckles (for the top position). Becca ended up going to do another short trail while I did the training.

We ran through the movements about a dozen times each. There were 5 other people there, one girl ended up leaving early because she could barely get on top of the wing while it was on the ground (they don't charge you anything until right before it's time to fly because they don't want people to feel financial pressure to do it). Two of the other people were from Chicago, one from India, and one from Brazil. Luckily I was going to be the first to go (because I was the first to contact them about booking).

Unfortunately, there was a bit of rain so we were delayed a few hours. Thankfully the weather cleared up after lunch. Becca ended up getting back from her hike and bringing me a hot dog from Costco to eat. We finally ended up starting the plane around 3pm, after warming up the engines I got in the front seat and we taxied for takeoff!

The plane was really cool, an old open cockpit Stearman (a bi-plane) I decided to do both the upper and lower wing positions. Getting up on top and strapping in was the scariest part (you're literally "held on" by a small cable and a carabiner/harness). Also reassuringly when I asked about the procedure if you were to fall Marilyn said "don't fall" and there was no procedure besides trying. to pull yourself back up. Once I was strapped I gave Mike (the pilot) the signal and we did 6 aerobatic maneuvers (loop, hammerhead, and barrel roll). The loop was the most intense because you pull 2-3 Gs (as if my legs weren't shaking enough just being up there). The hammerhead was also fun because you get weightless (0 G) at the top of the maneuver.

After the upper wing I climbed back into the cockpit and then walked out to the left wing. This side you aren't strapped in at all, you just hold on to the spear looking thing for dear life and do the same aerobatic maneuvers...it was a blast.

The flight took about 30 minutes in total and was exhausting! Once back on the ground we loaded back up in the car and drove across the peninsula and hiked to a beach called second beach. The beach was very picturesque, since I was the first one of the group done wing walking we had plenty of time left in the day to explore. We walked down the beach, I took some drone videos and we enjoyed the sunset.

After exploring the beach we drove to our tiny Airbnb in Forks and made some pizza for dinner before going to bed.

Day 2

Another fairly early wake up today. We made some breakfast again in the Airbnb, eggs and sausages, before packing up the car and heading an hour to our first stop the Hoh rainforest.

We did 3 hikes here - the first was the hall of mosses loop which as you might have guessed had lots of moss! It was growing over all the trees and looked really cool.

The second hike we did was the spruce nature trail. Another similar hike through the Forrest. Both trails were a bit over a mile long and flat.

After the two loops we made a quick pit stop and dropped some of our warmer clothes off at the car (it was warming up) and then hiked up the Hoh river trail. This trail goes for miles and miles, I think you can basically walk across the whole peninsula, however we only walked about 3 miles up to the mount Tom creek campsite. We stopped for a snack and break at a small shady spot on on the river shore and I also flew the drone around for a bit.

After we ate we made our way back up the trail to our car. We definitely timed the hikes right this morning, by the time we were back it was super crowded. We arrived a little before 8am and had no problems parking.

Next we drove to the Sol Duc falls trailhead. It was about an hour and a half drive. It’s actually super close to Hoh river and if you wanted to you could hike there (about 26miles), but instead we had to drive almost a complete circle around the mountains to get there (75 miles).

We arrived around 2pm and luckily found a parking spot up near the trail head. This was a super short trail only about 1.6 miles out and back. The falls were really cool, a bit crowded (definitely a popular trail).

I ended up walking a little further down another trail to the lovers lane falls while Becca relaxed and waited for me. The second falls weren’t nearly as impressive, but they were totally deserted so that was nice. After seeing the falls I hiked back to Becca.

We hiked back to our car from the falls and then drove up to crescent lake. There was a small beach there we relaxed at, it was more pebbles than sand but the views were nice!

Afterwards we drove to our next Airbnb in Port Angeles and had some quesadillas for dinner. The Airbnb was cool it had a huge garden and small lake in the back yard and was surrounded by trees so it felt very secluded.

Day 3

Today we had another early start, we ate some hard boiled eggs and bagels for breakfast before heading to hurricane hill. We heard they were doing work on the parking lot and only letting a certain number of cars in so we wanted to get there early we left around 6am and got to the trailhead about 7am with only a few cars in the parking lot.

The trail is very accessible - it’s completely paved and only 1.6 miles total, hence the popularity. We made the hike up to the top, there were awesome views of mount Olympus and the surrounding mountain ranges. I got some cool drone shots and we explored around the top for a bit.

While exploring around the ridge we found a few marmots hanging out so I went over to say hi to them. After hanging out for about 15 minutes we made our way back down to the parking lot (which was now completely full).

We drove about an hour back up to lake crescent Becca only wanted to do the one hike today so she dropped me off at the storm king trailhead and then went to the nearby beach to relax.

The storm king hike was great! About 4 miles and much steeper than all the other hikes so far (about 2,000’ elevation gain. I hiked up fast and was exhausted by the time I got to the top. At the very final section they had ropes so that you could use them to pull yourself up the steepest parts of the trail.

The top had a great view of the lake. I took some pictures, droned, and had a snack before heading back down to meet Becca.

At the bottom of the mountain I did another super short trail (~1mile) to see Marymere falls. It was pretty crowded but worth seeing since it was so close.

After the falls I made my way over to the beach where Becca was. Overall the whole hike only took about an hour and 40 minutes. We relaxed and rested some more on the beach for a couple hours and we had a few snacks.

Around 2 pm we made our way to the other side of the lake to do a short hike (~2 miles round trip) to a place called the devils punch bowl. I had heard about some cliff jumping there so naturally we had to go.

We luckily got a close parking spot (it was crowded) and made our way to down the trail. The punch bowl is basically a little cove with a bridge crossing over the one side. There were tons of people and multiple places to jump in the water from (it's really deep). I decided to skip all the smaller jumps and just go for the tallest one. It was about 30’ high and was a ton of fun! I jumped twice while Becca took some pictures and video. The water was super refreshing, cold but not freezing.

After drying off we made our way back to the parking lot this time going through an old train tunnel.

Next we drove to a place near the lake called Granny's cafe. We were looking for ice cream but all the had was soft serve so we ended up getting milkshakes instead. They were decent, hit the spot after a long day of hiking.

We continued on to our Airbnb in Tacoma (about an hour and a half drive). On the way we picked up some food at an indo Asian restaurant Becca’s sister recommended (I had Pad Thai - really good). At the Airbnb we ate and went in the hot tub to relax before going to bed.

Day 4

Today was an even earlier morning than yesterday (somewhat of a trend now). We woke up around 4:30 am and left the Airbnb at 5am to make the 3 hour drive to sunrise camp at Rainer national park.

We started the bourroughs hike trail, the weather was perfect so the views of Rainer were awesome! We did a counter-clockwise loop, starting with the climb up to Sourdough Ridge this was definitely the best way to go sa you get views of Rainer the whole time.

We had a snack and rested at the second borough - Becca made friends with a little mountain squirrel.

I hiked further to the third Burrough while Becca waited and relaxed on the second burrough. We have radios which is nice because we can communicate even though there is no cell reception.

After exploring the third burrough for ~15min I hiked back ~2 miles to meet back up with Becca on the second burrough. On the way back we continued the loop down to shaddow lake and back to the parking lot. The full hike was about 9.5 miles and 2,500' elevation gain.

After we got back to the car it was still early so we decided to drive another 2 hours to the south side of Rainer to a place called Paradise where a bunch of other trails start. I did the skyline loop while Becca decided to hang out near the car in the hammock. The skyline loop was much more crowded (the start of it was paved and more accessible).

The loop was a bit shorter than the burroughs hike (5.6 miles and 1,700' gain). It took me about an hour and 40 minutes to hike. I took a few pictures on the way up but didn't end of taking. thedrone out. This is the trail you would start on to summit Rainer (unfortunately you need a permit and all day to do it).

I met back up with Becca after the hike and we drove back to our Airbnb in Tacoma to relax in the hot tub and have some quesadillas for dinner before going to bed.

Day 5

Another early morning, we left the Airbnb at 4:30am to drop off the rental car and catch our 7am flight back to Charleston. The rest of the travel back went smoothly. Another successful national park trip in the books! Looking forward to the next one when Bennett is here!
