item.title: Istanbul - Day 0/1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I worked from home today, then we made our way to the airport to catch our 4:30pm flight to Philadelphia. We had a 4 hour layover in Philly, so we ate dinner at a smashburger place by our gate. Our second flight left at 11pm overnight to London. We arrived at Heathrow around 11am. Our final flight to Istanbul got delayed ~1 hour so we left at 2pm and landed around 8pm. We caught a taxi from the airport to our hotel in the center of the old city downtown ~1 hour drive. We checked in, our room was nice and so was the hotel. The spa was open until 10pm so I went down to try out the sauna for ~15min before it closed. After the sauna I went down the block to grab some late night food. I got a kebab and pide ( Turkish pizza) from a restaurant the hotel desk recommended.

Day 1

Today we woke up around 7:15 and ate breakfast downstairs at the hotel. The breakfast was a buffet and overall pretty good.

After eating we went back upstairs to get ready and then walked to the blue mosque, which was about half a mile away. it took a minute to find the entrance- there was only one, but there were a bunch of exits. Once we got in we were able to get into the blue mosque really quickly and take some pictures.

It looks really cool on the outside, to go inside you had to remove shoes, cover your knees and your shoulders, and women had to cover their heads. Surprisingly the blue mosque wasn’t really that blue inside.

After the blue mosque, we walked literally across the street to Hagia Sophia, which is another large mosque. We realized the line for Hagia Sophia was way longer, and ended up having to walk almost all the way back to the blue mosque to get in line. The line went relatively quickly.

It only took about 15 minutes to get inside, this mosque was much bigger and older looking than the blue mosque. We stayed inside for 5 to 10 minutes before heading out. Both Hagia Sophia and the blue mosque had free admission, but you have to time your visit around the prayer times.

Next we went a little further up to the main gate of the Topkapi palace. The palace is a huge complex. You had to pay $35 each to get in (which to be honest was a bit much, however the other two were free, so it balanced out).

We started by going to the harem of the palace. It was a secluded corner with lots of rooms where the 500 concubines lived.

After the harem we made our way counterclockwise around the grounds of the palace. There were tons of different areas and rooms you could go in- including the throne, hammams, the kitchen, etc. In one of the areas they had a museum of relics, which consisted of a bunch of random items the most interesting been the prophet Muhammad’s tooth and lots of his beard hair, they are very proud of these items.They also had lots of gemstones and a famous Topkapi dagger. After exploring with felt like over 100 rooms, we decided to leave the palace.

On our way out we stopped at an ice cream shop where they did a little show before giving you the ice cream. It was pretty funny and the ice cream was pretty tasty (I had chocolate and pistachio).

After the ice cream we continued on to Gülhane Park. This is a small park underneath the walls of the castle. We walked about a half a mile and saw the famous column of the goths, which is apparently one of the oldest Roman columns that still exists today. Honestly it wasn’t very impressive, but worth a quick stop since it’s right there.

The park let out right along the coast, so we walked down it. Here you could see both Europe and Asia being split by the Bosphorous strait.

We walked along the coast until we made it back to our hotel, which was again about half a mile away. We ate lunch at a small restaurant right by our hotel. I had a kebab wrap and Becca had kebab meat. It was really fast and good. We also tried Buffalo yoghurt, which was meh.

After eating, Becca was tired, so she decided to go back and rest at the hotel while I walked to the Suleymaniye Mosque, which was about half a mile the other direction from our hotel. Along the way, I stopped at the Egyptian bazaar which was a big market with tons of spices and fruits and other food.

The mosque was on a hill and had a really cool views of the city and water. I went inside the mosque, and it happened to be during prayer time which was interesting to see.

After visiting the mosque, I made my way back to the hotel along a different route to see the grand bazaar. This was essentially a huge street market with tons of different sections, grouped by the type of thing they were selling. For example, they had a gold section and a jewelry section. After walking through the bazaar I walked back to the hotel. Along the way I saw another ice cream shop so I had to try.

Back at the hotel, Becca and I went down to the spa to relax. I did the sauna and then we did the massage pool and the Turkish baths.

After the spa, we went up to the roof of the hotel to grab a snack before our Bosphorus cruise. We had hummus, and I tried the local beer. Views from the hotel were really nice.

We stopped back at the room after eating and I flew the drone a little bit to get some cool pictures.

We got picked up for our sunset cruise at 5:30. It was about a 10 minute drive to the port. The boat was fairly big and there were a ton of people. We got there fairly early so we were able to get a good seat. The worst part was some of the people felt like they had to take pictures of every single thing so they were constantly moving around and getting in our space to “get the shot”.

The cruise went up the Bosphorous strait about an hour, with a tour guide, explaining a bunch of the different buildings and monuments and attractions along the way. There were a ton of different mosques. Apparently the more minerets the more powerful the mosque, the most we saw was a newer mosque that had 6 minerets and was big enough for 40,000 people to pray at once (surprisingly only the eighth biggest in the world).

The tour included cookies and tea on the boat. The boat stopped on the Asia side for about an hour for shopping. However, there wasn’t really much to do on that side, so Becca and I walked down the street and then went back on the boat.

After the stop, the boat made its way back to the port, and we got dropped off back by our hotel. We made a quick stop for some dinner and Turkish delights- which we got to go and ate in our room before going to bed.

item.title: Kas Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 7:20. We had breakfast again downstairs at the hotel before packing up and checking out. We had a taxi pick us up at 8:30 to take us to the airport (there are two airports in Istanbul, this one was on the Asia side). The taxi driver tried to charge us a different amount than what the hotel told us which caused a bit of drama, but we worked it out.

Our flight left around 11:30 am, and we arrived in Antalya at 1 pm. Overall a quick smooth flight, we flew in over the Mediterranean on our approach and had nice views of the coast.

I got the rental car- we had to wait 20 minutes or so which would not have been so bad, however it was scorching hot outside. After we finally got the car we were off to Kas which is about a 3 Hour drive along the coast with beautiful views the whole way.

Before going to our hotel, we made a stop in the town to check in with the local dive shop and grab some food. The lady at the shop recommended a restaurant for dinner called ora kebab. The food part was OK (I had an adan kebab) but somewhat pricey. I also had a chocolate milkshake which literally tasted like water, it was probably the worst milkshake I’ve ever had, I didn’t even drink half of it.

After eating, we went to the main Square to grab some ice cream before heading to our hotel and checking in. We are staying at Hotel Cachet, which is on the Kas peninsula. The hotel is pretty sweet we have our own pool & patio outside our room and view of the Mediterranean.

After unloading our luggage we went down to the cliffs/beach area of the hotel, and jumped in to test the water, it was refreshing and super clear. Afterwards, we hung out in our pool before going to bed.

item.title: Kas SCUBA day 3
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7:40 for breakfast at the hotel at 8. Breakfast was good, I had an omelet and fruit. The views of the Mediterranean were awesome.

After breakfast I went down to the room and got ready before heading into town to SCUBA. Unfortunately Becca’s not allowed to SCUBA so she hung out at the hotel to relax. I surprisingly found a parking spot in the city close to the dock. I got to the boat a little before 9, got all my gear and we were off around 9:30. The boat itself was pretty massive, there were about 25 divers on board and the boat even had its own air compressor on board. Kas is a huge diving town because of how clear the water is, there are about 25 dive companies in the small port of Kas- all with their own dive boats.

We cruised for about an hour to the first dive spot. We were going to dive at Bisemi but the current was too strong, so we went a little further to Conan brunu-tunnel.

Our group was the last to go in, there were 5 of us Rory (England), Ramona and Dorian (Swiss), and our guide Aytun. Everybody was super friendly and nice. Our first dive went smoothly. We were under for about 45 minutes with a max depth of about 105’. The highlight was a swim through- a very large tunnel that was formed by the rocks.

The current was pretty strong, so I was tired after the dive. Ramona was actually low on air, so Aytun shared some with her at the end of the dive.

After the dive we relaxed and had lunch. They made a big spread of rice, salad, chicken, and bread. It was good! At lunch I got to know our group better, apparently Dorian and Romana are road tripping in their camper van for 6 months, and went all the way from Switzerland to Mongolia (crossing through Russia and Kazakhstan)- wild! Every time I talk to Europeans I’m jealous of how much vacation they get, and how easily they have access to other countries in Europe and Asia.

After lunch we cruised back towards the port and stopped for our next dive at Hevbeli Ada island.

Again our group went in last. This is a much shallower dive than the first with and average depth of 30’ and a max of 60’. There were small pieces of wreckage from a boat. We dove down and around the seagrass and then between the two islands. The main highlight for me was the calamari (squid). We saw a big group of them at the end of the dive.

After the dive we got all of our gear sorted and then cruised back to the port. We got back around 3:30. I went back to the shop to pay (they only took cash) and then hung out with our dive group for about 30 minutes before leaving to meet back up with Becca at the hotel.

Becca and I hung out at our pool and relaxed for a while. A little before sunset we drove towards the city and made a stop at Antiphellos Ancient City- old ruins of an amphitheater that were cool and had a good view of the sunset. Parking there was super easy and only a 1 minute hike to get to from the car.

We hung out at the top for a bit and I flew the drone around to get some cool shots.

After hanging for ~15min we walked back down to the city to get some dinner. We found a cute little restaurant tucked away in an alley called Naturel. The food was really good, we had humus appetizer and I had the falafel balls and lamb ravioli, Becca had the lamb shank.

After dinner we wandered around the town some more and stopped again for some ice cream. We also found a cool pillar looking column (we later found out was an old tomb) in the middle of one of the streets. It’s really cool how preserved some of these sites are and how the town is build around them.

Today’s ice cream shop was better than last nights. After eating we walked around the town a little longer before going to the car and heading back to our room to relax (watch some Indiana jones) and then go sleep.

item.title: Kekova Kayaking Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 7:30, got ready, and packed for our tour before heading up to breakfast at 8. We had a quick breakfast because our guide was picking us up at 8:15 to take us kayaking over the sunken ruins of Kekova.

We met our guide, Barbaros (aka Barbie) at the top of the road going to our hotel. He was in a big van and was worried it would be too steep. It was just us in the car so we ended up switching to a smaller vehicle before making the ~30 minute drive over to Kekova. Our guide was super friendly and talkative. It turns out he’s lived all over the world from California to Denver to Germany to Nepal and many others, always working as a tour guide- a really interesting life.

Once we arrived at the port we stopped at the local store for some waters before meeting up with the rest of our group - a family from London area on holiday, also super friendly and nice. At the port we got all the kayaks and gear ready and then made our way into the water. Becca and I shared a double kayak.

Our first stop was about a 3km paddle which didn’t take too long, the water was really calm and there wasn’t too much wind, the stop was in a small Bay area of Kekova island. These ruins were not protected, so we were allowed to swim around them as well as climb and explore.

We put the kayaks on shore and swam around a bit. We saw some small puffer fish and a school of calamari. We also saw some of the old structures/foundations of buildings from the town. After swimming for a few minutes we went back on land to explore around the area. There were a bunch more ruins. We climbed up a small hill of ruins and could see both sides of the island it was a really cool area to explore.

After exploring for a bit we went back to the shore and the guide gave us a small history lesson of the island. Kekova was a prominent city during the Lycian and Byzantine periods until an earthquake destroyed most of the city and submerged it underwater.

The guide also let us try a type of bean that is similar to caco, I thought it was really good! You just have to watch out for the hard seeds.

After talking about the history we got back in the kayaks and started paddling up the coast going over some of the ruins of the city. These ruins are protected, so we had to stay in the boat. With the water so clear you could easily see the structures. It was really cool, I took the drone out and flew to get some shots while Becca paddled for us :). Some of the structures we saw were cisterns that stored rain water, a bath house, and an old clinic where sailors had to quarantine for forty days before being allowed into the port (so they wouldn’t spread disease from town to town).

After paddling down the coast we cut back across towards the mainland city of Simena. We beached the kayaks here and then had lunch at a restaurant on the shore. The food was good: salad, rice, chicken kebab skewers, and bread.

After eating we had time to explore so we hiked up to the top of Kaleköy, a castle. The hike was super short but steep. The views from the top were really awesome.

We met another American couple at the top (we really haven’t met many Americans yet this trip). After hanging out and enjoying the view we started to make our way back down making a stop for some ice cream and a view. this time we were more adventurous I tried prickly pear and fig flavors and Becca tried pomegranate and goat milk. They were all pretty good!

After the ice cream we met back up with the group down by the docks and loaded back onto the kayaks. We kayaked through a really shallow area with a tomb in the middle of it. The tombs resemble an upside down boat. They contain the body in the bottom. If you were very wealthy, your favorite slave was buried with you…apparently it was an incentive for the slave to take good care of their master so they had a long life. If a family wasn’t as well off, they would share them. So when the next family member died they would take out the bones of the person in the tomb and replace them, putting the original inhabitants bones it the catacombs. Although most of the tombs had been robbed they did find some intact. In those they found jars that were full of tears from all the family that mourned their death.

We continued paddling to another shallower area with a small island. We tied up the kayaks and swam for a minute. Our guide asked if anyone liked cliff jumping…yes please! We swam to the other side of the island where there was about a 15’ jump. Not the biggest I’ve done, but still fun! I jumped 4 times while Becca watched and took some photos.

After cliff jumping we got back in the kayaks and paddled back towards the dock we started at. Along the way we saw a massive cemetery with all those big stone monuments. In the past, they would be stand alone as a way to show wealth and importance, but once the Romans came they grouped them together into a necropolis- cities of the dead.

After making it back to the dock we put away all the kayaks and gear, and then drove back to our hotel in Kas. Overall the tour was awesome, mostly because of our guide Barbaros. If you’re ever in the area I highly recommend Lukka outdoor kayak tours.

We chilled at our hotel pool for a while and then made our way into town for dinner. We had dinner at a place a little ways up the hill called Nazende. It had a nice terrace overlooking the dock and town. The views were really nice for sunset. For dinner we had hummus as an app and I had grilled meatballs and Becca had seabrim fish. The food was decent.

After dinner we made our mandatory stop for some ice cream which we ate by the square. This time I had cookie and brownie flavor and Becca had Nutella and strawberry yoghurt, all very tasty.

After eating we walked through the city and stopped at a small shop to get some Turkish delights, it’s a common candy treat in turkey that is super tasty- kinda like a gummy bear but better. Anyway I started to ask the shop owner for two rose flavored ones and then two of another flavor and then he literally started shoveling in handfuls of Turkish delights of every flavor 😂. I had to stop him before he got too carried away (they sell it based on weight so I guess he was trying to load it up!). Even after having him put a good chunk back we ended up with just over a kilo of Turkish delights 😂😂.

We made the way back to our hotel and watched some more Indiana jones before falling asleep.

item.title: Hadrian’s Gate & Chimera Day 5
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in a bit and woke up at 8:15. We then made our way up for breakfast on the terrace. I had another omelet and they had some mini pancakes today that were tasty (especially with Nutella). Becca had menemen- a Turkish dish of scrambled eggs and tomatoes…it tastes kind of like sundried tomatoes and herbs with eggs.

After breakfast we got semi packed and then went down to the cliff/beach area to relax. We hung out on the cliffs and did some mini cliff jumps into the water, I even got Becca to do one with me!

The water was much calmer early in the morning and was really refreshing. We hung out down there for a few hours before making our way up to the main pool (just to say we tried it) and then to our private pool until we had to get all packed up and checked out at 12.

At checkout we drove down into the city for lunch. On the walk from our car we made a quick stop at the ruins of a temple from Antiphellos.

No idea how we didn’t see these ruins before they’re literally 2 steps from the sidewalk and we walked by at least 3 times before this.

While looking for a place to eat in town, the first few restaurants we went to (higher on the hill) were all closed, apparently 12:30 is too early for lunch. We did find a place called the marina restaurant down by the main square. I had a cheeseburger and Becca had shrimp, the food was pretty good.

There was a cat that smelled Becca’s shrimp and tried to sneak up and steal a bite.

We finished lunch around 1:15. We made a quick stop at the store for some more waters, then drove to see what we thought was Hadrians Gate, about two hours away.

We actually ended up in the ruins of an ancient city called Phaselis. It was ~$15 to get in for the two of us and ended up being super cool. There were so many ruins and 3 beaches. The ruins were actively being restored in parts but you could climb and wander around the ruins to your hearts content. We learned the city was founded in 690 BC and was known for its harbors. It was an important center for trade and commerce. The city was influenced by The Persians, Egyptians, Roman’s, and the Greeks (a melting pot of culture).

There actually was a Hadrians gate at the site. We later found out there are several monuments known as Hadrians gate built to commemorate the the Roman emperor Hadrian’s visit to the city. This gate wasn’t really a gate- more like the ruins of one. It turns out the most famous gate is in Antalya. Other famous gates are in Athens and Jeresh (Jordan) which I think I’ve seen both.

We explored the ruins of the city for a while and climbed up to the amphitheater to take some pictures. I flew the drone to get a few arial shots. The complex was huge with multiple harbors, temples, and even a massive aqueduct.

After exploring the ruins we made a stop at the beach to relax. I went in the water while Becca laid out and took a nap. The water was super refreshing. The beach was mostly pebbles but it felt good on your feet when you walked, like a little massage.

We hung out at the beach till around 4:30. We changed and explored one last part of the city, the north port which was literally on the beach. It was crazy to see a bunch of beach goers laying out next to all these ruins, just a normal beach to them I guess.

After the beach we backtracked a little ways to the town of Cirali to see mount chimera. We planned our day so we would get there just before sunset, and our timing ended up being perfect. The mountain is known for the continuous flames that come out of holes in the rock at the top. It’s caused by methane leaking out of the ground and igniting with the air.

Mythology says a guy named Bellerophon tamed Pegasus, then used a lead spear to kill the Chimera- a mythical creature with the body of a lion, head of a goat, and tail of a snake….. and it could also spew fire. One version of the myth says Bellerophon was tasked to kill the chimera after declining the advances of Queen Anteia, who then turned around and accused Bellerophon of trying to seduce her (the ol’ switcheroo). The king, Proteus, then tasked Bellerophon with killing the Chimera in hopes he would die in the process (he couldn’t just sentence him to death because he was a hero). Anyway this is supposedly the mountain he killed the Chimera on and that’s the real reason for all the fires.

Before getting to the start of the hike we stopped at the local market to pick up some marshmallows and chocolate to make s’mores, it was an idea Becca had to take advantage of the fires :).

The entrance to the hike cost 50 lira for both of us which is on like 2 dollars (totally worth it). The hike was 1 km, all uphill and they had signs every 100 meters telling you how much more you have left.

The hike took 15-20 minutes. The fires coming out at the top were super cool! It was just before sunset so we got lots of pictures with light and also as it got darker.

And of course we roasted some marshmallows and made some s’mores using a stick we found. Everyone was jealous of us.

As the sun started setting I took out the drone and got some shots of the area.

After hanging out at chimera we made our way back to the car (it was dark now so we used our headlamps). Next we drove ~1.5 hours to Antalya, making a quick stop for gas before getting to our hotel right by the airport. As a side note the water pressure in Turkey is amazing- every shower we’ve had has been like a powerful massage, it’s awesome.

item.title: Cappadocia Day 6
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got up at 6 and drove ~10 minutes to the airport and dropped off the rental car. We flew sun express which is a budget airline - the check in process was smooth, but our flight got delayed an hour. Once we were in the air the flight was a quick 50 minute hop to Kayseri airport. As a side note much of the farming in this area is done in greenhouses to protect the plants from the scorching sun, so you end up seeing towns full of greenhouses.

We had to wait for the rental agency again - this time a random guy met us in the parking lot and gave us the car - there was no office or anything. We got another fiat rental car which looked fine on the outside, however we very quickly found out that the air conditioning did not work at all which was unfortunate because it was really hot outside.

We made the ~hour drive to a stop just outside Goreme (the town where we were staying) at a place called the Zelve open air museum. It cost ~$10 per person to enter and was a path through The Valley with tons of buildings that were cut into the rock that you could explore. It used to be a monastery. They had stables for livestock, a winery, food storage cellars, a church, and housing. It was really cool we explored a bunch of the caves. I took my drone out to fly and got yelled at almost immediately so unfortunately no good shots, just one video.

The Zelve valley was an early settlement dating back thousands of years, and habitants carved homes into the volcanic rock. During the night and 13th century’s, Zelve became a monastic retreat for Christians and was a significant religious center. One of the caves we explored was a really big church.

Further into the area (zelve is spread over 3 valleys) there were more cave houses you could climb in. One had a 10’ chimney type section I climbed up. Becca waited patiently for me while I climbed around:).

After the zelve museum we drove into town and checked into our hotel (at 2pm). We’re staying at the sora cave hotel, it’s up almost at the top of the hill in Goreme, and as you might have guessed, built into the mountain as a cave. Really cool and the hotel manager is super friendly…almost too friendly lol.

After checking in we went to grab lunch at a nearby restaurant called the wooden spoon. The restaurant was also in a cave and you sat on cushions on the floor to eat. I had the meat pide (pizza) and Becca had a diced lamb dish. We also tried Aryan, a salty yoghurt drink, I guess it wasn’t bad but I wouldn’t order it again. The food was good though!

After eating we went back to the hotel to rest for an hour. At four we went downtown to the bike shop to see if they had availability for mountain bikes this weekend. The guy there was super nice and they did have availability. Afterwards we went to a café called kings café, and had milkshakes. I had strawberry and Becca had mango. They’re both good but very sugary.

Afterwords, we went back to our hotel to rest until we went to Uchisar Castle (also built into rock) right before sunset. The castle was about 15 minutes away, and a little higher than Goerme and at the top had awesome views of the city and surrounding Valley’s. The Goerme vista was on the way to the castle so we made a quick stop there for a photo.

The castle was a bit crowded, but we were able to get some cool pictures and I was able to get some good drone shots.

After sunset, we made our way back down from the castle and drove back to our hotel. Becca was hungry, so we ended up going to a restaurant called Turkish ravioli so she could get a snack before we went back to the hotel and to bed.

item.title: Hot Air balloon, underground cities, & ATV Day 7
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up super early at 5:10 and got picked up from our hotel shortly after 5:30 for hot air ballooning! Cappadocia is known for its hot air balloons, so this was a must do for us. We were the last ones picked up in our transport van and we made our way ~15 minutes directly to the balloon launch site. The balloon company was called THK and recommended by our host. Every morning over one hundred balloons fly, and some of the companies are more sketchy than others so it was good to go with a trusted one.

There were a few other balloons at our launch site setting up. It took them about 20 minutes to get the balloon rigged up and inflated. There were already a bunch of balloons in the air so we took some pictures of them while we waited.

Once the balloon was inflated we hopped in. The basket is very large, 8 sections of 4 people. Becca and I got lucky and got on the corner section of the balloon. After everyone was loaded we took off.

The flight lasted about an hour. It was really cool to see all the balloons up in the air- I lost count around 100. The balloons don’t have any real control besides altitude, so they end up drifting whichever way the wind blows them. Once in the air we saw a very ominous cloud of dark smoke - we later found out that one of the buildings in the town caught on fire (at first we thought maybe it was a balloon crash).

We ended up drifting over the town of Goreme and then landed in a nearby field. The pilot and crew did an excellent job landing, putting it down directly on the trailer. After they strapped down the basket we unloaded and they had a celebratory non-alcoholic champagne and flight certificates for us lol.

After the celebration we were dropped back off at our hotel. We took a nap before getting breakfast on the terrace at 8:30. Breakfast was a buffet with tons of options, they even had gluten free bread for Becca.

We stayed at the Sora Cave Hotel. It has an upper terrace, and the best view is below. Goreme is pretty hilly, and this hotel is near the top. It is about a ten minute walk up the road to an excellent balloon view point (we went up another morning).

After eating we rested in our room for another hour before heading out to the underground city of Derikuynu. Derikuynu is about 30 minutes south by car.

The parking guard tried to get us to pay for parking on the street next to the entrance, we ended up driving literally a block over and parking for free (kind of a scam, there was tons of parking). Entrance price was about $8 a person for the cave. This cave is apparently the deepest in the area and was thought to hold 100,000-300,000 people.

The cave was cool, luckily not too crowded. There was a worker at the main cave entrance who gave us a tour of the first level before asking if we wanted an official tour, which he tried to sell us for $30 so we politely declined. We explored the rest of the cave system. There were tons of tunnels and different rooms. They had an area for all the horses and live stock, wells, churches, wineries, basically everything you would need to live. When the community out grew their current living situation, they would just carve out more rooms. Some of the tunnels got really tight- I explored them while Becca waited.

There was a really large room in the lower level of the cave that was an old church.

We explored around the the underground city for about an hour, it was actually smaller than I was expecting it to be. They don’t allow tourists to access the entire system. Once we got out we took a quick picture with the city sign before getting back in the car.

Our next stop was back towards Goreme at a town called Kaymakli that had another underground city. Although this cave system was supposedly smaller it definitely felt a lot more expansive- higher ceilings and better added lighting and infrastructure. Because of that there were a TON of tour groups and people. Which made it very slow to move around in since many of the passageways only fit one person. The other problem is the cave system doesn’t have the best ventilation so it was pretty hot and humid which results in lots of crowded people sweating and not the best smelling cave haha.

We explored around for probably 40 minutes before making our way back up to the surface. The entrance area had a pretty cool model of the cave system. There is a theory (unproved) that all the different caves in the area and ones 100s of miles away are all connected by underground tunnels.

There was a large empty parking lot area near where we parked our car, so we took advantage of the opportunity and I showed Becca how to drive stick shift. She did super well! After practicing around the parking lot for 20 minutes we switched back and I drove to Goreme and we stopped at an Indian restaurant for lunch.

We both had the chicken tikka Masala with rice and I also got garlic naan. Very tasty! The price of the food was pretty expensive but at least it was good!

After lunch we made a quick stop in town at Oze coffee shop, it’s a coffee shop owned by our hotel so our first drink was free. We tried a Turkish coffee - basically a very strong dark coffee. It wasn’t too bad just a little gritty for me.

Afterwards we made our way back to our hotel to rest until around 4:30 pm when we were picked up for our ATV tour. Originally Becca wasn’t going to go originally, but changed her mind when she found out it was on set dirt roads and not free roaming.

The ATV tour started at the main office area which had to have over 100 ATVs- there were so many of them! We paid, got helmets and our ATV. I drove the first leg which was to the sword valley ~15 minutes away. The tour was as I expected, follow the leader not going very fast or doing anything wild on the ATVs, but the scenery was nice!

We stopped at sword valley for ~10 minutes, we took some pictures and I droned before getting back on the ATVs. There were tons of ATV groups, I think our group had about 12 ATVs (24 people) and 2 guides.

After sword valley Becca drove the ATV to our next stop (she actually drove more aggressively than me!). Our next stop was the lookout point of love valley. The annoying bit about the ATV tour was there was sooo much dust when driving, we did our best to drive to the side of people (instead of directly behind them) to avoid the dust cloud but it was really unavoidable.

At the love valley viewpoint we took some pictures and I flew the drone some more before we got back on the ATVs and made our way to our final stop at sunset point.

Luckily we got to the sunset point relatively early so there weren’t as many people there. We got some nice pictures and drone shots on the point before a TON of people showed up. Disliking the massive crowd Becca and I hiked ~5min over to another spot that was much less crowded and also had some awesome views of the valley and the sunset.

After sunset we got back on the ATVs and made our way back to the starting office point. After dropping off the ATVs we got dropped back off at our hotel. We decided to hang out on the terrace and relax for a bit, I had got some Turkish wine to try out and also was researching potential routes for mountain biking tomorrow.

After hanging out for about an hour we were hungry so we walked down to the main strip of the city and had dinner at a place called Fatboys. The food was really good, I had a meat stew thing and we split some nachos.

After dinner we made our way back to our hotel to sleep.

item.title: Mountain Biking & Sunset Day 8
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 5:20 to go and watch the hot air balloons. We were attempting to go to a spot that the two Swiss people I met from SCUBA diving recommended. Unfortunately we realized very quickly that google maps could not be trusted! It ended up trying to get us to drive up this tiny path carved into the rock that only hikers were going up. At first I was going to try and drive it, but it became clear very quickly that there was just no way the car would fit. We looked at the map and found another route that looked promising so we circled back and went around the city to get to the other road. Fortunately we were able to get to the spot!

There was one other group of people there but there were plenty of secluded spots so Becca and I made our way to the precipice of one of the ridges, and laid out a blanket to watch the balloons. The views were great and of course we took a ton of pictures… and I did some drone flying.

After watching the balloons for about an hour we made our way back to the hotel for a quick nap until 8:30, when we went up to the terrace for breakfast. The buffet was mostly the same as yesterday, very good and filling.

After eating we rested a bit more in the room before I got my things ready and made my way down into town to rent a mountain bike. Of course Becca was not going to be able to mountain bike so she booked herself a Hamam (Turkish bath/massage) to do while I was away. Unfortunately they didn’t have any other day bike tours going (I knew this because I called in advance) but they did have bikes so I was able to do a “self-guided” tour. They did give me a google map of the bike routes and some general guidance of which ones to try.

The bike was super nice, a newer Trek mountain bike, they also gave me a fairly large bag of repair items and tools just in case I blew out a tire or something. I started off by going to the valley just north of the city. The bike ride up to the top of the ridge was strenuous, some guy tried to stop me and get me to pay for the viewpoint but after some

discussion he let me go. The views at the top of the ridge were nice. Trying to follow the directions using the GPS map was difficult - there are so many different paths you can take! Before making my way down the valley I took out the drone to try and get it to follow me as I went. It worked…sort of I could hear the controller hitting buttons in my backpack as I hit bumps. I got some good footage before it stopped recording.

The ride down was a lot faster than the way up. This first valley was relatively easy. I decided the drone footage wasn’t worth the hassle so I put it back in my bag and continued to follow the GPS.

The next ridge was even more of an uphill slog to get to it turns out I had to go up the same path we tried to take the car up! It was difficult enough just to ride the bike up it! In general the trails had a lot of ruts in the center you had to look out for (caused by the rain). I eventually made it to the top of the ridge overlooking the valley. This valley was called Meksender valley, at the top of the ridge I looked down at the trail and thought no way - it was way too steep for me (especially by myself), so I decided to stay on the ridge and ride over to the next valley.

The ride over wasn’t too bad as it was mostly flat and not too far - the next valley over was called the red valley, it was much more touristy, so I had to pass some people on the way down, but there were a ton of different paths to take so it mostly wasn’t an issue.

This valley was a little bit steeper and more technical so it took a bit longer to get down. After I made it down it was mostly flat and I ended up right near the town of causvin. I decided I would do one more valley (I think I had been riding for an hour and a half and about 10 miles at this point).

The last valley the shop recommended was the love valley. Unfortunately the directions were not clear and I ended up going the wrong way and going up the love valley instead of up the road next to it (and then down). The way up the valley was quite a slog to get through. I had run out of water and was cramping which made it even more challenging. As a plus though there were some cool rock formations and I also found a cool tunnel.

Thankfully I finally made it out of the valley and to the top of the ridge, there was a guy there who was selling drinks, but of course he didn’t have any water, only pomegranate juice, so I decided to keep going until I found another shop that had some water. Since I was on top of the ridge it was mostly flat. I made it to the main road and passed by the sign for Uchisar (the castle town) so I took a quick selfie.

Just down the road from the Uchisar sign I finally found a small little restaurant so I stopped and had to waters and a flavored tea drink to rehydrate and rest.

I was pretty spent at this point and was ready to meet Becca for lunch. I only had a short way back on the road to the bike shop and it was all down hill so it was super easy and went quickly.

All said and done the ride was just over 15 miles and 2,000 feet of elevation gain- pretty solid. It definitely would have been better with a guide but still worth doing self guided.

After I dropped the bike off at the shop I met Becca at the main strip down town and we decided to go to a restaurant called China Quick, it had a bunch of different Asian cuisine. We both had the chicken pad Thai and I also ordered some fried rice (I was super hungry).

After eating lunch we took the car back up to the hotel and rested for a bit until ~30 minutes before sunset. We took our hotel concierge’s advice and took a short hike up to an antenna at the top of a ridge overlooking the city. The hike was super short and the views of the city were great. We stayed until a few minutes after sunset. I brought the rest of the wine up to enjoy with the views.

After the sunset we made our way to dinner at the top deck cave restaurant (we made reservations for the day before when we tried to go but they were too busy). The restaurant was in a cave which was cool and was super busy again. The food was really good. I had the Turkish ravioli and we also shared a plate of mezze (basically hummus and other dips with bread/veggies). Becca had the lamb. The food was really good and it was also the cheapest dinner we’ve had yet.

After dinner we made our way back to the hotel and went to bed.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: That looks amazing! Looks like y’all had a great time!

item.title: Cappadocia -> Istanbul -> Home Days 9 & 10
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 9 Cappadocia

Today we woke up at 5:20 and left the room at 5:40 to make the short hike back up to the antenna to watch the balloons fly. There was someone already there with a full on picnic setup, but luckily our spot right under the antenna was still open. We set up our blanket and enjoyed the show.

I think this spot is probably the best place to watch the balloons- they’re literally all right there above the city. Of course we took a ton more photos and drone shots. I even got a cool Timelapse of about half of the balloon flights (I wish I thought to start it sooner).

After about an hour of watching the balloons most of them landed, so we made our way back down to our hotel for a quick nap and then another breakfast buffet. Our host was kind enough to let us have a late checkout today, so after breakfast we napped some more and hung out in the room until 12:30. After packing our things we checked out and made our way to the car. Since we had already done all the things we really wanted to we decided to go check out the Goreme open air museum. This one was right under where we watched the balloons yesterday. We avoided paying for parking by parking a block away on the street and then walked up.

We were able to walk into one of the main churches that was filled with lots of paintings. The paintings were supposedly preserved over the years by pigeon poop (according to Becca) and were only found after they started cleaning the walls.

After seeing the church we walked up to the main entrance (where you actually had to pay). The price was close to $20 USD per person and since we already saw the church paintings (which was the main differentiator from Zelve) we decided to skip it. Of course Becca took advantage of their free bathroom before we went back to the car.

We drove towards causvin, only a few miles away, and stopped for lunch at a place called Causvin pide. The food was pretty good and there seating was outside underneath a ceiling made from the grape vines and trees. I had the meat pide and chicken skewers. The pide was good but the chicken was pretty dry. There were also a bunch of flies that would not leave our food alone which was annoying.

After eating we walked into the center of the town, it was a little further than we realized and super hot. Supposedly there was a church there, it ended up being on top of the ridge, I made it there and took some pictures while Becca waited for me at the bottom of the steps. The church was cool, some deteriorating paintings and really big, all carved into the side of the mountain. Cool to see and kill time but not worth going super out of the way to see.

After the church we made a quick stop at the market to get some water before making the ~1 hour drive to Kayseri airport for our flight to Istanbul. Before getting there we made a quick stop for gas.

Our flight to Istanbul went smoothly, unfortunately we had to check our bags for Turkish airlines so we ended up having to wait ~20 minutes at the baggage claim before getting our bags. To make matters worse the line for taxis was MASSIVE. We ended up waiting at least another 20 minutes or so before finally getting a cab. I wish that was the end of it…but no. I showed the cab driver our hotel on google maps and he acknowledged it, which to me indicated that he knew where he was going…I couldn’t be more wrong. Not more than one minute after we got into the cab he said something in Turkish which seemed to indicate he had no idea where he was going. I helped him out showing him my phone again and he tried unsuccessfully to get the hotel in his phone’s GPS. No problem - I gave him my phone and we were off again, the hotel was only 10 minutes away so we should be there soon….nope. I loaded the directions in my work phone as well to “check” where he was going. Even with the directions from my phone he missed the turn. Becca and I immediately were telling him to take the exit and he seemed to have no idea what we were talking about. He continued driving, this time we were hyper aware of where he was going. The GPS re-routed us to have us go back the way we came and even with us literally yelling at the cab driver to take the exit, he decided to continue going the wrong direction. At this point we were livid and screaming at him, I even pulled out google translate to tell him to turn around. Finally he obliged, the 10 minute cab drive turned into a 30-45 minute ordeal.

When we finally got to our hotel the cab driver came inside with us and the receptionist helped translate. After all of that the drive still wanted us to pay for the whole bill. We told him tough luck and paid him 200 lira (which was in my mind a fair price if he went the correct route - the bill on the meter was 400). I later read that the taxis in Istanbul are basically terrible and not to use them lol.

Once we checked in (around 9:30) we got our room and went to bed.

Day 10

Today we woke up at 5:10. After the night before we were paranoid about the taxi to the airport so we wanted to give ourselves ample time. Luckily the taxi showed up quickly and the ride to the airport went smoothly. We had to check-in for our flight in person and the line took quite a while. After checking in we made our way to our first flight, to London, which left on time. We made it to London and the caught our next flight ~2 hours later to Miami. The Miami flight was relatively empty so I had an aisle seat with in the middle section with two open seats in the middle which was nice. After about 8.5 hours we made it to Miami. Unfortunately we had quite a long layover until our flight to Savannah ~9:15pm.
