item.title: Day 1 & 2 in Roatan
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 1

We woke up at 3:45am to get ready, pack the car, and head to the airport. I dropped Becca and Bennett off with the luggage, and then parked the car so they could get checked in quickly (we couldn’t check in online because we had a lap infant).

After parking the car I walked in and met Becca at the check-in desk for American. It turned out that whoever Becca had talked to on the phone from American to add Bennett as a lap infant only put him on the first flight to Miami and not the second flight to Roatan?! It made absolutely no sense and the agent she was talking to was SUPER rude and unhelpful acting like it was our fault. It took over an hour and the manager to come by - they made us pay for Bennett again at the desk and the best part was - after we paid again he still wasn’t on the ticket! At that point I think the manager realized that something was wrong with their system and let us go (using the receipt as proof to board with Bennett) and try to fix it on their side while we were in the air. I also forgot to mention that they charged Becca a $30 bag fee even though she is an American card member and it was supposed to be free. Not happy with American Airlines today!

As a result of all this craziness, we barely made it through security in time and got to the gate just as they were about to close. Even though Bennett wasn’t listed on the second ticket we were able to show the receipt that we had paid and they let us in the flight. STRESSFUL!

The flight to Miami was mostly empty. Becca and I each chose two random empty rows at the front of the plane (we honestly didn't care we just grabbed the first seats we saw). Bennett did really well on the flight, I held him in the chest carrier and he slept the entire 1.5 hour flight arriving in Miami at ~7am.

Once we got to Miami we went to the American help desk since we had 5 hours before our next flight. Unfortunately they weren’t able to help us but told us to fill out some forms on the website. So TBD on the compensation process.

My mom arrived in Miami a few hours later at 9:45 and met us at the gate (we're all on the same flight going into Roatan). Bennet had fun hanging out with my mom at the gate until our flight which left just after 12.

Shortly after Bennett passed out :D. We decided to block out Bennett's face for all the photos he's in (since this blog is publicly accessible to anyone).

Becca somehow (unrelated to all the ticket drama) got upgraded to first class - I say unrelated because she was upgraded the night before we left. She was able to talk to the gate agent and get me in the exit row as a consolation - which was nice to have the extra leg room. Because I was in the exit row Becca had Bennet with her in first class. She was sitting next to a guy dressed in all green with a big green hat, who later Becca mentioned was visibly texting people about how annoyed he was to be sitting next to a baby :D.

Luckily for him Bennett did great and slept all the way through the short 2 hour flight over to Roatan. We landed around 12pm - thanks to Bennett we got the priority lane through immigration/passport control. Becca and my mom waited for the bags while I got the rental car. The airport is super small so it didn't take long before we got everything. We had to squeeze everyone into the tiny rental car (a Kia picanto), but luckily the drive to the VRBO checkin was only 15 minutes away. The property was ready for us early which was nice, so we drove another 15 minutes to the VRBO and got everything unpacked and settled in.

The VRBO was very nice! Just a short walk away from the main strip of West End where all the shops and restaurants are. The place itself was massive, it was on the second floor and had a big open kitchen and living room with 3 separate bedrooms and a big balcony looking out into the Caribbean sea. It was right on the beach and had a small pool on the first floor deck.

After unpacking and settling in we walked ~2 minutes into town. Our first goal was to find a shop to dive with for the week. Unfortunately it turned out to be more difficult than we originally anticipated - the first few shops were either already closed for the day or were full. Fortunately we stumbled onto the Reef Gliders dive shop (which turned out to be awesome). They had a phone number on the door so even though they were closed for the day we were able to contact them and get on the schedule for the following morning. They also said they would be able to take us to one of the wreck dives that we were interested in!

After figuring out the diving we stopped for dinner at a place called Anthony's chicken (highly recommended on Reddit)

I had the jerk chicken and a salva vida beer. The chicken was really good!

After eating we stopped to pick up some basic groceries for breakfast, then stopped at a dock bar and had some giant margaritas. They were good but we ended up leaving early because Bennett was getting overheated.

We spent the rest of the day out by the pool and enjoying the sunset. The sunset was a bit cloudy so not much to see. Bennett thought it was hilarious everytime I would dunk my head under water and pop back up.

We also took a few family photos before heading back up and going to sleep.

Day 2 Wednesday

We woke up early today and ate breakfast at the VRBO, I had some scrambled eggs. We left at 8am to walk to the Reef Gliders dive shop to check in for our morning dives and get our gear in order. The plan was to do two morning dives, one at 9 and one at 11.

We met our dive guide, Louden who was young and really friendly. He briefed us on our first dive which was going to be at a dive site called Chief's Quarters. The dive site was only about a 5 minute boat ride from the dive shop (that's the best part about diving in Roatan - all the dive sites are right off the shore)!

The dive itself was good - max depth of 72' and average of 40'. We swam around the reef and saw lots of fish and cool coral formations.

After the dive we made the short boat ride back to the dive shop and did our 1 hour surface interval hanging out there on the dock. We had some snacks and met our next dive guide, Gigi. Gigi briefed us on our next dive - which was going to be in half moon bay at a dive site called Vern's Drop Off.

We geared up and made our way back on the boat for another quick ride to the dive site. This dive we started out on the reef and also made our way out to the wall for a max depth of 78' and average of 45'. Some notable things we saw were a moray eel, sea turtle, and a sleeping nurse shark.

Bennett SCUBA diving with us and checking out the turtle and eel! :D

After the dive we took the boat back to the dive shop and then went to grab a quick bite to eat....or so we thought. We stopped at the papusa shop on the way to our VRBO and it ended up taking much longer to get our food than we expected - the food was good though! Once we got our papusas we took them back with us and ate at the VRBO - Jamie and Nate had just gotten in so we got to hang out with everyone.

We hung out until dinner time and then we walked back into town to go to a place called Blue Elephant Thai. The food was good- I had pad thai of course!

After we finished eating it started to down pour, so much so that the power went out in the whole town (apparently a common thing). So we decided to wait it out ~20 min until the rain stopped and then walked back and went to bed.

item.title: Day 3 in Roatan
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 3 - Thursday

Today we woke up early for our two morning dives with Reef Gliders. I ate some eggs and toast for breakfast before walking over to the dive shop with Becca. Jamie and Nate started their open water dive training at a place called West End divers. Our first dive was the Aguila wreck which was a bit further away from the dive shop. Gigi was our dive guide again for this dive. She gave us a quick brief of the site at the shop before we left.

The max depth of the dive was 107' and an average of 61'. At the start of the dive we saw a bunch of grass eels and some sucker fish that were all over another one of the divers in our group. The wreck itself was super cool! It was a massive cargo ship that was sunk in 1997 (a typical thing they do to promote reef growth). We got a bunch of cool pictures with the GoPro.

Inside the wreck!

The front of the ship

Swimming back through the reef

After the dive we made our way back to the dive shop to do our surface interval. My mom ended up walking over to see us with Bennett so we got to see him before our next dive.

Our next dive was with Gigi again at a site called the 3 brothers (for the 3 channels that are in the reef).

This dive was more shallow: 71' max 45' average. We saw a turtle and a moray eel!

After the dive we ended up eating some lunch at the dive shop with Jamie and Nate (they walked over after their dive). I had a fish burger and Becca had shrimp tacos - both were really good!

Jamie and Nate had one more dive at 2 pm for their training, so after eating Becca and I walked back to the VRBO to hang out with my mom and Bennett. Once Jamie and Nate got back we continued to hang out at the pool. By the time we decided to get dinner it was Bennett's bed time so we ended up going into town to pick up some food while Becca stayed back with Bennett. We went to a place called Beachers.

While we were waiting for our food Nate, Jamie, and I decided to go get some gelato from a nearby shop. The gelato was good, but you had to eat it quickly because it melted so fast!

When we got back to Beachers my mom was talking to a "cowboy" who had moved from Texas to live permanently in Roatan. The guy was very friendly and was telling us his life story and trying to sell us an island tour. Thankfully our food came shortly after so we grabbed it and walked back to the VRBO to eat with Becca. After dinner we went to bed, diving is exhausting!

item.title: Brazil Day 0/1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 0 - Thursday

We made our way to the airport after work. This time it was much smoother checking in on our Delta flight to Atlanta. Delta actually let us check in before we even got to the airport, but we still ended up getting there two hours early just in case. The only small hiccup we had was while waiting for the airplane. Bennett pooped on Becca :).

Other than that everything was on time and the weather was great. We even boarded a little early and got our seats, but unfortunately, shortly after everyone boarded the pilots announced there was a problem with the GPS that they had to troubleshoot...you literally can’t make this up! Fast-forward two extremely frustrating hours later and we’re still sitting at the gate when finally the pilot announced they fixed the issue and we can go. So we left Savannah at 7 pm instead of 5 pm, and our connecting flight in Atlanta was leaving at 8:10. This meant essentially zero chance of us making the direct Rio flight.

We landed and got to the gate around 7:50. Of course the terminal we were at was on the complete opposite side of the airport from the Rio flight. I still had some hope since the plane hadn’t left yet, but by the time we de-boarded our connecting flight was taxiing away from the gate. It was super frustrating and stressful.

Fortunately, Delta automatically rebooked us onto another flight. The only bad thing was this flight went to São Paulo instead of Rio, and then had a three hour layover in São Paulo before going to Rio. This put us into Rio about seven hours later than we expected. To put a cherry on top when we got to the gate, they told us we would not have a bassinet, couldn't guarantee seats next to each other, and Becca would not have a gluten free meal.

This new flight departed at 10 PM so while we were waiting, Becca went back to the Delta service desk and they were able to get her some meal vouchers so that she could have something to eat on the flight. She ended up getting three Qdoba steak bowls with the $50 in vouchers Delta gave her (This was generous compared to the $70 we got for the two of us from American when we had to spend the whole day in Miami).

The new flight departed on time and in our first bit of luck, we ended up getting the whole four seat middle row to ourselves! This was a lifesaver! I was able to get a little bit of sleep on the flight by laying across the seats and even on the ground at one point. Bennett on the other hand, slept the entire nine hour flight until just before landing when they turned on all the lights and made a bunch of announcements.

Once we landed in São Paulo it took forever to get our gate checked stroller back. Fortunately we got to go to the front line for immigration so it kind of balanced out. We had to re-go through security (fortunately they didn’t care we had water in our backpacks). And then made it to our gate. Our flight to Rio left at 12:20pm and took about an hour to get to Rio. It took us an hour to figure out where enterprise rental car was, there were absolutely zero signs for it. We finally realized that enterprise was called localiza here, and then we had to wait for a shuttle at the very far end of the terminal (there were literally zero signs for this). We finally made it to the localiza office and got a “ password” (basically their version of a next in-line ticket). We waited for about 10 minutes . While waiting there was a friendly lady talking to us who basically said why are you going to Rio (implying that it’s not great for tourist), she also reminded us (probably the fourth person) to be careful of pickpockets and which areas you drive/grow go through. After the 10 minutes, they finally called our password and we checked in and got our car!

We loaded up and drove towards the Christ the Redeemer tram. Fortunately, we found a parking lot near a Pickleball court/church. It was only a few blocks away to the station where we able to get tickets for the 3:40 PM tram which departed 5 minutes later. The tram ride took about 20 minutes to get to the top. The statue itself was massive and really cool to see, also the views from the top were really nice. We could see Ipanema and the main center of Rio. Supposedly, it wasn’t very crowded, but there were still a ton of people at the top (I would hate to be there when it’s actually crowded). we took a few pictures and then left shortly after (way too many people and we were exhausted). We couldn’t figure out how to pay to leave the parking lot so we ended up following another car out.

The Airbnb was only 15 minutes away, and the traffic actually wasn’t too bad. We parked at the Airbnb lot and made our way up with all of our stuff. We unpacked a bit and I showered then we went to a steakhouse on the corner called Garota de Ipanema. Becca saw the people next to us with a sizzling plate of meat and told the waiter we want that. I also tried a chopp (basically a small cold draft beer) and Becca had a caprinha (their version of a mojito). The food was really good. You actually had to cook the meat on the sizzling pan. It was sliced really thin so by the time you moved it to the middle of the pan it would cook in a few seconds and then you would flip it to the other side. It was super delicious.

After dinner, we made our way to a nearby gelato shop and split a cup of gelato. We walked back to the Airbnb to wind down and get some sleep for the night. Quite the adventure for the first day.

item.title: Brazil Day 2 - Rio
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6:30 AM, I took a shower and hung out while Becca and Bennett slept another hour. Once they woke up, we got ready and went to a nearby breakfast café a block away from our place. At breakfast I had eggs, sausage and toast. We also got some eggs for Bennett. While we were eating, some ladies came up to say hi to Bennett. They loved him, we had no idea what they were saying though.

I also got a few pastries to try back at the Airbnb. We walked back and got ready for hiking. We left around 9 AM for a hike called Pedra da Gavea which was about a 20 minute drive west of Ipanema. We were able to drive right to the start of the trailhead and park there which was nice. The last bit of road is a little rough, but otherwise it’s not too bad. Here’s a really good blog. Post with lots of details if you want to do the hike.

https://www.halfwayanywhere.com/hikes/brazil-hikes/hiking-pedra-da-gavea/

We started the hike around 9:30 am after checking in at the guard shack. The hike was relatively short- only 3.3 miles round-trip. However it was very steep with a 2600 ft elevation gain. I carried Bennett strapped in the chest carrier. And carrying an extra 23 pounds of Bennett definitely made it more of a challenge!

There were also a few spots where we had to scramble up using our hands and legs. I had to be really careful to make sure Bennett didn't hit his head and that I didn’t fall. There were a few spots that had chains bolted to the rock that you could hold on to.

Bennett pooped right before we left so we thought we would be OK. However he pooped again while we were hiking so we had to change him on the trail 😅. My sister did the hike last year so we knew there was one spot that was particularly challenging, called the carrasqueira, and she had to use ropes to get up.

When we got to the start of the carrasqueira there were no ropes, but it’s seemed manageable to climb up so I strapped the carrier up tight and started climbing. Bennett and I climbed up. However, Becca was worried about how much further the climbing area went on, and about how we would get down with Bennett, so she wanted to turn back. So I started to down climb back to her, which was much more difficult than climbing up. Fortunately, we made it back down to the start where Becca was going to wait for me while I went to the top. But then we ran into the rope guy who was just getting there and setting up, and he told us we could easily do the ropes with Bennett.

So we waited for about 20 minutes for the guy to set up. Then we harnessed up and climbed up with the ropes on. After the climbing section, it was another 15 minutes to the top. There were awesome views and we took a bunch of pictures.

We hung out at the top for about 20 minutes before making our way back down. We ended up taking the ropes down as well, which was far easier than trying to down climb.

We got back to the start around 2:30pm, so about five hours of hiking. Going with Bennett definitely slow us down a bit. I think 3 1/2 to 4 hours would definitely be doable. It was a super fun hike. I highly recommend it.

We made the 20 minute drive back to our Airbnb where we showered and relaxed for a minute. Then we walked to the Ipanema beach which is only a block from where we staying. The clouds rolled in, so it was a lot cooler, but there were still a ton of people on the beach. They had a bunch of volleyball courts, but not everyone was playing traditional volleyball. A lot of people were playing with their heads, chest and legs (no arms).

We walked down to the north end of the beach where we found a restaurant to eat at called Colarhino. Becca and I got the filet mignon steaks, they were really good. I also got a craft beer, an IPA that was really good.

After eating, we walked down the Copacabana Beach, and then walked back to the Aporador (basically a viewpoint), which was supposed to have good views for the sunset. Unfortunately, it was too cloudy to see anything so we walked back to the Airbnb. Of course we made a quick stop for some gelato on the way 🙂.

At the Airbnb, we hung out for a little bit with Bennett and then went to sleep

item.title: Brazil Day 3 - Rio
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6:30 again, Bennett was up a lot and Becca didn’t get a whole lot of sleep. They ended up waking up around 8:20 and we left to go get breakfast around 9:30. We had breakfast at another restaurant just a block away called Empório Jardim na Praia. It was really busy and the food was good. I had scrambled eggs with sausage and a hot chocolate, which they said was chocolate milk but was basically pure liquid chocolate.

After breakfast, we walked through the nearby park on the way back to our Airbnb, it wasn’t much to see and it was slightly drizzly. There were two metro entrances, one on each end of the park. Back at the Airbnb we got ready and left to go on a free walking tour of Santa Teresa, a neighborhood in the historic area of Rio. We ended up taking an uber so that we wouldn't need to worry about trying to find parking there (Ubers here are actually super cheap - if we didn't have Bennett then we probably wouldn't have rented a car).

We met our guide, Lola, at the main square of Santa Teresa along with the rest of the tour group, about 30 people (fairly big). We started the tour walking down the streets of the town. Our guide pointed out some artwork on the walls, the town is known for it's street art. I learned that pucca shells represent the aboriginals in brazil - apparently aboriginal fortune tellers use them to tell fortunes. There is a lot of prejudice against the aboriginals in Brazil and the artwork we saw was political about equality for the aboriginals..

The city is also known for it's trolley cars that go up and down the streets (it's a very hilly town).

After continuing through the streets we stopped at a small park. Our tour guide pointed out a special tree - the Pau Brazil - which is where Brazil got its' name from. The wood produces purple and red dye, which was used for royalty very rare and expensive at that time and the tree was abundant along the Brazilian coast. In the 1500s the Portuguese explorers would cut down the trees for exportation. The word "brasa" means ember or red hot coal - referring to the color of the dye extracted from the tree and the word eventually morphed into Brazil. Also according to our guide the best violins bows are made from the wood.

Unfortunately, about halfway through the tour Becca started to feel really sick, so we dropped out. I ate lunch at a place the guide recommended. I got the mixed barbecue, which was not very good to be honest - the meat was very dry and chewy.

After lunch we walked about 10 minutes down the hill to see the Selaron steps. We accidentally arrived at the top of the steps, so we had to walk down them for the full effect. The project to revive the dilapidated steps began in 1990 by a local artist. He started by using tiles discarded from construction sites but later began incorporating tiles sent by visitors from around the world. The stairs have more than 2,000 brightly colored tiles from over 60 countries. It was really cool to see, but the steps were very crowded!

Becca was feeling even worse, so she and Bennett ubered back to the AirBnB. I ended up getting dropped off at Sugarloaf Mountain (on the way back). Because it was overcast there were absolutely no lines for the cablecars. The clouds were pretty high so there were still good views of the city.

The first of two cable cars.

At the top with Ipanema behind me - Christ the redeemer is covered in the clouds on the right.

After a quick visit to sugarloaf I went back to see Becca and Bennett. Becca wasn't feeling up for dinner so Bennett and I went out together to a nearby Italian restaurant a block away from our Airbnb. I ordered a beef lasagna and got this interesting looking dish with two different colored sauces on it (I have no idea what they were the menu was all Portuguese).

After eating dinner we went to get a quick acai for dessert - a very popular treat in Brazil.

After picking up the acai, we walked back to the AirBnB to eat the acai and hang out with Becca before going to bed.

item.title: Brazil Day 4 - Iguazu Falls
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 3am, loaded up the car and left for the airport. We made a quick stop for gas before dropping off the car and then taking the shuttle from the car rental place. We checked in with Azul Airlines, and then made our way through security to our gate. We stopped at "The House of Cheese Bread" for some breakfast. It was good! I had the traditional and a dulce de leche filled ball as well as a comically small panini.

While waiting for our flight our names were called to come to the desk. Using the translate app the guy at the desk told us they found a battery in my checked bag so I had to follow him to get it. We took a bunch of back hallways and eventually made it to my bag so I could grab the battery.

Literally no more than 10 minutes later they call us again and tell us that they switched us to a direct flight. We were extremely confused- I knew there was a direct flight with Gol airlines that we were trying to avoid (their website was terrible and they had tons of bad reviews)...also even though it was direct the flight arrived an hour later. The guy at the desk told us there were maintenance issues with the connection flight and it was expected to be delayed, so this new flight would get us there earlier (using a translate app).

So we left the gate and picked up our bags and went back to the Azul check in desk. They told us it would only be “a few minutes” while they finished up our new reservation- it ended up taking 45 minutes. While waiting Becca found out that one of the flight attendants called in sick and they had to reduce the number of people on the flight - the real reason. Also after numerous times of asking the desk lady why it was taking so long and to check on the progress- they told us they were going to put us in a flight for the next day! Absolutely not! After getting very frustrated with her she came back 10 minutes later with our reservation for the direct flight at 8:40 we were originally promised.

After that stressful ordeal we checked in with Gol Airlines and thankfully had an uneventful flight to Foz. Once at Foz we took a shuttle to the car rental (this time was much faster because we knew to look for Localiza). Once we got the car we drove straight to the falls which was only 5 minutes away.

At the falls we parked and took a double decker bus to the main hiking trail about 15 minutes away. We originally were on the top of the bus, but moved to the lower level because it was cold!

The hiking trail was short and relatively flat along a ridge that overlooked the river and the falls. The views were amazing ! Although it was a little colder the weather was perfect- sunny and not a cloud in the sky.

The trail ended after about a mile at a place called the devils throat. There was a platform that went out into the basin that catches the tallest part of the waterfall. It was the most impressive/powerful part of the falls. The platform was a bit crowded but we were able to get some good pictures (in general we were told it’s usually much much busier than this).

The falls at the beginning of the hike.

The falls in the devil's throat

After the viewing deck we took the elevator up to the top of the falls and then took a bus to the stop where they do the boat ride tours.

The tour started with a short golf cart train ride through the forest and then a short hike to the boat office check in. Our guide was really nice and spoke 6 different language, impressive! He said his dad was a diplomat so he lived all over the world.

There are two options for the tour: wet or dry. We elected to do the wet tour:).

The whole boat ride lasted probably 30 minutes . You first head upstream through some crazy rapids, then right up next to some of the falls which soaked us! The guide gave us a plastic poncho to hold over Bennett so he didn’t get too wet. They also had a lifejacket for him.

After the boat ride we dried off and caught a bus back to the entrance. We drove the car to the hotel to check in. After kind of unpacking and relaxing for a bit we drove about half a mile to a steak house called Park Foz that Jamie and Nate recommended. Becca and I shared the waygu steak platter which was pretty good though a bit overcooked.

After dinner we went back to the hotel for an early bedtime...or so we thought.

item.title: Brazil Day 5 - Jericoacoara
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We got woken up around 10:45 pm by the phone ringing in our room. Earlier I had asked the front desk about getting a to-go breakfast for the morning, and they decided to call at nearly 11pm and let me know they had it ready and could bring it up. I asked if we could pick it up in the morning and the guy said okay. However, about 45 min later the lights in our room flashed and there was a knock on the door - a guy with our breakfast…at 11:30pm ugh.

Unfortunately both the phone call and the knocking woke up Bennett, and and made waking up at 4 am for our flight even more painful. When we finally woke up for real I ate quickly (Becca didn't want anything), it was mostly fruit and some pastries (not worth the late night wake up!), then we got our car and got packed and drove about 20 min to the airport. Everywhere here has a “priority line by law” if you’re pregnant or have an infant or are handicapped - which is awesome (traveling with an infant has its perks!). So we went in that line for checkout. Unfortunately the priority line was extremlyyy slow! Otherwise though all the flights went smoothly today (thank god!). Our first flight was only an hour over to São Paulo.

After a short layover and a 3 hour flight we arrived in Fortaleza around 1 pm. Our driver picked us up to take us to Jericoacoara- about 4.5 hours away.

In the car! It was nice and spacious and our diver was very friendly.

We made a quick stop about 30 minutes into the drive to have a bathroom break and to get some food. We picked some snacks for the ride, nothing too substantial- Becca and I still weren’t feeling the greatest. Overall the drive went smoothly. We made one more stop just before the park entrance to deflate the tires (the park is all sand/dunes and no paved roads). We also had to stop at the entrance to Jericoacoara city to pay the tourism tax. We finally made it to our hotel around 6:30 pm. We unpacked, showered (the shower was amazing - the most water pressure I've ever experienced), and then relaxed before going to bed.

item.title: Brazil day 6 - Jericoacoara
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in till 8 AM. After we woke up, we went to the beach restaurant where breakfast was included. The breakfast was a buffet style with all sorts of pastries, scrambled eggs, etc. Becca's favorite was the "tapioca"- a crepe made from tapioca flour. The breakfast was good and had a great view of the beach. After eating, we decided to do a small hike to Pedra Furada (basically a big rock arch on the beach) which was about a mile and a half away.

Before walking out of town we took a quick picture at the Jericoacoara sign in the main square.

The hike was very picturesque. We hiked up a small hill and then along the coast. There were really good views looking back at the town and out down along the coast. I took my drone out and got some photos and videos. Hiking down the hill to the rock was basically a big sand dune, which of course I ran down.

The rock itself wasn’t anything too special, I mean, it was cool, but the views along the coast I thought were better.

After hanging out the rock for about 10 minutes, we decided to hike back- this time more along the coast. There were a bit of rocks at one part that we had to kind of scramble over. We also had to climb back up a dune to finally make it to the main beach where our hotel was on.

Back up the dune! Much more of a workout with a 23lb Bennett strapped to me!

Back at the hotel we decided to relax and hang out by the pool. Our hotel had two pools and both were really nice. I also decided to take the drone out and get some shots of the town in our hotel. The wind at Jeri is really strong- it is one of the top places for windsurfing, kite, surfing, and all other wind related activities. Unfortunately drones don’t do the best with wind and after about five minutes of taking some drone footage I realized the drone wasn’t able to come back because the wind was too strong blowing it further offshore! I quickly ran from the pool down to the beach and brought the drone down to a lower altitude- which thankfully wasn’t as windy - and I was able to get the drone back. It was a close one, lesson learned!

View above our hotel - one of the main pools.

View of Jericoacoara - the shot I almost lost my drone for! Pedra Furada is up the coast on the left.

After that ordeal we decided to walk through the town and find a place for lunch. We ended up at a restaurant called Jerizando pizza. The place was good. I had a meat pizza and a local beer. The pizza was way too much food for me so I ended up getting a to go box.

After lunch, we went back to the hotel and hung out at the pool until sunset. I went for a quick run down the beach. It was much easier running away from the city with the wind then it was returning into the wind. We watched the sunset from the beach, it was a really good sunset.

After the sunset, we walked into town for dinner. We ended up stopping at a place called Na Casa Dela. The atmosphere was really cool. It was outdoors with a sandy floor and an eclectic mix of antique furniture. The food was really good. I ended up having a steak with mushroom risotto and Becca had shrimp risotto.

After dinner, we stopped at a gelato store for dessert. I got chocolate, the ice cream was really good! Afterwards, we went back to the hotel and went to sleep.

item.title: Brazil Day 7 - Jericoacoara
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around seven and had breakfast again down by the beach.

After breakfast, we got ready and were picked up from our hotel to do the East Side tour of Jeri. Basically there are two different tours you can do: East Side and West Side. Our driver recommended we do the East Side tour since it’s not as active and we had Bennett to bring along with us.

For the tour we were driven around in a small dune buggy. Normally you sit on the back, but because we had Bennett, we had one person sit up front with the driver. The first stop was the sloth tree, which was about 20 minutes away from our hotel.

The sloth tree (aka Árvore da Preguiça) is basically a big tree that grew sideways due to the strong wind - kinda cool I guess!

After the sloth tree we drove through the nearby town Preá and stopped at Lagun Beach, which was a lagoon beach club you had to pay about four dollars a person to get into. The lagoon itself is really cool The water was super blue and there are lots of spots to take cool pictures. I took my drone out and got a few shots. We also jumped in and swam for a bit. The tours normally start at 9 AM so we were the first people there.

We stayed for about 30 minutes before getting back in the dune buggy and heading to the next stop. The next stop was another of the club called Buraco Azul. This one had a bit more people at it. The water here was more blue and they had a platform you could jump off of into the lagoon. I flew my drone for some more shots.

After I flew the drone, a helicopter came and landed right next to the lagoon - good thing I wasn’t flying! After hanging out for about 45 minutes, we got back in the buggy and made our way to the next stop, yet another lagoon called Lagoa Azul. This lagoon was more natural less built up than the other two. There was a beach club area that you needed to take a raft to on the other side, but Becca and I elected not to go there because it didn’t look like anything special and you had to pay 40 rials per person.

Instead, we continued to the next spot which I think was just across the water at another lagoon called Lagoa do Paraíso. Here there was yet another beach club that cost about seven dollars per person. We ended up staying here for about two hours and eating lunch. There were quite a few people at this club. It was called the Alchemist beach club. We had lunch basically in the water on the beach of the lagoon. I wasn’t super hungry so I just had fries.

They had hammocks in the water - which were actually really comfortable and are another photo stop for most people.

There is also a huge inflatable obstacle course floating on the water. Becca and I took turns watching Bennett while the other one did the course - it was fun!

There was also this weird dock that was painted so we took our picture there before we left.

We left around 1:30 pm and made our way to the final stop- Lagoa do Amancio. This Lagoon was a natural lagoon in the middle of the dunes caused by rainwater. It was super cool to see. I ran around the lagoon twice and up-and-down the dunes, jumping into the lagoon. we hung out for maybe 20 minutes. I flew my drone, got some really cool pictures, and then we made our way back to our hotel in our dune buggy.

After the tour, we stopped at the gelato shop right next to our hotel for a little afternoon treat.

Then we returned to the hotel to hang out and relax by the pool. we hung out at the pool until sunset. Becca went to get a bottle of wine and then we watched the sunset at the beach.

After the sunset, we went into town and found a restaurant called 576 burger. The food was really good and they had a guy playing guitar. I also had a Nutella milkshake which was really good, but I couldn’t finish it because it was so rich.

Obligatory stop at an I <3 Jeri sign.

After dinner, we continue to walk and explore the town. Becca stopped into a shop and bought a sundress thing. We walked back onto the beach, there was a DJ a few people dancing. We walked back to our hotel on the beach and went to bed.

item.title: Roatan Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 4 Friday

Today we woke up early again and made some eggs for breakfast. Becca and I drove to a different dive shop today called Blue Island Divers so we could dive the Odyssey wreck. It was about ~15min drive north/east up the coast from where we were staying.

The dive shop had a resort vibe to it and was very nice. We met our dive guide, Daniel, who was very nice and knowledgable. He debriefed our first dive which was the Odyssey wreck.

After briefing we got our gear and loaded up onto the boat. This boat was much smaller than Reef Gliders, but it was just us and Daniel on the boat. The dive started in the reef and we swam out towards the bow of the wreck. The dive was 96' max and 61' average depth. We got a bunch of good pictures with the GoPro.

We swam from the bow down to the stern over the cargo bay. We followed Daniel through bridge. There were multiple floors that we swam through - it was really cool!

View of the stern/bridge.

Becca in the bridge.

After swimming through the bridge we went up the mast and did our safety stop. Daniel is really into "macro life" - basically really small organisms. He pointed out some really small jelly fish - I literally had no idea they were they until he shined his flashlight on them and pointed them out. There were a bunch of them!

After surfacing we took a quick boat ride back to the dock and did our 1 hour surface interval at the dive resort. The second dive was at a spot called the Moray Channel - Daniel briefed the dive and then we got back on the boat for a quick trip to the site.

We started off in the sandy shallows and worked our way through massive coral reef canyons - max depth 78' average depth 38'.

The dive was fun - there were a bunch of different channels - Daniel was again very into the macro life - which was cool but got a bit old after he kept turning over little leaves :D. The water at the start of the dive was a deep green until we hit the main channel where it turned deep blue - it was really cool to see!

After the dive we got back in the boat and made our way back to the dive shop. The bar at the dive shop had a deal where if you left them a good review they would give you a free drink - so Becca and I both left them a good review! I had the mokey lala drink - a Honduran specialty that is a chocolate/coffee/coconut flavored drink, it was delicious!

After our drinks we drove back to the VRBO to see mom and Bennett. After connecting with them we decided to walk down to Half Moon Bay - just a bit past West End - to go to Loretta's. Unfortunately Loretta's was closed so we ended up getting lunch at an Argentinian grill that was close by instead. The food there was good! I had a steak sandwhich.

After eating lunch we decided to try the iSoar - which is a boat anchored in half moon bay that has a tall platform you can jump off of or swing off of with a rope (it was named iSoar because the locals thought it was an eye-soar and I guess it stuck hah). To get there we ended up going to the dock where the half moon bay submarine was - the guy there was not very friendly. After checking out the sub, Becca and I swam out to the boat to jump off while my mom hung out with Bennett in the shade on the shore.

The boat was really fun! There were a few other people there and they would rock the boat (quite a lot!) while you jumped. You had to time the rope swing right so that the boat was rising as you were at the bottom of the rope.

After we jumped/swung off a few times we swam back to shore. We walked back down the town and stopped at a few dive shops for Becca to check out dive computers and then met up with Jamie and Nate - now freshly certified SCUBA divers! After meeting up with them we went back to Half Moon bay and hung out on the beach taking some pictures.

Becca and I had planned to do a night dive with Reef Gliders tonight so we left mom, Jamie, Nate, and Bennett at the beach and walked over to the dive shop around 6 and got loaded up onto the boat around 6:30 - just before sunset. The dive site was Chris Fisher's and Blue Channel, our guide Louden briefed the dive before we left.

The dive was really cool! Max depth of 48' and average depth of 36'. We saw an octopus, puffer fish, and spotted eel. The pictures didn't turn out great because of the lack of light.

At the end of the dive we turned off all our lights and we were able to see all the bioluminescent creatures light up in the water - it was really cool!

After the dive we walked back to the VRBO to meet up with everyone else- they ended up going to Ginger's - a restaurant near where we were on the beach in Half Moon Bay. They got Becca and I some food to go which we ate once we were back at the VRBO.

item.title: Roatan Day 5
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 5 Saturday

Today was another diving day - after eating breakfast at the VRBO we walked over to Reef Gliders and did two more morning dives with Gigi - the first dive was further away at a site called Tortuga Terrace (turned out it was right next to the moray channel). The dive had a max depth of 77' and average of 47'. It was a really fun dive that had lots of swim throughs and coral canyons along the wall.

The ride back to the dive shop was very choppy and took longer than usual. We did our surface interval at the dive shop - my mom stopped by again with Bennett.

Becca ended up going back over to one of the shops. She had seen a good deal for a dive computer and wanted to ask about a cash discount (which they did do - tax here is ridiculous at 19%). The second dive was at a spot called Blue Moonshine, Gigi briefed the dive and then we loaded back up onto the boat. The dive wasn't particularly special, we did see a stingray at the very beginning of the dive..... and at the end of the dive when we were getting back to the boat the ladder broke off (due to all the waves) so we ended up having to take off our gear in the water and climb/get pulled up onto the boat.

After diving we met up with Jamie and Nate (who did two dives with their dive shop) and then we went to pick up the dive computer for Becca. After getting the computer we walked back to the VRBO to see mom and Bennett. We had a snack to hold us over and then we drove to the Gumbalimba park (we didn't want to miss it before it closed which is why we skipped lunch).

The park was about 20 minutes away and cost ~$30 per person to enter. We were the only ones there so we basically had a private tour. The whole tour took about an hour. We started with the Iguanas - there were a bunch of them in an outdoor area. The next stop was the insect museum - which was basically a bunch of different dead insects on display. Then we crossed a big suspension bridge over a river to get to the more interesting side of the park.

The first stop on this side was the Macaws - not only did we see them but we also got to hold them and take pictures with them. It was really cool and Bennett enjoyed seeing the birds up close!

After the Macaws we went over to the monkeys which were running around in the open/trees. They would climb and jump on you, one even climbed on top of Bennet's head! He wasn't too sure how to feel about that :D.

After gumbalimba we drove down to west bay. We ended up parking (I think) in a resort parking lot and then walking to a place called the Thirsty Turtle (at the Bananarama resort). On the way we took a picture at this massive chair on the beach.

The restaurant had a 2 for 1 special for pina coladas and a fish entree so that’s what Becca and I got - both were really good - the fish was especially delicious!

After eating Bennett was getting really hot so Becca and I went back to the VRBO with him. Mom, Jamie, and Nate hung out at the beach for a bit longer before heading back.

item.title: Roatan Day 6
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 6 Sunday

Today we woke up at the usual time and had a quick breakfast at the VRBO (eggs) before heading with Nate and Jamie to the other side of the island to do some diving. We were diving with a different shop called Key Divers - based out of little French key, which is a small island on the south/east side of the island. Normally people will pay to go hang out at the island for the day (like $90) however because we were diving we got to hang out there for free.

We got picked up from the dock and shuttled over to the island by the dive shop. We stopped at their small dive hut and got our gear ready. We were supposed to dive at 9 but there was another family that was diving and they didn't get there until 9:30 so we ended up leaving late.

The first dive we were doing was the Prince Albert wreck - this was another big cargo ship that was intentionally sunk. It's at a shallower deck than the other dives we did which is why we were able to do the dive with Nate and Jamie.

The dive was really cool - we got to swim through the ship and then swam along the reef wall for a bit before returning to the ship. There is also a nearby airplane wreck that we saw as well which was really cool!

Over the cargo bay

swimming through the ship!

Exploring the aircraft ruins

After the dive we went back to little French Key to hang out and do our 1 hour surface interval. After seeing it, I would not recommend anyone to pay to visit little french key. It looked very run down. There was a tiger in a cage pacing around - apparently it was waiting to be taken somewhere where they could properly care for it :/.

Our second dive was another, smaller, wreck dive called Mr. Bud. This wreck was much smaller than the last one - but I actually thought it was cooler with all the fish inside of it.

After the dive we stopped back at Little French Key Island to get our stuff and then got dropped back off at the dock on the main island. We drove about 15 minutes (back towards our VRBO) and stopped at the Roatan Island Brewery. I had the meat platter (which wasn't very good) and two beers - unfortunately they didn't have the citrus IPA that I had before and really liked.

After the brewery we drove back to the VRBO to meet up with mom and Bennett. We hung out there at the pool and took some pictures. For dinner we walked to West Bay and ate at Ipanema beach bar and grill for Jamies birthday (a day early, but tomorrow we were going to Loretta's - they weren't open today).

I had ribs for dinner - they were pretty good. The waiter brought out a cake for Jamie since it was her birthday and then got a picture of her with it to post on their facebook group :D. After dinner we walked back to the VRBO and hung out for a bit before going to sleep.

item.title: Roatan Day 7
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 7 Monday

Because you can't dive for 24 hours before you fly we got to sleep in today. We ran out of eggs so my mom and I walked down to the nearest mini mart to pick some up for breakfast. After we ate we left for Anthony's Key (further up the coast - on the way to Blue Island Divers) to do a dolphin swimming activity! We left the VRBO around 9:45 and drove about 15 minutes to Anthony's Key (which is a really fancy resort). My mom waited with Bennett on the mainland while the rest of us took a little boat out to the island with the dolphin enclosure. Becca had done a lot of research and apparently they are known for treating the dolphins extremely well, unlike some other resorts in the world that do dolphin activities (they were also very strict on limiting the number of people for each activity).

There were multiple types of activities you could do - we decided to do the most involved one which consisted of meeting two dolphins - shaking their fins, getting a kiss from them, and even riding them twice! Once by holding their dorsal fins and another time with them pushing your feet while you hold a boogie board.

The activity was super fun! Our dolphins were Ronnie and Sophie. Technically you weren't supposed to have a camera but I guess the trainers didn't notice, so we were able to get some really good pictures and videos.

Overall it was a super fun activity and would highly recommend trying if you have a chance! After the dolphin activity we decided to go back up to the island near Little French Key to go to AJ's Monkeys and Sloths. This was much smaller than the Gumbalimba park, but I liked it better. The cost was only $15 per person (half of Gumbalimba) and we got to see guinea pigs, sloths, macaws, and more monkeys. Holding the sloths was definitely the highlight!

The monkeys here were very naughty. One stole Becca's headband almost immediately once we entered there cage - thankfully the trainer was able to bribe the monkey with food to get it back :D. We spent about an hour at AJs and then drove a little further up the island to eat lunch at a place called Kristi’s Overlook. It was very tasty. I had a big beef burrito and the house margarita. There were also really nice views of the island from the deck.

After lunch we drove back to the VRBO and then walked up to West End to see the Roatan Chocolate Factory. They had free tours of the factory - which honestly wasn't much. They went over the process of how chocolate is made and gave you lots of samples. Honestly the samples alone were worth it. We ended up buying a few bars of chocolate to bring home after the tour.

After the our we made our way further up towards Loretta’s (which was finally open). On the way we stopped at half moon bay for some pictures.

At Loretta’s I had lobster with garlic butter and rice and fries. Really tasty but it was really hot because we were outside - we ended up getting two big fans pointed at our table to help cool us off :D.

After dinner we walked back to the VRBO. On the way we stopped to take a picture at yet another I heart Roatan sign.

item.title: Roatan Day 8 & 9
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 8 Tuesday

Today we had eggs for breakfast again and the got everything packed up. After packing my mom, Jamie, and I took kayaks out and paddled down to West Bay Beach (about 40 min each way).

Originally I went in a double with Jamie, but then mom and Jamie swapped spots half way because she was tired. Once we got to West Bay I jumped out of the kayak for a quick swim.

Back at the VRBO I hung out in the pool for a few minutes before going back up and flying the drone to get some cool shots of the VRBO and island.

You can see our VRBO in the bottom right (yellow and orange/red roof)

View looking to the west/south - you can see the West Bay area. Also a good view of the reef and how clear the water is!

After some droning we made our way to the airport. Check in was fairly slow and the security was even slower, but we eventually made it through. We ended up getting some food at the airport. I tried Baleadas - which were not good!

Our flight from Roatan to Miami left on time. My mom was on the same flight as us again, Jamie and Nate were flying out the next day (since it was a cheaper flight). Once we made it to Miami we said by to my mom, her flight was before ours which was scheduled for 10:30pm.

Unfortunately there were some crew and maintenance issues with our flight (we can't catch a break!), so our flight was cancelled after about an hour delay. So we made our way to the American help desk (around midnight at this point). The line was massive, but thankfully someone from American saw we had a baby and pulled us to the front of the line. We ended up getting a hotel that was farther away because all the nearby ones were booked up (due to other flight cancellations I think). We got to the hotel via a Lyft around 1:30 am. Thankfully the hotel was really nice. The other downside was that the next flight back to Savannah that they rebooked us on was a full 24 hours later - the next day at 10:30 pm :/.

Day 9 Wednesday

We slept in late today - since we had all day in Miami we stayed at the hotel until 11 am (checkout). I did some work at the hotel. We had already planned a day in Miami on our way back from Brazil (our next trip) so we ended up going and doing all the things we had previously planned. Thankfully we were able to store all our bags at the hotel while we went out and explored. Our first stop was Little Havana. We stopped at a store called dos croquetas. Becca wasn't able to eat anything, but I tried a few different types. After that we had lunch at a cuban restaurant called El Pub. I had the cuban sandwich and Becca had the ropa vieja. Both were really good!

After eating we walked around Little Havana some more, stoping in the El Azucar ice cream shop. The ice cream was really tasty, especially for the hot day!

After the ice cream we went to a place called Wynwood Walls - an outdoor street art gallery. There was some really cool graffiti and sculptures to see.

After the walls we went to the Bayside market district - similar to Navy pier in Chicago it was a bunch of restuarants and shops along the coast. There was also a big park there that we walked to.

After walking around for a while we were getting tired and figured we might as well head back to the airport. We called a Lyft and stopped back at our hotel to grab our bags before heading back to the Miami airport. We had a bunch of meal vouchers from American so we ended up getting dinner at a fancy restaurant. The food there wasn't very good and the prices were insane - my burger cost like $25!

Thankfully our flight back at 10:30pm didn't get cancelled and we finally got home and reunited with the dogs around 1am. Despite all the airline issues the trip was a blast and Bennett did so well! It was so nice having my mom there to help with him while Becca and I were able to do fun activities together. As always so grateful for the experience and excited for the next one!

item.title: Banff 2024
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
After a few weeks back in Savannah we're off again - this time to visit Banff national park in Canada! We previously went to Glacier national park in 2021 and absolutely loved it. Banff is part of the same mountain range as Glacier and is a "sister" park to Banff. We've got a full itinerary of hikes. With recent fires in Jasper it's still TBD whether or not we are going to stay there, but either way here's the map:

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/0/embed?mid=1mgluKC6aKmafeJ5R0sXrmhKeJ1MnU6oB&ehbc=2E312F&w=640&h=480]

And here's the current Itinerary of what we plan to do - we might end up swapping the Jasper hikes for other hikes in Yoho national park.

Day 0 Friday Sept 20
✈️ Fly 2:30pm Delta SAV-ATL (1:55 layover)-Calgary (YYC) arrive 8:09pm (25k miles + $60)
Drive 1:20 hrs Airport to Canmore
Stay Canmore

Day 1 Saturday Sept 21
Drive 1hr Rawson Lake and Sarrail Ridge - 5 hrs, 3.7 mi to lake and 6.2 mi to ridge, 2,300ft
Kananaskis Nordic Spa- last two hours has discount special in evening
Drive to Bow falls/tunnel mountain
Bow Falls - 1.7 mi, 167 ft, easy
Cliff jump? & Whitewater rafting
Tunnel Mountain Trail - 2.7 mi, 860 ft, 1.5 hrs
Stay Canmore

Day 2 Sunday Sept 22
Kananaskis Hiking Day 2 Driving route 2.5 hours
White Water Rafting - >5 yrs, ~$100pp
Grassi Lakes Hike - 2.1 mi, easy, 500 ft, 1 hr
Smutwood Peak - 11.1 mi, 3000ft, 6 hrs?- On Rosa’s list
Stay Banff

Day 3 Monday Sept 23
Drive to Lake Louise 1 hr- arrive before 7 am or parking lot fills and have to park in overflow/take shuttle
Lake Agnes Trail - 4.6 mi, 1260 ft, 2.5 hr
Lake Agnes Teahouse - no electricity or running water, cash only
Combine Longer trail Add on Little Beehive 1.1 mi more, 500ft, 1 hr
Big Beehive - 6.7 mi total, 2372 ft
Devil’s Thumb - 7.9 mi total, 2673 ft
Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise, Canoe? - $155 and don’t take reservations, can bring own
Johnston Canyon Upper Falls - waterfalls, rock formations. 3.3 mi, 885 ft, 2 hrs
Banff Upper Hot Springs - no reservations, $17 pp, baby free
Stay Banff

Day 4 Tuesday Sept 24
Lake Moraine, Valley of the Ten Peaks
Lake Moraine Shuttle Info - can’t drive and park, must reserve bus
Lake Moraine Shoreline Trail- 2.3 mi, 1 hr
Rockpile Trail - 0.5 mi, 15 mins - good views of Valley of Ten Peaks
Sulphur Mountain - take Banff Gondola to top $50 pp, Baby Free
Vermillion Lakes - good sunset spot, lounge spot

*** Option
Yoho National Park- drive 1 hr from Banff
Emerald Lake Canoeing - $90 per hour, no reservations
Emerald Lake Loop Trail- 3.2 mi, 150 ft, 1 hr
Natural Bridge - stop on the way to Emerald Lake Loop, by parking lot
Takakkaw Falls.- 1.1 mils, 200ft, easy
Stay Banff
***

Day 5 Wednesday Sept 25
Drive Banff to Jasper “Icefields Parkway Drive” ~2:45 hrs
App called Gypsy Guide Narrative Tour
Only places for gas are in Banff and in Jasper
Stop Peyto Lake - 1.5mi, 305’ 45 min
Calderon Peak Trail - LONG 12.5mi, 5k’
Closed Stop Sunwapta Falls - 2mi, 480’, 1 hr
Stop Horseshoe lake cliff jump youtube - spots on the W side & tall spot on far SE side
StayJasper AirBnB or backup

Day 6 Thursday Sept 26
Jasper Hiking Day Driving route 50 min
Closed Maligne Canyon - 2.3mi, 400’, 1hr
Closed Roche Bonhomme (old man mountain) - 5.2mi, 4,400’
Closed Pyramid Lake - 3.7mi, 700’
Stay Jasper


Day 7 Friday Sept 27
Jasper Hiking Day
MAYBE Sulpher Skyline *** - 4.9mi, 2,100’
Kinney Lake *** - 8.3mi, 1,100’ (Mt. Robson park area (highest peak in rockies))
Closed Edith Cavell *** - 4.6mi, 1,800’ 3hr
Closed Geraldine Lakes Trail *** - 7.3mi, 2,000’; can stop at first lake (3.2mi) Cliff jump!
Drive Calgary 4.5 hrs
Stay Calgary Airport Hotel
Car rental return Jack drive drop off and shuttle back to hotel

Day 8 Saturday Sept 28
Fly home at 9:55am YYC-JFK (2hr layover)-SAV 9:40pm

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: How exciting! I just got back from a quick trip to Banff myself!

item.title: Day 1 Canmore & Kananaskis
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 6:30 courtesy of Bennett. We had breakfast in the room (I had cheerios), then we packed up for the day and got loaded up in the car.

Today we are hiking Rawson Lake and Sarrail Ridge in the Kananaskis Park (boarders Banff). The drive to the trailhead took just over an hour. We made a quick stop on the side of the road before we lost cell service to try and get bus tickets for Lake Moraine when they released that morning, but had no luck :(. The drive in was mostly cloudy and foggy so we didn’t see much of the mountains.

We made it to the parking lot around 8:30am, put on our layers, and loaded Bennett in his hiking pack. We bought an Osprey Poco Plus used on facebook marketplace- it is comfortable for Bennett, comfortable for me, and has plenty of storage space.

At the star of the hike it was very overcast and hard to see much of the surrounding mountains.

The hike itself was excellent. It was 2-3 miles through a forrest trail to the upper lake that had some really nice views. There was a small waterfall and bridge along the way.

When we got to the upper lake I took my drone out and got some shots of us.

There were a decent amount of people on the trail including a big group of high schoolers that we passed. We also got some hiking recommendations from a girl who lived in Calgary.

After a short break at the upper lake we continued on ~1 mile up to the Sarrial Ridge. This part of the hike was very steep, slippery, and muddy. Luckily we brought our micro spikes which made it significantly easier to climb. There was a small section that had a rope because it was so steep.

We finally made it to the top of the ridge around 11:30. Bennett slept most of the way :D, it was definitely a workout carrying him up in the pack! The views from the top were stunning now that the clouds had all cleared out.

We continued hiking down the ridge and got a bunch of photos.

I also took my drone out here for some quick shots.

After taking pictures we made our way back down to the lake. I was more worried about going down, but with the micro spikes and hiking poles it was a breeze. It was also entertaining seeing people struggling to go down slipping and sliding :).

We took another short break at the lake and cleaned off our muddy spikes.

We continued back down to the parking lot which is at the base of the ridge we had just climbed and by a lake. During the hike the fog burned off and the views from the parking lot were incredible. It was a good spot for our picnic lunch.

After eating we got back in the car and drive about an hour and a half to the next hike, Tunnel Mountain. We made a quick stop for gas and some delicious hot chocolate from Tim Hortons (I was getting super tired and it was the perfect pick me up).

Luckily we got a parking spot right at the trailhead. This hike was significantly shorter. Only 3 miles and ~850’ of elevation. The trail was groomed and dry. We got to the top in about 30 minutes. There were some really nice views of the town of Banff and the surrounding area.

We enjoyed the views and took some pictures before heading back down. On the way we saw a wedding, a rock climber, and a nice looking golf course.

Once back at the car we loaded up our things and drove back to Canmore. We stopped for dinner at a brewery called the Grizzly Paw. Becca and I both had burgers and I tried one of their IPAs. It was tasty! Bennett really liked all the pictures of grizzly bears on the wall.

After eating we went back to the hotel. We stopped at the room and rested for a while before walking across the parking lot to the pool. The pool was massive! There was a big 3 story water slide and an indoor/outdoor hot tub.

We each tried the waterslide and then hung out in the hot tub. We brought Bennett in the car seat with us. While we were there a family came in with a lot of kids. He was happy watching us splash, but he loved watching all the kids. After the pool we went back to the hotel and relaxed before falling asleep.

item.title: Day 2 Kananaskis
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 5:30 and started to work on the blog. Around 6:30 Becca and Bennett woke up and we had some breakfast in the room. Unfortunately Bennett had a fever, so we gave him some Tylenol and then started getting everything packed up (we were moving to a hotel in Banff that day). We waited in the room until 8am to have wifi so we could get the shuttle tickets when they released for Lake Moraine - I used both my phones and iPad while Becca used her phone. Only Becca was successful in getting tickets for Tuesday!

After we secured the tickets we loaded into the car to head to the Smutwood Peak trailhead. Before leaving town we made a quick stop at a pharmacy for some more medication to have on hand for Bennett. The drive to the trailhead was about an hour on an unfinished (gravely and bumpy) mountain road.

This hike started in the forest and was mostly flat. At parts the trail was very tight and a bit difficult to maneuver with Bennett's big pack on my back. It continued around the mountain through a pass (open field) called Birdwood Pass. Bits of the trail were pretty muddy, but overall not too bad.

Eventually we made it to a pretty sheer rock face. The trail turned up the mountain and gained elevation quickly. We took a short break for lunch in a quiet wooded area and then continued up.

We eventually made it on the ridge to the first lake. It was extremely windy, and the rest of the trail to the peak was very exposed along the ridge. Because it was cold and windy and we had Bennett with us, we turned back around.

On the way down we stopped for a break and I flew my drone around to get some pictures.

We made it back to the car around 3 pm. We drove back towards town (about 40min) to another small hike called Grassi Lakes - only 2 miles total. Becca started off carrying Bennett but got tired and turned back for the car, so Bennett and I continued to the lakes.

The lakes were very serene with clear water. We took some pictures and walked around the two small lakes. We saw some rock climbers ascending the big wall behind the lakes.

After the hike, we made our way to our resort in Banff. We also called and got dinner reservations (typically its so busy you need to have reservations).

After unpacking in our room we drove into town to have dinner at Bear Street Tavern. They had a Sunday deal - 50% off pizzas and $10 Stein beers (and had gluten free dough!). We both got the big bird pizza and I had a stein of the Tokyo drift IPA. Everything was really good and the atmosphere of the restaurant was nice.

Just before we were getting ready to leave Becca reached over for her bag and spilled about a quarter of my stein all over myself and Bennett (who I was holding at the time)! I have suspicions she did it on purpose :D.

After cleaning up and paying we walked down the town and stopped at a grocery store to get some eggs, bacon, and ice cream. Our room has a kitchenette so its easier for us to cook a more filling breakfast.

Bennett fell asleep almost instantly when we got back to the car and drove to our resort. We left him in the car seat sleeping and brought him to the pool/hot tub. This place had TWO big waterslides. Indoor water slides seem to be very popular in Canada. We hung out in the hot tub and took turns testing out the water slides while Bennett slept. They were both fun but the yellow one was definitely the best.

After hanging out for about half an hour we walked back to our room. I had some ice cream for dessert and then we went to bed.

item.title: Day 3 Yoho
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6:30 and wrote my blog for the day before Becca and Bennett woke up. We eventually all got up at 8am and made some eggs and bacon for breakfast. After eating we loaded up the car and left for our first stop around 9am.

Our first stop was at a natural bridge. Basically a rock that was cut through by the river forming a bridge. It was about a 45 minutes from our resort. It was cool to see but super crowded - you didn’t have to hike at all to get to it which makes it too easy to access. There was a girl taking selfies on a dangerously slick rock right next to where the water rushed though - I swear she was going to fall in.

After the bridge we continued on toward Emerald Lake - another 15 min away. The lake was also packed, but luckily we were able to snag a parking spot in the lot. Becca carried Bennett with the chest carrier. We walked around the shore of the lake for a bit and took pictures.

The lake was very picturesque. They had canoes you could rent, but it was pretty overcast and cold so we gave it a miss. After hanging out at the lake we got back in the car and drove to our next stop, Takawa Falls.

The falls were a 30 minute drive from the lake. Parking here was also crowded, but we got a spot on the side of the road relatively close. The trail to and from the falls was only about a mile total.

The falls are very tall and fed by a glacier on top of the mountain- according to the diorama. It was a cool water fall. We took a bunch of pictures and I flew my drone to get some shots.

After seeing the falls we walked back to the start of the trail and ate our sandwiches for lunch on a bench.

After eating we got back to the car and drove back towards Banff to another hike called Johnston Canyon. On the highway there are land bridges over the road for the wildlife to avoid traffic - really interesting.

Once again, parking was crowded. We were able to park in the lower lot. The hike itself was only 3.5 miles round trip.

The trail was mostly paved with railings. Because it was so accessible it was very crowded. There were queues of people to take pictures at a few of the viewpoints (which were not near as pretty as some of the other hikes we had done)- Becca and I didn’t not wait to do that haha.

There were two sets of falls - lower and upper. They were nice, but walking through the canyon was the best part of the hike. We hung out at the upper falls for a snack before heading back down the canyon.

Going back down was a bit of a pain - it was very crowded with slower hikers not in the best of shape, and the path is very narrow. Luckily we were able to get though without too much delay.

We got back in the car and made our way back to the hotel. We decided to checkout the indoor “playroom” with Bennett. It was super random - picture the old McDonald's play areas on steroids. It was a massive 3 story playhouse with slides, tunnels, and other things you could climb around on/through. I took Bennett through to the slide, which was more difficult than I expected - the playhouse wasn’t built for a 6’4” 33 year old haha. Nonetheless it was fun.

After playing we went to the pool to hangout and relax. We took Bennett in the baby pool and I even took Bennett down the water slide (the more boring one).

After the pool we got changed and drove into town for dinner. We ate at an Indian restaurant called Masala. I had chicken tikka masala and garlic naan - it was very good. Bennett slept on Becca in the chest carrier for the whole meal.

After dinner we walked around the town and popped into a few shops. The downtown area is cute, but small.

We drove back to the hotel and had some ice cream for dessert before going to sleep.

item.title: Day 4 Banff Lakes
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early at 5:20, ate a quick breakfast, then loaded up the car and drove to the Lake Moraine shuttle area about 50 minutes away. The only way to get to Lake Moraine is by shuttle- they do not allow any private vehicles. We were very relieved we were able to get spots on the shuttle. Lake Louise does allow private vehicles, but you have to get there very early if you want to get a parking spot.

We arrived a little early and were able to get on a shuttle to Lake Moraine without an issue.

First we climbed the Rock Pile trail. It’s super short- only a few hundred meters. At the top it was absolutely packed with people and photographers. Becca and I took a couple of photos and then got out of there. We made at least one photographer angry for ruining their Timelapse :D.

We climbed down from the rock pile and stopped at the shore of the lake near the canoe rental house to take some pictures and enjoy the view.

We continued along the lake shore trail which was flat and only about a mile long, stopping for pictures at various points along the way. This was a very nice hike, and not crowded because everyone else was up at the rock pile.

At the end of the trail was a small river that fed the lake from the glacier on top of the mountain. We walked back down the shore a little ways and then stopped to rest. I took out the drone and flew around to get some nice aerial shots of the lake.

When we got back to the main area Becca went to grab a coffee. While Bennett and I were waiting a group of Chinese women asked if I could take their picture which I happily obliged. Then they asked if they could take a picture with Bennett :D.

We got on the Lake Louise connector bus around 9:30 am. It took about 20 minutes to get to Lake Louise. Once we arrived we took some pictures at the bottom of the lake and then started hiking up the trail.

The first stop was Mirror Lake, a small lake just below Lake Agnes. We took a couple pictures here before continuing on. On the way up we saw some riders on horses coming down the trail.

The next stop was Lake Agnes, famous for its teahouse (the line was super long!). We took some more pictures and had a small snack break.

Next we hiked to the first peak of the day called Little Beehive. This spot had some nice views of the lake. We hung out here for another snack and I took some drone shots of the lake. Also my sister called me - her and Nate got engaged! Becca and I were happy to hear the news!

After hanging out at Little Beehive we hiked back down to Lake Agnes, and then around to the other side of the lake and up to Big Beehive. We took a couple pictures of Big Beehive on the way down. The hike over wasn't bad at all since we didn't have as much elevation change as we did coming from lake Louise.

The top of big beehive had a small hut and another nice view of the lake

We hung out at the top of big beehive and took some pictures. I hiked down a little further to another viewpoint - it wasn't as good as the main area, just a bit lower and a slightly different angle.

After resting for a bit we made our way to the back of big beehive to hike to the devils thumb.

Once the uphill started we quickly realized that it would be very difficult/sketchy to bring Bennett along for this hike. Since Becca was already tired we got the walkie talkies out and I went ahead while Becca waited at the base for me to run up to the peak.

The hike itself was a lot of scrambling and up some pretty loose scree. I went at a pretty fast pace and it only took about 15-20 minutes for me to make it up to the top (it wasn't very far, just steep!). It was much easier to hike without ~30lbs of Bennett and gear on my back! At the top I took some selfies and flew the drone for a bit to get some really epic shots. Unfortunately there were a bunch of people at the top so getting pictures was kind of a pain.

After taking photos and flying the drone I made my way back down to Becca and Bennett. On the way down I ran into a girl who asked for help finding her phone. Apparently she had set it down to film herself walking towards it and then it either fell or she forgot where she had put it :D - influencer problems lol. After trying to call it and looking around we had no luck and I continued down to meet up with Becca and Bennett.

After meeting up we loaded up and made our way back down to lake louise - we went a slightly different route back down to the lake. At the lake we relaxed for a bit and took some more pictures.

After hanging out we took the bus back to our car and then went back to Banff. We ended up getting dinner at a mexican restuarnt in Banff called Magpie & Stump. The food was pretty good! after eating we walked through the town and then drove back to our hotel.
