item.title: Day 5 Banff to Jasper
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
We decided we liked Lake Louise so much that we wanted to spend another day there hiking Mount Fairview. So we woke up at 4:30 am to get there in time to get a parking spot.

We got to the parking lot around 5:45 and there were a ton of spaces still open. We ended up eating breakfast in the car and waiting until 6:30 am to start the hike to catch sunrise on the way up the hike.

It was still dark out, and I left my head lamp in the other pack, so Becca used her phone to light the trail. After about 30 minutes it was bright enough that we didn’t need the light anymore. The trail we were hiking was the Mount Fairview trail, a friend of mine from golf recommended it.

The hike up to the pass was well groomed. We caught some nice views of the sunrise over the mountains.

At the pass we stopped for a small snack. There was a German guy there who camped for the night so we talked to him for a minute. The final mile was straight up the mountain on a more shale/scree trail.

Overall the trail was good but steep!! Becca was feeling tired so I took her pack for her (I looked ridiculous 😂). Talk about a good workout!

Near the top the wind was whipping! We ended up stopping at the false summit (a flat area just below the actual summit because it was too gusty and windy - especially with Bennett in my back it was hard to stay balanced when the wind caught the pack.

Becca waited at the false summit with Bennett while I made a quick final push up to the summit (only about 200’ higher). I took a few pictures and then ran back down to meet them. It was even windier at the top! I had to drop down for one of the gusts because it was so strong!

Later I looked up the wind and at 10,000’ (just above the peak at 9,000’) the wind was 36kts - about 41mph!

After regrouping with Becca and Bennett we made our way back down to the pass quickly stopping for a snack and some pictures.

We then continued back down the trail to the lake. We had a drink by the lake. At this point the wind at the surface was picking up and it was funny watching the canoers struggle in the wind - there were white caps on the lake. A few of them had no idea what they were doing and crashed into the rocks near the shore. The canoe rental workers were running about furiously trying to get to the canoes before they crashed, it was hilarious.

Becca and I had considered canoeing but the price was $200 an hour…no thanks! I can’t believe people pay that much, especially people that clearly have no idea how to canoe.

After relaxing at the lake shore we got back into the car to head to Jasper - about 3.5 hours away. The drive is on a road called the icefield parkway and the views along the way are absolutely stunning. We made a few stops to break up the drive.

The first stop was about 45 minutes away at Peyto Lake. It was a short hike from the parking lot to two different view points. The first viewpoint was pretty crowded but the second one (better view in my opinion) wasn’t as crowded - probably because the trail isn’t paved to get there.

The views of the lake were awesome. An interesting fact we learned is that the lakes get their color from something called rock flour - basically as the glacier on top of the mountain grinds away the rock it makes a fine silt that flows in the runoff down and feeds the lake. This silt refracts the light in a way that makes the water look super blue. The color can change depending on the time of year and amount of silt in the water.

After taking some pictures we hiked back to the car. And drove another 35 minutes to a place called mistaya canyon. Mistaya canyon is a deep river that cut through the limestone rock over the years. It was a super short hike down. We took some pictures and got back to the car.

The next stop was another 45 minutes way at the toe of the Athbasca glacier. It was raining when we got there so we decided to stay in the car and hike it on the way back to Calgary.

Next to the glacier a few minutes up the road was the Columbia ice field skywalk. Basically a glass walkway. The view of it from the road did not look impressive and I think it’s about $20 a person to do!

We continued on to Jasper. There was a massive fire there this year so we had considered changing our plans. The fire damage really was noticeable until about 30 minutes from the city. As we got closer we could see massive amounts of trees burnt - it was pretty crazy. When we got to the town there was still a ton of damage - building completely leveled. It was surprising to see how some blocks were completely destroyed while others were untouched.

We finally got to our airbnb and unpacked and rested. We went to get dinner around 6pm. The first place we tried to go to was a bbq place that was closed. We ended up going to another restaurant called maligne range. The atmosphere in side was really cool (definitely newer build). Becca and I got the meat platter for two. It wasn’t a whole lot of food for two people - chicken and short rib with fries, carrots, and broccoli. The short rib was the best in my opinion.

After we ate we went back to the airbnb and relaxed before going to bed.

item.title: Day 6 Jasper
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in - well Bennett woke us up earlier but we went back to sleep and got up around 8:30 am. We ate some breakfast in the airbnb and then drove about an hour to the northeast to do a hike called the sulphur skyline.

The hike was really nice, through the forest and up to the peak. There was snow most of the way up on the trees and off the trail making it look very picturesque.

The peak was just after the treeline, we started to hike up to it but the wind was pretty strong, not unsafe but Bennett started getting mad (probably because it was cold). So we went back to the shelter of the trees and Bennett stayed with Becca while I continued up the last bit of the summit. After taking some pictures I made my way back down to Becca and Bennett.

It was definitely gusty at the top, but not as bad as yesterday.

We continued hiking back down to the parking lot. Once there we had a lunch break and unloaded most of our hiking gear. Conveniently there is a hot spring right on the same parking lot so we went there to relax.

The hot spring was really nice, basically two big hot pools and they also had two smaller cold pools. This hot spring is supposedly the hottest in the Rockies. They estimate that the water comes from 1500m below the surface based on its temperature.

We hung out at the springs for a few hours. I bounced between the hot and cold pools a few times. We ended up leaving to head back to town around 4:15.

Right before making it back into town we saw some Elk so we stopped to get a quick picture from the car. There are a ton of warning signs about the elk because it’s their mating season.

After stopping we drove up to pyramid lake, just 10 minutes outside of town. The lake and surrounding area was relatively unaffected by the fire. We stopped at a small island on the lake to walk around and take some pictures.

It’s called pyramid lake because it’s right below pyramid mountain. Which is a big mountain made out of a rare quartz.

After seeing the lake we drove into town and stopped for dinner at famosa pizza (many of the restaurants still aren’t open so the options are limited). The food was really good, I had the meat lovers pizza and we both got hot chocolate.

After eating we walked around the town. It was crazy to see how some buildings were burned down while others right next to it were unaffected.

Once back at the car we drove back to the airbnb and then went to sleep.

item.title: Day 7 & 8 Jasper to Calgary to Home
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6:30 and wrote my blog. Becca and Bennett got up around 8:30 am. We had breakfast at the airbnb and then packed up and loaded up the car at 10. We started the trek back to Calgary. On the way out of Jasper we saw a bunch of crews working on cutting the dead burnt trees down and we also saw more Elk hanging out by the side of the road.

Our first stop on the way back was Sunwapta falls about 45 minutes away from Jasper. No sign of fire damage here but it was raining a bit so we did our best to bundle Bennett up. I wore him on the chest carrier and wrapped him in my rain jacket. We also used Becca’s backpack cover on Bennetts head to keep him dry.

There were two parts of the falls: the upper and lower. The upper was right off the road with a bridge that went over the falls.

The lower was about a mile down and in my opinion was not as impressive. Bennett fell asleep for the lower falls so I don’t think he thought they were very impressive either 😂.

After hiking back we got in the car and drove another 45 minutes to the Toe of the Athabasca glacier. The rain had stopped but it was kind of hailing now and windy. The hike was super short, under a mile total. We originally thought the trail went into the glacier but unfortunately it only went up to it and not on it.

It was still a super cool view but also very cold with the wind and hail blowing in our face. Becca carried Bennett for this one and had him wrapped up tight.

They had various markers for where the glacier was and what year it was. It was crazy to see how much it has receded, apparently it’s been receding about 5m per year.

After taking some pictures we went back to the car and decided to check out the visitor center that was across the road. The visitor center was super crowded and super touristy. They sold glacier hiking tours but it didn’t look that cool plus Becca and I had been on a few glaciers already with much smaller groups.

We left the center and continued on the road. As we drove farther the weather improved. We were planning to stop at Crow glacier (about an hour away) but ended up deciding to skip it because it was only a viewpoint and we were able to see it and take some pictures as we drove by in the car.

The rest of the drive to Calgary was about 2.5 hours. We made a stop at Tim hortons of the highway and ended up getting Wendy’s frosties (it was a combined store).

We ended up getting to the hotel in Calgary around 5 and checking in and getting settled. We relaxed for a bit then left around 6pm to get dinner at a nearby Korean restaurant.

I ended up getting a fried rice dish and milk tea flavored bubble tea, it was really good. Bennett had a bunch of the fried rice and liked it!

After dinner I dropped Becca and Bennett back off at the hotel and then drove to the gas station to fill up and clean the car up before driving to the airport to drop the car off. After dropping the car off I got the shuttle back to the hotel.

We ended up hanging out at the hotel before going to bed.

Day 8

Today we woke up early to make our way to the airport. There was a really fun play area near our gate with a tunnel that Bennett enjoyed crawling through. We connected through JFK and then to Savannah without any issues. Unfortunately when we arrived in Savannah it was right after hurricane Helene hit and our house was without power for a week!

item.title: Guatemala 2024
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
And after only a few weeks it's time for another adventure! This time I'm heading to Guatemala with Patryk and Jimmy. Unfortunately Becca wasn't able to get time off and my work recently rolled out a policy that requires us to take all of our vacation before the end of the year which left me scrambling to find something to do. This trip should be fun - hiking volcanos and surfing!

Here's the map for the trip:

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/0/embed?mid=1Am7A0IBCGCfJaYa9PE9X2iXAOwC1u_Y&ehbc=2E312F&w=640&h=480]

And here's the rough itinerary

Day 0 Thursday 10/10 ✈️ Fly: Arrive ~1p Get rental car Drive to Antigua ~ 1.5-2 hours Arrive ~3p Explore city Stay Antigua Guatemala - El Carmen Hotel Day 1 10/11 City tour: Casa Santo Domingo, Jade Factory and History, Main square And Compañia de Jesus. Hobbitenango, Chocolate museum, Antigua brewing company, Hotel Casa Domingo Stay Antigua Guatemala - El Carmen Hotel Day 2 10/12 8am Acatenango hike - V Hiking Tours Stay volcano cabin Day 3 10/13 Acatenango hike Return ~1pm Drive lake Atitlan ~2.5 hours, Arrive ~3:30pm Stay Lake Atitlan Villas de Coco Day 4 10/14 SCUBA lake Atitlan(2 dives) Cliff jumping (San Marcos La Laguna) ATV tour (4 hours) $60 leave from Panajachel Stay Lake Atitlan Day 5 10/15 Dirt bike tour (6 hrs) 8:30am - 2:30pm Stay Lake Atitlan Day 6 10/16 Mountain Bike or San Pedro volcano hike trail 4.8 miles 3,800’ ~5hr or Rock climb or Paragliding Stay Lake Atitlan Day 7 10/17 Drive paredón (3.5 hours) Surf/beach Stay paredón Cocori Lodge Day 8 10/18 Surf/beach Stay paredón Cocori Lodge Day 9 10/19 Dive back to airport ~3 hours depart by 8am Flight home depart ~1p Arrive airport at 11am

item.title: Guatemala Day 0 & 1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
In the midst of hurricane Milton I made it to the airport around 5am. It was a refreshing surprise that all of the flights went smoothly. I arrived in Dallas almost 30 minutes early and had no problem making the connecting flight. In Dallas I met up with Patryk and Jimmy at the gate, it was good to see everyone!

The flight from Dallas was less than 3 hours to Guatemala City. The flight was smooth I watched a few shows, pat and I happened to be sitting next to each other. Once we landed getting into Guatemala was painless, we filled out a customs form online. I went ahead and got the rental car and jimmy and pat followed behind shortly after.

We drove from Guatemala City to Antigua Guatemala, the drive took about an hour and a half and we arrived at our hotel around 2:30pm. Traffic driving here was pretty bad getting out of the city, but in general the drivers weren’t that aggressive. We’re staying at the el Carmen hotel, it’s a great location right in the center of the city.

We didn’t have anything really planned for today so we got settled and rested in the hotel for a bit before heading out to the Antigua brewing company for a beer. The place had a rooftop with nice views of the city. The city is pretty small and nestled in the mountains surrounded by volcanos. We had a drink and hung out there.

Afterwards we walked two blocks both to check out a check and archway thing. Pretty standard nothing special. We also stopped in a market.

We continued down to the main square and went to dinner at a place that pat found called las antorchas. The food was good Jimmy and I had amazing pork marinated in guacamole and pat had a burger. I also had a strawberry smoothie.

After eating we stopped to pick up waters and some cash and then dropped the waters off at the room. Before walking to a big and famous old hotel called casa de Santo Domingo. The hotel was cool, we got a drink there and hung out before heading back and watching a movie before going to bed.

item.title: Antigua Guatemala Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
I woke up pretty early today, around 4 am - to be fair it’s 6 am Savannah time! I wrote the blog and researched some things to do before waking everyone up at 7. Once everyone was up we made our way upstairs to the hotel rooftop terrace for breakfast. I ended up getting the Guatemalan breakfast which consisted of eggs guava and cheese on a hard flat taco, it was pretty good!

After breakfast we went back to the room and got our stuff ready and walked to the tour office to start our atv tour. Jimmy and I ended up going to the main square and ended up finding a store that sold sunglasses since we both forgot to bring ours.

We were doing the Sky High ATV tour today with our guide Alejandro from Simoon tours. We got checked in, got our helmets and then walked a few blocks to where the ATVs were parked. After a brief explanation we got on the ATVs and started the tour. It was just the 3 of us and the guide which was nice, we were able to go a lot faster and stay however long we wanted at each stop.

Driving the ATVs was fun, we started out on the cobblestone streets and then on to a mix of paved and dirt streets to get up the ridge of a mountain near the city. I had the GoPro on and a chest mount so I got some photos and videos of the ride.

The first stop was a place called Alta Mira. Basically a “park” with a bunch of photo ops and random things to do. We had to park our ATVs and take a truck some of the way up because it “was too steep” seemed fine to me but I’m sure someone got hurt or something so they don’t do it anymore.

At the top was the entrance to the park and so nice views of the town and volcanoes. Apparently in Guatemala they like their outstretched hands (there were 3 of them at this park) that you walk out onto to take a picture.

There were a bunch of other random things like a kangaroo, airplane, zoo animals made from tires, a butterfly chair. We took a bunch of photos because why not.

The views of the volcanoes surrounding the city were great you could even see the one volcano erupting! which happens ~15 minutes, it was really cool to see (tomorrow we’re hiking it!).

The place also had mini golf (but we couldn’t find any balls) and a fake gym lol. After hanging out for a bit we met our guide took the truck back to the ATVs and drove about 5 minutes to the next stop for lunch at an avocado farm called earth lodge. Again we had to park our ATVs amd walk a good ways down to the farm.

The place had a commune vibe. He people there were very nice (mostly American) and were there on work exchange programs where they work at the lodge and get food/accommodation. The menu had lots of vegan options which wasn’t a surprise, jimmy and I got the avocado chicken tacos which were actually amazing and fries which were also really good! I also had a smoothie which unfortunately wasn’t that good.

They also had a spa menu which included options for shamanic rituals haha - unfortunately we didn’t have enough time to do it. After eating and hanging out we walked around the farm to check it out. There really wasn’t a whole lot to see, then we met our guide and walked back up the hill to our ATVs to head to the next stop.

The final stop was a place lower down the mountain called cerro de la Cruz. It was a nice viewpoint of the city with a big stone cross that was placed there in the 1930s. It replaced an earlier wooden cross, which symbolized the Christianization of the region during the Spanish colonial era.

One of the volcanos next to the city is called the agua or water volcano and used to have a big lagoon at the top but after an earthquake a big crack caused the water to flow down closer to the city.

The other volcano fuego (next to acatenango) had its last major eruption in 2018 which caused hot lava, gas, and ash to flow down the slope and ended up killing hundreds of people in the nearby city. According to our guide the people had a few days warning to evacuate however many chose to stay (kinda sounds like what happens with hurricanes in the us), either way very sad.

After some pictures we got back in the ATVs and drove into town. We walked back to the tour office to return the helmets and then went back to the room for a bit to relax.

After resting we decided to go check out hobbitenango which was actually really close to Alta Mira. We got the car and drove up (~20 min). We tried to drive all the way up but ended up parking in a lot below and taking a truck up (which definitely was required even though the website said there was free parking at the very top).

Hobbitenango was pretty fun (better than Alta Mira). They had a mini golf course with 7 holes. The putters were basically wooden mallets lol. The holes were very janky but fun.

We played match played match play (1 point per hole won) Pat got up 3 and then I tied him and won in the last hole, it was an exciting match haha. The mini golf ended at the top of the park so we ended up keeping our putters and using them as walking sticks.

There was a big swing thing, it had a weight limit of 200 lbs (I’m 195 - which they verified by having me hang from a grocery store type scale haha) it looked pretty sketchy, but fun. Unfortunately pat and jimmy were too heavy for it. the line was kind of long but it went fast. One lady absolutely freaked out while on the platform and didn’t do it which was pretty funny.

Thankfully I survived the swing! Next we went to yet another hand to take some pictures. There was a small line, this hand had a stone/mossy look to it and I think had the best views so far.

We took a few pictures and then went to the archery/axe throwing station, however the line was too long and it didn’t look that fun so we ended up skipping it. Finally we took a few pictures with the hobbit houses before heading back to the exit and taking the truck back down to our car.

There is absolutely zero chance they are paying licensing fees to lord of the rings haha. Overall I was pretty impressed with the park for Guatemala. We drove back down and parked the car and walked to our hotel. We got somewhat packed up and then watched some more of the movie (invisible man) before going to dinner.

Unfortunately the first place we tried was randomly closed so we ended up going to a place near our hotel called tacool. I had a burrito which was good, it was definitely a super Americanized place.

After eating we went back to the hotel and finished packing and watching the movie before going to bed.

item.title: Day 3 Acatenango
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up way too early again (4am) I wrote my blog and then everyone got up at 6:30am. We left the hotel just before 7 and walked to the car and drove ~1 hour to the village below Acatenango (the volcano) to meet our tour group. Apparently they didn’t realize we drove ourselves even though I whatsapped them the day before and waited extra for us in town.

After we parked we had breakfast at the tour house which was eggs, pancakes, and tostadas.

We filled our waters and rented some poles for like $2. After we got all our stuff organized we had a meeting in front of the tour house explaining the hike. We’re hiking from 2400m to about 3500m stopping at the camp tonight and then leaving early tomorrow morning for the summit. There’s an optional hike to the el fuego volcano that we plan on doing after we get to camp. There’s group was massive 32 hikers in total with 6 guides. We took a quick group picture before getting in the vans to drive to the start of the hike.

The hike was basically all up hill we started out surrounded by corn fields and hiked maybe 30 minutes before our first stop it was entertaining to hear Jimmy complain about the steepness (he doesn’t hike much).

After the quick first stop we continued up to the entrance to the park. Overall the trail was superrr crowded and very tight which made passing difficult. The pace was also very slow. Luckily one of the guides broke off a group of 8 of us so that we could hike at a more reasonable pace. After stopping at the entrance for a quick break and to get our wristbands we continued up. The trail itself is only like 8 miles to the peak and back but 5,000’ of gain - pretty steep but I’ve definitely done steeper.

We as we ascended the visibility got worse, it was pretty clear we were in the clouds.

We got to camp around 1pm and sadly there was absolutely no view of the mountains. Jimmy arrived maybe 20 minutes after Pat and I. We ate lunch in our cabin which was pretty small and made out of sheet metal.

Lunch was chicken and rice, pineapple, an apple, and Oreos. It was pretty good, we also got some hot chocolate. We were supposed to do the optional el fuego hike at 4, however the weather was so bad the guides said we couldn’t do it today but instead could do it tomorrow instead of the peak.

We hung out at in the cabin and at camp until 7pm to get dinner. The guides made a fire using strange strategies to get it started by pouring gasoline and throwing plastic things in it haha, eventually they got it going. Dinner was spaghetti pasta and fried chicken, it was okay nothing amazing.

We ended up going back to the cabin and watching a few movies before trying to get some sleep.

item.title: Day 4 Acatenango & Lake Atitlan
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 3 am after a night of very little sleeping - we didn’t have much space and the mattress was super thin and uncomfortable, I maybe got 2-3 hours of sleep. 3am was the planned time to leave for the hike but the visibility was still awful so the guides said that we would wait until 4am to decided. We ended up watching some more of a movie until 4 am and luckily when we got out of our cabin the visibility had started to improve so the guides said we could go.

Unfortunately we had to choose either the Acatenango summit or el fuego. We all decided to do the el fuego hike. It was about a half hour downhill and then an hour uphill, really not bad. At the top we waited for sunrise- the visibility was kind of in and out. After sunrise we hiked up a little farther but the visibility just got worse and worse :(.

We waited at the top hopping it would clear and we could see but unfortunately it never did. We ended up hiking back down.

As we descended we started to exit the cloud we were in and had some visibility. We could see the town, acatenango ahead, Agua volcano to our right, and lake Atitlan to our left. We took pictures in the way down.

Once we got back to our camp we got our stuff organized and ate some breakfast. We were hoping for the clouds to clear el fuego so we could see it but they never fully did. We could feel and see the smoke from the eruptions after it passed by the cloud.

Breakfast was cereal and peanut butter sandwiches pretty basic. After we ate we packed up and took a few final pictures at camp before descending down. I forgot to mention this trail was a 10/10 for trail dogs, there were literally dozens of them and the hiked with us the whole time and even stayed at our camp (I’m pretty sure one slept under our cabin lol.

We took a few last photos at the camp before heading back down the volcano.

The hike back down was fairly quick and easy the views were definitely better since we were below the cloud. We also passed some Guatemalans that were hauling wood up the volcano on their backs, it was impressive.

We ended up getting to the end and taking the van back to the tour house. At the tour house we had a snack and still had to pay for the “extra” fuego hike which was a bit annoying. After we got to our car and started the 2 hour drive to panajachel on lake Atitlan.

The roads were actually pretty good for the most part considering this is Guatemala. However as we got closer they got a bit worse - sections where landslides covered up the road and some dirt roads. There was even a part of the road where you had to drive through a small river!

Thank god we saw another car drive through going the other direction which gave us confidence we could make it lol. We arrived in pana and found our Airbnb which is called villa de coco. It was a pretty big house in a small compound of houses with a pool and jacuzzi!

We hung out and relaxed at the airbnb before going to an Indian restaurant in the main town about 5 minutes away. The restaurant was called Delhi 6 I had the chicken tikka masala and garlic naan it was really good!

After dinner we stopped for some gelato at a place called dolce gelato. It was a lot of vegan gelato, I tried a few of the flavors and they were pretty bad so I go a Nutella popsicle instead.

While we are the gelato we kept getting approached by random people to try and sell us stuff. It was really annoying so we left and walked down to the coast and walked along looking at the docks and some of the shops.

We made a quick stop at a mini market, I picked up some eggs and bread for breakfast tomorrow. Back at the hotel we watched a movie called Northmen and then went to sleep, we were all pretty exhausted!

item.title: Day 5 Lake Atitlan SCUBA
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6, I made some eggs and toast for breakfast and got packed and ready to go diving. I stopped at the atm for more cash and then took a lancha to Santa Cruz which cost 25Q.

The ATI dive shop was right in front of the dock. I got there a bit early at 7:30 so I hung out and wrote my blog.

At 8am I met Ian the divemaster and Joshua, another diver. We checked in and then got our gear fitted. Lake Atitlan is a lake in a crater of the caldera of a volcano, its high elevation (5,100’) so there are specific things you need to be careful with while scuba diving at high altitude.

After getting our gear and getting briefed about the dive we loaded up on the boat. The boat was small but it was just the 3 of us. The first site we went to was called el árbol. It’s an underwater tree. Ian did some drills under water with Josh as a refresher and then we started the dive.

The underwater tree was interesting. There weren’t too many fish. We continued along the shore and it became kind of like a wall dive. At one part of the dive there was sand where if you put your hand in it it was super warm.

Overall the dive was interesting super unique the max depth was 78’ with an average of 45’ for 50 minutes total.

We took off our gear in the water and then climbed back up onto the boat. The ride to the site was only 10min tops. We did a surface interval of about 40 minutes before changing the tanks and then heading back out to the next dive site, Ramb II.

This dive was a wall dive. The start of the dive had a chimney swim through that was pretty fun, I tried to get a picture of it but it was pretty difficult.

After the chimney we swam along the wall. We saw volcanic rocks, a weird fungus, some small fish, a crab, and some stuff that looked like destroyed building materials. The dive had a max depth of 87’ and an average of 40’ for 47 minutes.

Overall it was a unique dive. The lake itself was formed by the explosion of a massive volcano 85,000 years ago with a max depth of over 1,000’. Apparently there is also an underwater Mayan city - however you’re not allowed to dive there unless you get special permission from the government.

After the dive we went back to the dive shop to drop off the gear and settle up. From there I took another lancha to the town of San Marcos to meet Pat and Jimmy. It was about 1:30 so we went to lunch in the town at a place called the hidden garden. It had super hippy vibes. We met a guy there named river who tried to sell us his “Nero coding” massages haha. Besides the interesting atmosphere the food was good. I had the teriyaki chicken bowl and a peanut butter smoothie. Both were good! We also had a very friendly and cute pup sit by us and kept us company.

After lunch we went back toward the dock of the town and then to the natural reserve cerró tzankujli. The town itself had some cool little streets.

The park cost 50Q to enter and was along the coast. The main attraction was a 12m cliff jump into the lake!

I did the jump 4 times and jimmy did it twice. There was another jump that was like 3m high that we all did. It was a lot of fun and had some great views of the lake!

After jumping the weather started to look bad so we made our way back to the dock and got in a lancha. After we got in it started to rain - luckily the boat is covered. The ride back took a while and the water was really choppy.

Once we got back to pana we decided to eat at a place called tuscani. We all had pizzas they were okay, nothing special. While we ate it started to rain harder and the streets became completely flooded!

Luckily we had covers for our packs and were in our swimsuits because we got drenched on the walk back to the Airbnb compound. Once we were back we hung out in the jacuzzi for a bit before going inside to watch a movie then go to bed.

item.title: Day 6 Lake Atitlan
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6 and wrote my blog. I made some eggs and toast for breakfast at 7. Pat and jimmy woke up slightly later. The weather outside looked great so we decided to rent some ATVs and dirt bikes. I wanted to switch to a dirt bike since we already drove ATVs in Antigua. They required that you have a motorcycle license to rent them so Pat and jimmy had to stick with the ATVs.

On the walk to the rental place we stopped for an obligatory picture at the I love pana sign and also got followed by a pack of cute street dogs.

We left the rental shop a little before 9 and cruised about 30 minutes to a spot called ojo de agüilla. Unfortunately the gps took us down a wrong turn and we ended up going up a steep dirt road that was a big pain with the dirt bike -I didn’t want to have the dirt bike slip and hurt myself so I went slow which stalled the engine a lot :D. After finally struggling to the top we figured out that we were at the wrong spot!

To make matters even worse the spot we stopped was absolutely covered with fire ants which proceeded to destroy my ankles! We quickly left and cut our losses and decided to go to the next stop instead of trying to continue to find the ojo de agüilla.

The next stop was Santa Catarina a small town just south of pana. The views on the ride to the town were great! We ended up parking for free just outside the town and walking in and exploring. The main square was cool, tons of uniquely painted buildings.

We walked down to the coast and saw a little kids soccer match. They had Sesame Street character jerseys and even an announcer. It was fun to see.

We decided to stop for lunch at a hotel and restaurant that we passed near the soccer field. I had a burger and Coca-Cola. The food was good.

After eating we got back on the road and drove further down to the town of San Antonio Palopo. The road through the town went along the coast and had really nice views of the lake. We stopped a few times to take some pictures.

We rented for 3 hours so we drove back to the shop in pana and dropped off all the vehicles. We decided to check out the reserva natural Atitlan by hailing a Tuktuk and getting a 10min ride to the reserve.

The reserve ended up being way cooler than I thought it would be. There were a ton of hanging bridges, a monkey, and a decent sized waterfall. Overall well worth the 80Q entry! There was quite a lot of trash in the park which was sad to see.

After walking through the reserve we got a tuktuk back to town and walked to the Airbnb. We rested for a bit and then decided to walk to a nearby supermercado that we saw to pick up some snacks - popcorn, gummies, chocolate.

We got back to the Airbnb and relaxed a bit more before heading to get massages at 4. The massage place was great! Jimmy and I ended up sharing a room and Pat got his own. Although the masseuses were tiny they had super strong hands and the massage was probably one of the best I’ve had. They did some unique things like stretch you and scratch your head haha!

After the massages we walked down to the lakeshore and found a hotel/restaurant to stop at for dinner. We started sitting outside but moved inside because of the rain and wind. I ended up getting the fettuccini pasta with crab and shrimp and it was really good!

After dinner we quickly walked back to our Airbnb to try and avoid the rain. Luckily it slowed up slightly for our walk. Once back we watched a movie before going to bed.

item.title: Day 7 Lake Atitlan
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up around 6 and wrote my blog. My stomach was not feeling too well so I didn’t sleep great. I made some breakfast around 7 and we hung out until about 8:30 before walking down to the dock to catch a lancha to take us over to San Juan, a town on the other side of the lake. In the way to the lancha we saw a pup on the roof of a building.

We walked through and explored some of the streets of San Juan. It was a cool little town. The Main Street called Calle de las sombrillas had a bunch of umbrellas strung up over the street.

Anther street a little further up had a bunch of hats.

After walking around we decided to walk over to the mirador (viewpoint) of the city. It was about 1km to get to the start of the trail and then about 0.25 miles up the mountain to the viewpoint. There was a big cross at the end of the viewpoint with a platform that had really good views of the lake and the city. On the trail we had another trail dog keep us company. The entrance to the hike cost 30Q each which was annoying but the views were nice.

After enjoying the view and taking pictures we hiked back down into town and found a restaurant with a rooftop view of the lake and had lunch. I had the fajitas and a strawberry smoothie. Both were really good!

After eating we decided to grab a Tuktuk and go to the next town over, San Pedro, which was about a 10 minute drive. In San Pedro we walked through the town and explored the streets. We came across a I heart San Pedro sign and took a photo. We also saw a bunch of cool graffiti on the walls.

We walked through the town to the tornado cafe, a place Pat was recommended. The cafe had a cool courtyard buried between the buildings with lots of vines and some really comfy rocking chairs. Jimmy and I had the caramel frappe, it was pretty good so we both had another.

We hung out at the cafe for a while until the weather started to look like it was going to rain and then left and walked towards the port to catch a lancha back.

Back at pana it was raining, we went back to the villa. Jimmy and I played a little bit of ping pong and then we relaxed in the house.

We watched a few episodes of a tv show before going for another massage. This time the massage wasn’t quite as good but still a really good deal, $60 for 90 minutes!

After the massage we went to a nearby restaurant called Humaya Restaurante. It was an interesting restaurant, definitely targeted more towards vegans. I had a burger and smoothie. The burger was good but the smoothie was meh.

After dinner we went back to the Airbnb and watched a movie before going to bed.

item.title: Day 8 Lake Atitlan to Paredón
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in a little later. We got up around 8 and packed and left the Airbnb and got on the road with the car around 8:30 am. The drive to the coastal city of Paredón was supposed to take about 3.5 hours. The route google had us going was on some pretty spicy roads! Very steep dirt/rock roads. There were a few that were super tight, I’m not sure we were supposed to drive down. Google also tried to get us to take a couple one way roads the wrong direction.

Fortunately we made it through the mountains surrounding the lake and onto more flat roads which made the rest of the drive easy.

Paredón is a small surf town on the pacific coast of Guatemala. We arrived at our hostel called Cocori lodge, parked the car in their lot and checked in. Unfortunately it was around 12 and our room wasn’t going to be ready until 3 so we walked out to the beach (which has black sand - very hot!) and then went to a nearby restaurant called Pez paredón. The food was decent, I had some tacos and loaded fries.

After eating we went back to the hostel and hung out in the pool until 3. There was a beer pong tournament going on tonight so Jimmy and I signed up as team USA and Pat signed up with an Irish girl we met who needed a partner.

Once we got our room we unpacked and got settled in. The room is a private villa that is a big circle with one bed downstairs and another upstairs. The upstairs also has a big net that you could lay in, very interesting layout!

After relaxing we decided to go eat some dinner at the hostel. I got a burrito and fries. They were pretty good. After dinner we hung out a bit more, we walked out of the hostel to a small convenience store called super24 to get some sunscreen, cereal/milk for breakfast, and a few other snacks.

We hung out at the room until 8 when the tournament started. Jimmy and I ended up playing pats team first. There were quite a few teams - at least 16. They had the first 3 rounds of “pool play”. Jimmy and I won our first game, got destroyed in the second game by some Guatemalans, and then tied the last game (there was a 4 minute time limit).

We thought there was no chance of making it out of pool play (only the top 8 moved on), but somehow we did! We came back and won our first playoff game and then won the semifinal game handily. The championship game came down to two cups each but we were able to come away with the W!

For winning the tournament we got $100 USD! We hung out after the tournament at the bar for a bit. Then we walked to the hostel next door to check it out. We stayed there for a bit chatting with the people from the tournament and then went back to the room to sleep.

item.title: Day 9/10 Paredón and home
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in, we ate some breakfast at the room (cereal and milk) and then hung out in the net watching some tv on the iPad. Pat went ahead and scheduled us surf lessons at 11.

We ended up going to the pool around 10 and hanging out until our lessons started. The lessons were much of “lessons”, we each had an instructor (who didn’t speak much English). My instructor didn’t even get in the water while Pat and jimmys at least helped them. We surfed for 1 hour, it was totally exhausting, the waves were constant and even though my instructor wasn’t good I was able to consistently catch the waves. The lessons were only $20 so I wasn’t too worried about the instructor.

After surfing we went back to the pool to relax. We chilled for a bit and then went to the pizza place across the street for lunch. I had a meat pizza. Pat showed us a fun card game to play while we waited. There was also a cute pupper there hanging out with us.

The pizza was good! After we finished we finished playing the game and then went back and hung out at the hostel. Pat really wanted to play some volleyball so we recruited one of the beer pong players and played on the court right in front of the hostel.

It was a pretty fun game Pat and Timo vs Jimmy and I. We ended up winning. After the game we went back to the pool.

After relaxing we hung out in the room and then went out for dinner. We tried to go to a papusa place but it looked pretty bad. We stopped at the super24 for some more snacks and then went to another restaurant called Saya.

This was a fancier looking restaurant with fancier dishes. I got the ribs. They were pretty meh. It was also super hot, there was absolutely no breeze so we were all sweating!

We ate quickly and then went back to the room to hang out and watch some more of the TV show. Not Jimmy and I ended up passing out during the show so we went to bed for an early night.

Day 10

Today we woke up and got packed and checkout of the hostel. We got on the road at 7:30 to drive back to the airport. The drive took about 3.5 hours with pretty bad traffic once we got to the city. We ended up stopping at a gas station about 5 miles from the airport to fill up.

We dropped the car back off - I had seen a lot of bad reviews about this Avis car rental but everything went smoothly. We got through the airport security and to the gate. I stopped at subway to use the rest of my Quetzales on a sandwich for lunch.

Jimmy ended up on a different flight connecting through Dallas while Pat and I were connecting through Miami. Our flight to Miami was slightly delayed but we made up a lot of the time in the air. Once in Miami I went in to Savannah and Pat went on to Chicago. Overall smooth trip back. I ended up getting back to Savannah at 9:20 and got back home just before 10.

Once again an awesome trip with my good friend and cousin! Glad we were able to sneak it in before the end of the year! I’ll see them both again next weekend when Becca, Bennett, and I all head up to Chicago to visit the family! As always looking forward to the next Adventure!

item.title: Kauai Day 0/1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Day 0

Today we woke up around 3:30 am thanks to Bennet - we weren’t upset though because it just meant a few more snuggles before we left. We officially got up and ready at 4am and got packed into the car and left just after 5am.

We drove 2 hours up to Charleston for our flight (it was much cheaper). The drive was smooth and the Charleston airport is really nice. Becca had a surprise for me when we got there, more on that later. Our first flight to Atlanta went off on time without a hitch. We were forced to check our big backpacks which was annoying but not a huge deal. It was a short flight so I just listened to my audiobook on the way. The next flight was to LAX and an hour layover in Atlanta which meant we basically started boarding right when we got to the new gate.

The flight to LAX was also uneventful- about 3.5/4 hours. We didn’t see any fires while flying in. The layover here was also an hour so we boarded our final flight to Lihue (pronounced li-who-ee) relatively quickly. Unfortunately while we were racing to the runway the pilot announced there was a problem with one of the 4 fuel pumps and we needed to return to the gate so maintenance could take a look at it.

Long story short we ended up staying on the plane and they ended up getting the issue solved resulting in about a 2hour delay. Besides that slight hiccup the flight was uneventful. We landed in Kauai around 9:30pm. I went to get the car rental from Avis which took longer than anticipated and then we made our way to our motel which was only 5 minutes from the airport.

Day 1

Today we woke up early (still on east coast time) we stayed in the room until 7 and then went downstairs to the tip top motel cafe and bakery. The breakfast was actually pretty substantial and good. Becca and I both got omelets.

After breakfast we got loaded back up in the car and drove about 5 minutes back to the airport for our helicopter tour. After a quick safety briefing we met our pilot, Joe, and got into the helicopters!

Becca and I had been on a helicopter before in New Zealand, but the unique thing about these helicopters were that they had no doors. Which made the tour much more thrilling!

After getting strapped in the helicopter started and we took off. Becca and I were sitting in the back (it was like twice the price for front seats), but the views in the back were still awesome. Here’s a snapshot of our flight path:

I definitely don’t remember all the names of everything but here are the highlights of what we saw. The first big highlight was the Jurassic falls - which if you couldn’t guess is famous from the Jurassic park movie.

After seeing the falls we made our way over to the Waimea canyon - known as the Grand Canyon of the pacific.

We passed though some other canyons that had waterfalls until finally making our way to the famous Napali coast (the north coast of the island). This was by far my favorite part - amazing cliff formations jutting right into the ocean.

We weaved into and out of a few of the cliffs seeing some waterfalls and mountain goats. We also flew over kalaulua beach and the trail (part of which we’ll be hiking later).

After flying along the north coast we reached hanalei bay and the turned to head towards the middle of the island. Our last main stop was the kawaikini crater. This was a massive, half blown up crater in the middle of the island, super cool!

After the crater we made our way back to the Lihue airport for a smooth landing. I highly recommend a helicopter tour if you visit!

After the the tour we made a quick stop back at Avis (the car rental agency) they had charged me the wrong amount when they gave me the car last night and were able to fix it.

After that we made another quick stop at Walmart to get some snacks and breakfast food. Then we stopped at the Lydgate beach park. The beach was really nice, we found a spot by a “pool” created by rocks to lay our stuff down and relax.

Since I can’t sit still for too long I went on a run down the beach. The beach wasn’t too long, I ran 4.25 miles (just over 2 miles down and then back). On the run I ran into a seal sunbathing on the beach! Unfortunately I didn’t have my phone but I ended up going back with Becca and we got a picture :).

We left the beach around 1 and went to get lunch at a place called the Pono market. Unfortunately when we got there they had a sign up saying they were all sold out :(. So we ended up going to a place called Paco’s tacos that was right next door. The food was good, I had the special which was a carnitas burrito and Becca has tacos.

After eating we drove up north to where our Airbnb is, in princeville. We made a quick stop at the foodland grocery store to get some refrigerator items like milk. We also got some sushi and poke to have for dinner later (it was super inexpensive here!).

We had a bit of a difficult time finding our Airbnb due to the wrong address listed and the poor directions from the host. The Airbnb was also really quirky. It was basically a room in a condo with the only entrance being a sliding glass door into the bedroom. You could also tell they put a door in the halfway to partition off the room - but they didn’t separate the hallway light switch which we found out later when whoever is living in the other side of the hallway turned on their light :D.

After settling in we decided to go for a walk. We first checked out the shared pool, it wasn’t anything special. Then we went on a small hiking trail in the neighborhood that took us to the sea lodge beach.

The trail was really not that long -maybe 10 minutes tops. The beach was really cool though! Super secluded and surrounded by steep cliff walls. The sand was also really nice and there were big overhanging mango trees. We hung out at the beach for a while and watched the big waves crash in.

There was also a a rope swing attached to one of the mango trees so of course I had to try it. It was pretty small, hence the kind of lame looking pictures :D.

After hanging out at the beach we made our way back to the Airbnb and had our dinner. It was really good! We hung out in the room the rest of the night and watched Moana before passing out.

item.title: Kauai Day 2
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up early again (still on eastern time I guess). Becca ended up waking up around 7a. We ate some breakfast in the room and then got in the car and drove back to the east side of the island to get our kayak rental at 9a.

The kayak shop we rented from was xxxx, they were super friendly and helped us load up the two person kayak on top of the roof of our car with foam pads. They also gave us a map with directions on where to put the kayaks in and how to hike to the secret falls.

After loading up the kayak we drove about 2 miles to the Wailua river boat ramp to put in. It turned out there was some sort of school or club rowing race so the ramp was packed with people. Luckily we were able to unload and find a parking spot in the small lot.

Once on the river we paddled upstream for about 45 minutes and took the fork to the right and beached our kayaks at the start of the “secret” falls trailhead. Secret is a bit of a misnomer as just about everyone knows about as evidenced by the 1000 kayaks on the google maps aerial photo. Luckily for us they don’t do any guided tours on Saturdays so it was essentially empty.

After getting out of the kayaks we continued on foot about a mile. There was one big river crossing right at the start and after that it was a really well kept and flat trail to the falls.

The falls were really cool. There were only two other people there when we arrived. I went in the water to about my waist, it was really cold and I didn’t feel like going all the way in. We took a bunch of pictures and I flew the drone around for a bit.

Another thing I forgot to mention was there were a bunch of chickens/roosters at the falls. In general we’ve seen tons of roosters around Kauai, they’re literally everywhere. While resting at the falls I took the drone out and got a few shots.

After a nice break at the falls we hiked back to our kayaks. Unfortunately as we left one of my sandals randomly broke. It was still kind of wearable so I kept it on till we go to the kayaks. On the way back we passed a ton of other people (glad we went early!).

At the kayaks we paddled back to the fork in the river and this time went down the other side to see the fern grotto. The landing area for the kayaks was tiny and very sporty. Basically and muddy ledge you had to pull the kayak up onto.

Once on shore we walked 2 minutes to see the grotto. The other way to visit the grotto is by boat in a tour group which costs $35 per person. I’m super glad we didn’t do that, the grotto was cool but definitely underwhelming and I would have been really annoyed if I payed money to see it.

After taking a few pictures we went back and loaded into the kayak and continued paddling down the river. We heard there was a cliff jump spot so we wanted to check it out. After about 5–10minutes of paddling we found the spot. The cliff was pretty small and the water was cold so I decided to skip jumping.

After floating for a minute we turned around and started the paddle back to the dock. It probably took us an hour or so to make it back. Once at the dock we loaded up the kayak and then drove back to town for a quick lunch stop.

We ended up stopping at a Thai food truck. Becca got the fried rice and I got a chicken skewer.

After eating we returned the kayak to the rental shop and then drove to do a small hike called the sleeping giant. There are two trails for the hike and we did the west side.

The hike was short and relatively steep 1.7 miles and 600’ elevation.

The top of the hike was on the ridge of the Mountain and had awesome 360 views of the island. We took a bunch of pictures here and I flew the drone around for some videos and pictures.

After enjoying the views we hiked back down to the car and drove to a nearby beach called kealia beach. We relaxed and the beach for a couple hours.

After the beach we drove back and changed and then went to downtown Hanalei to the Kaylpso Island grill for dinner. I had a burger with grilled onion and Becca had a tuna salad.

After dinner we got ice cream at a place called Pinks. Becca and I split a 2 scoop bowl of the chocolate chip ripple and Mac nut. It was really good!

After the ice cream we went back to the Airbnb to get some rest for a big hiking day tomorrow!

item.title: Kauai Day 3 - Nā Pali Coast Hike
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up early at 5:20, we ate breakfast in the room and got all our stuff ready for the hike. We loaded up the car and left around 6am to drive to the shuttle parking lot. Our tickets were for 7am but we were told you could go on standby and get an earlier shuttle (the earliest starting at 6:20).

Luckily the early shuttle was practically empty so it was no problem getting on. The shuttle started in Waipa and we further along the coast to Haena park and the start of the Kalalau trail. The parking is very limited which is why a shuttle is required.

After dropping us off a park ranger gave us a quick briefing on the trail before letting us head out. We started on the trail just before 7am, it was still pretty dark so we used a head lamp for the first 30 minutes or so.

The trail was really nice, it basically weaves in and out of the mountains along the coast with great views. The first stop was past the first mountain ridge at a beach called Hanakapi’ai beach. There wasn’t much of a beach here due to the high surf which also meant no swimming allowed (the waves were enormous).

Here the trail splits one way goes down the valley between the two ridges to the Hanakapi’ai waterfall and the other continues down the coast until the Kalalau beach. To continue down the coast you need to have a permit (which we had) however no one checked it.

We continued hiking up and around the ridges of the coast for another ~3.5 miles taking a couple stops to enjoy the views and to get some drone shots.

I ended up hiking by myself a bit further (Maybe a mile and a half) while Becca rested. We had the walkie talkies with us so we could communicate and Becca was able to see me when I was out on the points. I hiked to a spot that jutted out pretty far towards the water and hiked down for some pictures. It was really windy and a steep ridge so I didn't even try to take the drone up.

The full trail goes even further, another ~4 miles to the beach, but we decided to turn back toward Hanakapi’ai beach so that we could have time to hike to the waterfall.

The hike to the waterfall was relatively short, 2 miles in 2 miles out with a couple river crossings. There was also a section with tons of bamboo.

The falls themselves were massive! We ended up eating a snack and enjoying the views for a bit. We also took some pictures and drone shots here too.

By the time we left the falls it was about 1pm. We made in back to Hanakapi’ai beach around two and had a short break before continuing back to the shuttle stop, arriving back at ~3:30. We made a quick stop at ke’e beach (right before the shuttle) and refilled our waters. We were really lucky with the great weather we had for the hike, perfectly clear skies and sunny. There were parts of the trail that you could tell would get really muddy if it rained.

The shuttle took us back to the car. We decided to make a stop at wishing well shave ice. I got “the local” and Becca got the Hanalei sweetie. The shave ice was delicious, it’s on top of ice cream and is drizzled with condensed milk, so yummy, I highly recommend!

After the shave ice we walked to a nearby food truck called elephant Thai and got some pad Thai to go.

We ended up going back to the room to shower and eat before going to sleep. We noticed that someone clearly was in our room (the adjoining door to the main house had moved the microwave we had set in front of it) so that was concerning. We contacted the folks from Airbnb and they told us that the cleaning crew had mistakenly opened the door, nothing seemed to be missing so that was good! Also they sent us $100, I guess to bribe us with a good review lol. The Airbnb is definitely strange - we have to enter through the sliding glass door and there is virtually no window treatment, the screen they have is completely see-through when the lights are on at night!

item.title: Kauai Day 4
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we slept in and had breakfast in the room again. Today was a much more chill day with no plans except to relax on the beach. We ended up FaceTiming with Bennett and my parents in the morning and taking our time getting up.

We left around 9am to go to Hanalei beach, which is the big beach right near the main town. We parked sort of in the middle of the beach and walked all the way to the west end and then back to the east where the pier is. There were really big waves near where we parked and much more mellow waves near the pier which is also where all the surfers were, besides a few really good surfers who were way out.

I jumped in the water at the pier which was refreshing. It was mostly sunny but drizzled a little but on our walk. At the east most part of the beach there is a small river and lagoon that we checked.

After we walked back to where we parked and payed out in the beach relaxing until about 1pm. We drove into town and had lunch at the chicken in a barrel BBQ restaurant. Becca got the ribs and I had the pulled pork, the food was good! There were even live chickens walking around the restaurant haha!

After eating we got a strawberry banana smoothie and walked around exploring the shops in the small downtown.

We decided to head back to the beach, this time we parked further east, closer to the pier. We relaxed on the beach some more and went in the water a few times.

We stayed until ~4 a went to the car when a quick rain shower hit (it passed in ~5min). We decided to stop again for some shave ice. This time we tried tropical bliss and rainbow, both were good but the local is still my favorite.

After eating we stopped at the Foodland to get poke for dinner, but sadly they were all out of poke!! I didn’t even realize that was possible! We ended up getting some sushi instead which was good but not as good as the poke :(.

We are back at the room and after eating we walked out on the golf course (backyard of the condo area) to see the course and watch the sunset. Right by our place there were a few albatross dancing and clucking their beaks to each other. We found out later that they mate for life and do their mating ritual to each other to strengthen their bonds.

We walked down hole 15 and 16 of the makati golf course (which looked really nice, right along the ocean). we couldn’t really see the sunset but the views were still great! There were lots of other people out walking around the course too.

On the way back to our room we saw that there was an albatross nesting right next to another one of the condo buildings!

Once back in the room we watched a movie and went to sleep.

item.title: Kauai Day 5
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today was another relaxing day we slept in, which for me was 6am :D, but to be fair we didn’t actually get up out of bed until 8 ish. We ate breakfast in the room and then got in the car to explore.

This first stop we tried to go to was called the queens bath. It was only about 5 minutes from our Airbnb and unfortunately we found out it was closed when we got there (there surf is too dangerous).

The next beach we tried was a little further down the road called hideaway beach. The parking lot for the beach was only 4 cars and was completely full so we ended up not going to this one either!

Next we decided to drive east about 20 minutes to Kauapea Beach, aka the secret beach. We noticed the light house was right nearby the beach trail so we made a quick stop there only to find out that it was closed as well!

Luckily the lot for the secret beach was open and had parking. To get to the beach we had to hike down for about 5-10minutes.

The beach itself was really nice, there wasn’t many people there and there were a bunch of good surfers.

The beach was relatively small with big rocks on either side. I walked out to the rocks which had good views of the coast.

After relaxing at the beach we hiked back up to the parking lot. There happened to be a right foot sandal sitting at the trailhead (the same side that broke for me) so I took it as a replacement!

We got in the car and drove to the foodland back in princeville for lunch. I had the poke bowl (thankfully they still were in stock!) and Becca had sushi.

After eating we drove to another beach a little closer east of princeville called Anini beach. This beach was a much longer beach and had more people. The water was also super shallow for a long way off the beach. I ended up going out and snorkeling.

Unfortunately I didn’t see anything except for a sea slug and two little fish.

We relaxed in the beach until about 3:30 and then drove to Hanalei for some shaved ice at wishing well. This time Becca got the local and I decided to try a smoothie from their coffee shop next door. The smoothie was banana and peanutbutter, it was pretty good but the local is still the best in my opinion!

After we walked two blocks down to the Tahiti Nui restaurant, we made reservations for 5pm, but they were able to seat us early (4:30). We saw this place in the movie The Descendants with George Clooney so we figured that we’d give it a try. I ended up getting the Tiki Man Pizza which had a bit of everything on it including pineapple, meat, and BBQ and Becca had the traditional Hawaiian pizza, gluten free of course.

The pizzas were good but a bit small and expensive, but they were tasty. After eating we drove back to the room to shower. I decided to go for a run. I ended up running down to the hideaway beach (it was only 2 miles away). The beach was cool, very small, and some steep steps to get down to.

After taking a quick selfie and enjoying the view, I ran back through the back nine of the Makati golf course and ended up meeting Becca in the tee box of the 13th hole to watch the sunset.

After enjoying the sunset we walked back to the room stopping to say hi to the albatross.

item.title: Kauai Day 6
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we had a slow morning, we ate in the room, packed everything into the car, and left around 9. We were heading down to stay at the south end of the island!

On the way to the south we stopped to do a little hike called Hoopii falls. The hike is in a neighborhood and you have to park along the side of the street. There was a cute trail dog who helped us find the start of the hike.

The hike was 2.6 miles total. We probably spent an hour and a half total. There were actually two sets of falls, the first on being about 2/3rds of the way down the trail.

After the first set you continue down the trail, there was also a cool frame and part of an engine of an old abandoned car.

Once you get to the end of the trail you’re at the top of the falls, we took some pictures there.

Then we hiked down to the base of the falls, it was a bit muddy and slippery so you had to be careful of your footing.

We explored the base of the falls and took some more pictures before heading back to the car.

Next we drove back towards the coast and stopped at Pono market to get some lunch. Luckily this time they were open! I ended up getting so poke with pineapple chicken and Becca had the pork laolao. We also got a berry smoothie to share. We got all the food to go and continued driving down to poipu beach.

On the way to Poipu we made a quick stop at Wailua waterfalls. You literally just drive up to it from the road. The view wasn't the best, but it was a really easy stop.

We also had to drive through the "Tree Tunnel" which was cool I guess but very underwhelming, basically just a road with a bunch of trees lol.

We ate the food at the picnic area by the beach being careful to not let any chickens steal it. I don’t think I mentioned this yet but Kauai is absolutely infested with chickens. They’re seriously everywhere - at the beach’s, on all the trails - and they aren’t afraid of humans at all.

The food was good after eating we went down to the beach which was fairly small and much more crowded than all the other beaches we had been to so far. There was also another sleeping seal on the beach, this one was roped off by volunteers.

We learned that these are monk seals and there are only about 1600 of them currently (their population is growing). They come up to the beach during the day to sleep and rest for around 10 hours and then they forage and hunt at night.

On the other side of the beach were a bunch of turtles who do the opposite, they come up to the beach to sleep at night. There were only two turtles when we first got to the beach but more and more kept coming up.

We ended up laying out by the turtles and relaxing. The beach was in a little bay/cove which made it good for snorkeling. Becca and I each took a turn snorkeling. There wasn’t a whole lot to see except for the big turtles.

We relaxed at the beach until 4 and then drove to our VRBO, the Ashton at Poipu, which was only a minute away. We checked in and got our keys and unit number and then drove to the condo.

This VRBO was so MUCH nicer than where we stayed in the north. It was huge, there was a full kitchen, living room, two beds, and two baths and most importantly there were blinds :D. After settling in we decided to go walk around. There were two different pools we could use. One was much more secluded and the other was bigger and had a hot tub! We also found out that the complex is connected to the berneccke beach and poipu beach by a nice walking trail that was only a few blocks away.

After exploring the resort area we decided to make a quick run to the Big Save grocery store for some snacks and dinner. After driving back and stocking the refrigerator we walked down to poipu beach to watch the sunset by the seal.

Before Walking back from the beach we counted 25 turtles! So many!

We walked back to the condo and made steaks and salad for dinner and then watched a movie before going to bed.

item.title: Kauai Day 7 - Waimea Canyon
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got up early at 6am, we ate some breakfast in the condo. We got packed in the car and left around 7 to drive west to the Waimea canyon. We were hiking the Awa’awapuhi trail, which was about 1 hour and 20 minutes drive.

We ended up being the first car in the parking lot of the trailhead. The trail itself was a bit muddy, I slipped and fell once but otherwise it wasn’t too bad.

The trail was all downhill for just under three miles, it started off chilly and warmed up as we descended and the sun came out. We stopped about halfway at a relatively open clearing on the ridge to take some pictures and drone shots.

The way down took about and hour and a half. At the end of the trail was an incredible view of the Nāpali coast! There was a small ridge you could hike out onto to get really cool pictures. We ended up taking a lot of pictures and flying the drone around (being careful not to fly when the helicopters were around).

We stayed on the ridge and enjoyed the view while we ate a snack. We hadn’t seen a single person on the trail so we had the hike and the view completely to ourselves!

After the snack we started the hike back up to the car. The hike back up was more strenuous than going down of course but the footing was easier going up. It ended up taking us about an hour and a half to get back up to the car. On the way back we passed by at least a dozen different people and the trailhead lot was fairly full of cars.

After doing the best to get the mud off our shoes we got in the car and drove further up the road to the Kalalau lookout. The lookout was pretty packed with people. The clouds were also a bit overcast so it was hard to see much.

We didn’t spend much time there before getting back in the car. Since we were already all the way down the road we figured we might as well drive to the end which is where the start of the alakai trail is. However the road was closed right after the viewpoint which would have added an extra 2 miles to the alakai trail (glad we didn’t choose to hike that one!).

Next we drove to the Pu’u Hinahina Lookout. There wasn’t any parking so we created a spot, we ended up only staying for a quick picture at the lookout and then drove back down the road a few blocks to park and start the cliff lookout trail that goes to the waipo’o falls.

The trail was relatively short. The first half mile was down a dirt road that you could drive down if you had a 4wd car. After the road it was only 0.1 miles to the cliff lookout which had really good views of the canyon.

After the cliff lookout it was only another 0.6 miles to the falls. Honestly the falls you could see were pretty tiny but the view of the canyon was really nice. We took some pictures and ended up eating a snack and enjoying the view.

We made the short hike back to the car and the. Started the drive back down to the coast. On the way down we stopped at two more viewpoints. The first viewpoint was the Pu'u Ka Pele Lookout. It was a quick pull off in the side of the road that had views looking back across the canyon to the cliff we were just hiking and the falls that we hiked above.

The next stop was called the Waimea Canyon Lookout. This was a much bigger stop with lots of people. The view was pretty similar to the last stop.

Unfortunately a massive tour bus left just before us so we were stuck following it slowly most of the way back down.

Once we got back to the coast we decided to stop in port Allen at the Kauai Island Brewing Company. The food was good I had the grilled chicken sandwich and Becca had a pulled pork bowl over rice. I also tried one of their hazy IPAs called pillow talk that was also really good.

After eating we drove over to the nearby glass beach. A glass beach is exactly what it sounds like a beach with a bunch of glass. They actually call it sea glass, and the glass comes from discarded glass trash which overtime got broken up and smoothed into little glass pebbles and washed up on the beach. It’s actually really hard to tell there’s glass on the beach unless you look closely. Most of the glass is brown but there are a lot of other colors as well. There are only a handful of glass beaches in the world.

It was interesting to see but after staying for a few minutes and taking some pictures we hopped back into the car and drove back to the condo.

We decided to go to the pool to relax and hangout in the hot tub and then walked down to the beach to checkout how many turtles there were tonight, there weren’t as many. We took a quick picture and made our way back to the condo to eat and hangout before bed.

item.title: Kauai Day 8
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 7 and made a big breakfast in the condo of eggs and bacon. I ended going out for a run down the coast at 8. I ran past shipwreck beach where there is a super nice hotel called the grand hayatt. And then I ran down the Maha'ulepu (Heritage) Trail which took me through a deep sandy bluff and past some really nice coastline and onto a golf course!

The view from the course was really nice. The trail continued back down to the coast and ended near the Makauwahi Cave Reserve. I ran through and took a picture of the “cave” it wasn’t much to look at but I think the main cave was closed. The trail was blocked by a massive puddle of water.

After seeing the trail I decided to take another route back this time following the roads. The views weren’t as good as the coast but it was definitely easier not having to contend with the sand.

I made it back about an hour later and 5.5 miles. After showering we walked down to the hot tub to relax for a bit.

For lunch we decided to get some Thai food from the Anatta’s thai food truck. We both got the pad Thai which was really good. There were a bunch of chickens and chicks walking around begging for food while we ate.

After lunch we decided to drive to see the spouting horn (just a few minutes west of us). The horn was definitely a tourist trap, there were two massive tour buses there so it was packed with people. It’s basically just a blowhole that shoots water up in the air occasionally when the waves hit. We took a quick picture and then got out of there.

We stopped at Lawa'i Beach on the way back to relax. It was a really small beach but not quite as crowded as Poipu. There was a shave ice food truck across the street from the beach called Riptides so we had to try it. I got strawberry, Blue raspberry, and cherry with ice cream and condensed milk. It was really good but still not as good as wishing wells shave ice.

After relaxing at the beach we made our way back to the condo and then decided to walk over to shipwreck beach. It’s a little farther than poipu (about 0.5 miles) but it’s still connected to the greenway so very easy to walk to.

We rested at the beach for the rest of the afternoon. There was a big cliff that juts out at the end of the beach. I hiked out there to see about jumping off. It was really hard to tell how deep the water was below it so I decided to not jump. I did see a cool turtle swimming by though!

There was also a group that had a pretty legit volleyball court setup on the beach. Unfortunately the people playing weren’t legit so I didn’t try to play.

After the beach we went back to the pool/hot tub for a bit. Then for dinner we went and picked up some Indian food from a nearby restaurant. Becca and I both got the chicken tikka masala, it was really good.

We ate at the condo and then decided to walk down to Poipu beach again to see the turtles. Since the sun had already gone down there was a ton of them. We stayed and watched for a while as more came ashore.

After hanging out for 20 minutes or so we went back to the condo to sleep.
