item.title: Kauai Day 9
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today I woke up before Becca and had some eggs for breakfast. I left around 7:10 to drive down to Koloa Landing for scuba diving, unfortunately Becca wasn’t able to scuba :). It turned out that I was the only person signed up for scuba today so it was just me and two guides: Jimi and Alejandra. Also since it was just me instead of taking a boat we were taking DPVs (diver propulsion vehicles), basically underwater scooters, to the dive sites.

We were in the water by 7:40. I played with the DPV at the surface to get the hang of it while Jimi set up the mooring buoy. We went underwater at 7:50 and then made our way out to the first dive site called rock house. Right off the landing was a massive bait ball (basically a ton of fish, like thousands), we also saw two sharks - they were a bit further away and I wasn’t able to get a picture of them quick enough.

We scootered about 10 minutes to get to the site. The scootering was so fun! I’m sold. Whenever we live somewhere where we have quick access to scuba diving I’m definitely buying one!

The dive site was basically a bunch of big rocks in the sand. We parked the scooters at the mooring line and then swam around the site for about 30 minutes. We saw some fish, a few big turtles and some little crabs in the coral.

After exploring the site we got back in the scooters and made our way back to Koloa landing. We parked the scooters underwater at the mooring line, went back on the shore for our surface interval, and exchanged our tanks.

After about 40 minutes we got our gear back on and swam out to the mooring line to start the second dive. We descended and got the scooters and then began heading out to our next dive site called Sheraton Caverns. The dive site took about 15 minutes to get to with the scooters. Once at the site we tied up the scooters and began exploring the site.

The site is actually collapsed lava tubes around 60’ under water. We swam through a bunch of the collapsed tubes. There were tons of big turtles swimming around and a lot sleeping.

After exploring the site we got back in the scooters and made our way back to the boat ramp. We did our safety stop near the bait ball so I got to swim around all the fish. There was also a turtle swimming nearby so we said hi to him.

Once back at the dock we got all the gear out of the water and dried off. I drove back to the condo and met up with Becca.

My back was a bit sore (I think from slipping on the mud), so we did some yoga to loosen up before heading to the pool.

At the pool there were a bunch of older people doing a water aerobics class. I stayed in the hot tub and relaxed. After the pool we went back to the condo and then drove about 20 minutes to see the “historic” town of Hanapepe.

The town itself was pretty tiny, there was a cool old wooden suspension bridge that we walked across, but other than that there wasn’t much to see.

After the town we went to the nearby salt pond beach park. It’s named that because there is a salt pond right next to the beach. We walked past it on the way to the beach park- it wasn’t much to see, just some small ponds. There was a family that arrived there when we did and scraped some salt off the top of one of them.

We relaxed at the beach for a few hours. There was a seal on this beach too so we went and said hi to him.

The beach was also right next to a small airport. Unfortunately no airplanes landed or took off while we were there. After relaxing we drove to the port to go on our whale watching tour. We arrived a little early so we got some ice cream at the store near the shop before meeting the boat captain and going down to the boat.

I really wasn’t expecting much from the tour, however it was a blast! The boat captains were pretty young guys that were hilarious and had great music selection to go along with their commentary.

There were only 8 others on the boat which meant we had a lot of space to get up and see the whales.

On the way out from the dock we saw a pod of dolphins, there must have been at least 2 dozen of them! It didn't take long before our captains spotted some whales and began cruising over to them. To spot the whales you basically look for their spouts which isn't as difficult as it sounds to see on the horizon.

The first few whales we found were just showing their tails, but after a little while we found two whales that were breaching. It was super cool to see, the whales are absolutely massive and they launch themselves out of the water and make a massive splash (all in an attempt to woo the female whales for mating of course).

After the tour we drove back to the hotel stopping at the Big Monster Sushi food truck. The Bowl I got was super delicious.

After eating we went back to the hotel and then to bed.

item.title: Nicaragua 2025
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Back again, this time with a mobile Bennett and a baby Scott in tow which will certainly lead to more fun challenges! We’re going down to explore Nicaragua! We’ve decided to keep our recent travel to Central America and the Caribbean to avoid long flights and time changes with Bennett.

Some fun facts about Nicaragua: It is the largest country by land mass in Central America and is home to the largest lake in Central America.

Here's the map of where we're planning to go and the rough itinerary.

item.title: Day 8/9 - Naples to Milan to USA
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we finally slept in till around 10am. It was kind of a crappy day with storms coming in and out. We didn't have anything planned so we went to the nearby pastry shop to grab some breakfast. Pat and Sarah had to leave afterwards to catch their flight so Rachel and I decided to walk around the city. We ended up walking down towards the docks to see about possibly going to the nearby island of procido but the times the ferry was available wasn't going to get us back soon enough. We ended walking into a local grocery store to pick up some snacks for the train ride and then made our way down Toledo street to a local restaurant that was down one of the alleyways. It was a really small place and we were the only Tourists there, we got some sort of combo meal and they ended up bringing us out 2 huge plates of food each! Everyone in the restaurant was really nice to us but were nervous that Rachel didn't like the food because she couldn't finish all of it. I was barely about to stuff all the food down. 

After eating we walked to the Toledo metro station, which according to Giovanni is the most beautiful metro station in the world! It was decorated very uniquely. We took the metro to the Naples train station and got there about 2.5 hours before our train which gave us time to catch up on our blogs and do some reading.

item.title: Kauai Day 10/Home
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we got up around 7:30. We just checked into our flight online when less than an hour later we got notified that the flight was delayed from 9pm to 1am!! Which of course meant we would miss all our connections.

Fortunately we were able to work with delta and we got on an earlier flight home at 2:30pm. This time going to Honolulu and then to Atlanta and finally Charleston. It honestly worked out a lot better!

We ended up making a big breakfast finishing all the eggs and bacon.

Then we packed up most of our stuff and walked down to poipu beach to see the turtles one last time. There were only two there this early in the morning.

From the beach we stopped at the pool. I hung out in the hot tub for a while talking to a friendly guy who’s lived on the island for 10 years.

After the hot tub we got everything packed up into the car and checked out of our condo. We left at 10:30 to go to the Kauai plantation railway at kilohana tour. We had booked the tour to kill some time before our late flight. The tour was a train ride around the plantation. It was interesting, we made a stop to feed some pigs, horses, a cow, and a donkey which was fun!

The tour was only 40min. After the tour we drove to the fish express to get some poke. The food was good!

After eating in the car we drove 5 minutes to the airport to drop off the car and then get to the gate. Unfortunately the TSA here was very strict and confiscated Becca’s hiking poles :(.

The rest of the trip back home was pretty uneventful. We made it to Atlanta and then to Charleston and then drove back home. It was great to see Bennett again!

item.title: Nicaragua Day 0/1
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 3:45 am, ate breakfast, packed the car, and drove to the airport for our 7am flight. The flight to Miami was painless and surprisingly Bennett slept for most of it! In Miami our connection gate was in the same terminal, and we had plenty of time to get there - much better than our recent experiences sprinting through the Miami airport! The flight from Miami to Managua was also easy, just over two hours and Bennett slept for over half of it!

snacks in MIA

Everything was going so smoothly, it was refreshing! That is until we went through customs in Nicaragua and my bag got flagged… it turns out Nicaragua has a very strict no drones policy. I was starting to freak out because I didn’t want to lose my drone- especially to customs. There was another person there who had a drone that was also being confiscated. The customs agents ended up taking lots of pictures and letting me take a picture of the "form" they filled out. We also had some tape with us so we ended up quickly labeling everything with my name and information. Once it was all documented they put my drone in an old liquor box...hopefully I see it again!

After leaving customs we got our rental car. The car rental was smooth- a quick shuttle across the street and no surprises. We had a small manual Suzuki Dzire. From the airport we had a 2 hour drive to the city of Leon. Bennett slept the entire car ride - he's such a trooper! We’re staying at the Hotel el Convento- one of the best in the city but still inexpensive. After checking in and unpacking, we explored the hotel and the pool.

We walked to the main square downtown and ate dinner at el Sesteoro. I had the beef skewers and Becca had the pork. A lady selling stuff came up to us and Bennett firmly said "No!" to her :). At the end of dinner our waitress picked Bennett up (without talking to us) and took him back into the kitchen to show him to the rest of the workers. Becca and I freaked out a little, and Becca followed her, luckily she wasn't abducting him!

Bennett loved the beans!

After eating we walked inside the church and then stopped at a super market to get some water and cash. We walked back to the hotel and hung out. Bennett went to sleep at 7. My volcano tour for tomorrow cancelled (not enough people) so I scrambled to rebook with a different company. I also booked massages for us. $40 total for two of us 40 minutes each... we’ll be doing a lot more of these this trip!

Day 1

We woke up around 5:45am (Bennett's usual). We ate breakfast at the hotel which was a buffett with sausage, bacon, fruit, and pastries. Bennett ate so much!

We got ready and Becca walked with me to the Bigfoot Hostel where I got my refund for the previously cancelled tour. The other tour was directly across the street in another hostel called Via Via. The tour was done through Volcano Day. I did the basic tour for $25. The only difference between the basic and “all-in” tour was you paid $10 more for a shirt and sandwich.

I said bye to Becca and Bennett as my tour left for the volcano around 9am. We took a big truck that drove us ~1 hour to the entrance of the nature reserve, and then to the parking lot at the start of the hike. The horn on the truck was obnoxiously loud, like it seriously hurt your ears and the driver was happy to honk it every chance he got!

We arrived at the base of the volcano and got our gear (overalls, goggles, and a board), took a team picture, and started the hike up. The hike itself was super easy. I think we took more breaks than actual hiking (there were a few very slow people that were very out of shape and clearly not hikers, they even paid extra for someone to carry their board up). At the breaks we took some pictures the view of the volcano and surrounding area was beautiful.

It took around an hour to get to the top (including the stops). At the top we left our boards and walked along the ridge of the volcano to see the crater. The ground is actually super hot when you dig down an inch past the top layer - you can actually like a cigarette or cook and egg with the ground.

After seeing the crater we went back to the boards and got some quick instructions on how to go fast and slow. You are not able to wear your backpack on your back, it has to go in the front, which looks a bit silly. The basic instructions were to lean back and keep your feet off the board (for stability).

Next we hiked down a short ways to the start of the sled run. I was the first to go down, the start of the run was relatively slow and then it picked up speed (supposedly 100kph ~60mph). I was holding my GoPro with one hand which made it a bit more difficult to control the board.

I ended up fishtailing and wiping out near the end of the run. Overall the run took about 2 minutes to sled down. It was a fun and unique experience. I do wish I could’ve done it multiple times since the hike really was pretty short. I could’ve definitely done it at least twice in the time it took the slow people to hike up.

Since I was first I waited at the bottom and watched as the rest of the group made their way down. There was one girl who tried to snowboard down - she failed miserably. The tour guide said he’s only ever seen 2 people do it successfully and one was a professional snowboarded.

Once everyone was done we loaded back into the truck and drove back to Leon. Bennett and Becca were napping. I walked back to the hotel and stopped at a smoothie shop on the way.

When I got back Bennett had just woken up from his nap. We relaxed for a bit enjoying our smoothies in the air conditioning - it’s hot here!

After our siesta we walked about 10 minutes to a spa to get massages. We had to alternate since one of us had to watch Bennett - so Becca went first. While Becca was getting her massage we walked down to the main square with Bennett to kill some time.

We made our way back to the spa after about 30 minutes. Becca didn’t end up finishing until 4:30...an hour and a half later... I’m not sure if the lady lost track of time or what lol. Once she was done Becca took Bennett back to the hotel while I did my massage. Overall it was not nearly strong enough for me, but it was cheap so hard to complain. They also did this thing called cupping at the end which is basically suctioning glass cups to your back. It felt like how it sounds and it left some massive marks on my back, basically big hickies.

After my massage I met Becca and Bennett at a nearby restaurant called Tacuba. I had a beef burrito that was pretty good!

After dinner we went back to the hotel and relaxed before going to bed.

item.title: Nicaragua Day 2 - Granada
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we had our typical Bennett 5:30 am wake up call :). The hotel buffet breakfast opened at 6 am and they had an omelette station today which was tasty. The hotel is square shaped with a big courtyard in the middle and a fountain. The fountain had a bunch of fish in it that Bennett loved looking at.

After breakfast we took a dip in the pool- Bennett’s favorite part of Nicaragua. He’s learning to blow bubbles! He also really enjoyed being thrown up in the air and splashing.

After the pool, we got dressed and walked to the main square. We tried to go to the top of the main church in the city center, but we had a lot of difficulty finding the entrance. We looked everywhere with no luck and thought it was closed. I called the phone number on google maps to be sure and found out it was indeed open- the ticket office was in a tiny alcove on the back of the church.

We climbed the narrow staircase up to the top of the church (it’s not a super tall church).

At the top you had to remove your shoes and walk around barefoot. There were nice views of the city and you could see the surrounding volcanoes.

The top of the church had lots of domes and was all white- it was very reminiscent of Santorini Greece to me.

After visiting the church we went back to the hotel to relax. We ended up checking out and loading up the car around 10:30am to head towards the city of Granada, a ~2.5 hour drive.

We arrived in Granada around 1pm at the hotel. They were able to hold our bags for us and let us park the car while we waited until 2pm for our room.

We ended up waiting at the hotel pool which was in the courtyard. The pool/courtyard area was beautiful. Bennett loved splashing and blowing bubbles in the pool.

Our room was finally ready just after 2 - it was actually one of the rooms on the ground floor of the courtyard just steps from the pool. After settling into our room we walked to a nearby restaurant called La Frontera for a late lunch/early dinner. I had a burger that was really good!

After eating we decided to take a quick walk to the free chocolate museum to check it out. There were some signs and a gift shop- really not worth it if it's at all out of your way, but it was close to our hotel.

After a quick walk through the chocolate museum we decided to walk down to the boardwalk ~1 mi from the city center. The board walk is on lake Cociboica (where Ometepe island is).

The walk down was nice, there was an old church we passed and some Nicaraguan ladies who thought Bennett was super cute and wanted to take pictures with him :D.

We took some pictures at the lake and hung out enjoying the view before heading back to the hotel to relax. At the hotel we had some smoothies at the attached smoothie bar, they were pretty delicious. Becca ended up getting hungry so she ended up walking around the block to get some food from a nearby restaurant.

Once back at the hotel Becca took a picture of my back with the aftermath of the cupping from the massage 😳.

Basically looks like a bunch of big hickies/bruises. Hopefully it doesn't stay like this for too long! We hung out in our room for the rest of the night before going to bed.

item.title: Nicaragua Day 3 - Ometepe
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up around 5:30 am again, thanks Bennett ;). Unfortunately breakfast didn't open until 7am, so we hung out in the room and packed up to go.

Breakfast was poolside at a table just outside our room. They had a menu (instead of a buffet). I had the American breakfast which consisted of eggs, bacon, toast, and fruit. It was pretty good. Bennett had the pancakes and Becca had the Nicaraguan tradicional which was eggs, fried plantains, rice & beans, and fruit.

Everything was good. After eating we finished packing and checked out of the hotel. I went around to get the car and we loaded up. This drive was about an hour and a half to the town of San Jorge, which is a main port on the lake for the Ometepe ferry.

The drive was smooth though we did get “stopped” twice by female police officers to check our documents. I’m not sure if I was driving too fast or something (probably) but they didn’t stop any of the cars behind me. We got to the port just after 9. A man there helped us figure out how to get all the tickets and everything for the car, he seemed sketchy at first, but he never asked for money or anything from us. It was way easier than I thought it would be. Overall it was around 800 cordoba for everything.

After we got the tickets we got our car lined up for the ferry. About 10 am (30 minutes before) they had us load the cars onto the ferry. We ended up parking with the passenger side super close to the wall of the boat so Becca had to climb over the car seat to get out!

The ferry left right at 10:30 am (surprisingly prompt for Nicaragua). The ride was really smooth and the boat was relatively empty so there was a lot of space.

The ride took about an hour. Getting off was easy and we decided to stop for lunch at a nearby restaurant called Comedor Esmeralda. I had a burrito that was really good and big.

Some random dudes, Gustavo and Allen, came up to us and chatted. They were really friendly (definitely drunk) and of course one was trying to promote his tour company lol. Also of course the cook and waitress loved Bennett.

After eating we drove about 50 minutes to our hotel, Totoco Eco-Lodge. On the way we had to drive across the literal runway of the island airport which was pretty cool.

We had read reviews that the road up to our hotel was bad and you needed a 4x4 suv to make it - that was not at all the case. The road was mostly paved the whole way- a little rocky and steep but overall not bad.

Our hotel was... interesting. Any place with “Eco” in the name should probably be a big red flag. Overall the place was nice- beautiful views and friendly staff. We were disappointed the pool was pretty dirty with algae- Bennett was especially disappointed he didn’t get to swim. There was also a minor ant infestation in our bathroom…and no air conditioning.

On the plus side they had a spiritual OM class in their Yoga hut haha. Bennett loved all the strange instruments they had and the views were great. We stayed for ~10 min which was plenty for us!

Afterwards we ended up hanging out in the main lobby of the lodge enjoying the views. The island is made up of two volcanos, the lodge is on the side of one of the volcanoes and has a great view of the other one.

Eventually we ate dinner their too. I had a chicken pasta that was pretty good.

After eating we went to bed with the fans on full blast trying to stay cool and not get eaten by insects haha.

item.title: Nicaragua Day 5 - Maderas Volcano
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 5 AM, thanks again Bennett :-). We hung out in the room until 6:30 and then made our way up to reception for breakfast.

Because I was doing the volcano hike they had an early breakfast already prepared for me at 6:45. I had the scrambled eggs and toast.

After eating, I met my guide Moises, got my sandwich from the kitchen for lunch on the trail, my $3 entrance ticket, and then we loaded up into our car.

I think technically you don’t need a guide to hike the volcano. However, everything I read online recommended it because the trail is confusing. It was $45 for a private guide which is a bit steep for Nicaragua, but I wanted to do the hike.

We drove about 10 minutes from the lodge to get to the entrance of the trail. The entire trail was in the forest and was very steep. Luckily it hadn’t rained much, but you could tell if it was wet it would be very, very muddy.

After about an hour of hiking, we made it to the Mirador, which is a viewpoint where you can see the other volcano. Unfortunately, it was cloudy so all we could see was some of the coastline.

We continued hiking. I was actually leading the hike and it seemed pretty easy to follow the trail. I’m not sure I really needed a guide at all. The guide was super friendly though. We talked mostly in Spanish so I could practice, but his English was pretty good. We talked about sports, work, life, politics, just about everything lol.

It was super hot and I was drenched in sweat, my shoes were actually starting to get soggy. It was pretty gross! The last bit of the trail was also fairly muddy, even though there wasn’t a whole lot of rain. We made it to the peak after two hours. Luckily the clouds had cleared and we were able to get some really good views of the crater and the lagoon inside of it.

We hopped down into the crater, which took about 10 minutes, and then ate lunch. I had a snack bar and sandwich. The sandwich was skimpy on the meat. Because it hadn’t rained a lot the water level in the lagoon was too low to swim. I tried to walk to the edge to put my feet in and sank up to my shins in mud, not worth it!

After eating, relaxing, and taking some pictures, we started to make our way back down. The hike down was a bit quicker. We passed by several groups of people on their way up. We took one short break at the Mirador. The clouds had dispersed and we could see the volcano, so I took a few pictures.

From there we continued all the way back down to the car. The total time of the hike was about four hours (including the breaks and lunch). Originally the hotel receptionist told me it would take eight hours lol.

We got back in the car and drove the 10 minutes back to the Toto Eco Lodge. I had a celebratory beer with the guide (his request lol). The national beer Toña was actually pretty good.

After the beer and settling up I went back to our cabin to see Becca and Bennett. Bennet had just gone down for a nap so we hung out on our porch and relaxed in the hammock.

Bennett woke up at 1:45 pm and we decided to go check out the “best beach in Ometepe”, Playa Santo Domingo. We made a quick stop at the Ocean Mart our or way and got some cash, drinks, and snacks. We ended up deciding to stop at a restaurant on the beach called Comedor Julia.

The restaurant was pretty janky, but was well reviewed on Google. The first table we sat down to had ants that started biting me, so we shifted a couple tables over. We ended up getting a fish to share. It was tilapia and it was really delicious.

While waiting for the food, I went to put my feet into the water just to say I did, but the beach itself was not very nice.

There was also a flock of very aggressive birds eying our food who were very happy to see Bennett dropping pieces of food left and right.

After eating, we made our way back to the lodge for our massages. This massage did not disappoint. They were so good and so cheap we immediately scheduled another one for the next day. Becca went first at 4pm while Bennett and I played in the pool and at the reception building. Then I had my massage at 5pm. Afterwards I met Becca and Bennett for dinner in the reception area. I had the chicken again and it was really good.

After eating, we made our way back to the lodge for our final night without AC. ￼

item.title: Nicaragua Day 6 - Playa El Coco
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at five again and cuddled with Bennett. We got most of our things packed and ready, and then went up to breakfast around 6:30. It was a little early for breakfast, but they were able to actually get our breakfast a little before seven. We had the same thing as before-I had the continental, Becca had the Nicaraguan, and Bennett had pancakes.

After eating, Becca decided to do the yoga class at 8 am while I hung out with Bennett. Bennett and I went in the gross pool one last time, played, showered, and packed up the car.

Yoga ended at 9am, Becca said the yoga class was really good. We all went back to the cabin while Becca showered and packed, and then we left around 10am to go back to the ferry at Mayogalpa.

The drive took a little under an hour. We made a quick stop at a bank right before the ferry. There was a strange looking dude as we pulled up to the ferry entrance who helped us get the tickets and everything settled for the car which was slightly confusing. We were supposed to have a reservation for 12 but since we were there early, they were able to load us on the 11:30 ferry, which was super nice.

This ferry had an open air top, which was a lot nicer. On the ride back we had some really good views of the island and the volcanoes. After just over an hour on the ferry, we made it to San Jorge. We loaded back into the car and started driving towards the Pacific coast- San Juan del sur.

It was about 45 minutes to San Juan Del Sur. We stopped at Pali - the local grocery store- then made a quick stop at the gas station before driving into town for lunch.

We ate at a place called King Curry which was right on the beach. While waiting for our food, I went out onto the beach to put my feet in the water and to check it out. The views were really nice and the water was the perfect temperature.

I had their version of butter chicken, which was really good. It was like a fusion between Asian and Indian curry that had a sweet flavor to it with pineapples. Which sounds kind of weird, but it was actually really good. The naan bread with the dish was also delicious.

After eating, we got back into the car and drove another 30 minutes to Playa El Coco, a small beach south of San Juan del Sur where we were staying. The road to get there was a mix of really nice new highway and bumpy dirt road. It honestly is kind of in the middle of nowhere and I was very pleasantly surprised to see how nice the condos were that we are staying in.

The place was literally a compound- a private gate with at least six security guards patrolling. The unit we were in was very nice. Downstairs there is a large kitchen, dining room, living room, and a sliding door that opens to the garden area with the pool and beach. On the second floor there are three bedrooms and an upper deck. And most importantly it had air conditioning!

The condo also has a really nice shared pool that had a big shallow end, which was perfect for Bennett, and was directly on the beach. This beach is much more secluded and private. On the busiest day we maybe saw ten other people there.

We spent the rest of the day in the pool and on the beach. We watched the sunset at 6 PM on the beach. We started a family tradition of eating mangoes on the beach at sunset.

A cool photo one of our condo neighbors took of us having a sunset picnic on the beach.

item.title: Nicaragua Day 4 - Horseback Riding
item.dc:creator: jackjmwelter22
item.content:encoded:
Today we woke up at 5am, we hung out in the room and got all ready until just before 7am. At 7 we walked up to the reception area to eat our breakfasts. I had the continental breakfast which was eggs, toast, fruit, coffee, and juice. Becca had the Nicaraguan and Bennett had the pancakes. It was all tasty!

After breakfast we finished getting ready and loaded into the car. We made a stop at the nearby supermarket to get some cash and a few snacks for the horseback riding trip.

After the quick stop we drove about 25 minutes to the south side of the island to Finca Montana to meet our tour guide and horses. They took some time to get us sorted out they originally had Bennett and I on different horses, but then decided to switch us because Bennet and I weighed too much for the small horse :/.

After getting comfortable on the horses and taking a few pictures we made our way to the main road to start the trip around 9 am.

After literally 20 minutes my horse was not having a good time we ended up switching horses with the guide - who was on a much bigger white horse. This horse was much more comfortable, however he was also more "wild" so the guide had to hold onto him with a rope (instead of letting us ride free).

We rode on the road which went along the coast with lots of nice views and then turned inland into a nature preserve where the trail part began. We chose this trip because it went to a very popular waterfall (which you can also hike to), it was a little longer, but because we were able to knock out two things at once (horseback riding, and waterfall hike) it was worth it.

Becca was really good at riding - she had some practice from when she was little.

We made it past the entrance into the preserve and then pretty quickly onto some steep and tight trails. We put a lot of faith into the horses not to trip!

After about an hour and a half we made it to a tie off point for the horses (it was too steep beyond for them) and hiked about 15 minutes up to the waterfall. The waterfall was nice, nothing super spectacular but very isolated.

Once at the waterfall we took a snack break and went into the fall to cool off and take some pictures.

We made our way back to the farm the same way we came. on the way back Bennett fell asleep on the horse. I have no idea how he was able to sleep with his head bouncing up and down so much :D!

We made it back to the farm around 1pm and got the horses put away and everything settled up. We got back in the car and stopped for lunch at a restaurant on the way back to the lodge. I'm writing this blog well after the fact and can't quite remember what I had.

Bennett was starting to fuss and the waitress brought him a mango to eat and he absolutely loved it! It may be his new favorite food - she gave us a bunch more to bring back with us for later.

Back at the lodge we hung out - Becca and I had some massages booked. Becca went first so I watched Bennett - we ran around and explored the lodge. I had a massage after Becca - it was probably one of the best I've had, the lady was superr strong!

After the massages we ate dinner at the lodge. I had a chicken plate which was good.
